## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Governing Body authorized and documented the closure/CHOW decision. | Review of Governing Body meeting minutes. | Decision documented in minutes with rationale, authorization, and designated lead. |
| All regulatory notifications submitted within required timeframes. | Review of notification submission dates against regulatory deadlines. | 100% of notifications submitted within required timeframes. |
| All patients notified in writing at least 30 calendar days before closure. | Review of patient notification records. | 100% of patients and caregivers notified at least 30 calendar days before closure. |
| All patients safely transitioned before the agency's last date of service. | Review of Patient Transition Plans and discharge/transfer documentation. | 100% of patients transitioned; zero patients abandoned. |
| Employees received required advance notice. | Review of employee notification dates against WARN Act requirements. | WARN notice provided at least 60 calendar days in advance if applicable; all employees notified. |
| Financial closeout completed and reported to Governing Body. | Review of final financial report. | Report completed within 30 calendar days of closure; all outstanding financial obligations documented. |
| All records preserved and custodian designated. | Review of custodian designation and records inventory. | Records custodian formally designated before closure; all records accounted for. |
| All credentials surrendered or transferred. | Review of Agency Credential Register and surrender confirmations. | All credentials surrendered, terminated, or transferred with confirmation documented. |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors and state agency reviewers assessing a closure or CHOW will verify:
Evidence that patients were properly notified and transitioned. This is the primary regulatory concern. CMS will verify that all patients received advance written notice, were offered a choice of alternative providers, and were safely transitioned with appropriate clinical documentation (OASIS, clinical summaries, medication reconciliation). Patient abandonment — a patient left without arranged continued care — is the most serious potential finding.
Evidence that CMS and state notifications were timely. CMS will review the timing of the agency's notification relative to the closure or CHOW effective date. Late or absent notifications are regulatory violations.
Evidence that clinical records were preserved and accessible. CMS may request records for patients served during the agency's period of certification. Inability to produce records is a post-closure compliance failure.
Evidence that OASIS submissions were completed. CMS will verify that all required OASIS assessments (transfer, discharge) were completed and transmitted per OASIS requirements.
Evidence that financial obligations were resolved. CMS may conduct a post-closure audit of claims submitted during the agency's period of certification. Unresolved overpayments, late-filed claims, or billing irregularities are compliance concerns.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patients not notified in advance; services abruptly cease. | Patient abandonment; CMS enforcement; state investigation; potential harm to patients. | Patient notification per Section 6.4.2 at least 30 calendar days in advance; individualized transition plans per Section 6.4.3; continuation of services until all patients are placed per Section 6.4.7. |
| Regulatory notifications not submitted or submitted late. | Violation of 42 CFR Part 489; California licensure violation; potential penalties. | Notification timelines per Sections 6.2 and 6.3; Compliance Officer tracking of all notification deadlines. |
| Clinical records not preserved after closure. | HIPAA violation; inability to respond to patient access requests or regulatory audits; potential False Claims Act exposure. | Records custodian designated per Section 6.7.2; records preserved for full retention period per CO-HP-007. |
| OASIS transfer/discharge assessments not completed. | OASIS submission violation; CMS data integrity finding. | Director of Nursing ensures all OASIS assessments completed before last date of service per Section 6.4.4 and Section 6.6.2. |
| WARN Act notice not provided when required. | California WARN Act violation; employee lawsuits; financial penalties. | HR Director assesses WARN Act applicability per Section 6.5.2; 60-day notice issued if applicable. |
| Overpayments not identified or refunded during closeout. | False Claims Act exposure; CMS audit finding; potential civil monetary penalties. | Financial reconciliation per Section 6.6.3; overpayment reporting per FN-BC-004. |
| Governing Body does not authorize the closure/CHOW through a formal vote. | Unauthorized agency action; governance failure; legal challenge by stakeholders. | Formal Governing Body authorization per Section 6.1.1; documented in meeting minutes. |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 The Administrator, Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, CFO, and HR Director shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of appointment. Training shall cover: (a) the types of events that trigger this policy; (b) the regulatory notification requirements and timelines for CMS, HCAI, and DHCS; (c) the patient transition process and the paramount priority of patient safety; (d) the employee notification and WARN Act requirements; (e) the financial closeout process; (f) the record retention and transfer obligations; (g) the post-closure obligations.
10.2 All Governing Body members shall receive orientation to this policy as part of their governance onboarding per GV-GB-001, Section 10.1, with emphasis on: (a) the Governing Body's exclusive decision-making authority for closure and CHOW; (b) the Governing Body's oversight role during the transition; (c) the regulatory consequences of non-compliance.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.
10.4 In the event this policy is activated, the Administrator shall conduct an orientation session for all agency staff within 7 calendar days of the Governing Body's closure/CHOW decision, informing staff of: (a) the nature and timeline of the event; (b) their role in patient transition activities; (c) the employee notification and separation process; (d) confidentiality obligations; (e) the prohibition on patient abandonment.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.
11.5 This policy is assigned a Triggered review cycle. It shall be reviewed: (a) immediately upon any event described in Section 3; (b) biennially as a minimum floor, regardless of whether a triggering event has occurred; (c) upon any change to CMS regulations governing CHOW or voluntary termination (42 CFR Part 489) or California HCAI licensure requirements.

## 2. Purpose

This policy establishes the enterprise-wide taxonomy, classification standards, and metadata schema governing how all policies, procedures, and related governance documents are structured, identified, categorized, and maintained at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The taxonomy is the backbone of the agency's policy governance framework and enables:

- Unique, durable identification of every policy across all regulatory jurisdictions and operational domains
- Classification of policies by domain, subdomain, tier, lifecycle status, and access protection level
- Consistent metadata that supports audit trail, survey readiness, and regulatory traceability
- Cross-reference integrity across the 10-domain policy library
- Compliant management of the policy library per OIG Corporate Compliance Program Element 1 (written standards) and CMS 42 CFR §484.105 (administrative organization)

This policy governs the taxonomic rules. Lifecycle procedures (approval, review cycles, version control, archival) are governed by EN-LC-001.

---

## 3. Scope

This policy applies to:

* All policy documents issued under the authority of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. across all 10 governance domains (GV, CL, QA, HR, CO, FN, OP, IT, RM, EN)
* All staff responsible for drafting, reviewing, approving, or publishing policy documents
* The Compliance Officer, Administrator, and all Domain Stewards responsible for domain-level policy governance
* All policy management systems (electronic and physical) used to store, retrieve, and publish policies

This policy does not govern clinical protocols, operational checklists, or job aids that are sub-documents issued under a parent policy. Those items are classified as "controlled documents" under EN-LC-001 but use a simplified form of the taxonomy.

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Taxonomy | The structured classification system by which all policies are organized into hierarchical domains, subdomains, and sequential policy numbers, with standardized metadata. |
| Domain | A primary organizational unit of the policy library representing a major functional area. The agency currently has 10 domains: GV, CL, QA, HR, CO, FN, OP, IT, RM, EN. |
| Subdomain | A secondary classification within a domain representing a specific program, functional area, or regulatory cluster within the domain. Each subdomain has a 2-letter code unique within its domain. |
| Policy ID | The unique identifier for each policy, constructed as: [Domain Code]-[Subdomain Code]-[Sequence Number] (e.g., GV-GB-001). Policy IDs are permanent; a policy ID retired upon policy sunset is never reused. |
| Tier | The classification of a policy's regulatory/operational urgency: REQUIRED (directly mandated by federal or state regulation, licensure, or CMS CoP), ESSENTIAL (industry standard or accreditation required), RECOMMENDED (best practice), GOOD TO HAVE (operational enhancement). |
| Lifecycle Status | The stage of a policy's active lifecycle: Draft, Under Review, Active (approved and in force), Sunset Pending, Archived. |
| Access Tier | The information sensitivity classification for the policy document itself: Tier 1 — Public, Tier 2 — Restricted (agency staff only), Tier 3 — Confidential (role-limited access), Tier 4 — Privileged (Governing Body / Executive only). |
| Domain Steward | The designated role responsible for the content integrity of all policies within a domain. Domain Stewards are the subject matter authorities for their domain. |
| Metadata | The structured data elements required for each policy record: Policy ID, Title, Domain, Subdomain, Tier, Lifecycle Status, Review Cycle, Access Tier, Owner/Steward, Effective Date, Version, Regulatory References, Cross-References. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 All policy documents issued by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall conform to the taxonomy and classification standards established in this policy. Non-conforming documents shall not be considered official agency policies.

5.2 Every policy shall be assigned a permanent, unique Policy ID upon creation (per Section 6.1). Policy IDs shall not be modified after assignment. A policy that is significantly revised retains its original ID with an incremented version number.

5.3 Every policy shall contain all required metadata fields as specified in Section 6.2. Policies that are missing required metadata fields shall be returned to the drafting owner for completion before approval.

5.4 The Tier classification (REQUIRED, ESSENTIAL, RECOMMENDED, GOOD TO HAVE) shall reflect the regulatory basis of each policy as determined by the Compliance Officer at the time of classification. Tier classification changes require Compliance Officer approval.

5.5 The 10-domain structure is the authoritative organizational framework for this agency's policy library. New domains may only be added by action of the Administrator with Governing Body notification. New subdomains may be added by the Compliance Officer with Administrator approval. Both require updates to this taxonomy policy within 90 days.

5.6 All cross-references embedded in any policy must use the standard Policy ID of the referenced policy. Free-text titles without Policy IDs are not acceptable in cross-reference sections.

5.7 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a current Policy Registry (Appendix A) — a master index of all policies with their taxonomy metadata — and shall update the Registry within 7 calendar days of any policy action (new policy, revision, sunset, or archive).

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 Policy ID Assignment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Policy Drafter / Domain Steward | Before drafting a new policy, submit a Policy ID Request Form (Appendix B) to the Compliance Officer specifying: (a) proposed domain; (b) proposed subdomain (existing or new); (c) brief description of the policy scope; (d) intended Tier classification. | Before commencing policy draft. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Review the Policy ID Request Form: (a) confirm the proposed domain and subdomain are consistent with the taxonomy; (b) verify no existing policy already covers the proposed scope (duplication check against the Policy Registry); (c) if a new subdomain is required, create the subdomain record in the Registry and assign the next available 3-digit sequence number within that subdomain; (d) assign and return the Policy ID in writing. | Within 5 business days of receiving the request form. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Record the new Policy ID assignment in the Policy Registry (Appendix A) with status "Draft" and the date of assignment, before the policy document is complete. | At assignment. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Reserve retired Policy IDs permanently in the Registry with status "Archived" or "Sunset." Do not reassign any retired Policy ID to a new policy. | Continuous. |

### 6.2 Required Metadata Standards

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Policy Drafter | Every policy document submitted for review shall include all of the following metadata fields in the Policy Header table (Section 1): Policy ID; Policy Title; Domain; Subdomain; Classification Tier; Status; Review Cycle; Access Tier; Policy Owner/Steward; Effective Date; Version; Approved By; Last Reviewed; Next Review Date; Supersedes. Fields may not be left blank — use "N/A" where a field is genuinely not applicable. | At initial draft submission. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | During policy review, verify all metadata fields are complete and accurate before the policy advances to approval. Reject for correction if any required field is blank or non-conforming. | During pre-approval review. |
| 6.2.3 | Domain Steward | Ensure the Regulatory References and Cross-References sections of every policy use: (a) for regulatory references: the specific CFR, CCR, or statute citation (e.g., "42 CFR §484.55"); (b) for cross-references: the standard Policy ID format (e.g., "CL-CA-001"). Free-text descriptions without legal citations or Policy IDs are not acceptable. | At time of drafting; verified at review. |

### 6.3 Tier Classification Standards

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Classify each policy's Tier at the time of ID assignment using the following standards: (a) REQUIRED — the policy addresses a requirement that is directly mandated by a federal statute, federal regulation (CFR), CMS Condition of Participation, California state statute, California regulation (CCR), licensure requirement, or Court order; non-compliance could result in citation, license suspension, or Medicare certification termination; (b) ESSENTIAL — the policy addresses an accreditation standard (e.g., ACHC, CHAP), OIG enforcement guidance, or an industry standard where non-compliance represents a significant organizational risk; (c) RECOMMENDED — industry best practice where adoption is common and expected but not directly enforceable by a regulatory body; (d) GOOD TO HAVE — operational or efficiency enhancement with no direct regulatory basis. | At ID assignment; verified at annual review. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Maintain the Tier Basis Log (Appendix C) for all REQUIRED-tier policies documenting the specific regulatory citation that mandates the policy. The Tier Basis Log shall be reviewed annually and updated within 30 days of any regulatory change that affects a policy's Tier classification. | Maintained continuously; annual review. |
| 6.3.3 | Domain Steward | If a policy's Tier classification changes as a result of a regulatory change, notify the Compliance Officer in writing within 30 days of identifying the change. The Compliance Officer shall update the Policy Registry and the policy's metadata within 7 business days of receiving the notification. | Within 30 days of identifying change; Registry update within 7 days. |

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

The Domain Registry is updated only when a domain is added or modified per the governance requirements in Section 5.5. | Maintained continuously. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Maintain the official Subdomain Registry (Appendix E) specifying for each subdomain: Subdomain ID (e.g., GV-GB), Subdomain Code, Subdomain Name, Domain, Steward, Review Cycle, Access Tier, and description. | Maintained continuously; updated within 30 days of any subdomain addition or modification. |
| 6.4.3 | Domain Stewards | Review the subdomain structure and any subdomain assignments for their domain at least annually to ensure the taxonomic structure remains current and accurately reflects the agency's regulatory landscape. Report gaps to the Compliance Officer. | Annually; report within annual policy review cycle. |

### 6.5 Policy Registry Maintenance

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Maintain the Policy Registry (Appendix A) as a live, always-current master index of all policies including: Policy ID, Title, Domain, Subdomain, Tier, Lifecycle Status, Current Version, Review Cycle, Last Review Date, Next Review Date, and Regulatory Basis (for REQUIRED-tier policies). The Registry shall be accessible to the Administrator and all Domain Stewards at all times. | Maintained continuously; updated within 7 calendar days of any policy action. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Produce a Policy Registry Summary Report for the Administrator monthly. The report shall flag: (a) any policy overdue for review; (b) any REQUIRED-tier policy in "Draft" status beyond 90 days; (c) any policy lacking a designated Domain Steward. | Monthly. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Present a Policy Registry Audit Report to the Governing Body annually as part of the compliance report per CO-CP-003. The annual report shall include: total policy count by domain, count by Tier, count by Lifecycle Status, overdue review count, and any policy sunset actions taken in the prior year. | Annually at second quarterly Governing Body meeting. |

Compliance Officer assigns ID and initiates formal review per GV-PM-001. | Remove from circulation within 2 business days. |
| Regulatory change requires new subdomain | Compliance Officer identifies change per CO-RA-001. | Create subdomain, assign ID, initiate new policy development per GV-PM-001. Update taxonomy policy within 90 days. | Subdomain created within 30 days; taxonomy policy update within 90 days. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Policy Registry is current (updated within 7 days of policy actions) | Spot audit comparing Registry update date vs. policy action dates | 100% of policy actions reflected within 7 calendar days |
| All REQUIRED-tier policies have Tier Basis Log entry | Review of Tier Basis Log vs. REQUIRED-tier policy count | 100% have documented regulatory citation |
| No duplicate policies (scope overlap) | Annual duplex audit during taxonomy review | 0 unresolved duplicates |
| All policies in circulation have valid Policy IDs | Random audit of documents in staff circulation | 100% of circulating documents have registered Policy IDs |
| Policy Registry Audit Report presented to Governing Body annually | Review of Governing Body minutes | Annual report documented in second quarterly minutes |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and OIG reviewers will specifically verify:

1. That the agency can produce a complete inventory of its policies (equivalent to the Policy Registry) demonstrating that it knows what policies it has and their status.
2. That policies referenced in a survey finding are identifiable by unique identifier and version, allowing precise determination of what was in effect at the time of a care episode.
3. That cross-references between policies are consistent and use specific policy identifiers — not vague references like "per our privacy policy."
4. That the Governing Body receives reports on the state of the policy library, confirming oversight per GV-GB-001.
5. That REQUIRED-tier policies have a documented regulatory basis — surveyors may ask "what requires you to have this policy?"

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| No policy inventory — agency cannot produce a list of its policies | OIG compliance vulnerability; surveyor adverse inference | Policy Registry (Appendix A) is the required master inventory; Compliance Officer owns and updates it |
| Policy IDs are inconsistent or missing | Cross-referencing fails; audit confusion | No policy issued without a registered ID; non-conforming documents removed from circulation |
| REQUIRED-tier policies not identified as such | Agency cannot prioritize review cycle; survey prep fails | Tier Basis Log (Appendix C) formally classifies all REQUIRED policies |
| Policy taxonomy not updated after new subdomain added | New policies placed in wrong domain or ad hoc | Taxonomy policy updated within 90 days of new subdomain; Compliance Officer owns update |
| Governance Body never sees policy library status report | No executive oversight of policy state | Annual Registry Audit Report required at second quarterly Governing Body meeting |

# EN-TG-002 — Regulatory Cross-Reference & Mapping
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | EN-TG-002 |
| Title | Regulatory Cross-Reference & Mapping |
| Domain | EN — Enterprise Control |
| Subdomain | TG — Taxonomy Governance |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy mandates the systematic mapping of all agency policies to applicable federal, state, and local regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, and industry guidelines. The regulatory cross-reference matrix ensures that: (a) every regulatory requirement is addressed by at least one agency policy; (b) every agency policy is linked to its authorizing regulatory basis; (c) gaps in regulatory coverage are identified and remediated; (d) regulatory changes are traceable to affected policies; and (e) CMS surveyors can rapidly identify the policy addressing any specific Condition of Participation or regulatory standard. Without a maintained cross-reference matrix, the agency cannot demonstrate systematic regulatory compliance and is at risk for survey deficiencies.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Compliance Officer (primary owner of the cross-reference matrix)
The Administrator
All Domain Owners responsible for policies that map to regulatory requirements
All personnel involved in regulatory change monitoring (per CO-RA-001)
All personnel responsible for policy development or revision (per GV-PM-001)
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix that maps every agency policy to its applicable regulatory requirements and maps every applicable regulatory requirement to the agency policy or policies that address it.
4.2 The cross-reference matrix shall cover, at minimum: (a) 42 CFR Part 484 — Home Health Agency Conditions of Participation; (b) HIPAA Privacy Rule, Security Rule, and Breach Notification Rule; (c) OSHA standards applicable to home health operations; (d) OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies; (e) CMS State Operations Manual interpretive guidelines; (f) applicable California state home health licensure requirements; (g) accreditation standards (if applicable).
4.3 The Compliance Officer shall update the cross-reference matrix within 30 calendar days of any: (a) new policy creation; (b) policy revision that changes regulatory scope; (c) policy retirement; (d) new or amended regulation affecting the agency; (e) new CMS interpretive guidance.
4.4 No regulatory gap — a regulatory requirement not addressed by any agency policy — shall remain unresolved for more than 60 calendar days from identification. A Regulatory Gap Remediation Plan (Appendix B) shall be initiated within 7 calendar days of gap identification.
4.5 The cross-reference matrix shall be presented to the Governing Body annually with a gap analysis report identifying: (a) any unaddressed regulatory requirements; (b) any policies without regulatory basis (candidates for retirement or reclassification); (c) changes since the last report.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix | A structured mapping document that links each agency policy to its applicable regulatory citation(s) and each regulatory citation to the agency policy or policies that address it. |
| Regulatory Gap | A specific regulatory requirement (statute, regulation, CMS CoP, state requirement) for which no current agency policy provides coverage. |
| Regulatory Basis | The specific legal or regulatory authority that mandates or authorizes a policy. |
| Coverage Mapping | The process of linking a regulatory requirement to one or more agency policies that address that requirement. |
| Gap Remediation | The process of developing a new policy, amending an existing policy, or reassigning coverage to address an identified regulatory gap. |
| Forward Mapping | Regulatory citation → Agency policy (answering: "Which policy addresses this regulation?"). |
| Reverse Mapping | Agency policy → Regulatory citation(s) (answering: "What regulation does this policy address?"). |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Matrix Construction and Maintenance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Construct and maintain the Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix (Appendix A) with the following structure: (a) Forward Map — each regulatory citation listed with the corresponding agency policy ID(s); (b) Reverse Map — each agency policy ID listed with its corresponding regulatory citation(s). | Initial construction at framework launch; maintained continuously thereafter. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Include the following regulatory sources in the matrix: 42 CFR Part 484 (all Conditions of Participation and Standards), HIPAA (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164), OSHA (29 CFR 1910 applicable sections), OIG Compliance Program Guidance, CMS State Operations Manual Appendix B, California Code of Regulations Title 22 (applicable home health sections), and accreditation standards (if applicable). | At matrix construction; expanded as new regulations apply. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Review and update the matrix within 30 calendar days of any: (a) new policy creation; (b) policy revision that changes regulatory scope; (c) policy retirement; (d) new or amended regulation; (e) new CMS interpretive guidance; (f) state regulatory change. | Within 30 calendar days of triggering event. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Version-control the matrix with date stamps for each update. Maintain a change history showing what was added, modified, or removed and why. | At each update. |

### 6.2 Annual Gap Analysis

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct a comprehensive annual gap analysis comparing all applicable regulatory requirements against the current policy inventory. Document results in the Annual Gap Analysis Report (Appendix C). | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of the start of each fiscal year. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Identify two categories of findings: (a) Regulatory Gaps — regulatory requirements with no corresponding policy coverage; (b) Orphan Policies — policies with no identifiable regulatory basis (candidates for retirement or reclassification as RECOMMENDED or GOOD TO HAVE). | During annual gap analysis. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | For each regulatory gap identified, initiate a Regulatory Gap Remediation Plan (Appendix B) within 7 calendar days. The plan shall specify: (a) the gap; (b) the remediation approach (new policy, policy amendment, or coverage reassignment); (c) responsible Domain Owner; (d) target completion date (not to exceed 60 calendar days from identification). | Plan initiated within 7 days; gap closed within 60 days. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Present the annual gap analysis results and remediation status to the Governing Body. Include: (a) total regulatory citations mapped; (b) total gaps found; (c) gaps remediated; (d) gaps pending; (e) orphan policies identified; (f) changes since last report. | At the quarterly Governing Body meeting following the annual analysis. |

### 6.3 Regulatory Change Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon identification of a new or amended regulation per policy CO-RA-001, assess impact on the cross-reference matrix. Determine: (a) which existing policies are affected; (b) whether new policies are needed; (c) whether existing mappings require update. | Within 14 calendar days of regulatory change identification. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Update the matrix to reflect regulatory changes. If a new regulatory requirement creates a gap, initiate Appendix B remediation plan. | Within 30 calendar days of regulatory change effective date. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Notify all affected Domain Owners of regulatory changes that impact their policies and the required response timeline. | Within 7 calendar days of regulatory change identification. |

### 6.4 Survey Readiness Support

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Maintain the cross-reference matrix in a format that enables rapid retrieval during CMS surveys. A surveyor requesting "the policy for 42 CFR § 484.65" must be served within 5 minutes using the forward map. | Continuous. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Include a printed or readily accessible electronic copy of the cross-reference matrix in the agency's survey readiness binder per CO-RA-003. | Continuous; verified quarterly. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-reference matrix is current and complete | Annual gap analysis; quarterly spot checks | 100% of applicable regulatory citations mapped; 0 gaps exceeding 60 days |
| Matrix updated within 30 days of triggering events | Review of matrix change history against policy creation/revision dates and regulatory change notifications | 100% of updates within 30 calendar days |
| Gap remediation plans initiated within 7 days | Review of Appendix B dates against gap identification dates | 100% within 7 calendar days |
| Gaps closed within 60 days | Review of remediation completion dates | 100% of gaps closed within 60 calendar days |
| Annual gap analysis completed | Review of Appendix C date | Completed within 60 calendar days of fiscal year start |
| Governing Body receives annual report | Review of Governing Body minutes | Annual presentation documented |
| Matrix accessible for survey readiness | Survey readiness binder review | Matrix locatable within 5 minutes |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No cross-reference matrix exists | Agency cannot demonstrate systematic regulatory coverage; surveyors identify coverage gaps | Implement and maintain Appendix A per this policy |
| Matrix exists but is not maintained after initial creation | Stale mappings do not reflect regulatory changes or new policies; false sense of compliance | Mandatory 30-day update window; quarterly spot checks; annual comprehensive audit |
| Regulatory gaps identified but not remediated | Known non-compliance; heightened survey risk; potential sanctions | 7-day plan initiation; 60-day closure deadline; Governing Body escalation |
| Matrix not accessible during surveys | Surveyors perceive disorganization; policy retrieval delays create negative impression | Include in survey readiness binder; verify quarterly accessibility |
| One-directional mapping only (forward or reverse, not both) | Incomplete analysis; orphan policies and hidden gaps persist | Maintain both forward and reverse maps in Appendix A |

# EN-LC-001 — Policy Lifecycle Control & Version Management


## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Policy ID | EN-LC-001 |
| Policy Title | Policy Lifecycle Control & Version Management |
| Domain | EN — Enterprise Control |
| Subdomain | LC — Lifecycle Control |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Compliance Officer / Administrator |
| Effective Date | 2026-04-01 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Administrator — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2026-03-27 |
| Next Review Date | 2027-04-01 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

---

## 2. Purpose

This policy establishes the rules governing the complete lifecycle of every policy document at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., from inception through active use, revision, and final archival or sunset. Effective lifecycle control ensures:

- Only currently approved policy versions are in active use — never expired or superseded versions
- All policy reviews are completed on schedule, meeting CMS, OIG, and California regulatory expectations for maintained, current policies
- Version control prevents reliance on outdated procedures that may not reflect current regulatory requirements
- The agency can demonstrate to CMS surveyors, OIG reviewers, CDPH/HCAI inspectors, and accreditation bodies that every policy in its library is current, approved, and has a documented review history
- The policy approval process is appropriately controlled with required executive oversight per GV-PM-001

This policy is the lifecycle management companion to EN-TG-001 (Enterprise Policy Taxonomy & Classification Governance). The taxonomy defines what a policy IS; this policy defines how a policy moves through its stages of existence.

---

## 3. Scope

This policy applies to:

* All policy documents registered in the Policy Registry under EN-TG-001
* All draft, active, and archived policies across all 10 governance domains
* All Domain Stewards, policy drafters, reviewers, approvers, and publishing custodians
* The Compliance Officer, Administrator, and Governing Body in their oversight roles
* All controlled sub-documents (procedures, checklists, job aids) issued under an authorizing parent policy

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Lifecycle | The complete arc of a policy document: Creation → Draft → Review → Approval → Active → Scheduled Review → Revision or Reaffirmation → Active (updated) → [Sunset Pending] → Archived. |
| Draft | The initial or revised state of a policy that has not yet been approved. Draft documents shall not be distributed to staff as authoritative guidance. |
| Active | A policy that has been formally approved by the appropriate authority, assigned an effective date, and published for staff use. Only Active policies are operative. |
| Reaffirmation | The formal documentation that a policy has been reviewed on schedule and no changes are required. The policy retains its Policy ID and increments its version number by 0.1 (e.g., v1.0 → v1.1 after reaffirmation). |
| Revision | A change to any substantive element of a policy through the full review and approval process. Revisions increment the version number by a full integer (e.g., v1.0 → v2.0 for significant changes) or 0.1 for minor corrections. |
| Sunset | The intentional termination of a policy, with full documentation of the reason, regulatory basis for termination, and handling of any downstream cross-references. A sunset policy is moved to Archived status. |
| Review Cycle | The maximum interval between scheduled reviews of a policy, based on its Tier and regulatory requirements: REQUIRED-tier policies — Annual; ESSENTIAL-tier — Annual or Biennial; RECOMMENDED-tier — Biennial; GOOD TO HAVE-tier — Triennial. |
| Triggered Review | An out-of-cycle review initiated by: regulatory change, survey finding, incident, significant process change, or Compliance Officer determination. |
| Version History | A permanent record of every version of a policy — the document text at each version, the date, approver, and nature of changes. Retained permanently. |
| Controlled Distribution | The management of which staff receive policy notifications and acknowledgments, and the tracking of policy distribution to ensure no staff member is working with an superseded version. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Every policy of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. must be actively maintained through a documented lifecycle. No policy shall remain Active without a completed scheduled review at the interval defined by its Review Cycle.

5.2 Only Active-status policies shall be distributed to staff or referenced as current agency policy. Draft policies are for internal development use only. Archived policies are permanently inaccessible to staff except for historical audit reference.

5.3 All policy revisions must be approved by the appropriate authority per GV-PM-001 (Policy Development & Approval Process) before the revised version becomes Active. The prior version does not expire until the revised version's effective date.

5.4 The effective date of a revised policy shall not precede the approval date. Retroactive policy effective dates are prohibited.

5.5 When a policy is revised or reaffirmed, the prior version is immediately retired to Archived status. The system shall not permit access to a prior version as if it were current.

5.6 Every revision of every policy shall be accompanied by a complete version history entry identifying the nature of changes, the person who approved the revision, and the date.

5.7 Policies overdue for review shall be flagged in the Policy Registry and reported in the monthly summary per EN-TG-001 Section 6.5.2. A REQUIRED-tier policy overdue by more than 60 calendar days beyond its scheduled review date is elevated to a compliance risk requiring Administrator notification.

5.8 This policy itself, as a REQUIRED-tier Enterprise Control policy, shall be reviewed and reaffirmed or revised annually.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 Policy Creation (Draft Stage)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Domain Steward / Policy Drafter | Submit a Policy ID Request per EN-TG-001 Section 6.1. Once a Policy ID is assigned, the draft policy is registered in the Policy Registry with Lifecycle Status "Draft" and the draft date. | Before drafting commences. |
| 6.1.2 | Policy Drafter | Prepare the draft policy using the Agency Policy Template (Appendix A), which includes all required metadata fields per EN-TG-001 Section 6.2. The draft shall include preliminary regulatory references and cross-references. | During drafting. |
| 6.1.3 | Domain Steward | Review the draft for: (a) accuracy of regulatory content; (b) completeness of regulatory references; (c) absence of scope overlap with existing Active policies (cross-check Policy Registry); (d) conformance to the policy format template. Return for correction or advance to Compliance Officer review. | Within 14 calendar days of receiving the draft. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Review the draft for: (a) Tier classification accuracy; (b) regulatory compliance; (c) consistency with other policies in the library; (d) cross-reference accuracy. Approve for advancement to approval stage or return for revision. | Within 14 calendar days of receiving the draft from Domain Steward. |

### 6.2 Policy Approval

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Route the reviewed draft to the appropriate approval authority per GV-PM-001: (a) REQUIRED-tier policies: Administrator approval; Governing Body notification for policies affecting patient rights, clinical standards, or compliance program; (b) ESSENTIAL-tier: Administrator approval; (c) RECOMMENDED/GOOD TO HAVE: Domain Steward approval countersigned by Compliance Officer. | After Compliance Officer review is complete. |
| 6.2.2 | Approving Authority | Review and sign the policy approval. The approval signature creates the official approval record. Update the Lifecycle Status in the Policy Registry from "Draft" to "Active" upon execution of approval. Record the effective date (must equal or follow the approval date). | Within 14 calendar days of receiving routing. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Upon approval: (a) assign the effective date and Version number (v1.0 for new policies); (b) publish the Active policy to the agency's policy management system; (c) initiate controlled distribution and acknowledgment per GV-PM-003; (d) update the Policy Registry to Active status with current version, effective date, and next review date. | Within 5 business days of approval execution. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Remove all Draft versions of the policy from any circulation channel. Draft markings must not appear on the Active version. | Immediately upon publication of Active version. |

### 6.3 Scheduled Review and Reaffirmation/Revision

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Generate a Scheduled Review Report monthly, listing all policies due for review within the next 60 calendar days. Distribute the list to applicable Domain Stewards no later than 45 days before the review due date. | Monthly; distribution 45 days before review due date. |
| 6.3.2 | Domain Steward | Commence review of each assigned policy upon receiving the 45-day notice. Review the policy against: (a) any regulatory changes since last review (per CO-RA-001); (b) any audit findings, incident investigations, or corrective actions affecting the policy's procedures; (c) any operational changes that affect the policy scope. | Commence within 5 business days of 45-day notice. |
| 6.3.3 | Domain Steward | Determine outcome: (a) No Changes Required → prepare Reaffirmation Memo (Appendix B) documenting the review checklist outcome and confirming no changes are warranted; (b) Changes Required → initiate the revision process per Section 6.4 with a marked-up draft. | Within 21 calendar days of commencing review. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer | Execute Reaffirmation or advance Revision per outcome: (a) Reaffirmation — co-sign Reaffirmation Memo with Domain Steward; update Policy Registry: increment version by 0.1, update Last Reviewed date, set Next Review Date. The policy content is unchanged; (b) Revision — advance to Section 6.4. | Within 7 calendar days of receiving reaffirmation memo or revised draft. |
| 6.3.5 | Compliance Officer | Flag any policy not reaffirmed or revised by its scheduled review date as Overdue in the Policy Registry. Immediately notify the Domain Steward and Administrator. For REQUIRED-tier: escalate to Administrator; 60-day overdue = compliance risk per Section 5.7. | On the business day following the review due date. |

### 6.4 Revision Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | Domain Steward | Prepare the revised draft using tracked changes against the current Active version. Clearly identify every change: (a) the specific text changed; (b) the reason for the change (regulatory update, incident finding, process change, other); (c) the regulatory or operational basis for the change. | Within 14 calendar days of determining revision is needed. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Review the revised draft for: (a) regulatory accuracy; (b) consistency with other library policies; (c) completeness of version history entry; (d) cross-reference updates required as a result of this revision. | Within 14 calendar days of receiving revised draft. |
| 6.4.3 | Approving Authority | Approve the revised policy per the Tier-based approval authority in Section 6.2.1. Sign and date. | Within 14 calendar days of receiving for approval. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | Upon approval of revision: (a) assign the new version number (increment by 1.0 for substantive changes, 0.1 for minor corrections); (b) set the effective date; (c) publish the revised Active version; (d) immediately archive the prior version; (e) update the Policy Registry — version, effective date, next review date; (f) initiate re-acknowledgment process per GV-PM-003 for staff affected by the change; (g) update Version History log (Appendix C). | Within 5 business days of approval. |
| 6.4.5 | Compliance Officer | After publishing the revision: review all policies that cross-reference this policy. If a cross-reference is now inaccurate (e.g., the referenced section number changed), flag the cross-referencing policies for correction at their next scheduled review or sooner if the cross-reference inaccuracy creates a compliance risk. | Within 30 days of revision publication. |

### 6.5 Triggered Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer or Domain Steward | Initiate a Triggered Review when any of the following occur: (a) a regulatory change affects the policy content (per CO-RA-001); (b) a CMS, CDPH, or Cal/OSHA survey finding cites a procedure covered by the policy; (c) an incident investigation RCA (QA-AE-002) identifies a policy-level deficiency; (d) a significant operational change renders a policy's procedures non-operational. | Within 14 calendar days of triggering event. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Document the Triggered Review in the Policy Registry: note the trigger event, the initiating party, and the date. Update Lifecycle Status to "Under Triggered Review." | At initiation. |
| 6.5.3 | Domain Steward | Complete the triggered revision within 30 calendar days of the trigger event (or per regulatory/survey response timeline if sooner required). Advance through approval per Section 6.4 on expedited timeline. | Within 30 calendar days of trigger (or shorter if survey-directed). |

### 6.6 Policy Sunset and Archival

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.6.1 | Compliance Officer or Domain Steward | Initiate a sunset action when: (a) the regulatory basis for a REQUIRED-tier policy is eliminated; (b) the policy is redundant due to consolidation into another policy; (c) the policy covers a service or function the agency has formally discontinued. Document the sunset rationale in the Sunset Request Form (Appendix D). | At identification; submit form to Compliance Officer. |
| 6.6.2 | Compliance Officer | Review the sunset request: (a) verify no active regulatory requirement still mandates the policy; (b) verify all cross-references to the policy are updated or will be updated to remove the reference; (c) verify no downstream controlled documents (checklists, job aids) depend solely on the sunsetted policy. | Within 14 calendar days of receiving sunset request. |
| 6.6.3 | Administrator | Approve the sunset action. The Governing Body shall be notified at the next scheduled meeting for any REQUIRED-tier policy sunset. | Administrator approval within 14 days; Governing Body notification at next meeting. |
| 6.6.4 | Compliance Officer | Upon approval of sunset: (a) remove the Active policy from staff access; (b) update Policy Registry status to "Archived"; (c) retain the archived policy (all versions) permanently in the policy archive; (d) update any other policies that cross-reference the sunsetted policy within 30 days. | Within 3 business days of approval; cross-reference updates within 30 days. |

### 6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| REQUIRED-tier policy overdue for review by 60+ days | Compliance Officer escalates to Administrator by written memo. | Administrator directs Domain Steward to complete review within 14 days. If Domain Steward resource capacity is insufficient, Administrator reallocates resources. | Escalation: immediately at 60-day mark. Completion required: 14 days from escalation. |
| Superseded policy found circulating to staff | Any employee may report to Compliance Officer or Domain Steward. | Compliance Officer removes document from circulation within 2 business days. Retraining issued to staff who may have relied on the superseded version. | Removal: 2 business days. Retraining: within 14 days. |
| Approval authority is unavailable for a REQUIRED revision needed within a regulatory deadline | Administrator designates alternate approver per GV-OG-005 (Delegation of Authority). | Alternate approver reviews and approves in emergency capacity. Document the basis for alternate approval in the Version History log. | Alternate approval executed within the regulatory deadline. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| All REQUIRED-tier policies reviewed within their scheduled cycle | Registry audit — days overdue count for each policy | 0 REQUIRED-tier policies overdue beyond their review date |
| All policy revisions have complete version history entries | Audit of Version History Log for each revised policy | 100% of revisions have complete version history |
| No superseded policy versions in active staff circulation | Random audit of documents in staff circulation | 0 superseded versions in circulation |
| Reaffirmation memos on file for policies not needing revision | Review of reaffirmation memo file vs. policies due for review | 100% of due-for-review policies have either reaffirmation memo or revision documentation |
| Policy Registry is updated within 7 calendar days of lifecycle actions | Spot audit of registry update dates vs. policy action dates | 100% within 7 calendar days |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and OIG reviewers will specifically assess:

1. Whether the agency's policies are current — they will request the most recent version of key policies and compare effective dates and version numbers against internal records. A policy unchanged for 5+ years without a reaffirmation memo is suspect.
2. Whether the agency has a documented process for identifying when policies need revision — co-RA-001 regulatory monitoring tied to policy lifecycle triggers is essential.
3. Whether a superseded version of a policy was in use at the time of a care episode in question. This is critical in deficiency investigations where surveyors ask "what was your policy at the time?"
4. Whether significant changes (like a new regulation) were promptly incorporated into policy documents.
5. Whether staff were notified of policy changes (acknowledgment records per GV-PM-003).

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Policies not reviewed on schedule — no system for tracking overdue reviews | CMS cites lack of policy maintenance; OIG compliance concern | Compliance Officer generates monthly scheduled review report; 45-day advance notice system |
| No version history — cannot demonstrate what changed when | Cannot defend policy history in survey deficiency review | Version History Log (Appendix C) required for every policy from v1.0 |
| Superseded policy found at patient bedside or in field bag | Creates confusion about what clinical standard was operative | Controlled distribution + staff acknowledgment per GV-PM-003 ensures only current versions are distributed |
| Reaffirmation not documented — review was conducted verbally | Surveyor treats unreviewed policy as out-of-date | Reaffirmation Memo (Appendix B) is required for all scheduled reviews, even for no-change outcomes |
| REQUIRED-tier policy overdue without escalation | Compliance program gap; regulatory risk | 60-day overdue automatic escalation to Administrator per Section 5.7 |

# EN-LC-002 — Policy Exception & Waiver Management
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Subdomain | LC — Lifecycle Control |

| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the formal process for requesting, evaluating, approving, documenting, and time-limiting exceptions or waivers to established policies within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Policy exceptions are sometimes operationally necessary due to unique circumstances, but uncontrolled exceptions create compliance risk, inconsistency, and audit exposure. This policy ensures that every exception is: (a) formally requested; (b) risk-assessed; (c) approved by appropriate authority; (d) documented with specific conditions and time limits; (e) tracked to expiration; and (f) reviewed for potential permanent policy amendment.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All agency staff, contractors, and leadership who seek an exception to any established agency policy
The Compliance Officer (exception process owner and approver for most exceptions)
The Administrator (approver for REQUIRED-tier exceptions not involving regulatory mandates)
The Governing Body (approver for exceptions to regulatory-mandated requirements — limited circumstances)
All Domain Owners who may receive exception requests within their domain
Critical limitation: No exception may be granted that would cause the agency to violate any federal or state law, regulation, CMS Condition of Participation, or HIPAA requirement. Regulatory mandates are not subject to waiver.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 No deviation from an established agency policy shall be practiced without a formally approved Policy Exception/Waiver. Informal, verbal, or undocumented exceptions are prohibited.
4.2 Every exception request shall be submitted in writing using the Policy Exception/Waiver Request Form (Appendix A) and routed to the Compliance Officer for evaluation.
4.3 No exception may be granted that would cause violation of any federal or state law, regulation, CMS Condition of Participation, HIPAA Privacy Rule, HIPAA Security Rule, OSHA standard, or state licensure requirement. Such requests shall be denied with written explanation.
4.4 Approval authority for exceptions is determined by the classification tier of the policy to which the exception applies:

| Policy Tier | Exception Approval Authority |
| --- | --- |
| REQUIRED (regulatory basis) | No exception permitted — regulatory mandates cannot be waived |
| REQUIRED (operational basis, non-regulatory) | Governing Body or Administrator with Compliance Officer concurrence |
| ESSENTIAL | Administrator with Compliance Officer concurrence |
| RECOMMENDED | Compliance Officer with Domain Owner concurrence |
| GOOD TO HAVE | Compliance Officer |

4.5 Every approved exception shall specify: (a) the exact scope (who, what, where); (b) the conditions under which the exception applies; (c) the maximum duration (not to exceed 180 calendar days without re-evaluation); (d) mitigating controls to manage risk during the exception period; (e) the review/expiration date.
4.6 All approved exceptions shall be logged in the Policy Exception Register (Appendix B) and monitored for expiration.
4.7 Upon expiration, each exception shall be reviewed. The Compliance Officer shall determine: (a) the exception is no longer needed (close); (b) the exception should be renewed (requires new approval cycle); or (c) the underlying policy should be amended to permanently accommodate the condition (initiate triggered review per EN-LC-001__
4.8 The Compliance Officer shall report all active and expired exceptions to the Administrator quarterly and to the Governing Body annually.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Policy Exception | A formal, documented, time-limited deviation from a specific requirement within an established agency policy, approved by the appropriate authority.__ |
| Policy Waiver | Used interchangeably with "exception" in this policy. A formal authorization to deviate from a policy requirement under specified conditions and time limits. |
| Mitigating Controls | Alternative procedures, safeguards, or monitoring measures implemented during an exception period to manage risk created by the policy deviation. |
| Exception Register | The centralized log of all requested, approved, denied, active, expired, and renewed exceptions (Appendix B). |
| Regulatory Mandate | A requirement imposed by federal or state law, regulation, CMS Condition of Participation, HIPAA, or OSHA that cannot be waived or excepted by agency action. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Exception Request Submission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.__ | Any staff member or manager | Identify the need for a policy exception. Complete the Policy Exception/Waiver Request Form (Appendix A). Include: (a) the specific policy ID and section; (b) the requirement from which exception is sought; (c) the reason/justification; (d) the proposed alternative or mitigating controls; (e) the requested duration; (f) the impact assessment__ | As needed. |
| 6.1.2 | Requestor | Submit the completed form to the Compliance Officer. If the exception is urgent (patient safety or operational continuity), mark the form as "URGENT" and notify the Compliance Officer directly. | Immediately upon identification of need. |

### 6.2 Exception Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Receive and log the request in the Policy Exception Register (Appendix B). Assign an Exception ID. | Within 24 hours of receipt. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Conduct a risk assessment. Evaluate: (a) whether the policy requirement has a regulatory basis — if yes and the regulation cannot be waived, deny the request; (b) the patient safety impact; (c) the compliance risk; (d) the operational impact of granting vs. denying; (e) adequacy of proposed mitigating controls; (f) duration reasonableness. | Standard: within 7 calendar days. Urgent: within 48 hours. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Consult with the Domain Owner of the affected policy to obtain domain-specific input on the exception request. | During the evaluation period. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Prepare a written recommendation: APPROVE, APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS, or DENY. Include risk assessment summary and recommended conditions/mitigating controls. | At completion of evaluation. |

### 6.3 Exception Approval

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Approval Authority (per Section 4.4__ | Review the request and Compliance Officer recommendation. Approve, approve with modifications, or deny. Document the decision, conditions, mitigating controls, and expiration date. | Standard: within 7 calendar days of recommendation. Urgent: within 48 hours. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | If approved, update the Policy Exception Register with: Exception ID, policy ID, scope, conditions, mitigating controls, expiration date, and approver. Notify the requestor and affected Domain Owner. | Within 48 hours of approval decision. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | If denied, provide written rationale to the requestor within 7 calendar days. The requestor may appeal to the next level of authority within 14 calendar days__ | Within 7 calendar days.__ |

### 6.4 Exception Monitoring and Expiration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Monitor all active exceptions for: (a) adherence to specified conditions; (b) effectiveness of mitigating controls; (c) approaching expiration dates. Generate a 30-day advance notice before each exception expiration. | Continuous; advance notice at 30 days. |
| 6.4.2 | Requestor / Domain Owner | Prior to expiration, determine if the exception is: (a) no longer needed — notify Compliance Officer for closure; (b) still needed — submit a renewal request (new Appendix A form); (c) should become permanent — request policy amendment per EN-LC-001 triggered review. | At least 14 calendar days before expiration. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Process expiration: (a) close expired exceptions and update register; (b) process renewals through the full approval cycle; (c) initiate policy amendment process if requested. No exception may be renewed more than twice (total maximum 540 calendar days) without either permanent policy amendment or closure. | At expiration date. |

### 6.5 Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Prepare and submit a quarterly exception status report to the Administrator including: (a) new exceptions requested; (b) exceptions approved/denied; (c) active exceptions and compliance with conditions; (d) exceptions expired; (e) exceptions renewed; (f) exception-to-policy-amendment conversions. | Quarterly. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Present an annual exception summary to the Governing Body including trends, high-risk exceptions, and recommendations for policy amendments. | Annually at a quarterly Governing Body meeting. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All exceptions formally documented | Review of Exception Register against operational practices | Zero undocumented exceptions |
| No exception granted to regulatory mandate | Review of approved exceptions against regulatory basis | Zero exceptions to regulatory requirements__ |
| All exceptions carry expiration date not exceeding 180 days | Register audit | 100% compliance__ |
| No exception renewed more than twice without policy amendment | Register audit | Zero violations__ |
| Quarterly reports submitted to Administrator | Review of report dates | 4 per year__ |
| Annual summary presented to Governing Body | Governing Body minutes | Annually |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Informal/verbal exceptions practiced without documentation | Non-compliance; inconsistent practices; survey risk | Zero-tolerance policy; all exceptions through Appendix A |
| Exceptions to regulatory mandates approved | Direct regulatory violation; potential sanctions | Mandatory regulatory basis check in evaluation; automatic denial for regulatory mandates |
| Exceptions without expiration dates or mitigating controls | Open-ended deviations become permanent non-compliance | Mandatory fields in Appendix A; maximum 180-day duration__ |
| Exception register not maintained | Cannot demonstrate governance of exceptions during audits | Compliance Officer responsible for register maintenance; quarterly reporting__ |
| Expired exceptions not reviewed | Uncontrolled ongoing deviations | 30-day advance notice; mandatory expiration processing |

# EN-LC-003 — Policy Assignment and Role-Based Applicability Governance
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | EN-LC-003__ |
| Title | Policy Assignment and Role-Based Applicability Governance |
| Domain | EN — Enterprise Control |
| Subdomain | LC — Lifecycle Control |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0__ |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the formal process for assigning policies to specific workforce roles, managing role-based applicability, and governing the reassignment of policies when roles change, policies are revised, or organizational structure evolves. Without governed policy assignment, staff may be unaware of policies that apply to them, may receive policies irrelevant to their role, or may miss critical compliance requirements. This policy ensures every employee, contractor, and governing body member knows exactly which policies apply to them and that assignment is traceable, documented, and enforced.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Compliance Officer (assignment process owner)
The Administrator
All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners
HR Director (coordinates role-based assignment with onboarding and role changes)
All agency employees, contractors, per diem staff, and governing body members
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Every policy in the enterprise taxonomy shall have a defined applicability scope specifying which workforce roles, departments, or personnel categories are subject to that policy.
4.2 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a Policy-Role Assignment Matrix (Appendix A) that maps every policy to its applicable workforce roles.
4.3 Upon hire, role change, promotion, or transfer, the HR Director (in coordination with the Compliance Officer) shall ensure the employee receives and acknowledges all policies applicable to their new role within 14 calendar days.
4.4 When a policy is created, revised, or retired, the Compliance Officer shall review and update the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix to reflect any changes in applicability.
4.5 Access to policies shall be governed by the Access Tier system (EN-TG-001, Section C4). Staff shall have access only to policies within their authorized access tier and applicable to their role.
4.6 Contractors and per diem staff shall be assigned the same policy set as equivalent permanent employees in the same role, plus any contractor-specific policies (e.g., HR-WM-002__
4.7 The Compliance Officer shall conduct an annual Policy Assignment Audit (Appendix B) verifying that all personnel have acknowledged all policies applicable to their current role.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Policy Assignment | The formal determination that a specific policy applies to a specific workforce role or individual, creating an obligation to read, acknowledge, and comply. |
| Policy-Role Assignment Matrix | A structured document mapping each policy ID to the workforce roles to which it applies (Appendix A). |
| Workforce Role | A defined position category within the agency (e.g., Registered Nurse, Home Health Aide, Administrator, Compliance Officer). |
| Assignment Trigger | An event requiring policy assignment review: new hire, role change, policy creation, policy revision, policy retirement, or organizational restructuring. |
| Policy Assignment Audit | Annual verification that all personnel have acknowledged all policies applicable to their current role (Appendix B). |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Initial Policy Assignment (Onboarding)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | HR Director | Upon hire of any employee or onboarding of any contractor, notify the Compliance Officer of the individual's name, hire date, and assigned role. | Within 24 hours of hire/onboarding. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Using the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix (Appendix A), generate the individual's policy assignment list — all policies applicable to their role and access tier. | Within 48 hours of notification. |
| 6.1.3 | HR Director / Compliance Officer | Deliver all applicable policies to the individual through the policy management system, orientation packet, or electronic distribution__ | During orientation; no later than 7 calendar days from hire. |
| 6.1.4 | New hire / contractor | Read and sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form for each assigned policy per GV-PM-003__ | Within 14 calendar days of hire. |
| 6.1.__ | Compliance Officer | Verify 100% acknowledgment completion. Report any non-compliance to the HR Director and Domain Owner. | Within 21 calendar days of hire. |

### 6.2 Role Change Reassignment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | HR Director | Upon any role change (promotion, transfer, reassignment, scope change), notify the Compliance Officer of the individual, prior role, and new role. | Within 48 hours of effective date. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Compare the policy assignment lists for the prior and new roles. Identify: (a) policies that apply to the new role but not the prior (new assignments); (b) policies that applied to the prior role but not the new (revocations). | Within 7 calendar days. |
| 6.2.__ | Compliance Officer | Deliver newly applicable policies to the individual and collect acknowledgments. Revoke access to policies no longer applicable (per access tier controls). | Delivery: within 7 calendar days. Acknowledgment: within 14 calendar days. |

### 6.3 Policy Creation/Revision Reassignment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | When a new policy is created or an existing policy's scope is revised, determine the applicable workforce roles using the policy's Scope section. Update the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix. | Within 7 calendar days of policy activation. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Distribute the new/revised policy to all personnel in applicable roles. Collect acknowledgments per GV-PM-003__ | Within 14 calendar days of effective date. |

### 6.4 Annual Policy Assignment Audit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct the annual Policy Assignment Audit (Appendix B). For every active employee and contractor: (a) verify current role; (b) verify policy assignment list matches the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix; (c) verify 100% acknowledgment of all assigned policies. | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of fiscal year start. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Identify and resolve gaps: (a) personnel with missing acknowledgments; (b) personnel assigned to policies outside their role scope; (c) policies with no assigned personnel (orphan assignment). | Within 30 calendar days of audit completion. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Report audit results to the Administrator. Include: (a) total personnel audited; (b) acknowledgment compliance rate; (c) gaps identified and resolved; (d) recommendations. | At next Administrator meeting following audit. |

### 6.5 Separation and Access Revocation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.__ | HR Director | Upon employee separation (voluntary or involuntary), notify the Compliance Officer. | Within 24 hours of separation. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Revoke the individual's access to all policies in the policy management system. Update the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix to remove the individual. | Within 48 hours of notification. |

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |

| Policy-Role Assignment Matrix | Appendix A | Compliance Officer | Policy governance repository | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually |
| Annual Policy Assignment Audit | Appendix B | Compliance Officer | Policy governance repository | Annually; retained 7 years |
| Individual policy assignment lists | Generated per hire/role change | Compliance Officer | Personnel file (copy); policy governance repository | At hire/role change; retained duration of employment + 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgments | Per GV-PM-003 | Each employee; Compliance Officer (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of assignment__ |
| Policy acknowledgment | Appendix C: this policy | All in scope | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Policy-Role Assignment Matrix is current | Annual audit; spot checks during new hires | Matrix updated within 7 days of any change |
| All new hires acknowledge applicable policies within 14 days | Review of acknowledgment dates | 100% within 14 calendar days |
| Role changes trigger reassignment within 7 days | Review of reassignment records | 100% within 7 calendar days |
| Annual audit completed | Audit report date | Completed within 60 calendar days of fiscal year start |
| Overall acknowledgment compliance rate | Annual audit | Target: 100%; minimum acceptable: 95% with corrective action for gaps |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No formal assignment matrix; policies distributed ad hoc | Staff miss critical policies; compliance gaps during surveys | Maintain Appendix A; integrate with onboarding per HR-TA-005__ |
| Role changes not communicated to Compliance Officer | Employees operating under wrong policy set | HR Director notification within 48 hours; integrated HR/Compliance process__ |
| Contractors not assigned equivalent policy sets | Contractors operate without governance; compliance liability | Section 4.6 mandate; contractor onboarding checklist per HR-WM-002 |
| No annual audit of assignments | Drift between actual roles and assigned policies undetected | Annual Appendix B audit; report to Administrator |

10.1 The Compliance Officer, HR Director, and all Domain Owners shall receive training on the policy assignment process, matrix maintenance, and audit methodology.
10.2 All supervisors shall be trained on their responsibility to notify HR/Compliance of role changes.
10.3 Policy acknowledgment (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days.
