## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the formal criteria, process, and documentation requirements for retiring policies that are obsolete, superseded, no longer applicable, or redundant. Failure to retire outdated policies creates direct compliance risk: staff may follow superseded requirements, surveyors may encounter conflicting policies, and the agency's policy inventory loses credibility. This policy ensures that retirement is governed, documented, and that all downstream effects (cross-references, assignments, taxonomy, regulatory mapping) are addressed systematically.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Compliance Officer (retirement process owner)
The Administrator
All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners
The Governing Body (for REQUIRED-tier policy retirements)
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 A policy shall be retired when it meets one or more of the following criteria: (a) the regulatory requirement it addresses has been repealed or replaced; (b) the policy has been superseded by a new or revised policy; (c) the operational function the policy governs no longer exists; (d) the policy is redundant with another policy and has been merged; (e) the annual taxonomy audit identifies the policy as an orphan with no continuing purpose.
4.2 Policy retirement shall follow the formal retirement process described in this policy. Policies shall not be informally deleted, removed, or ignored.
4.3 Retirement of a REQUIRED-tier policy requires Governing Body approval. Retirement of ESSENTIAL-tier policies requires Administrator approval. Retirement of RECOMMENDED and GOOD TO HAVE policies requires Compliance Officer approval.
4.4 Upon retirement: (a) the policy's status shall be changed to DEPRECATED in the taxonomy and Master Version Registry; (b) the Policy ID shall be added to the Reserved ID Registry per EN-TG-001 (never reused); (c) the Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix shall be updated per EN-TG-002; (d) the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix shall be updated per EN-LC-003; (e) all cross-references in other policies shall be updated; (f) the retired policy shall be archived with "DEPRECATED — NOT FOR USE" marking; (g) all personnel previously assigned the policy shall be notified.
4.5 Retired policies shall be retained in the archive for a minimum of 7 years per CO-HP-007.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Policy Retirement | The formal process of changing a policy's status to DEPRECATED and removing it from active use, while retaining it in the archive for the required retention period. |
| Obsolete Policy | A policy that is no longer current, relevant, or applicable due to regulatory changes, operational changes, or supersession by another policy. |
| Superseded Policy | A policy that has been replaced in its entirety by a new or revised policy. |
| Orphan Policy | A policy identified during taxonomy audit as having no current regulatory basis, operational purpose, or active audience. |
| Reserved ID | A retired Policy ID that is permanently reserved and may never be reassigned to a new policy. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Retirement Initiation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Any Domain Owner, Compliance Officer, or personnel identified through audit | Identify a policy that may meet retirement criteria. Complete the Policy Retirement Request Form (Appendix A) and submit to the Compliance Officer. Sources of identification: (a) annual taxonomy audit; (b) regulatory change monitoring; (c) policy review cycle; (d) organizational restructuring; (e) domain owner recommendation__ | As needed. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Receive and log the request. Assign a Retirement Request ID. | Within 48 hours. |

### 6.2 Retirement Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Evaluate the retirement request against the criteria in Section 4.1. Determine: (a) does the policy meet one or more retirement criteria? (b) has the regulatory requirement been repealed? (c) has a replacement policy been created or is coverage provided elsewhere? (d) are there any remaining operational dependencies? | Within 14 calendar days.__ |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Conduct a cross-reference impact analysis: (a) identify all other policies that reference the candidate policy; (b) identify regulatory cross-reference entries that map to the candidate; (c) identify role assignments that include the candidate; (d) identify any active exceptions (EN-LC-002) related to the candidate. | During evaluation period. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Consult with the Domain Owner and Subdomain Owner of the candidate policy to confirm retirement is appropriate. | During evaluation period. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Prepare a Retirement Impact Assessment (Section 3 of Appendix A) and recommendation: APPROVE RETIREMENT or DENY RETIREMENT with rationale. | At completion of evaluation. |

### 6.3 Retirement Approval

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Approval Authority (per Section 4.3) | Review the retirement request and impact assessment. Approve or deny. For REQUIRED-tier: Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes. For ESSENTIAL-tier: Administrator approval signature. For RECOMMENDED/GOOD TO HAVE: Compliance Officer approval. | REQUIRED: At next Governing Body meeting. Others: Within 14 calendar days. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Upon approval, execute retirement actions per Section 6.4. | Within 14 calendar days of approval. |

### 6.4 Retirement Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Change the policy's status to DEPRECATED in the Enterprise Policy Taxonomy Framework and Master Version Registry (EN-LC-001, Appendix B). | Within 7 calendar days of approval. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Add the retired Policy ID to the Reserved ID Registry per EN-TG-001. The ID is permanently reserved and shall never be reused. | Within 7 calendar days.__ |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Update the Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix per EN-TG-002. If the retired policy was the sole coverage for a regulatory requirement, initiate a Regulatory Gap Remediation Plan (EN-TG-002, Appendix B) — a regulatory gap must not be created by retirement. | Within 14 calendar days. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | Update the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix per EN-LC-003. Remove the retired policy from all role assignments__ | Within 7 calendar days. |
| 6.4.5 | Compliance Officer | Update all cross-references in other policies that reference the retired policy. Replace references with the superseding policy (if applicable) or remove the reference with notation. | Within 30 calendar days. |
| 6.4.6 | Compliance Officer | Archive the retired policy with a "DEPRECATED — NOT FOR USE — Retired [date]" header/watermark. Move to the policy archive. | Within 7 calendar days. |
| 6.4.7 | Compliance Officer | Notify all personnel previously assigned the policy that it has been retired. If a replacement policy exists, distribute and collect acknowledgment per EN-LC-003/GV-PM-003. | Within 14 calendar days. |
| 6.4.8 | Compliance Officer | Record the retirement in the Taxonomy Change Log (EN-TG-001, Appendix A). | Within 7 calendar days. |
| 6.4.9 | Compliance Officer | Log the completed retirement in the Policy Retirement Register (Appendix B). | Within 7 calendar days. |

### 6.5 Safeguard Against Regulatory Gap Creation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Before finalizing any retirement, verify that the retirement does not create a regulatory gap. If the policy's retirement would leave a regulatory requirement unaddressed, retirement MUST NOT proceed until a replacement policy is active or the requirement has been formally repealed. | Before final retirement execution. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | If a gap would be created, hold retirement in "PENDING" status and initiate either: (a) new policy development per GV-PM-001; or (b) amendment of an existing policy per EN-LC-001 to absorb the coverage. Only after the replacement is ACTIVE may the retirement proceed. | Retirement held until gap resolved. |

| Policy acknowledgment | Appendix C | All in scope | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retired policies carry DEPRECATED status | Taxonomy audit | 100% of retired policies have DEPRECATED status |
| Retired Policy IDs in Reserved Registry | Registry audit | 100% of retired IDs registered |
| No regulatory gap created by retirement | Regulatory cross-reference audit | Zero gaps created |
| Cross-references updated in all affected policies | Cross-reference audit | 100% within 30 days |
| Retired policies archived with marking | Archive audit | 100% compliance__ |
| Staff notified of retirements | Notification records | 100% within 14 days |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Policies informally deleted without process | No audit trail; regulatory gaps created; staff confusion | All retirements through this formal process |
| Retirement creates regulatory gap | Direct non-compliance | Section 6.5 safeguard — retirement blocked until gap resolved |
| Policy ID reused for new policy | Audit trail confusion; cross-reference errors | Reserved ID Registry; IDs permanently retired |
| Cross-references in other policies not updated | Staff following broken references | 30-day cross-reference update deadline |
| Retired policies still accessible in active system | Staff may follow deprecated requirements | Immediate archival with "DEPRECATED" marking; system access revoked |

## 2. Purpose

This policy establishes the enterprise compliance metrics program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It defines the indicators, measurement methodology, reporting infrastructure, and governance accountability required to continuously measure the agency's compliance posture across all 10 governance domains.

Effective compliance metrics enable the agency to:

- Detect emerging compliance risk before it becomes a regulatory finding or civil liability
- Provide the Governing Body with quantitative evidence that the Compliance Program is functioning, as required by OIG Compliance Element 5 (Monitoring and Auditing)
- Demonstrate to CMS surveyors and CDPH that the agency actively measures, reports, and acts on compliance performance data
- Link QAPI's data-driven quality improvement mandate (42 CFR §484.65) to compliance-specific performance tracking
- Identify domains or subdomains where policy adherence is consistently low, triggering targeted corrective action

This policy is companion to EN-TG-001 (what the policy library is) and EN-LC-001 (how policies are maintained current). Together, the three policies in the EN domain constitute the enterprise governance and control framework that makes the agency's compliance program auditable, measurable, and defensible.

---

## 3. Scope

This policy applies to:

* All 10 governance domains and their respective Domain Stewards
* The Compliance Officer as program owner and data custodian
* The Quality Assurance Director as co-steward for QAPI-linked metrics (42 CFR §484.65)
* The Administrator and Governing Body as receiving authorities for Compliance Metrics Reports
* All staff, supervisors, and managers whose activities generate compliance metric inputs
* All CMS, OIG, California, and accreditation compliance obligations of the agency

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Compliance Metric | A quantifiable measure of the agency's adherence to a specific regulatory requirement, policy standard, or compliance program element. |
| Enterprise Compliance Score (ECS) | An aggregate percentage-based score representing the agency's overall compliance posture across all domains for a reporting period, calculated as: (total compliant indicators ÷ total indicators measured) × 100. |
| Domain Compliance Score (DCS) | The ECS calculated at the domain level (e.g., CL domain, GV domain), representing compliance performance within one governance domain. |
| Key Performance Indicator (KPI) | A selected metric designated as an agency priority for regular monitoring. KPIs are tracked every reporting period; non-KPI metrics may be tracked quarterly or annually. |
| Threshold | The minimum acceptable compliance score for a metric or domain. Breach of threshold triggers escalation and corrective action. |
| Green / Yellow / Red Rating | Status classifications applied to each metric: Green = at or above threshold (compliant); Yellow = 90–99% of threshold (warning — monitor closely); Red = below threshold (deficient — corrective action required). |
| Compliance Dashboard | The agency's internal reporting tool — a structured display of all KPIs with current scores, trend data, and Green/Yellow/Red status designations. Updated monthly and provided to the Administrator. |
| Baseline | The initial measured value of a metric upon first collection, used as the reference point for improvement trending. |
| Regulatory Audit Trail | The documented evidence that a compliance metric was measured, the data source used, the result, and any responsive action taken. Required to demonstrate OIG Compliance Element 5. |
| Corrective Action Threshold | The pre-defined score level at which a metric automatically triggers a formal CAP under QA-AE-003. For REQUIRED-tier compliance metrics: 90%; for ESSENTIAL-tier: 85%. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an active, data-driven Enterprise Compliance Metrics Program operated by the Compliance Officer. The program shall measure compliance KPIs across all 10 governance domains on a continuous basis.

5.2 Each governance domain shall have defined KPIs. The minimum number of active KPIs per domain is three (3). REQUIRED-tier compliance areas shall always have at least one KPI each. KPIs are approved by the Compliance Officer and documented in the KPI Registry (Appendix A).

5.3 Compliance metrics shall be reported on the following cadence: monthly dashboard to Administrator; quarterly Compliance Metrics Summary to Compliance Committee; semi-annual report to Governing Body. The semi-annual Governing Body report shall include: trend analysis, domains below threshold, open CAPs with status, and comparative analysis vs. prior period.

5.4 When any compliance metric falls below its corrective action threshold, the Compliance Officer shall initiate a formal Corrective Action Plan (CAP) per QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days.

5.5 The ECS and all Domain Compliance Scores shall be incorporated into the agency's annual QAPI Program Evaluation per 42 CFR §484.65(b)(5), with specific analysis of whether any compliance metric deficiency correlated with a patient care quality issue.

5.6 Compliance data is confidential — access is limited to the Compliance Officer, Administrator, Governing Body members, Domain Stewards (their own domain data), and authorized auditors. Compliance metrics data shall not be shared with staff below the supervisory level except in aggregate, anonymized, educational formats.

5.7 This policy shall be reviewed annually. The KPI Registry (Appendix A) shall be reviewed and updated at each annual cycle to add new regulatory KPIs, retire obsolete KPIs, and adjust thresholds based on performance history.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 KPI Definition and KPI Registry

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Identify minimum KPIs for each domain. For each KPI, define: (a) KPI ID (e.g., EN-KPI-01); (b) description; (c) regulatory basis; (d) data source; (e) measurement method; (f) reporting frequency; (g) threshold (and corrective action threshold); (h) Green/Yellow/Red definitions; (i) responsible party for data collection. | At initial program adoption; update at each annual review. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Publish the KPI Registry (Appendix A) to the Policy Registry. The KPI Registry is a governing document protected at Tier 2 access. | Within 30 days of initial program adoption; within 30 days of each annual update. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | When a new regulatory requirement is identified per CO-RA-001, assess whether a new KPI is needed to measure ongoing compliance with that requirement. If yes, add to KPI Registry via the annual update cycle, or immediately for emergency regulatory changes. | Within 30 days of regulatory change identification (or annual cycle). |

### 6.2 Baseline Measurement Collection

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer (with Domain Stewards) | Collect baseline data for each KPI upon adoption of this program. Document the baseline value, the data collection date, the data source, and any limitations noted (e.g., incomplete records for the prior period). Record in the KPI Registry Baseline column. | Within 60 days of program adoption. |
| 6.2.2 | Domain Stewards | Provide Compliance Officer with access to domain-specific data sources (audit logs, training records, incident reports, policy acknowledgment records, chart review results) needed for KPI measurement. | Ongoing; within 5 business days of any Compliance Officer data request. |

### 6.3 Monthly Compliance Dashboard Production

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | By the 10th calendar day of each month, collect data for all monthly-frequency KPIs from applicable data sources. Document the data point for each KPI for the preceding month. | By the 10th of each month. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Calculate scores for each KPI: (measured compliant instances ÷ total measured instances) × 100. Apply Green/Yellow/Red status per KPI threshold definitions. | By the 12th of each month. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Calculate Domain Compliance Scores and Enterprise Compliance Score: (a) Domain Compliance Score = average score across all KPIs in the domain; (b) Enterprise Compliance Score = average score across all domains. | By the 12th of each month. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer | Produce the Monthly Compliance Dashboard (Appendix B template): (a) ECS and trend (vs. prior month); (b) domain-level table with DCS and trend; (c) KPI detail table for each domain — KPI, score, rating, trend, open CAPs; (d) any metrics newly entering Yellow or Red status; (e) escalation summary for metrics at Red status. | By the 15th of each month. |
| 6.3.5 | Compliance Officer | Distribute the Monthly Compliance Dashboard to the Administrator. Retain a copy in the compliance management record. | By the 15th of each month. |

### 6.4 Quarterly Compliance Metrics Summary

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Produce a Quarterly Compliance Metrics Summary at the close of each calendar quarter (Q1: Jan–Mar, Q2: Apr–Jun, Q3: Jul–Sep, Q4: Oct–Dec). The Summary shall include: (a) quarterly-average ECS and DCS; (b) trend analysis vs. prior quarter; (c) metrics that remained Red for ≥2 consecutive months; (d) open Corrective Action Plans with progress status; (e) new metrics added to the KPI Registry this quarter; (f) upcoming regulatory compliance obligations and associated KPI watch. | Within 30 days of quarter close. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Present the Quarterly Summary to the Compliance Committee (or Administrator if no formal committee exists). Document meeting attendance and discussion in meeting minutes. | Within 30 days of quarter close. |

### 6.5 Semi-Annual Governing Body Compliance Report

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Prepare the Semi-Annual Governing Body Compliance Report, which shall include: (a) 6-month ECS trend by month; (b) domain-level performance summary for all 10 domains; (c) identification of any domain scoring below threshold for ≥2 consecutive months; (d) all open CAPs — description, responsible party, target date, current status; (e) CAPs closed this period — description, outcome, and whether metrics improved; (f) regulatory changes incorporated this period and KPIs added in response; (g) upcoming regulatory compliance milestones; (h) Compliance Officer certification that the Compliance Program is functioning per OIG Element 5. | 30 days before each Governing Body semi-annual meeting. |
| 6.5.2 | Administrator | Present the Semi-Annual Report to the Governing Body. Document Governing Body discussion, questions, and any directives in Governing Body meeting minutes per GV-GB-001. | At Governing Body meeting. |
| 6.5.3 | Governing Body Chair | Acknowledge receipt of the Semi-Annual Compliance Report in meeting minutes. If any domain has been below threshold for ≥2 quarters, the Governing Body directs corrective action and requests a status update at the next meeting. | At and following Governing Body meeting. |

### 6.6 Corrective Action Triggers and Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.6.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon identifying any metric at Red status (below corrective action threshold): (a) notify the Domain Steward immediately; (b) initiate a formal CAP per QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days; (c) document the CAP in the Compliance Dashboard's open CAP tracking section. | CAP initiated within 14 calendar days of metric falling to Red status. |
| 6.6.2 | Domain Steward | In collaboration with Compliance Officer: (a) conduct a root cause analysis (RCA) of the compliance failure; (b) propose corrective actions with specific tasks, responsible parties, and target dates; (c) implement corrective actions; (d) provide progress updates to Compliance Officer monthly. | RCA within 30 days; corrective action implementation per CAP timeline. |
| 6.6.3 | Compliance Officer | Monitor the metric that triggered the CAP monthly after implementation of corrective actions. Document whether the metric returns to Green status. If after 3 months of corrective action the metric has not improved to ≥yellow status, escalate to Administrator and consider whether the CAP needs redesign. | Monthly post-CAP monitoring; 3-month escalation if no improvement. |
| 6.6.4 | Compliance Officer | When a CAP is closed successfully (metric returns to Green for ≥2 consecutive months), document the closure: (a) final metric scores; (b) corrective actions implemented; (c) sustainability plan to prevent regression; (d) notify the Governing Body at next semi-annual report. | Upon achievement of 2 consecutive Green months. |

### 6.7 QAPI Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.7.1 | Compliance Officer / QA Director | At the start of each QAPI cycle (quarterly), the Compliance Officer shares the compliance metrics data with the QA Director for integration into the QAPI performance dataset per QA-PG-001 and QA-PG-002. | At the start of each QAPI quarter. |
| 6.7.2 | QA Director | Assess whether any compliance KPI at Yellow or Red status corresponds to a patient care quality indicator. If a compliance deficit correlates with care quality risk, initiate a joint QAPI-Compliance review process. Document the correlation analysis in the QAPI record. | Within 30 days of receiving compliance metrics data each quarter. |
| 6.7.3 | Compliance Officer | Incorporate the compliance metrics program performance into the agency's Annual QAPI Program Evaluation per 42 CFR §484.65(b)(5). The evaluation shall specifically address whether the compliance program has contributed to quality improvement outcomes. | At annual QAPI Program Evaluation. |

| QAPI compliance integration records | Correlation analysis, QAPI actions linked to compliance gaps | QA Director | QAPI records file | Per QAPI cycle; retained per QAPI-PG-001 schedule |
| Baseline data records | KPI baseline values with source documentation | Compliance Officer | KPI Registry (Appendix A) | At program adoption; retained permanently |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Monthly dashboards produced on time | Audit of dashboard production dates vs. 15th of month standard | 100% within allotted timeframes; 0 missed months |
| All Red-status metrics have active CAPs | Audit of open CAPs vs. count of Red-status metrics | 100% of Red-status metrics have an associated CAP within 14 days |
| Governing Body received semi-annual compliance report | Governing Body meeting minutes showing report received and acknowledged | 100% per year (two reports per year minimum) |
| KPI Registry reviewed and updated annually | Version history of KPI Registry document | Annual update documented; 0 years without update |
| QAPI compliance integration documented each quarter | QAPI records showing compliance data integration | 100% of quarters with documented integration |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors and OIG reviewers conducting compliance program assessments will ask:

1. How does the agency know its compliance program is working? This policy is the answer — quantitative KPI measurement provides the evidence.
2. What happens when a compliance metric is deficient? The CAP→QA-AE-003 pathway with Governing Body oversight demonstrates accountability.
3. Has the Governing Body been informed of compliance performance status? Semi-annual reports with Governing Body meeting minutes prove this.
4. Is QAPI integrated with compliance monitoring? The QAPI integration procedure (Section 6.7) and documented cross-references to 42 CFR §484.65 provide this evidence.
5. What is the agency's Enterprise Compliance Score? The Compliance Officer should be able to produce the most recent Monthly Dashboard immediately on request.

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Compliance program exists on paper but metrics are not actually measured | OIG Element 5 failure — monitoring and auditing is not being performed | KPI Registry with defined data sources, responsible parties, and measurement methods makes measurement concrete and auditable |
| Red-status metrics identified but no corrective action initiated | Survey finding: agency failed to act on known compliance deficiency — highest risk condition | Automatic CAP initiation at 14 days when a metric hits Red |
| Governing Body not receiving compliance reports | Survey finding: Governing Body lacks meaningful compliance oversight, violating its 42 CFR §484.105 responsibilities | Semi-annual report schedule with mandatory Governing Body meeting minutes documentation |
| Compliance metrics siloed from QAPI — parallel but disconnected programs | Missed opportunity to link compliance deficits to care quality risks; 42 CFR §484.65 integration requirement missed | Formal QAPI integration procedure (Section 6.7) with documentation requirement |
| KPI thresholds set too low to drive improvement | Meets the paper standard but does not identify meaningful compliance risk | Initial thresholds set at 95% for REQUIRED-tier metrics; reviewed annually for adjustment |
| No trend data — each month's data is standalone | Cannot identify gradual compliance deterioration before it becomes a Red crisis | Monthly Dashboard includes trend (vs. 3-month rolling average) for every KPI |

# EN-CM-002 — Inter-Domain Policy Coordination & Conflict Resolution
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | EN-CM-002 |
| Title | Inter-Domain Policy Coordination & Conflict Resolution |
| Domain | EN — Enterprise Control |
| Subdomain | CM — Compliance Metrics |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the process for identifying and resolving conflicts, inconsistencies, overlaps, or gaps between policies across different domains within the enterprise taxonomy. In a 244-policy framework spanning 10 domains, cross-domain conflicts are inevitable without proactive coordination. Unresolved conflicts create contradictory requirements for staff, compliance confusion, and survey risk. This policy establishes a systematic identification process, a resolution methodology, an escalation hierarchy, and documentation requirements.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Compliance Officer (conflict resolution process owner and final arbitrator for most conflicts)
The Administrator (escalation authority)
All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners
The Governing Body (final escalation for unresolvable conflicts)
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 No two policies within the enterprise taxonomy shall contain contradictory requirements applicable to the same personnel, function, or process. Where conflicts are identified, they shall be resolved per this policy.
4.2 Inter-domain policy conflicts shall be identified through: (a) annual taxonomy audit (EN-TG-001); (b) policy review cycles (GV-PM-002); (c) new policy creation/revision (EN-LC-001); (d) staff or Domain Owner reports; (e) audit findings or survey observations.
4.3 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a Policy Conflict Register (Appendix A) documenting all identified conflicts, status, and resolution.
4.4 Resolution of inter-domain conflicts follows a defined hierarchy: (a) direct negotiation between affected Domain Owners; (b) Compliance Officer mediation; (c) Administrator decision; (d) Governing Body final resolution.
4.5 When policies from different domains contain overlapping but not contradictory requirements, the Compliance Officer shall determine whether the overlap should be: (a) maintained (each policy serves a distinct purpose despite overlap); (b) consolidated (merge into one policy per EN-LC-004/EN-TG-001); or (c) cross-referenced (each policy references the other to eliminate duplication).
4.6 Regulatory mandates always take precedence. If one policy reflects a regulatory requirement and a conflicting policy does not, the regulatory policy controls.
4.7 The Compliance Officer shall conduct an annual Inter-Domain Coordination Review and report results to the Administrator.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Inter-Domain Conflict | A situation where two or more policies from different domains contain contradictory, inconsistent, or incompatible requirements applicable to the same personnel, process, or function. |
| Policy Overlap | A situation where two or more policies address the same topic or requirement without contradiction, but with unnecessary duplication that could cause confusion. |
| Conflict Resolution | The process of identifying, analyzing, and resolving inter-domain policy conflicts through negotiation, mediation, or authoritative decision. |
| Domain Owner Negotiation | Direct communication between the affected Domain Owners to reach consensus on conflict resolution. |
| Compliance Officer Mediation | Facilitated resolution by the Compliance Officer when Domain Owners cannot reach consensus. |
| Regulatory Precedence | The principle that requirements derived from federal or state law, regulation, or CMS Conditions of Participation take precedence over operational policies in any conflict. |

## 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Conflict Identification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Any staff member, Domain Owner, or auditor | Identify a potential inter-domain policy conflict through any of the following channels: (a) annual taxonomy audit; (b) policy review cycle; (c) new policy creation; (d) operational experience; (e) audit finding; (f) survey observation. Submit a Policy Conflict Report (Appendix A) to the Compliance Officer. The report must identify: (a) the two or more policies believed to be in conflict; (b) the specific sections/requirements that conflict; (c) the nature of the conflict (contradictory, inconsistent, overlapping, or gap); (d) the operational impact observed or anticipated. | As needed; within 7 calendar days of identification. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Receive and log the conflict report in the Policy Conflict Register (Appendix B). Assign a Conflict ID using the format CON-[NNN]. Acknowledge receipt to the reporter within 48 hours. | Within 48 hours of receipt. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct an initial assessment to determine: (a) whether a genuine conflict exists (vs. a misinterpretation of policy scope); (b) the severity of the conflict (Category 1 — Critical: contradicts a regulatory mandate or creates patient safety risk; Category 2 — Significant: creates operational confusion or contradictory requirements for staff; Category 3 — Minor: cosmetic overlap or inconsistent terminology without operational impact); (c) the affected domains and Domain Owners. | Within 7 calendar days of receipt. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | If the initial assessment determines no genuine conflict exists, document the rationale, close the report in the Conflict Register, and notify the reporter with explanation. If a conflict is confirmed, proceed to Section 6.2. | Within 7 calendar days. |

#### 6.2 Conflict Resolution — Domain Owner Negotiation (Level 1)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Notify the affected Domain Owners of the confirmed conflict. Provide each Domain Owner with: (a) the Conflict Report; (b) copies of the conflicting policy sections; (c) the severity category; (d) a request to negotiate a resolution. | Within 7 calendar days of conflict confirmation. |
| 6.2.2 | Affected Domain Owners | Engage in direct negotiation to resolve the conflict. Options include: (a) one policy yields to the other (the policy with regulatory basis takes precedence); (b) both policies are amended to eliminate the conflict; (c) one policy is retired and the other expanded; (d) a cross-reference is added to clarify the relationship; (e) scope boundaries are clarified to eliminate overlap. Document the proposed resolution in writing. | Within 14 calendar days of notification. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Review the proposed resolution for: (a) regulatory compliance; (b) consistency with the enterprise taxonomy; (c) impact on other policies; (d) operational feasibility. If acceptable, approve the resolution and proceed to Section 6.4 (Implementation). | Within 7 calendar days of receiving proposed resolution. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | If Domain Owners cannot reach agreement within 14 calendar days, or if the Compliance Officer determines the proposed resolution is inadequate, escalate to Level 2 (Compliance Officer Mediation). | At the 14-day deadline or upon determination of inadequacy. |

#### 6.3 Conflict Resolution — Compliance Officer Mediation (Level 2)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Convene a mediation session with all affected Domain Owners. The Compliance Officer serves as mediator with authority to: (a) request additional information; (b) propose resolution options; (c) determine which policy has regulatory precedence; (d) direct specific amendments. | Within 7 calendar days of escalation. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Apply the following resolution hierarchy: (a) Regulatory Precedence — the policy that directly implements a federal or state regulatory requirement controls; (b) Classification Tier Precedence — REQUIRED-tier policies take precedence over ESSENTIAL, RECOMMENDED, or GOOD TO HAVE in any conflict; (c) Specificity — a policy specific to a function takes precedence over a general policy; (d) Recency — if all other factors are equal, the more recently reviewed and approved policy is presumed current. | During mediation. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Issue a written Conflict Resolution Determination documenting: (a) the conflict; (b) the resolution; (c) the rationale; (d) the policies to be amended; (e) the implementation timeline. Both Domain Owners shall receive copies. | Within 7 calendar days of mediation. |
| 6.3.4 | Affected Domain Owners | If either Domain Owner disagrees with the Compliance Officer's determination, they may appeal to the Administrator within 7 calendar days by submitting a written appeal with rationale. | Within 7 calendar days of determination. |

#### 6.4 Conflict Resolution — Administrator Decision (Level 3)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Administrator | Receive and review the appeal, the Conflict Report, the Compliance Officer's determination, and the Domain Owner's written rationale. | Within 7 calendar days of appeal receipt. |
| 6.4.2 | Administrator | Issue a final decision. The Administrator's decision is binding on all Domain Owners and the Compliance Officer, subject only to Governing Body override for conflicts involving REQUIRED-tier policies with regulatory basis. | Within 14 calendar days of appeal receipt. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | If the conflict involves two REQUIRED-tier policies both with regulatory basis and the Administrator's decision is appealed, escalate to the Governing Body for final resolution at the next quarterly meeting. The Governing Body's decision is final and not subject to further appeal. | At the next quarterly Governing Body meeting. |

#### 6.5 Conflict Resolution Implementation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon final resolution (at any level), develop an implementation plan specifying: (a) which policies require amendment; (b) specific language changes; (c) responsible Domain Owner for each amendment; (d) cross-reference updates required; (e) staff notification requirements; (f) timeline for completion. | Within 7 calendar days of final resolution. |
| 6.5.2 | Affected Domain Owners | Execute policy amendments per the implementation plan. Route through the standard policy review and approval process per EN-LC-001 on an expedited basis. | Per implementation plan timeline; not to exceed 30 calendar days for Category 1; 60 calendar days for Category 2; 90 calendar days for Category 3. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Verify all amendments are completed, cross-references updated, and staff notified. Update the Policy Conflict Register (Appendix B) to reflect resolution completion. Close the conflict record. | Within 7 calendar days of amendment completion. |
| 6.5.4 | Compliance Officer | If the conflict resolution reveals a systemic issue (e.g., recurring conflicts between two domains, structural taxonomy weakness), initiate a systemic review recommendation to the Administrator for potential taxonomy restructuring per EN-TG-001. | As needed; documented in annual report. |

#### 6.6 Overlap Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | Compliance Officer | When policies from different domains contain overlapping but non-contradictory requirements, evaluate the overlap using the following criteria: (a) Do both policies serve distinct regulatory or operational purposes that justify the overlap? (b) Does the overlap create confusion for staff who must comply with both? (c) Would consolidation improve clarity without losing essential content? | During conflict assessment or annual coordination review. |
| 6.6.2 | Compliance Officer | Determine disposition: (a) Maintain — overlap justified; add cross-reference in each policy noting the related policy; (b) Consolidate — merge overlapping content into one policy; retire the other per EN-LC-004; (c) Clarify — add scope boundaries to each policy eliminating the perception of overlap. Document the decision and rationale. | Within 14 calendar days of evaluation. |
| 6.6.3 | Compliance Officer | Implement the disposition per Section 6.5 implementation procedures. | Per Section 6.5 timelines. |

#### 6.7 Annual Inter-Domain Coordination Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.7.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct an annual Inter-Domain Coordination Review covering: (a) all conflicts identified during the year; (b) resolution status and outcomes; (c) recurring conflict patterns; (d) domains with the highest conflict frequency; (e) overlap assessments conducted; (f) systemic recommendations. Document results in the Annual Inter-Domain Coordination Report (Appendix C). | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of the start of each fiscal year. |
| 6.7.2 | Compliance Officer | Present the annual report to the Administrator. Include recommendations for: (a) taxonomy restructuring if warranted; (b) Domain Owner cross-training; (c) process improvements; (d) policies requiring proactive coordination during upcoming review cycles. | At the next Administrator meeting following report completion. |
| 6.7.3 | Compliance Officer | Proactively identify policies scheduled for review in the upcoming quarter and assess potential cross-domain impacts. Notify affected Domain Owners of coordination needs before their review cycle begins. | Quarterly; 30 calendar days before each quarter's review cycle policies are due. |

### 8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All identified conflicts are formally documented | Review of Conflict Register against operational reports and audit findings | Zero undocumented conflicts |
| Conflicts resolved within defined timelines | Review of Conflict Register dates against resolution deadlines | 100% Category 1 within 30 days; 100% Category 2 within 60 days; 100% Category 3 within 90 days |
| No contradictory policies remain unresolved | Annual taxonomy audit cross-check | Zero open Category 1 or Category 2 conflicts exceeding resolution deadline |
| Domain Owner negotiation attempted before escalation | Review of conflict resolution records | 100% — Level 1 attempted before Level 2 |
| Annual Inter-Domain Coordination Review completed | Review of Appendix C report date | Completed within 60 calendar days of fiscal year start |
| Regulatory precedence applied correctly | Review of resolution determinations | 100% — regulatory-based policies always take precedence |
| Conflict Register is current and complete | Quarterly spot check | Updated within 48 hours of each event |
| Policy amendments completed per implementation plan | Cross-check plan deadlines against actual completion | 100% within plan timelines |

#### 8.2 Surveyor Expectations
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will assess whether:
The agency's policies are internally consistent and do not contain contradictory requirements. A surveyor who identifies contradictory policies during a document review will cite organizational deficiency.
Staff can identify the applicable policy for a given function without confusion. If staff report conflicting guidance from different policies, the surveyor will investigate the agency's policy coordination process.
The agency has a systematic process for managing cross-domain policy relationships. Surveyors view a coordinated policy system as evidence of mature governance.
When policies from different domains address related functions (e.g., clinical documentation standards in CL-CD vs. documentation compliance in CO-DC), they are aligned and cross-referenced.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No formal conflict identification or resolution process | Contradictory policies persist; staff confusion; survey citations | Implement this policy; maintain Appendix A/B processes |
| Conflicts identified but not resolved — left in "open" status indefinitely | Staff follow whichever policy they prefer; inconsistent practices; compliance risk | Mandatory resolution timelines by severity; escalation hierarchy |
| Domain Owners protect "their" policies and refuse to coordinate | Organizational silos; contradictions persist; governance breakdown | Escalation to Compliance Officer and Administrator; binding resolution authority |
| Resolution determined but policy amendments never completed | Resolution exists on paper only; operational conflict persists | Implementation plan with deadlines; Compliance Officer verification; closure only after amendments confirmed |
| Overlap treated as conflict when no actual contradiction exists | Unnecessary policy changes; wasted effort; potential loss of important content | Section 6.6 overlap management process; maintain justified overlaps with cross-references |
| No annual coordination review | Recurring patterns undetected; systemic issues persist | Annual Appendix C report; proactive quarterly cross-domain coordination |

### 10. Training Requirements
10.1 The Compliance Officer and all Domain Owners shall receive training on the conflict identification process, the resolution hierarchy (Level 1 through Level 3), the regulatory precedence principle, the overlap management process, and the annual coordination review within 14 calendar days of assignment to a policy governance role.
10.2 All Subdomain Owners shall receive training on how to identify potential cross-domain conflicts during their policy review cycles and how to submit a Policy Conflict Report (Appendix A).
10.3 Annual refresher training for Domain Owners covering: (a) any conflicts resolved during the prior year; (b) lessons learned; (c) proactive coordination requirements for upcoming review cycles.
10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.
### 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Compliance Officer and Administrator; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the Enterprise Policy Taxonomy Framework and Master Policy Index.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Administrator. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

# CO-CP-001 — Corporate Compliance Program

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the Corporate Compliance Program ("Program") for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Program is the agency's formal, systematic commitment to conducting all operations with integrity, in full conformity with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and the standards issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the Office of Inspector General (OIG), and all other regulatory bodies having jurisdiction over the agency's operations. The Program satisfies the requirements set forth in the OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies and supports compliance with 42 CFR § 484.100 (Condition of Participation: Compliance with Federal, State, and Local Laws) and the agency's obligation to maintain Medicare certification. The Program provides the structural foundation upon which all other compliance-related policies in the CO domain operate.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All Governing Body members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
The Agency Administrator
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Compliance Officer and Compliance Committee members
All full-time, part-time, per diem, and contracted employees
All volunteers performing services on behalf of the agency
All third-party vendors, contractors, and business associates who interact with agency operations, billing, or patient care
Note: This policy does not supersede any applicable federal or state law. Where this policy conflicts with a law or regulation, the more stringent requirement governs.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a fully operational Corporate Compliance Program that satisfies the seven foundational elements of an effective compliance program as defined by the OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies.
4.2 The seven required elements of the Program are:
Written policies, procedures, and standards of conduct
Designation of a Compliance Officer and Compliance Committee
Effective training and education
Effective lines of communication
Internal monitoring and auditing
Enforcement of standards and well-publicized disciplinary guidelines
Prompt response to detected offenses and development of corrective action
4.3 The Governing Body shall maintain ultimate accountability for the effectiveness of the Program and shall receive compliance reports at no less than quarterly intervals per policy GV-GB-001.
4.4 The Program shall be operationally independent. The Compliance Officer shall have direct reporting access to the Governing Body and shall not be subject to retaliation, pressure, or interference in performing compliance functions.
4.5 Participation in compliance training and adherence to the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004) are conditions of continued employment and/or contract with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
4.6 The agency shall not employ or contract with any individual or entity that appears on the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) or the System for Award Management (SAM) exclusion database, per policy HR-TA-003.
4.7 All known or suspected violations of law, regulation, agency policy, or the Code of Conduct shall be reported promptly through mechanisms established in policy CO-CP-006 and investigated per policy CO-CP-007.
4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all workforce members within scope within 14 calendar days.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Corporate Compliance Program | The formal, structured system of policies, procedures, oversight mechanisms, training, and accountability structures designed to prevent, detect, and correct violations of law, regulation, or ethical standards. |
| Compliance Officer | The individual designated by the Governing Body with authority and independence to operate the Corporate Compliance Program, per policy CO-CP-002. |
| Compliance Committee | The multi-disciplinary body chaired by the Compliance Officer that provides operational oversight of the Program, per policy CO-CP-003. |
| OIG | Office of Inspector General of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — the federal body responsible for combating fraud, waste, and abuse in federal health care programs. |
| LEIE | List of Excluded Individuals/Entities — the OIG database of individuals and entities excluded from participation in federal health care programs. |
| SAM | System for Award Management — the federal database that includes parties excluded from receiving federal contracts, certain subcontracts, and certain federal financial and non-financial assistance and benefits. |
| False Claims Act | Federal law (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733) imposing civil and criminal liability for knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims to the federal government. |
| Fraud, Waste, and Abuse (FWA) | Fraud: intentional deception to obtain unauthorized benefits. Waste: overutilization or misuse of resources. Abuse: practices inconsistent with sound fiscal, business, or medical practices. |
| Code of Conduct | The written document that defines the ethical standards, behavioral expectations, and legal obligations of all workforce members, per policy CO-CP-004. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Program Establishment and Governance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Governing Body | Formally adopt and approve the Corporate Compliance Program through a documented resolution recorded in Governing Body meeting minutes. | Prior to initial Medicare certification and at each substantive Program revision. |
| 6.1.2 | Governing Body | Designate a qualified Compliance Officer per the requirements of policy CO-CP-002. Document the designation in Governing Body minutes. | Prior to agency operation; within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Establish and chair the Compliance Committee per policy CO-CP-003. | Within 30 calendar days of Compliance Officer designation. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a current written description of the Program, its seven elements, the authority of the Compliance Officer, and the Program's reporting structure. | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually. |
| 6.1.5 | Administrator | Ensure adequate resources are allocated in the annual budget to support Program operations including staffing, training, auditing, and technology, per policy FN-FP-005. | Annually, prior to budget approval. |

### 6.2 Written Standards Development and Maintenance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a current, complete policy index for all CO-domain policies. Ensure all REQUIRED-tier policies are current, approved, and accessible to all applicable workforce members. | Continuously; verified at each quarterly Compliance Committee meeting. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all workforce members have access to the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004) in a readable format at the time of hire and upon each revision. | At hire; upon each revision. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Coordinate with the Administrator to ensure that policy revisions triggered by regulatory changes are processed within 30 calendar days of the effective date of the regulatory change, per policy CO-RA-001. | Within 30 calendar days of regulatory change effective date. |

### 6.3 Training and Education

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all new employees and contractors receive compliance orientation training covering: (a) the Program and its seven elements; (b) Code of Conduct; (c) fraud, waste, and abuse prevention; (d) HIPAA; (e) reporting mechanisms and non-retaliation policy; (f) exclusion screening. | Within 14 calendar days of hire or contract commencement. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all workforce members complete annual compliance refresher training per policy CO-CP-008. | Annually; completed within 30 calendar days of the start of each calendar year. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Maintain training completion logs and report compliance to the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |

### 6.4 Communication and Reporting Lines

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Maintain multiple accessible reporting mechanisms per policy CO-CP-006 including a compliance hotline, anonymous reporting option, and direct email to the Compliance Officer. | Continuously. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Ensure all workforce members are informed of reporting mechanisms at hire, during annual training, and upon any change to reporting channels. | At hire; annually; upon change. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Prepare and deliver a written compliance status report to the Governing Body no fewer than 7 calendar days before each quarterly meeting. The report must address: (a) active compliance investigations (without compromising confidentiality); (b) audit findings and trends; (c) regulatory changes affecting the agency; (d) training completion rates; (e) exclusion screening status; (f) corrective action plan status. | 7 calendar days before each quarterly Governing Body meeting. |

### 6.5 Internal Monitoring and Auditing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Develop and maintain an annual compliance audit work plan. The work plan shall prioritize: (a) billing and claims accuracy; (b) OASIS data integrity; (c) medical necessity documentation; (d) exclusion screening compliance; (e) policy acknowledgment rates; (f) fraud and abuse risk areas identified by OIG Work Plan. | Approved at first Compliance Committee meeting of each calendar year. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Conduct or commission audits per the annual work plan and document all findings, methodology, sample sizes, and corrective actions, per policy CO-RA-002. | Per audit work plan schedule. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Present audit findings and status of corrective actions at each quarterly Compliance Committee meeting and Governing Body meeting. | Quarterly. |

### 6.6 Enforcement and Discipline

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | Compliance Officer / HR Director | Ensure disciplinary standards for compliance violations are defined in the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004) and Employee Handbook. Disciplinary standards must be consistently applied without exception for seniority or role. | Continuously. |
| 6.6.2 | HR Director | Apply progressive discipline for compliance violations per policy HR-ER-002. All disciplinary actions related to compliance violations shall be reported to the Compliance Officer within 5 calendar days. | Within 5 calendar days of disciplinary action. |
| 6.6.3 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a disciplinary action log for all compliance-related violations. Report aggregate trends to the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |

### 6.7 Response to Detected Offenses

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.7.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon receipt of a compliance report or self-identified concern, initiate investigation per policy CO-CP-007 within 7 calendar days. | Within 7 calendar days of receipt. |
| 6.7.2 | Compliance Officer | If investigation confirms an overpayment, initiate refund process per policy FN-BC-004 within the CMS 60-day repayment window. | Within 60 calendar days of identification. |
| 6.7.3 | Compliance Officer | Develop and implement corrective action plans for all confirmed violations per policy QA-AE-003. | Within 14 calendar days of confirmation. |
| 6.7.4 | Compliance Officer | Determine whether voluntary self-disclosure to OIG, CMS, or other regulatory bodies is required. Engage legal counsel for any disclosure determination. | Within 30 calendar days of confirmed violation. |

### 6.8 Annual Program Effectiveness Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.8.1 | Compliance Officer | Conduct an annual assessment of Program effectiveness using the metrics in Section 8 of this policy. Present findings to the Governing Body at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year. | Annually at Q1 Governing Body meeting. |
| 6.8.2 | Governing Body | Review the annual Program effectiveness assessment and direct any structural improvements. Document review and directives in meeting minutes. | Annually at Q1 meeting. |
| 6.8.3 | Compliance Officer | Update the Program description and all CO-domain policies as needed based on the effectiveness review. | Within 60 calendar days of Q1 meeting. |

| Annual Program effectiveness assessment | Written assessment report. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file; presented to Governing Body. | Annually; retained 7 years. |
| Exclusion screening logs | OIG/SAM screening records for all workforce members. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file. | At hire; monthly. Retained 7 years. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Program is formally adopted by Governing Body. | Review of Governing Body minutes for adoption resolution. | Documented adoption on file at all times. |
| Compliance Officer is designated and functioning. | Review of designation documentation; Governing Body minutes. | Current designation documented; no vacancy exceeds 30 days without interim designee. |
| Annual audit work plan is approved. | Review of Compliance Committee minutes; work plan document. | Approved at Q1 Compliance Committee meeting; 100% of planned audits initiated. |
| Quarterly compliance reports submitted to Governing Body. | Review of report submission dates vs. quarterly meeting dates. | 100% of reports submitted at least 7 days before each meeting. |
| All workforce members complete annual compliance training. | Review of training completion logs. | 95% completion rate within 30 days of deadline; 100% within 45 days. |
| Investigations initiated within required timeframes. | Review of investigation log with initiation dates. | 100% initiated within 7 calendar days of report receipt. |
| Confirmed overpayments refunded within 60 days. | Review of refund documentation and identification dates. | 100% compliance with 60-day repayment rule. |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points and Mitigation

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Program exists on paper but is not operationally active. | OIG and CMS will treat a non-functional Program as equivalent to having no Program. | Compliance Officer must demonstrate active operations through documented audits, meeting minutes, and training records. |
| Compliance Officer reports to Administrator rather than directly to Governing Body. | Independence is compromised; conflicts of interest may be suppressed. | Governing Body must establish direct reporting line in the designation document. |
| Training completion rates fall below 95%. | OIG views low completion as evidence of a non-effective Program. | Compliance Officer must track and escalate to Governing Body Chair within 7 days of missed deadline. |
| Investigations are not documented in writing. | Undocumented investigations are treated as not having occurred in any subsequent audit or survey. | All investigations must be opened, tracked, and closed in writing per CO-CP-007. |

## 10. Training Requirements
All workforce members shall complete the Corporate Compliance Program orientation module within 14 calendar days of hire or contract commencement.
All workforce members shall complete annual compliance refresher training per policy CO-CP-008.
The Compliance Officer shall complete at minimum 8 hours of continuing compliance education annually, with documentation retained in the compliance file.
All Governing Body members shall receive orientation to this policy and the Program structure within 14 calendar days of appointment.
Training completion shall be tracked and reported to the Governing Body quarterly.
## 11. Version Control
This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
Only the most current approved version of this policy is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose.
Any substantive revision requires: (a) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all applicable workforce members within 14 calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections) may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the qualifications, designation process, authority, independence, reporting structure, and responsibilities of the Compliance Officer of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Compliance Officer is the individual designated by the Governing Body who holds primary accountability for the day-to-day operation of the Corporate Compliance Program established under policy CO-CP-001. This policy ensures that the agency satisfies the OIG requirement that an effective compliance program include a designated Compliance Officer with sufficient authority and operational independence to fulfill all compliance functions without conflict or interference.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Governing Body (as the designating authority)
The individual designated as Compliance Officer
The Administrator
Any individual serving in an interim Compliance Officer capacity
The Compliance Committee
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall designate a qualified Compliance Officer prior to agency operation and maintain that designation continuously thereafter.
4.2 The Compliance Officer shall be designated by the Governing Body and the designation shall be documented in Governing Body meeting minutes with the full Designation and Authority Letter (Appendix A).
4.3 The Compliance Officer shall have the authority, independence, and resources necessary to fulfill all compliance functions. No member of agency leadership — including the Administrator — shall have the authority to override, impede, or retaliate against the Compliance Officer's performance of their duties.
4.4 The Compliance Officer shall have a direct reporting line to the Governing Body. The Compliance Officer may also have an administrative reporting relationship to the Administrator for operational purposes, provided that this reporting relationship does not compromise the independence of the Compliance Officer.
4.5 Any vacancy in the Compliance Officer role shall be filled within 30 calendar days. An interim Compliance Officer shall be designated within 14 calendar days of a vacancy and documented in writing.
4.6 The Compliance Officer role shall not be combined with the role of Agency Administrator or any clinical role that would create a conflict of interest in performing compliance oversight functions.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Officer | The individual designated by the Governing Body to operate the Corporate Compliance Program, investigate compliance concerns, coordinate auditing and monitoring, and report directly to the Governing Body on all compliance matters. |
| Independence | The ability to conduct compliance oversight functions, investigations, and reporting without interference, pressure, or retaliation from any member of agency management or the Governing Body. |
| Designation | The formal act of the Governing Body appointing an individual to serve as Compliance Officer, documented in meeting minutes and the Designation and Authority Letter. |
| Interim Compliance Officer | An individual temporarily fulfilling Compliance Officer responsibilities during a vacancy, with full authority granted by the Governing Body. |
| Conflict of Interest | Any situation in which the Compliance Officer's personal, financial, or professional interests could reasonably be perceived to compromise the independent performance of compliance functions. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Minimum Qualifications

| Requirement | Standard |
| --- | --- |
| Education | Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent professional compliance experience may substitute. |
| Experience | Minimum 2 years of experience in healthcare compliance, regulatory affairs, or health care law; home health experience strongly preferred. |
| Knowledge | Working knowledge of: Medicare home health Conditions of Participation (42 CFR Part 484); OIG Compliance Program Guidance; HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules; False Claims Act; Anti-Kickback Statute; CMS billing requirements for home health. |
| Certification | Certified in Healthcare Compliance (CHC) through the Compliance Certification Board preferred; not required if experience standard is met. |
| Exclusion Screening | Must not appear on OIG LEIE or SAM exclusion lists at time of designation and must clear monthly screening thereafter per policy HR-TA-003. |
| Background | Must pass criminal background check per policy HR-TA-002. |

### 6.2 Designation Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Governing Body | Identify, evaluate, and select a qualified candidate for the Compliance Officer role. Evaluate qualifications against Section 6.1 minimum standards. | Prior to agency operation; within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 6.2.2 | Governing Body | Formally designate the Compliance Officer through a documented vote recorded in Governing Body meeting minutes. | At the Governing Body meeting at which designation is approved. |
| 6.2.3 | Governing Body Chair | Execute the Designation and Authority Letter (Appendix A) and provide a signed copy to: (a) the Compliance Officer; (b) the Administrator; (c) the governance file. | Within 7 calendar days of Governing Body vote. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Complete any required orientation to agency operations, the existing compliance program, and current regulatory requirements. | Within 30 calendar days of designation. |
| 6.2.5 | Compliance Officer | Conduct OIG/SAM exclusion screening on own name at designation and submit results to Governing Body Chair. | At designation; monthly thereafter. |

### 6.3 Authority and Responsibilities

| Authority/Responsibility | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Policy authority | Authority to draft, revise, and recommend approval of all CO-domain policies. |
| Investigation authority | Authority to initiate, conduct, or commission investigations of any compliance concern without prior approval from the Administrator. |
| Records access | Unrestricted access to all agency records, files, systems, and personnel necessary to conduct compliance functions, subject to applicable law. |
| Reporting access | Direct, unfiltered access to the Governing Body — may request a special Governing Body meeting at any time for matters of significant compliance concern. |
| Corrective action authority | Authority to direct implementation of compliance-related corrective action plans in coordination with the Administrator. |
| External reporting authority | Authority to consult legal counsel and, in consultation with the Governing Body, engage with OIG, CMS, or other regulatory bodies on compliance matters. |
| Staff interview authority | Authority to conduct confidential interviews of any workforce member in furtherance of compliance investigations or audits. |

### 6.4 Vacancy Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Administrator | Notify all Governing Body members in writing within 48 hours of a Compliance Officer vacancy. | Within 48 hours of vacancy. |
| 6.4.2 | Governing Body | Designate an interim Compliance Officer in writing with full authority. The interim may not be the Administrator. | Within 14 calendar days of vacancy. |
| 6.4.3 | Governing Body | Initiate recruitment and selection process for permanent Compliance Officer. | Immediately upon vacancy; permanent appointment within 90 calendar days. |
| 6.4.4 | Governing Body Chair | Execute a new Designation and Authority Letter upon permanent appointment. | Within 7 calendar days of permanent appointment vote. |

### 6.5 Annual Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Governing Body | Conduct or commission an annual performance evaluation of the Compliance Officer in executive session. Evaluation must address: (a) Program effectiveness metrics from CO-CP-001; (b) audit completion rates; (c) training completion rates; (d) investigation timeliness; (e) reporting quality. | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of end of each fiscal year. |
| 6.5.2 | Governing Body Chair | Document evaluation findings and any directives in executive session minutes. | At time of evaluation. |

| Interim designation | Written designation of interim CO with authority granted. | Governing Body | Governance file. | Within 14 days of vacancy; retained 7 years. |
| Monthly exclusion screening | OIG/SAM screening documentation for CO. | Compliance Officer / HR Director | Compliance file. | Monthly; retained 7 years. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compliance Officer is designated and documented. | Review of Governing Body minutes and Appendix A letter. | Current designation on file at all times; Appendix A letter executed. |
| No vacancy exceeds 30 days without interim designee. | Review of vacancy notification and interim designation dates. | 100% compliance; interim appointed within 14 days of vacancy. |
| Compliance Officer has direct Governing Body reporting line. | Review of Designation and Authority Letter; Governing Body meeting minutes. | Documented direct reporting line in Appendix A. |
| Compliance Officer conflict of interest is absent or managed. | Review of CO's Conflict of Interest Disclosure Form. | Annual COI disclosure current; no unmanaged conflicts. |
| Annual evaluation is conducted. | Review of executive session minutes. | Evaluation completed within 60 days of fiscal year end each year. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the structure, composition, responsibilities, meeting requirements, and documentation standards for the Compliance Committee of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Compliance Committee is the multi-disciplinary operational body that supports the Compliance Officer in implementing, monitoring, and evaluating the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001). The Committee provides the mechanism by which compliance risk, audit findings, regulatory changes, and corrective actions are reviewed at a cross-functional level and escalated to the Governing Body as appropriate.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all Compliance Committee members, all departments represented on the Committee, and all senior leadership personnel whose operational decisions affect the agency's compliance posture.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a functioning Compliance Committee, chaired by the Compliance Officer.
4.2 The Compliance Committee shall meet at minimum quarterly and shall maintain formal meeting minutes.
4.3 The Compliance Committee shall serve as the primary operational body for reviewing audit findings, monitoring corrective actions, evaluating training compliance, and preparing compliance reports to the Governing Body.
4.4 The Compliance Committee shall not have authority to override Governing Body directives or the Compliance Officer's independent compliance determinations.
4.5 Attendance at Compliance Committee meetings is a professional obligation for all designated members. Absence without advance notice and a designated alternate is not acceptable.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Committee | The multi-disciplinary body chaired by the Compliance Officer that provides operational oversight of the Corporate Compliance Program. |
| Quorum | A majority of standing Committee members must be present to conduct official business. |
| Compliance Risk | Any identified area of agency operations where regulatory violation, FWA exposure, billing error, clinical documentation deficiency, or privacy breach could occur. |
| Corrective Action Plan (CAP) | A documented plan with specific actions, responsible parties, and deadlines to remediate an identified compliance deficiency. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Committee Composition

| Standing Member | Role on Committee | Alternate Required? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compliance Officer | Chair | Yes — designated in writing |
| Administrator | Member | Yes |
| Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager | Member | Yes (Clinical Designee) |
| Revenue Cycle Director / CFO | Member | Yes |
| HR Director | Member | Yes |
| Risk Manager | Member | Yes |
| QAPI Coordinator | Member | Yes |
| IT Director / CISO | Member (may attend via video) | Yes |

Ad hoc members may be invited at the Chair's discretion for specific agenda items. Ad hoc members are not standing members and do not count toward quorum.
### 6.2 Committee Standing Agenda Items
Every Compliance Committee meeting shall include the following standing agenda items:

| # | Standing Agenda Item | Presenter | Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Approval of prior meeting minutes | Chair | Minutes |
| 2 | Compliance Officer report (hotline, investigations update, regulatory changes) | Compliance Officer | Written report |
| 3 | Audit findings update (current period) | Compliance Officer / Auditor | Audit summary |
| 4 | Corrective action plan status review | CAP owners | CAP tracking log |
| 5 | Training completion rate report | Compliance Officer / HR | Training log summary |
| 6 | Exclusion screening status | Compliance Officer | Screening log |
| 7 | QAPI linkage items | QAPI Coordinator | QAPI report excerpt |
| 8 | Financial compliance indicators | Revenue Cycle Director | Revenue cycle summary |
| 9 | Regulatory change notifications | Compliance Officer | Regulatory update memo |
