## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the Code of Conduct and Ethics ("Code") of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Code defines the ethical standards, behavioral expectations, legal obligations, and prohibited conduct applicable to every individual who works for or on behalf of the agency. The Code is a foundational element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and reflects the agency's commitment to conducting all operations with honesty, integrity, and respect for patients, employees, referral partners, and payers.
## 3. Scope
This Code applies without exception to:
All Governing Body members
The Administrator and all senior leadership
All full-time, part-time, per diem, and contracted employees
All volunteers
All vendors, business associates, and contractors acting on behalf of the agency
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every individual within the scope of this policy shall conduct themselves in accordance with the standards of this Code at all times, whether on or off agency premises, when representing the agency in any capacity.
4.2 Adherence to this Code is a condition of employment or contract with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Violations are subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination or contract cancellation.
4.3 No one in a position of authority — including the Administrator or Governing Body members — may authorize conduct that violates this Code, applicable law, or regulation.
4.4 All workforce members have the affirmative obligation to report known or suspected violations of this Code through the mechanisms established in policy CO-CP-006.
4.5 No individual shall be retaliated against for good-faith reporting of a Code violation, per policy CO-CP-005.
## 5. Core Standards of Conduct
### 5.1 Patient-Centered Care and Dignity
All workforce members shall:
Treat every patient with dignity, respect, and compassion regardless of diagnosis, age, race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, or ability to pay.
Protect patient privacy and confidentiality at all times per policies CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002.
Honor patient rights as defined in policy CL-PR-001.
Never exploit, abuse, neglect, or mistreat a patient. All suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation shall be reported immediately per policies CL-PR-006 and HR-ER-009.
Provide only services that are ordered, medically necessary, and within their scope of practice.
### 5.2 Integrity in Billing and Documentation
All workforce members shall:
Document clinical services accurately, completely, and truthfully.
Never document services not actually rendered, alter clinical records to support billing, or fail to document care that was provided.
Never submit or participate in the submission of a false claim to Medicare, Medicaid, or any other payer.
Report suspected billing irregularities or documentation falsification through CO-CP-006.
### 5.3 Conflict of Interest
All workforce members shall:
Disclose any personal, financial, or professional interest that could conflict with the agency's interests or their professional obligations.
Never allow a conflict of interest to influence a patient care decision, business decision, or compliance determination.
Governing Body members shall comply with the full conflict of interest management requirements of policy GV-GB-003.
### 5.4 Gifts, Gratuities, and Kickbacks
All workforce members shall:
Never accept or offer gifts, meals, entertainment, or gratuities that exceed $25 per occurrence or $50 annually from any patient, vendor, referral source, or competitor.
Never offer, pay, solicit, or receive anything of value in exchange for patient referrals, in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b).
Report any solicitation of a kickback or improper referral arrangement immediately to the Compliance Officer.
### 5.5 Confidentiality and Privacy
All workforce members shall:
Never access, use, or disclose patient health information beyond the minimum necessary for their assigned duties.
Never discuss patient information in non-private settings (hallways, vehicles, social settings).
Never share login credentials, access patient records on behalf of another, or circumvent system access controls.
Report any known or suspected breach of patient information per policy CO-HP-003.
### 5.6 Workplace Respect and Anti-Harassment
All workforce members shall:
Treat colleagues, supervisors, and subordinates with respect and professionalism at all times.
Never engage in harassment, discrimination, or hostile conduct based on any protected characteristic.
Report harassment or discrimination per policy HR-ER-004.
### 5.7 Compliance with Laws and Regulations
All workforce members shall:
Comply with all applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and agency policies relevant to their role.
Never perform, authorize, or conceal any act that they know or reasonably believe violates applicable law.
Cooperate fully with all internal compliance audits and investigations.
### 5.8 Stewardship of Agency Resources
All workforce members shall:
Use agency resources (equipment, supplies, technology, time) only for legitimate agency business purposes.
Never misappropriate, steal, or misuse agency property.
Report waste, misuse, or misappropriation of agency resources through CO-CP-006.
### 5.9 Social Media and Public Communications
All workforce members shall:
Never post patient information, clinical photographs, or identifiable patient details on any social media platform.
Never make public statements that misrepresent the agency's services, credentials, or compliance status.
Comply with policy IT-UP-003 for all social media and public communications.
## 6. Reporting Violations
6.1 All workforce members have an affirmative obligation to report suspected violations of this Code, applicable law, or agency policy.
6.2 Reports may be made through any of the following mechanisms (per policy CO-CP-006):
Direct contact with the Compliance Officer
Agency compliance hotline (anonymous option available)
Direct contact with the Governing Body Chair (for matters involving the Compliance Officer or Administrator)
6.3 Reports may be made anonymously. Anonymous reports will be investigated to the extent practicable given the information provided.
6.4 No individual will be retaliated against for making a good-faith compliance report, per policy CO-CP-005.
## 7. Consequences of Violations

| Severity Level | Examples | Potential Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 — Minor | Unintentional policy deviation; minor documentation error (without billing impact); failure to attend required training by deadline. | Documented counseling; mandatory retraining; corrective action plan. |
| Level 2 — Moderate | Repeated policy violations; unauthorized PHI disclosure; gift acceptance above threshold; failure to report a known violation. | Written warning; performance improvement plan; suspension; retraining. |
| Level 3 — Serious | Fraudulent billing; falsification of records; patient abuse or neglect; kickback participation; retaliation against a reporter; intentional HIPAA violation. | Immediate suspension pending investigation; termination; regulatory reporting; referral for civil or criminal prosecution. |

Discipline shall be applied consistently regardless of seniority, role, or tenure. The Administrator shall be notified of all Level 2 and Level 3 violations within 24 hours. The Governing Body shall be notified of all Level 3 violations within 24 hours.
## 8. Procedures — Acknowledgment and Distribution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 8.2 | All workforce members | Read the Code and sign the Policy Acknowledgment and Code of Conduct Attestation (Appendix A). | Within 14 days of hire or revision. |
| 8.3 | Compliance Officer | Maintain attestation records and report completion rates to the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |
| 8.4 | Compliance Officer | Post the Code (or an accessible summary) in a location visible to all agency staff and patients. | Continuously. |
| 8.5 | Compliance Officer | Review the Code annually and present any recommended revisions to the Governing Body for approval. | Annually at Q1 meeting. |

# CO-CP-005 — Whistleblower Protection & Non-Retaliation
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CO-CP-005 |
| Policy Title | Whistleblower Protection & Non-Retaliation |
| Domain | CO — Compliance & Regulatory |
| Subdomain | CP — Compliance Program |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Compliance Officer |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the protections afforded to individuals who, in good faith, report suspected violations of law, regulation, agency policy, or the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004), and prohibits retaliation of any kind against such individuals. Effective compliance programs depend on a workforce that feels safe reporting concerns. This policy provides the legal and operational framework for non-retaliation consistent with the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. § 3730), applicable California whistleblower statutes (California Labor Code § 1102.5), and OIG Compliance Program Guidance.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., including Governing Body members, the Administrator, all employees, contractors, volunteers, and business associates. It applies to all reports of suspected violations, regardless of whether the report ultimately results in a finding of wrongdoing.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. strictly prohibits retaliation of any form against any individual who, in good faith, reports a suspected compliance violation, cooperates with a compliance investigation, or refuses to participate in conduct they reasonably believe violates law or agency policy.
4.2 Retaliation is defined broadly and includes but is not limited to: termination, demotion, suspension, reduction in hours or pay, reassignment, harassment, intimidation, exclusion from meetings, negative performance evaluations influenced by the report, or any other adverse employment or contractual action.
4.3 The protection of this policy applies to all good-faith reporters regardless of whether the reported concern is ultimately substantiated.
4.4 An individual who knowingly makes a false or malicious report with the intent to harm another individual or the agency is not protected by this policy and is subject to disciplinary action per CO-CP-004.
4.5 The Governing Body shall be directly notified of any alleged retaliation against a reporter within 24 hours of the allegation. The Compliance Officer may not serve as the sole investigator if they are the subject of the retaliation allegation.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Whistleblower | Any individual who reports, in good faith, a suspected violation of law, regulation, or agency policy, including suspected fraud, waste, abuse, patient harm, privacy breach, or Code of Conduct violation. |
| Good Faith | A sincere belief, based on reasonable information available to the reporter at the time, that a violation may have occurred or is occurring. |
| Retaliation | Any adverse action taken against an individual because they made a good-faith compliance report, participated in an investigation, or refused to participate in unlawful conduct. |
| False Claims Act (FCA) qui tam provision | The federal law provision (31 U.S.C. § 3730(h)) that specifically prohibits retaliation against employees who take action in furtherance of a False Claims Act lawsuit. |
| California Labor Code § 1102.5 | California state law prohibiting employer retaliation against employees who disclose information about suspected legal violations to government agencies or internal compliance authorities. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 How to Make a Protected Report

| Method | Contact | Anonymity Available? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct report to Compliance Officer | [Compliance Officer contact maintained in agency directory] | No (but confidentiality maintained) |
| Compliance Hotline | [Hotline number maintained in agency directory per CO-CP-006] | Yes |
| Anonymous written report | Submitted per CO-CP-006 instructions | Yes |
| Direct report to Governing Body Chair | [Governing Body Chair contact per GV-GB-001 roster] | No (but confidentiality maintained) |
| External report to OIG Hotline | 1-800-HHS-TIPS (1-800-447-8477) | Yes |
| External report to California DHCS | Per DHCS complaint process | Variable |

### 6.2 Confidentiality of Reporter Identity

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Maintain strict confidentiality of reporter identity to the maximum extent practicable. Disclose identity only if: (a) the reporter consents; (b) disclosure is required by law or legal proceedings; (c) disclosure is unavoidable due to the nature of the investigation. | Continuously throughout investigation. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Notify the reporter (if known) before disclosing their identity in any proceeding and provide an explanation of why disclosure is necessary. | Before any disclosure. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Document all disclosures of reporter identity, the justification, and any consent obtained. | At time of disclosure. |

### 6.3 Non-Retaliation Enforcement

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon receipt of an allegation of retaliation, open a formal retaliation investigation within 5 calendar days, separate from any underlying compliance investigation. | Within 5 calendar days of allegation. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Notify the Governing Body Chair in writing within 24 hours of receiving a retaliation allegation. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | If the Compliance Officer is the subject of the retaliation allegation, the Governing Body Chair shall designate an independent investigator (may be external legal counsel or independent HR professional). | Within 5 calendar days of allegation. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer / Investigator | Conduct retaliation investigation per CO-CP-007 standards. Interview the reporter, the alleged retaliator, and relevant witnesses. Document all findings. | Within 30 calendar days of initiation. |
| 6.3.5 | Governing Body / Administrator | If retaliation is substantiated, impose disciplinary action per CO-CP-004 severity scale, up to and including immediate termination. Any substantiated retaliatory termination shall be subject to an offer of reinstatement with back pay. | Upon conclusion of investigation. |
| 6.3.6 | Compliance Officer | Document investigation findings, disciplinary action, and corrective measures. Report to Governing Body at next quarterly meeting. | At meeting following investigation conclusion. |

### 6.4 Workforce Communication of Rights

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Administrator | Ensure all workforce members are informed of their whistleblower rights at hire (via orientation) and annually (via compliance training per CO-CP-008). | At hire; annually. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Post the Non-Retaliation Notice (Appendix A) in a visible location accessible to all workforce members, including break rooms, common areas, and the agency intranet. | Continuously. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Include whistleblower rights and reporting mechanisms in the annual compliance training curriculum per CO-CP-008. | Annually. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Retaliation investigations | Written investigation file per CO-CP-007 standards. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file (confidential). | Retained 7 years minimum or per litigation hold. |
| Retaliation notifications to Governing Body | Written notification within 24 hours. | Compliance Officer | Governance file. | Retained 7 years. |
| Non-Retaliation Notice posting | Evidence of posting locations (photo or log). | Compliance Officer | Compliance file. | Updated annually. |
| Workforce notification at hire | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B). | Administrator / HR Director | Personnel file. | At hire; retained 7 years. |
| Annual training records | Documentation of whistleblower training completion. | Compliance Officer / HR Director | Training records. | Annually; retained 7 years. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement

| --- | --- | --- |
| Non-Retaliation Notice is posted and accessible. | Physical and intranet review. | Posted in all required locations continuously. |
| All retaliation allegations investigated within 5 days. | Review of investigation log with initiation dates. | 100% initiated within 5 calendar days. |
| No substantiated retaliation goes undisciplined. | Review of investigation outcomes and disciplinary records. | 100% of substantiated retaliation results in documented disciplinary action. |
| Workforce trained on whistleblower rights annually. | Training completion records. | 95% completion within 30 days of annual training deadline. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the multiple accessible mechanisms through which any workforce member, patient, family member, vendor, or business associate may report suspected compliance violations, fraud, waste, or abuse to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The existence of accessible, well-publicized reporting mechanisms is a required element of the Corporate Compliance Program under OIG guidance. Effective reporting channels are essential to the agency's ability to detect, investigate, and correct compliance violations promptly.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all individuals who interact with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. — including workforce members, patients, family members, vendors, business associates, and members of the public who have reason to report a compliance concern.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain multiple accessible reporting mechanisms at all times, including at minimum: a compliance hotline (with anonymous option), a direct email to the Compliance Officer, and a physical mailbox.
4.2 All reporting mechanisms shall be publicized to all workforce members at hire, in annual training, and through posted notices in accessible locations.
4.3 All reports received through any mechanism shall be logged, assigned a tracking number, and responded to within the timeframes established in this policy.
4.4 Anonymous reports shall be accepted and investigated to the extent practicable given the information provided. The agency shall not attempt to identify anonymous reporters.
4.5 No individual who makes a good-faith report through any mechanism shall be retaliated against, per policy CO-CP-005.
4.6 Reports involving the Compliance Officer shall be directed to the Governing Body Chair. Reports involving the Administrator shall be directed to the Compliance Officer and Governing Body Chair simultaneously.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Hotline | A dedicated telephone line (or third-party service) for receiving compliance reports, available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, with an anonymous option. |
| Report Tracking Number | A unique identifier assigned to each compliance report upon receipt, used to track the status of investigation and resolution. |
| Substantiated Report | A report in which the investigation finds that the reported concern is supported by sufficient evidence to conclude that a violation occurred. |
| Unsubstantiated Report | A report in which the investigation does not find sufficient evidence to support the reported concern. Unsubstantiated reports are closed with documentation; reporters are not penalized. |
| Anonymous Report | A report submitted without the reporter identifying themselves. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Available Reporting Mechanisms

| Mechanism | Access Method | Availability | Anonymous Option | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compliance Hotline | [Phone number — maintained in agency directory] | 24/7 — voicemail if unanswered | Yes | Urgent reports; preferred anonymous channel |
| Direct Email to Compliance Officer | [Email — maintained in agency directory] | Business hours response; monitored daily | No (email traced) | Non-urgent reports; providing documentation |
| Physical Compliance Mailbox | Located at agency main office — marked "COMPLIANCE — CONFIDENTIAL" | Drop-in during office hours | Yes | Written reports; document submission |
| Direct Contact — Compliance Officer | [Contact — maintained in agency directory] | Business hours | No | In-person discussion |
| Governing Body Chair (for reports involving CO or Administrator) | [Contact per GV-GB-001 Appendix A roster] | Business hours | No | Leadership-level concerns |
| External — OIG Hotline | 1-800-HHS-TIPS (1-800-447-8477) | 24/7 | Yes | Reports involving Medicare fraud |
| External — California DHCS | [DHCS Complaint Line] | Business hours | Variable | California state regulatory concerns |
| External — CMS | [1-800-MEDICARE] | 24/7 | Yes | Medicare program concerns |

### 6.2 Report Receipt and Logging

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer (or designee) | Log every report received through any channel in the Compliance Report Log (Appendix A) within 1 business day of receipt. Assign a unique tracking number to each report. | Within 1 business day. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Acknowledge receipt of non-anonymous reports within 5 business days. Anonymous hotline reports: no acknowledgment (to protect anonymity). | Within 5 business days. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct initial triage of the report to determine: (a) urgency (immediate patient safety risk vs. standard investigation); (b) whether interim protective action is required pending investigation; (c) referral to appropriate investigation process per CO-CP-007. | Within 5 business days of receipt. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | For reports involving immediate patient safety: notify the Administrator and Director of Nursing within 2 hours and initiate emergency response as required. | Within 2 hours of identification of immediate patient safety risk. |

### 6.3 Hotline Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer | Check the compliance hotline voicemail (or third-party hotline system) no less than once every business day. | Daily on business days. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | If a third-party hotline service is used, ensure the service meets the following requirements: (a) available 24/7; (b) anonymous option; (c) reports delivered to Compliance Officer within 24 hours; (d) Business Associate Agreement in place per CO-HP-005. | Prior to activation; reviewed annually. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Test the hotline by conducting an anonymous test call at least quarterly to verify functionality. Document test results. | Quarterly. |

### 6.4 Feedback to Reporters

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Provide non-anonymous reporters a status update acknowledging that the investigation is in progress. | Within 30 calendar days of report receipt. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Notify non-anonymous reporters when the investigation is closed and whether the report was substantiated or unsubstantiated. Specific findings are not disclosed if confidentiality of others would be compromised. | Within 7 days of investigation close. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | For reports that result in corrective action, notify the reporter (if non-anonymous) that corrective action has been taken (without disclosing confidential details of personnel actions). | Within 7 days of corrective action implementation. |

### 6.5 Publicizing Reporting Mechanisms

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Administrator | Distribute reporting mechanism information to all workforce members at hire. | At hire. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Maintain posted Non-Retaliation Notice (CO-CP-005 Appendix A) with hotline and reporting contact information in accessible areas throughout the agency. | Continuously. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Include reporting mechanisms in the annual compliance training per CO-CP-008. | Annually. |
| 6.5.4 | Compliance Officer | Post reporting mechanism information on the agency intranet or shared drive accessible to all workforce members. | Continuously; updated within 5 days of any change. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standardized process for initiating, conducting, documenting, and closing compliance investigations at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A structured, consistent investigation process is essential to ensure that reported concerns are addressed promptly, that evidence is properly preserved and assessed, that confidentiality is maintained, that corrective action is implemented where warranted, and that the agency fulfills its obligations under the False Claims Act, OIG guidance, and applicable federal and state law.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All compliance investigations initiated under the reporting mechanisms of CO-CP-006
All self-identified compliance concerns identified through internal auditing (CO-RA-002)
All retaliation investigations under CO-CP-005
All investigations directed by the Governing Body
All investigations of potential fraud, waste, or abuse under CO-FA-003
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every compliance report or self-identified concern shall be evaluated for investigation within 5 business days of receipt.
4.2 Formal investigations shall be initiated within 7 calendar days of receipt of a compliance report that, upon triage, warrants investigation.
4.3 All compliance investigations shall be documented in writing from initiation through closure.
4.4 All investigation records are confidential compliance documents. Access shall be restricted to the Compliance Officer, legal counsel (when engaged), and the Governing Body.
4.5 The Compliance Officer shall preserve investigation records under a litigation hold protocol if there is any indication that civil or criminal proceedings may arise from the subject matter.
4.6 The agency shall cooperate fully and promptly with any government investigation. All document requests or inquiries from government agencies shall be immediately routed to the Compliance Officer and legal counsel.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Investigation | A structured, documented inquiry into a reported or self-identified compliance concern to determine whether a violation occurred, its scope, its cause, and the appropriate remedial response. |
| Investigator | The Compliance Officer or designee appointed to conduct the investigation. Must be independent of the subject matter and individuals under review. |
| Investigation File | The complete documentation package for an investigation including the opening memo, evidence collected, interview notes, findings memo, and closure documentation. |
| Litigation Hold | A directive to preserve all records, communications, and data that may be relevant to anticipated or active legal proceedings. |
| Voluntary Disclosure | The proactive disclosure of a confirmed compliance violation to a federal or state regulatory agency. May mitigate penalties if conducted promptly and in good faith. |
| Overpayment | Any funds received from Medicare, Medicaid, or another payer to which the agency is not entitled. Must be reported and refunded within 60 days of identification per the False Claims Act. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Investigation Initiation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon receiving a report (via CO-CP-006) or self-identifying a compliance concern, complete the Initial Triage Assessment (Appendix A) within 5 business days. | Within 5 business days of receipt. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Based on triage, classify the concern as: (a) Requires Formal Investigation — credible allegation of violation; (b) Administrative Review — policy question or minor deviation; (c) No Action Required — report not credible or not a violation; (d) Referral — matter outside agency jurisdiction (e.g., patient abuse requiring mandatory reporting). Document triage decision with rationale. | Within 5 business days. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | For matters classified as Requires Formal Investigation: open a formal investigation file, assign a tracking number (linked to CO-CP-006 log), designate the investigator, and prepare an Investigation Opening Memorandum (Appendix B). | Within 7 calendar days of report receipt. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Notify the Governing Body Chair in writing of investigations involving: (a) fraud, waste, or abuse; (b) Level 3 Code of Conduct violations; (c) potential False Claims Act exposure; (d) patient harm. | Within 24 hours of opening Level 3 investigations; at next quarterly meeting for others. |
| 6.1.5 | Compliance Officer | Determine whether an interim protective measure is needed pending investigation conclusion (e.g., temporary reassignment of an employee under review, suspension of a billing function, interim clinical oversight enhancement). Document the determination with rationale. | Within 5 business days of investigation opening. |

### 6.2 Evidence Collection

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Investigator | Identify and collect all relevant evidence including: (a) clinical records; (b) billing records; (c) scheduling records; (d) email and electronic communications; (e) system audit logs; (f) personnel records (if applicable). | Within 10 business days of investigation opening. |
| 6.2.2 | Investigator | Preserve all original evidence. Do not alter, destroy, or allow access to evidence under review. If litigation hold is applicable, issue written hold notice to all custodians of relevant records. | Immediately upon opening investigation. |
| 6.2.3 | Investigator | Conduct confidential interviews of relevant witnesses. Notify each interviewee that: (a) the interview is confidential; (b) their supervisor may not be present; (c) they may have HR representation if subject to potential discipline; (d) retaliation for participating is prohibited. Document interview notes contemporaneously (Appendix C). | Within 14 business days of investigation opening. |
| 6.2.4 | Investigator | Where applicable, engage external subject matter experts (e.g., coding auditor, legal counsel, clinical expert) if the investigation requires specialized expertise. | As needed; no later than 10 business days of opening. |

### 6.3 Investigation Analysis and Findings

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Investigator | Analyze all evidence against the applicable regulatory standard, policy requirement, or Code of Conduct provision. Prepare a written Findings Memorandum (Appendix D) that documents: (a) the allegation or concern; (b) evidence reviewed; (c) findings (substantiated/unsubstantiated); (d) root cause (if applicable); (e) financial exposure (if applicable). | Within 30 calendar days of investigation opening for standard matters; within 14 days for expedited/urgent matters. |
| 6.3.2 | Compliance Officer | Review and approve the Findings Memorandum. Consult legal counsel if: (a) the matter may involve mandatory government disclosure; (b) there is potential civil or criminal exposure; (c) the matter involves a False Claims Act violation and potential 60-day repayment obligation. | Within 5 business days of Investigator submission. |

### 6.4 Corrective Action

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | For substantiated investigations: develop a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) per policy QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days of the Findings Memorandum approval. The CAP must address: (a) root cause; (b) immediate corrective measures; (c) systemic process improvements; (d) responsible parties; (e) deadlines; (f) monitoring metrics. | Within 14 calendar days of Findings Memorandum approval. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer / HR Director | For substantiated investigations involving individual employee misconduct: recommend disciplinary action per CO-CP-004 severity scale and HR-ER-002 progressive discipline policy. | Within 5 business days of Findings Memorandum approval. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | For substantiated overpayment identification: initiate refund process per FN-BC-004 and track against the 60-day repayment deadline. | Immediately upon identification of overpayment. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | For matters requiring voluntary disclosure: engage legal counsel and present recommendation to Governing Body. | Within 30 calendar days of Findings Memorandum approval. |

### 6.5 Investigation Closure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Prepare an Investigation Closure Memorandum (Appendix E) upon: (a) completion of investigation and CAP implementation; (b) determination of no further action required; (c) referral to external authority. | Within 7 days of CAP confirmation or determination of no action. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Update the Compliance Report Log (CO-CP-006 Appendix A) with investigation outcome and closure date. | Within 1 business day of closure. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Notify non-anonymous reporters of investigation closure and outcome (without disclosing confidential details) per CO-CP-006 Section 6.4. | Within 7 days of closure. |
| 6.5.4 | Compliance Officer | Present investigation summary (without identifying details) to the Compliance Committee at the next regular meeting and to the Governing Body in the quarterly compliance report. | At next quarterly meeting. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial Triage Assessment | Appendix A form for every report evaluated. | Compliance Officer | Investigation file (confidential). | Within 5 business days; retained 7 years. |
| Investigation Opening Memorandum | Appendix B. | Compliance Officer | Investigation file. | Within 7 calendar days of report receipt; retained 7 years. |
| Evidence log | Log of all evidence collected with chain of custody notation. | Investigator | Investigation file. | Maintained throughout investigation; retained 7 years or per litigation hold. |
| Interview notes | Contemporaneous notes per Appendix C. | Investigator | Investigation file (confidential). | Retained 7 years or per litigation hold. |
| Findings Memorandum | Appendix D. | Investigator / Compliance Officer | Investigation file. | Retained 7 years or per litigation hold. |
| Corrective Action Plan | Per QA-AE-003 template. | Compliance Officer | Investigation file; CAP tracking log. | Retained 7 years. |
| Investigation Closure Memorandum | Appendix E. | Compliance Officer | Investigation file. | Retained 7 years. |
| Compliance Report Log | Updated per CO-CP-006 Appendix A. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file. | Updated within 1 business day of closure. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All reports triaged within 5 business days. | Review of triage date in CO-CP-006 log. | 100% triaged within 5 business days. |
| Formal investigations initiated within 7 calendar days. | Review of Opening Memorandum dates. | 100% initiated within 7 calendar days. |
| Findings Memoranda completed within 30 days (standard). | Review of memorandum completion dates. | 90% completed within 30 days; 100% within 45 days. |
| Overpayments refunded within 60 days. | Review of refund documentation and ID dates. | 100% compliance with 60-day rule. |
| All investigations have complete written files. | Compliance file audit. | 100% of investigations have complete documentation. |

## 2. Purpose
This policy mandates initial and ongoing compliance training and education for all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective compliance training is a foundational element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and is required by OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies. Training ensures that all workforce members understand their individual compliance obligations, the agency's standards of conduct, applicable laws and regulations, reporting mechanisms, and the consequences of non-compliance.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. including Governing Body members, the Administrator, all clinical and administrative employees, contractors, per diem staff, and volunteers. Role-specific training requirements are defined in Section 6.3.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All workforce members shall complete compliance orientation training within 14 calendar days of hire or contract commencement.
4.2 All workforce members shall complete annual compliance refresher training within 30 calendar days of the start of each calendar year.
4.3 Completion of required compliance training is a condition of continued employment or contract. Failure to complete training within the required timeframe shall result in escalation per Section 6.5.
4.4 Training shall be delivered in a manner and language accessible to all workforce members. The agency shall provide interpreter assistance for workforce members with limited English proficiency upon request.
4.5 All training completions shall be documented with the workforce member's name, role, training module, completion date, and assessment score (if applicable).
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Orientation Training | The initial compliance training completed by all new workforce members within 14 calendar days of hire covering the foundational elements of the Corporate Compliance Program. |
| Annual Compliance Refresher Training | The recurring annual training required of all workforce members to maintain awareness of compliance obligations, regulatory updates, and agency policy changes. |
| Role-Specific Training | Compliance training modules targeted to specific workforce roles addressing regulatory requirements most relevant to that role's functions. |
| Competency Assessment | A post-training evaluation (quiz, skills demonstration, or attestation) confirming the workforce member's comprehension of training content. |
| Training Completion Rate | The percentage of workforce members required to complete a specific training module who have done so by the specified deadline. |

## 2. Purpose

This policy establishes Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.'s obligations and operational procedures under the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA), California Civil Code §§56–56.37. The CMIA imposes requirements upon healthcare providers operating in California that are legally distinct from, and in many respects more stringent than, the federal HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart E). This policy supplements but does not replace CO-HP-001 (HIPAA Privacy Program). Where CMIA and HIPAA requirements conflict, the more protective standard shall govern, consistent with California law.

The primary purposes of this policy are to:
- Define the specific protected categories of medical information under CMIA that require heightened authorization standards beyond HIPAA;
- Establish authorization, disclosure, and access procedures for CMIA-protected information;
- Identify the $1,000 nominal damages exposure and actual damages liability for any unauthorized disclosure under Civil Code §56.36;
- Ensure staff understand the distinction between CMIA authorization requirements and HIPAA authorization requirements;
- Satisfy the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) and HCAI survey expectations for California-licensed home health agencies.

---

## 3. Scope

This policy applies to:

* All employees, contractors, volunteers, and students of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
* All Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined by HIPAA, interpreted through the additional lens of CMIA's definition of "medical information" (Civil Code §56.05(j))
* All patient records, including paper, electronic (EHR), audio, video, and any other medium
* All workforce members who create, receive, maintain, transmit, access, or destroy records containing medical information about current, former, or prospective patients
* Business Associates and agents acting on behalf of the agency where CMIA obligations transfer

This policy does not displace or reduce any HIPAA privacy obligation. Both frameworks apply simultaneously.

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| CMIA | California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act, California Civil Code §§56–56.37. California's primary medical privacy statute for healthcare providers, insurers, and employers. |
| Medical Information (CMIA) | Any individually identifiable information, in electronic or physical form, in possession of or derived from a provider of health care, health care service plan, pharmaceutical company, or contractor regarding a patient's medical history, mental or physical condition, or treatment. (Civil Code §56.05(j)) |
| Provider of Health Care | A licensed professional of the healing arts or any clinic, health dispensary, or health facility that is licensed, or health care service plan licensed, under applicable licensing laws. Home health agencies licensed under California Health & Safety Code §1726 are providers of health care under CMIA. |
| Authorization (CMIA) | A specific written permission by the patient (or authorized representative) that meets the requirements of Civil Code §56.11. CMIA authorizations must be separate from HIPAA authorizations unless the document meets all requirements of both laws. |
| Sensitive Category Information | Medical information in categories afforded heightened protection under CMIA beyond the federal standard: (1) mental health and psychiatric records; (2) substance use disorder records; (3) HIV/AIDS status and test results; (4) genetic information; (5) reproductive health information; (6) sexual assault and domestic violence records; (7) sexually transmitted infection records. |
| Nominal Damages | Civil Code §56.36(b) awards $1,000 per violation regardless of whether actual harm is proven, in addition to actual damages, attorney fees, and costs. |
| Confidentiality Statement | The written statement required by Civil Code §56.10 that patients have certain rights over their medical information and describing how information may be disclosed. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall comply fully with the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (Civil Code §§56–56.37) for all medical information of patients served in California, in addition to all applicable HIPAA requirements under CO-HP-001 through CO-HP-007.

5.2 The agency shall apply CMIA's heightened protection standards to Sensitive Category Information. Disclosure of Sensitive Category Information (as defined in Section 4) requires a valid CMIA-compliant authorization that includes all elements specified in Civil Code §56.11, even in circumstances where HIPAA would permit disclosure without authorization.

5.3 The agency shall not require any patient to authorize the disclosure of medical information as a condition of receiving treatment, except as specifically permitted by CMIA (Civil Code §56.17 — insurance verification, workers' compensation, and similar specific exceptions).

5.4 The agency shall not disclose medical information for purposes other than treatment, payment, and healthcare operations without a valid CMIA authorization, except where Civil Code §56.10(b) or (c) provides a permitted exception. Permitted disclosures must be documented in the patient's record.

5.5 All authorizations obtained by the agency for release of medical information shall meet the requirements of Civil Code §56.11 (patient/patient's representative signature, description of information, identification of recipient, purpose, expiration date, right to revoke) and, where applicable, HIPAA authorization requirements (45 CFR §164.508).

5.6 For Sensitive Category Information, the agency shall provide specific disclosure guidance to workforce members identifying which disclosures require an authorization vs. a permitted exception, and shall not rely solely on HIPAA guidance for those categories.

5.7 Any unauthorized disclosure of a patient's medical information shall be reported to the Compliance Officer within 24 hours of discovery. The Compliance Officer shall assess whether the disclosure constitutes a HIPAA breach (CO-HP-003) AND/OR a CMIA violation requiring separate notification and potential response.

5.8 The agency shall maintain a Confidentiality Statement available to all patients describing their rights under both HIPAA and CMIA, updated to reflect any legislative changes within 90 calendar days of the effective date of any such change.

5.9 Workforce members shall receive CMIA-specific training at orientation and no less than annually thereafter, covering the differences between HIPAA and CMIA requirements.

5.10 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all Compliance Office and clinical leadership staff within 14 calendar days.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 CMIA Authorization Processing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Patient Intake / Clinical Staff | Upon intake, provide the patient with: (a) HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices (CO-HP-001); (b) Agency CMIA Confidentiality Statement identifying California-specific rights; (c) explanation that certain categories of information receive heightened protection under California law. Obtain patient acknowledgment. | At or before first billable visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Clinical Staff / Compliance Officer | Before disclosing any medical information upon request, determine whether the request falls within a CMIA permitted disclosure (Civil Code §56.10(b)/(c)) or requires a valid CMIA authorization. Use the CMIA Disclosure Decision Tree (Appendix A). | Before each disclosure — no retroactive authorization accepted. |
| 6.1.3 | Clinical Staff / Compliance Officer | If the requested information is Sensitive Category Information (see Section 4), require a signed CMIA authorization even if the disclosure would otherwise be permitted under HIPAA. Do not release Sensitive Category Information based on HIPAA authorization alone. | Before disclosure of any Sensitive Category Information. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer / Administrator | Review all CMIA authorization forms at least annually to confirm they meet the requirements of Civil Code §56.11. Update forms within 30 calendar days of any legislative change affecting required elements. | Annual review; update within 30 days of legislative change. |
| 6.1.5 | Releasing Staff Member | Log all disclosures of medical information (consistent with CO-HP-006 Accounting of Disclosures procedures) including: (a) date and recipient of disclosure; (b) description of information disclosed; (c) authorization or permitted exception basis; (d) whether information includes a Sensitive Category. | At time of each disclosure. |

### 6.2 Sensitive Category Information — Heightened Handling

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | All Clinical Staff | When documenting in the EHR, flag records that contain Sensitive Category Information using the system's designated marking/category field. If the EHR does not support flags, alert the Compliance Officer for alternative segmentation. | At time of documentation. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a current list of Sensitive Category Information categories (Appendix B) that is distributed to all clinical and administrative staff. Update within 30 calendar days of any statutory change to CMIA sensitive categories. | Maintain continuously; update within 30 days of change. |
| 6.2.3 | Clinical Staff / Administrative Staff | When a third-party requests records, if any records requested include Sensitive Category Information: (a) verify authorization specifically covers that category; (b) do not release even if within treatment/payment/operations unless authorization exists or a specific CMIA exception applies; (c) if uncertain, escalate to Compliance Officer before release. | Before each third-party release involving Sensitive Categories. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | If a valid authorization for Sensitive Category Information cannot be obtained (e.g., emergency), document the applicable CMIA emergency exception (Civil Code §56.10(b)(8)) in the disclosure log with the specific factual basis for the exception. | At time of emergency disclosure. |

### 6.3 Employer Access to Employee Medical Information

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | HR Director / Compliance Officer | The agency, in its capacity as an employer, shall NOT access any employee's medical information—including workers' compensation records, fitness for duty exam results, or health insurance claims—unless: (a) the employee provides written authorization; (b) a specific CMIA employer exception applies (Civil Code §56.20–56.245); or (c) access is required by law. | At all times—zero tolerance for unauthorized employer access. |
| 6.3.2 | HR Director | Where the agency receives employee medical information in permitted channels (e.g., FMLA certification, workers' compensation), the information shall be maintained in a separate confidential file, accessible only to persons with a need-to-know as defined in the HR-WM-007 personnel file policy, and shall not be shared with supervisors except to the extent that restrictions on work activity are necessary for compliance. | At all times. |
| 6.3.3 | HR Director | Do not make employment decisions (hiring, termination, promotion, reassignment) based on medical information obtained in any CMIA-permitted channel except where the specific medical condition is a bona fide occupational requirement. Document rationale for any employment action that intersects with known medical information. | Before any affected employment action. |

### 6.4 Unauthorized Disclosure Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | Any Workforce Member | If an unauthorized disclosure of medical information is discovered or suspected, report to the Compliance Officer immediately by phone or urgent message. Do not attempt to independently remediate or contact the recipient without Compliance Officer direction. | Within 24 hours of discovery. |
| 6.4.2 | Compliance Officer | Upon receiving an unauthorized disclosure report: (a) document the date/time of discovery, discoverer, and facts known; (b) assess whether the disclosure constitutes a HIPAA breach (initiate CO-HP-003 if applicable); (c) separately assess CMIA violation under Civil Code §56.36; (d) assess whether nominal damages exposure ($1,000/violation) and/or actual damages apply; (e) consult agency legal counsel within 48 hours if actual harm is identifiable or multiple patients are affected. | HIPAA assessment: within 24 hours. CMIA assessment: within 48 hours. Legal consult: within 48 hours if actual harm indicated. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer / Administrator | If the disclosure constitutes a CMIA violation: (a) notify the affected patient per Civil Code §56.36 requirements and agency legal counsel guidance; (b) document all notifications; (c) implement corrective action per QA-AE-003; (d) report to the Governing Body at the next scheduled meeting unless severity requires emergency meeting. | Patient notice: per legal counsel guidance, typically within 30 calendar days. Corrective action: initiated within 14 days. |
| 6.4.4 | Compliance Officer | Complete a CMIA Violation Documentation Form (Appendix C) for every confirmed CMIA violation. Maintain all violation records for minimum 6 years from the date of the violation (per statute of limitations under California law). | At time of confirmed violation; retain for 6 years. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Staff releases Sensitive Category Information without valid CMIA authorization | Immediately escalate to Compliance Officer. | Compliance Officer conducts root cause analysis; implements retraining; corrective action per QA-AE-003. Document in compliance log. | Root cause analysis within 14 days; retraining within 30 days. |
| Patient files complaint related to CMIA privacy rights | Compliance Officer receives complaint, initiates formal investigation per CO-CP-007. | Respond to patient within 14 calendar days; resolve within 30 calendar days; document resolution in compliance system. | Initial response: 14 days. Resolution: 30 days. |
| State agency (CDPH/HCAI) initiates investigation of CMIA complaint | Administrator immediately notifies legal counsel and Compliance Officer. | Preserve all relevant records; cooperate fully with investigation; prepare documentation demonstrating CMIA compliance program. | Preservation: immediate. Compliance documentation: within 7 business days of notice. |
| Legislative amendment to CMIA enacted | Compliance Officer monitors state legislation per CO-RA-001. | Update policy, authorization forms, and training materials within 90 calendar days of enacted amendment's effective date. | Within 90 days of effective date of amendment. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| CMIA Confidentiality Statement provided at intake | Audit of 10% of patient records quarterly — verify acknowledgment present | 100% compliance |
| Sensitive Category Information disclosures have valid CMIA authorization | Quarterly audit of disclosure log — review all Sensitive Category disclosures | 100% have valid authorization or documented CMIA exception |
| CMIA violation incidents | Count from compliance log quarterly | 0 confirmed violations; any violation triggers immediate investigation |
| Staff CMIA training completed | Training completion rate from HR records | 100% at orientation; 100% annual within calendar year |
| CMIA authorization forms are current | Annual legal review of authorization form against current Civil Code §56.11 | Form reviewed and confirmed current within 12 months |
| Employer access to employee medical information is segregated and controlled | HR file audit — verify medical information is in separate file, not combined with standard personnel file | 100% compliance |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

California CDPH and HCAI surveyors, as well as CMS surveyors examining applicable California overlay requirements, may assess:

1. Evidence of a CMIA-specific compliance policy distinct from HIPAA. Surveyors will look for whether the agency treats CMIA as an add-on to HIPAA rather than a parallel obligation with additional requirements.
2. Patient intake acknowledgment of California-specific privacy rights. Providing only the federal NPP without a CMIA Confidentiality Statement is a compliance gap.
3. Sensitive Category Information handling procedures. Surveyors may request examples of mental health, substance abuse, or HIV-related disclosures to verify proper authorization was obtained.
4. Staff awareness of CMIA vs. HIPAA differences. Frontline staff interviews may reveal whether staff understand that California law imposes additional restrictions.
5. Disclosure logs and authorization form completeness. Both must evidence compliance with Civil Code §56.11 elements.
6. Complaint and violation response records.

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Treating CMIA as identical to HIPAA | Unauthorized disclosures of Sensitive Category Information; $1,000/violation nominal damages exposure | Staff training explicitly addresses CMIA additions; policy clearly distinguishes both frameworks |
| Releasing mental health records based on HIPAA authorization alone | Civil Code §56.36 violation; patient lawsuit | Sensitive Category checklist embedded in release process (Appendix A) |
| No CMIA-compliant patient notification at intake | CDPH/HCAI survey deficiency | CMIA Confidentiality Statement incorporated into standard intake packet |
| Employer accessing employee medical information without CMIA basis | Civil Code §56.20 violation; employee lawsuit | Separate medical file; HR policy training; zero access without authorization |
| Not updating policy after CMIA legislative amendments | Non-compliant practices continue after law changes | CO-RA-001 regulatory monitoring captures CMIA amendments; Compliance Officer owns update obligation |

## Policy Header

## 2. Purpose
This policy mandates the systematic monitoring of federal, state, and local regulatory changes affecting Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and establishes a defined process for assessing the impact of regulatory changes on agency operations, policies, and training, and implementing required updates within defined timeframes. Regulatory non-compliance resulting from undetected regulatory changes constitutes a significant survey and financial risk. This policy ensures the agency maintains continuous compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, HIPAA, California home health regulations, OIG guidance, and all other applicable regulatory frameworks.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to the Compliance Officer, Administrator, Director of Nursing, Revenue Cycle Director, HR Director, IT Director, and all department heads whose operational areas are subject to regulatory oversight.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a systematic regulatory monitoring program that tracks all regulatory changes affecting the agency's operations from CMS, OIG, DHHS, California HCAI, California DHCS, and other applicable bodies.
4.2 All identified regulatory changes with an effective date within 90 days shall be triaged for impact within 10 business days of identification.
4.3 Policy revisions required by regulatory changes shall be completed and approved within 30 calendar days of the regulatory change effective date, or earlier if the change imposes immediate compliance obligations.
4.4 Workforce notification and training on regulatory changes shall be completed within 30 calendar days of policy revision.
4.5 The Compliance Officer shall present a regulatory change summary to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Regulatory Change | Any new, amended, or rescinded federal or state law, regulation, rule, guidance document, or official interpretive policy that affects the agency's operations, billing, clinical practices, or compliance obligations. |
| Impact Assessment | A documented analysis of how a regulatory change affects the agency's current policies, procedures, workflows, staff training requirements, and billing practices. |
| Final Rule | A CMS regulation published in the Federal Register that has completed the notice-and-comment rulemaking process and carries the force of law. |
| Proposed Rule | A regulation published for public comment that has not yet been finalized. Monitoring for proposed rules allows the agency to prepare for anticipated changes. |
| CMS Transmittal | A CMS-issued update to the State Operations Manual, Claims Processing Manual, or other operational guidance. |
| Monitoring Sources | The authoritative regulatory sources the Compliance Officer monitors on a defined frequency (see Appendix A). |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Monitoring Program

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Frequency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Monitor all sources listed in Appendix A — Regulatory Monitoring Source List on the defined frequencies. | Per Appendix A schedule. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Officer | Maintain a Regulatory Change Log (Appendix B) documenting all identified regulatory changes, their effective dates, and their triage status. | Updated within 5 business days of identification. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Subscribe to automatic notification services from: CMS MLN (Medicare Learning Network); OIG Work Plan updates; California HCAI regulatory alerts; Federal Register final rule RSS feed for 42 CFR Part 484. | Subscriptions maintained continuously. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Review the OIG Work Plan upon annual publication and update the annual compliance audit work plan (CO-CP-001 Appendix B) to incorporate OIG-identified high-risk areas. | Annually upon OIG Work Plan publication (typically October). |

### 6.2 Impact Assessment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Upon identifying a regulatory change, complete the Regulatory Change Impact Assessment (Appendix C) within 10 business days. The assessment must identify: (a) affected policies, procedures, and workflows; (b) affected departments and roles; (c) training implications; (d) billing or coding implications; (e) effective date of required compliance; (f) risk level if not implemented by effective date. | Within 10 business days of identification. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Route the completed impact assessment to all affected department heads for review and operational input within 5 business days. | Within 5 business days of assessment completion. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer | For High-Risk regulatory changes (potential Condition-level survey deficiency or immediate financial exposure): notify the Governing Body within 14 calendar days of identification and present a preliminary implementation plan. | Within 14 calendar days of identification. |

### 6.3 Policy and Procedure Update

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Compliance Officer / Policy Owner | Initiate revision of all affected policies per the policy development standards in GV-PM-001. | Within 10 business days of impact assessment completion. |
| 6.3.2 | Policy Owner | Submit revised policy drafts to the Compliance Officer for review and to the Governing Body (for REQUIRED-tier policies) or Administrator (for ESSENTIAL/RECOMMENDED-tier) for approval. | Within 20 calendar days of regulatory change effective date. |
| 6.3.3 | Governing Body / Administrator | Approve revised policies and document approval in meeting minutes or by written administrative approval. | Within 30 calendar days of regulatory change effective date. |
| 6.3.4 | Compliance Officer | Distribute approved revised policies to all affected workforce members and initiate re-acknowledgment per policy GV-PM-003. | Within 14 calendar days of policy approval. |

### 6.4 Training and Communication

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Develop or update training materials for any regulatory change requiring workforce education. | Within 14 calendar days of policy approval. |
| 6.4.2 | HR Director / Compliance Officer | Deliver targeted training to affected workforce members on the regulatory change and updated policies. | Within 30 calendar days of policy approval. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | Issue a Regulatory Change Notification memo (Appendix D) to all affected workforce members simultaneously with or prior to training deployment. | Simultaneously with or prior to training. |

### 6.5 Quarterly Reporting to Governing Body

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | Include a Regulatory Change Summary section in each quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body (per CO-CP-001 Section 6.4.3) covering: (a) all regulatory changes identified in the quarter; (b) impact assessments completed; (c) policy revisions in progress or completed; (d) training deployments completed; (e) upcoming regulatory changes requiring preparation. | 7 calendar days before each quarterly Governing Body meeting. |
| 6.5.2 | Governing Body | Review and discuss the Regulatory Change Summary. Direct any additional action required. Document discussion and directives in meeting minutes. | At each quarterly meeting. |

## Policy Header

| Domain | CO — Compliance & Regulatory |
| Subdomain | RA — Regulatory Affairs |

| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |

| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the internal compliance auditing program of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Internal auditing is a required element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and provides the agency's primary mechanism for proactively identifying compliance deficiencies, billing errors, documentation gaps, and operational non-conformities before they result in government action, survey deficiencies, or financial penalties. This policy defines the scope, methodology, frequency, reporting, and corrective action requirements for all internal compliance audits.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all audit activities conducted by or on behalf of the Compliance Officer including billing audits, clinical documentation audits, OASIS accuracy audits, HIPAA compliance audits, exclusion screening audits, and policy acknowledgment audits. It does not govern external audits by CMS, OIG, or other regulatory bodies (see CO-RA-003).
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an active internal compliance auditing program with an annual risk-based audit work plan approved by the Compliance Committee.
4.2 All audit findings shall be documented in writing and reported to the Compliance Committee and Governing Body per the escalation standards of this policy.
4.3 All deficiencies identified through auditing shall be addressed through corrective action plans per policy QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days of audit report finalization.
4.4 Corrective action effectiveness shall be validated through re-audit within 90 calendar days of CAP implementation.
4.5 All audit records are compliance documents and shall be maintained for a minimum of 7 years per policy CO-HP-007.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance Audit | A structured, systematic review of records, processes, or transactions against a defined regulatory, policy, or billing standard to identify deviations, deficiencies, or risk areas. |
| Billing Audit | An audit focused on the accuracy, completeness, and regulatory conformity of claims submitted to Medicare or other payers. |
| Clinical Documentation Audit | An audit focused on the accuracy, timeliness, completeness, and authentication of clinical records. |
| OASIS Audit | An audit focused on the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of OASIS data collection and transmission. |
| Triangulation Audit | An audit that cross-references physician orders, visit delivery documentation, and billed claims to verify alignment across all three sources. |
| Sample Size | The number of records selected for review in a given audit; must be statistically sufficient to support conclusions. |
| Extrapolation | The statistical process of projecting audit findings from a sample to the universe of transactions to estimate total financial exposure. |
| CAP (Corrective Action Plan) | A documented plan with specific actions, responsible parties, and deadlines to remediate identified audit deficiencies per QA-AE-003. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Annual Audit Work Plan

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Compliance Officer | Develop the annual compliance audit work plan using the template in CO-CP-001 Appendix B. Risk-prioritize audit areas based on: (a) prior year audit findings; (b) OIG Work Plan; (c) CMS survey findings trends; (d) internal incident and claim denial data; (e) regulatory changes from prior year. | Drafted by December 31 of preceding year. |
| 6.1.2 | Compliance Committee | Review and approve the annual audit work plan at the Q1 Compliance Committee meeting. | Q1 Compliance Committee meeting. |
| 6.1.3 | Compliance Officer | Present the approved audit work plan to the Governing Body at the Q1 quarterly meeting. | Q1 Governing Body meeting. |
| 6.1.4 | Compliance Officer | Review the work plan quarterly and adjust based on emerging risks, new regulatory changes, or significant audit findings. Document any amendments to the work plan in Compliance Committee minutes. | Quarterly. |

### 6.2 Audit Execution — Standard Protocol

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer / Auditor | Prepare an Audit Initiation Notice (Appendix A) for each audit specifying: audit type, scope, time period reviewed, sample size, and methodology. | 5 business days before audit initiation. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer / Auditor | Conduct the audit per the defined scope and methodology. For all billing audits: use the minimum sample size of 10% of claims or 30 claims (whichever is greater) for the review period. For documentation audits: minimum 20 records per review period, stratified by clinician and patient type. | Per audit work plan schedule. |
| 6.2.3 | Compliance Officer / Auditor | Document all findings contemporaneously using the Audit Findings Worksheet (Appendix B). Note each finding with: (a) record ID; (b) standard violated; (c) deficiency description; (d) severity level; (e) financial impact (if applicable). | During audit execution. |
| 6.2.4 | Compliance Officer | Finalize the Audit Report (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days of audit completion. The report must include: (a) executive summary; (b) methodology; (c) sample description; (d) findings by category; (e) deficiency rate; (f) financial exposure estimate (if applicable); (g) recommendations; (h) prior audit comparison (if repeat audit). | Within 14 calendar days of audit completion. |

### 6.3 Audit Types and Minimum Standards

| Audit Type | Minimum Frequency | Minimum Sample | Key Standards Assessed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Billing & Claims Accuracy (Medicare) | Semi-annual | 30 claims or 10%, whichever greater | Coding accuracy; medical necessity; face-to-face compliance; homebound documentation; order signatures |
| OASIS Data Integrity | Semi-annual | 20 records, stratified by assessor | Item-level accuracy per CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance; completeness; transmission timeliness |
| Clinical Documentation Completeness | Quarterly | 20 records per quarter | Authentication; timeliness; content standards per CL-CD-001 through CL-CD-004 |
| Face-to-Face Encounter Compliance | Quarterly | All new admissions in period | Presence, timeliness, content adequacy per CL-CA-006 and CL-CA-007 |
| Triangulation Audit (Orders/Visits/Bills) | Quarterly | 20 episodes | Order vs. visit delivery vs. billed claims alignment per CO-DC-004 |
| OIG/SAM Exclusion Screening | Monthly | All workforce members | Active enrollment status per HR-TA-003 |
| Policy Acknowledgment Compliance | Annual (Q1) | All applicable workforce | 100% acknowledgment rate per GV-PM-003 |
| HIPAA Privacy & Security | Annual | Risk-based | Minimum necessary; access logs; PHI handling; BAA currency |
| Conflict of Interest Disclosure Currency | Annual (Q1) | All Governing Body members | Annual disclosure per GV-GB-003 |

### 6.4 Findings Reporting and Escalation

| Severity Level | Definition | Reporting Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High | Condition-level regulatory deficiency potential; financial exposure >$10,000; fraud indicator; patient safety issue | Compliance Officer notifies Governing Body within 14 days; special meeting may be requested |
| Moderate | Systematic documentation deficiency; claims denial rate > 5%; policy non-compliance pattern | Reported at next Compliance Committee meeting; CAP required within 14 days of report |
| Low | Isolated deficiency; no financial exposure; correctable through education | Reported at next Compliance Committee meeting; education/counseling required |

### 6.5 Corrective Action and Re-Audit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Compliance Officer | For every High or Moderate finding: develop or direct development of a CAP per QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days of audit report finalization. | Within 14 calendar days of report. |
| 6.5.2 | Department Head | Implement CAP per assigned deadlines. Report progress to Compliance Officer monthly until CAP is closed. | Per CAP deadlines. |
| 6.5.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct re-audit of CAP areas within 90 calendar days of CAP implementation to validate effectiveness. | Within 90 days of CAP implementation. |
| 6.5.4 | Compliance Officer | If re-audit shows deficiency rate has not improved by at least 50% from baseline, escalate to Governing Body with enhanced corrective action plan. | Upon re-audit conclusion. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements (COMPLETED)

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Annual audit work plan | Approved work plan. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file; governance file. | Q1 approval; retained 7 years. |
| Audit Initiation Notices | Appendix A for each audit. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file. | Retained 7 years. |
| Audit Findings Worksheets | Appendix B for each audit. | Compliance Officer / Auditor | Compliance file. | Retained 7 years. |
| Audit Reports | Appendix C for each audit. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file; Compliance Committee minutes. | Within 14 calendar days of completion; retained 7 years. |
| CAP documentation | Per QA-AE-003 template. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file; CAP tracking log. | Retained 7 years. |
| Re-audit documentation | Re-audit findings validating CAP effectiveness. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file. | Within 90 days of CAP implementation; retained 7 years. |
| Quarterly audit status reports | Summary report for Compliance Committee and Governing Body. | Compliance Officer | Compliance file; governance file. | Quarterly; retained 7 years. |

## 8. Compliance Measurement
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual audit work plan is approved at Q1. | Review of Compliance Committee minutes. | 100% — approved at Q1 meeting annually. |
| All planned audits are initiated per schedule. | Review of Audit Initiation Notices vs. work plan. | 100% of planned audits initiated per schedule. |
| Audit Reports completed within 14 calendar days. | Review of report completion dates. | 90% within 14 days; 100% within 21 days. |
| CAPs developed for all High and Moderate findings. | Review of CAP log vs. findings. | 100% of High/Moderate findings have CAP within 14 days. |
| Re-audits conducted within 90 days of CAP implementation. | Review of re-audit documentation dates. | 100% re-audited within 90 days. |
| Re-audit shows 50% or greater improvement. | Comparison of baseline vs. re-audit deficiency rate. | 100% of re-audits show ≥50% improvement; failures escalated. |
| Quarterly audit status reported to Governing Body. | Review of quarterly report submission dates. | 100% submitted 7 days before each quarterly meeting. |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points and Mitigation

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audit work plan exists but no audits are actually conducted. | OIG and CMS treat a non-functional audit program as equivalent to no program. | Compliance Officer must demonstrate active audit operations through documented Audit Initiation Notices, Findings Worksheets, and Reports. |
| Audit sample sizes are too small to support conclusions. | Findings may be unreliable; surveyors may cite inadequate monitoring. | Use minimum sample sizes defined in Section 6.3 consistently. |
| Findings are identified but no CAP is developed. | Undiscovered or unaddressed deficiencies constitute knowing non-compliance. | Mandatory 14-day CAP development for all High and Moderate findings; Compliance Committee tracks at each meeting. |
| Re-audits are not conducted to validate CAP effectiveness. | Agency cannot demonstrate that corrective action was effective. | 90-day re-audit requirement with documented comparison to baseline. |

## 10. Training Requirements
The Compliance Officer and all individuals who conduct or assist with internal compliance audits shall complete training on audit methodology, documentation standards, and regulatory requirements applicable to each audit area prior to conducting their first audit.
The Compliance Officer shall complete at minimum 8 hours of continuing compliance education annually, including audit-related content, with documentation retained in the compliance file.
All department heads whose areas are subject to audit shall receive orientation to the audit process, their responsibilities during an audit, and CAP development requirements within 30 calendar days of assuming their role.
Annual refresher training on the audit program shall be included in the compliance training curriculum per CO-CP-008.
## 11. Version Control
This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001. Only the most current approved version is valid. Any substantive revision requires: (a) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all applicable workforce members within 14 calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001. Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.
