# CL-OA-010 — CMS Look-Back Period Compliance for Assessment Items
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-010 |
| Policy Title | CMS Look-Back Period Compliance for Assessment Items |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires that all OASIS items with CMS-defined look-back periods at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. be coded using only information falling within the specified timeframe as measured from the applicable assessment date. Look-back periods are a fundamental structural feature of the OASIS instrument. They exist because many clinically important conditions — such as falls, incontinence episodes, behavioral symptoms, pressure injury occurrence, and high-risk medication use — cannot be fully assessed through a single-point-in-time clinical examination. They require information about what has happened to the patient over a defined preceding interval. The look-back period establishes the boundary of that interval — precisely enough that two assessors evaluating the same patient at the same time, using the same clinical information, should arrive at the same response for look-back-period items.
When look-back periods are ignored — when an assessor codes a 7-day look-back item based on information from 30 days prior, or uses information from within the look-back period that was actually generated at a prior care setting rather than during the applicable home health period — the result is an OASIS response that does not accurately describe the patient at the applicable time point. This produces payment classification errors and quality measure distortions. The integrity of the entire OASIS program as a quality measurement and payment instrument depends on every agency applying look-back periods correctly and consistently.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors, the OASIS Quality Reviewer, and the Director of Nursing. It governs all OASIS assessment time points where look-back period items are applicable.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every OASIS item with a CMS-defined look-back period shall be coded using only information that falls within that look-back period as measured backward from the applicable assessment date per the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. Information outside the look-back period shall not be used as the basis for coding, regardless of its clinical relevance.
4.2 Look-back periods are measured from the assessment date — the date of the SOC visit, the ROC visit, the RECERT visit, or the FU assessment — not from any other reference point. For SOC assessments following hospital discharge, this means the look-back begins at the SOC assessment date and extends backward from that date.
4.3 When a look-back period overlaps with a prior care setting (hospital, SNF, prior home health episode), events that occurred within the look-back window at the prior care setting are included in the assessment. The setting in which an event occurred does not exclude it from the look-back window. An incontinence episode during a hospital stay that falls within the 14-day look-back of the SOC assessment date is within scope.
4.4 Information from outside the look-back period shall not be used to code look-back items, even when that information is more clinically compelling or more severely represents the patient's condition than information within the look-back window. The look-back boundary is a hard boundary.
4.5 When no information about the look-back period is available — for example, when a patient is transferred and the only functional information is from clinical records predating the look-back — the assessor shall document the limitation, apply the best available evidence within the look-back window, and use clinical reasoning documentation per CL-OA-012 to explain the coding decision.
## 5. CMS Look-Back Period Reference Table
The following table summarizes look-back periods for key OASIS-E2 items. This table is based on the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. When CMS updates the Guidance Manual, this table shall be updated within 30 calendar days per CL-OA-004. In all cases, the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual governs over this table.

| Look-Back Period | Applicable OASIS Items (Representative) | Data Collection Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Point-in-Time (Assessment Day) | GG0130 (Self-Care — SOC/ROC), GG0170 (Mobility — SOC/ROC), M1830 (Bathing — SOC/ROC/DC), M1840–M1860 (Toileting, Transferring — SOC/ROC/DC), M1870 (Eating — SOC/ROC/DC) | Reflects the patient's performance or status at the time of the assessment encounter. Activities should be directly observed during the visit when feasible. |
| Past 24 Hours | Some clinical symptom items per OASIS-E2 Guidance | Covers the 24-hour period immediately before the assessment. Patient and caregiver report are the primary sources for the preceding hours not directly observed. |
| Past 7 Days (7-calendar-day look-back) | M1700 (Cognitive Function), M1710 (When Confused), M1720 (When Anxious), M1740 (Behavioral Symptoms), M1745 (Frequency of Disruptive Behaviors), M1800–M1870 (ADL assistance items at applicable time points), GG0130/GG0170 items at RECERT/DC | Covers the 7 calendar days prior to and including the assessment date. Patient and caregiver report supplement direct observation for the full 7-day window. |
| Past 14 Days (14-calendar-day look-back) | M1730 (Depressive Feelings — PHQ-2/PHQ-9 covers "past 2 weeks"), M2001 (Drug Regimen Review), M2010 (High-Risk Medication Education), M2020 (Management of Oral Medications), M2030 (Management of Injectable Medications) | Covers the 14 calendar days prior to and including the assessment date. PHQ-2/PHQ-9 use the phrase "past 2 weeks" — this is equivalent to the 14-day look-back. |
| Since the Last Home Health SOC or RECERT | M1311 (Pressure Injury — number) | Tracks events or conditions since the start of the current certification period or since the last SOC if no prior certification occurred. |
| During the Current Certification Period | Certain wound-tracking and outcome items | Reflects cumulative status across the certification period. |
| Current/Active (no look-back — present status) | M0110 (Episodic Information), M1000–M1023 (Prior Care History), M1030 (Therapies at Home), M1033–M1036 (Risk Assessment items), M1200–M1242 (Integumentary Status — current), diagnoses | Coded based on current status or current history — not limited by a look-back window. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Look-Back Period Calculation and Application

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assessing RN | Before beginning OASIS coding at each assessment time point, identify the assessment date and calculate the applicable look-back windows: (a) Assessment date minus 7 calendar days = beginning of the 7-day look-back window; (b) Assessment date minus 14 calendar days = beginning of the 14-day look-back window. Record these dates in the assessment narrative to document that the correct window was applied. | Before OASIS coding at each assessment. |
| 6.1.2 | Assessing RN | For each item with a look-back period, gather evidence from within the defined window: (a) Directly observe the patient's current status during the assessment visit; (b) Ask the patient and caregiver about occurrences within the look-back window — not "ever" or "recently" but specifically within the defined number of days; (c) Review clinical record entries (visit notes, communication notes, physician contact notes) dated within the look-back window. | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assessing RN | Document in the assessment narrative that the look-back period was applied: "M1700 — BIMS administered today. Patient and caregiver interviewed regarding cognitive function over the past 7 days. Review of visit notes from [date] through [assessment date] completed." This type of documentation demonstrates that the assessor consciously applied the look-back period — not just that the assessment was conducted. | In the assessment narrative. |
| 6.1.4 | Assessing RN | When asking patients or caregivers about look-back period occurrences, use time-anchored questions: "In the past 7 days — that's since [specific date] — has there been any time when [the patient] seemed confused or disoriented?" or "In the past 2 weeks, have you noticed [the patient] feeling down or depressed on more days than not?" Time-anchored questioning produces more accurate recall than open-ended questions and demonstrates adherence to the look-back window. | During the patient and caregiver interview portion of the assessment. |
| 6.1.5 | Assessing RN | When information within the look-back window is limited — because the patient was recently discharged from a facility and has been home for fewer days than the look-back window covers — include both the home-based information (since discharge) and the inpatient-period information within the look-back window. Do not limit the look-back to only the home period. Document: "Patient discharged from hospital on [date], which is [X] days before the SOC assessment date. Look-back window for 7-day items extends from [date] through [assessment date], including the period of the hospital stay." | In the assessment narrative when the look-back overlaps with a prior setting. |

### 6.2 Common Look-Back Period Application Scenarios
Scenario 1 — SOC Assessment 3 Days After Hospital Discharge:
SOC assessment date: July 10. Hospital discharge date: July 7. For items with a 7-day look-back, the window is July 3–July 10. Four of those seven days (July 3–7) occurred during the hospital stay. Incontinence episodes, behavioral symptoms, and ADL assistance levels that occurred during the hospital stay between July 3 and July 7 are within scope for the look-back items. The assessor shall ask the patient and caregiver about those hospital days, and may contact the discharging facility for information if necessary. Document: "7-day look-back for M1700 covers July 3–10. Patient hospitalized July 3–7. Patient and caregiver interviewed regarding cognitive function during both the hospital stay (July 3–7) and at home (July 7–10). Hospital nursing notes reviewed for the July 3–7 period."
Scenario 2 — RECERT Assessment at Day 58:
RECERT assessment date: October 28 (Day 58 of the certification period beginning September 1). For 7-day look-back items, the window is October 21–28. For 14-day items, the window is October 14–28. Events from earlier in the certification period (September 1–October 13) are outside the look-back window for 7 and 14-day items and shall not be used to code those items. Document: "RECERT OASIS at Day 58. 7-day look-back window: October 21–28. 14-day look-back window: October 14–28. Information from earlier in the certification period not applicable to look-back items."
Scenario 3 — FU/SCIC Assessment Following Hospitalization:
FU (SCIC) assessment date: August 15. Patient was hospitalized August 5–12 and returned home August 12. For 7-day look-back items, the window is August 8–15. Three days of this window (August 8–12) were inpatient days. The inpatient-period behavioral, functional, and clinical information from August 8–12 is within scope for the look-back items. Document: "7-day look-back for FU OASIS: August 8–15. Patient hospitalized August 5–12. August 8–12 falls within the look-back window. Hospital records and patient/caregiver report used for the inpatient portion of the window."
## 7. Look-Back Period Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Look-back window dates documented in assessment narrative | Explicit look-back window dates for each applicable item category | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | Before OASIS coding; retained minimum 7 years |
| Time-anchored patient/caregiver interview documentation | Interview questions and responses with look-back period specified | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | During assessment; documented within 24 hours |
| Look-back window overlap with prior care setting documentation | Specific notation when look-back includes inpatient or prior care setting days | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | In the assessment narrative |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look-back period window dates documented in assessment narrative | Monthly OASIS audit | ≥90% of assessments with look-back items having documented window dates |
| Time-anchored interview questions used for look-back items | Supervisory observation during assessments; documentation review | ≥95% of observed assessments using time-anchored questioning |
| Look-back overlap with prior settings documented and applied | Monthly audit of post-hospitalization assessments | ≥95% of SOC/FU assessments following hospitalization with look-back overlap documentation |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will focus on whether look-back items reflect information from the correct window. The most common finding is that assessors code behavioral and functional items based on information from the beginning of the episode (which is outside the look-back window by the time of RECERT) rather than from the RECERT look-back window. Another common finding is that assessors limit their look-back to only the home health period when a patient recently returned from a facility — missing events that occurred within the look-back window during the inpatient stay.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessor applies look-back from discharge date rather than assessment date | Incorrect look-back window; coding errors | Annual training with look-back calculation exercises; OASIS Quality Reviewer validates look-back documentation at each review |
| Look-back limited to home health period only — excludes inpatient events within the window | Undercoding of events that occurred during the inpatient portion of the look-back | Specific training scenario on post-hospitalization look-back overlap; assessment narrative documentation requirement |
| PHQ-2/PHQ-9 administered as "past 2 weeks" but patient has only been home 3 days | 11 days of the look-back are at the prior facility — inpatient events within the window are still in scope | Annual training covers PHQ look-back in the post-hospitalization context |

# CL-OA-011 — Standardized Assessment Tool Administration and Validity
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-011 |
| Policy Title | Standardized Assessment Tool Administration and Validity |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires that all CMS-mandated standardized assessment tools — including the BIMS, PHQ-2/PHQ-9, and MAHC-10 — be administered by authorized assessors at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. in strict accordance with their validated administration protocols, and that any deviation from the validated protocol is explicitly documented with a clinical justification. Standardized assessment tools are not interchangeable clinical judgment instruments — they are psychometric instruments whose validity, reliability, and normative scoring frameworks depend entirely on administration according to the validated protocol. A BIMS administered without the word repetition component does not produce a valid BIMS score. A PHQ-9 where the assessor substitutes their own questions for the validated 9 items does not produce a valid PHQ-9 score. An abbreviated or modified tool produces data that is incomparable to the normative framework, cannot be interpreted using the validated scoring ranges, and cannot be relied upon for OASIS coding purposes.
Beyond the psychometric validity issue, there is a compliance dimension: CMS OASIS item responses that are keyed to standardized tool scores — M1700 (BIMS), M1730 and M1750 (PHQ) — are required to be derived from the validated tools, not from clinical impression or informal assessment. Coding M1700 from clinical observation of the patient's general orientation without administering the BIMS is a coding rule violation per the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, regardless of whether the resulting response is clinically plausible.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors who administer standardized assessment tools, the OASIS Quality Reviewer who validates tool administration, and the Director of Nursing who oversees tool competency.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The BIMS, PHQ-2/PHQ-9, and MAHC-10 (where applicable) shall be administered during every applicable OASIS assessment time point at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., unless a documented clinical exception applies per Section 6.3.
4.2 Each tool shall be administered exactly as specified in its validated protocol and as required by the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. No item shall be omitted, reworded, reordered, or supplemented with non-protocol questions. The validated administration protocol for each tool is specified in Section 6 of this policy.
4.3 Tool administration results shall be documented at the individual item level — not only as total scores — to demonstrate that each component of the tool was administered and scored individually per the validated protocol.
4.4 An OASIS response that is keyed to a standardized tool result shall not be coded from clinical impression, from prior assessment scores, from other assessors' reports, or from informal screening — unless a documented clinical exception applies per Section 6.3 and the applicable CMS guidance for the alternative pathway.
4.5 All authorized OASIS assessors shall demonstrate competency in the administration of every required standardized tool before conducting independent OASIS assessments, per CL-OA-003. Annual re-competency shall include re-demonstration of BIMS administration as a mandatory component.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Validated Protocol | The specific, published administration instructions for a standardized assessment tool — including the exact wording of items, the sequence of administration, the response option structure, the scoring methodology, and the normative interpretation framework — that constitute the tool as validated in the published research literature and as required by CMS. |
| BIMS (Brief Interview for Mental Status) | A CMS-developed standardized cognitive screening tool consisting of three components: word repetition (3 words), temporal orientation (year, month, day of week), and word recall. Scored 0–15. Required for coding M1700 when the patient can communicate. |
| PHQ-2 (Patient Health Questionnaire — 2 Item) | A validated two-question depression screening instrument requiring verbatim question reading and a 0–3 frequency response scale. Required as the initial screening for coding M1730 and M1750. |
| PHQ-9 (Patient Health Questionnaire — 9 Item) | A validated nine-question depression assessment instrument required when PHQ-2 score is ≥3 or when clinical presentation indicates depression. |
| MAHC-10 (Missouri Alliance for Home Care — 10 Item) | A validated fall risk assessment tool used in the OASIS context for applicable items. |
| Clinical Exception | A documented clinical circumstance in which the validated administration protocol cannot be completed in full — including patient refusal, communication limitations, cognitive inability, or medical instability — requiring use of an alternative pathway specified in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. |
| SAMS (Staff Assessment for Mental Status) | The alternative cognitive assessment pathway used when a patient cannot complete the BIMS — consisting of staff observation-based assessments of cognitive function. Used to code M1700 when BIMS cannot be administered. |

## 6. Tool Administration Protocols
### 6.1 BIMS — Brief Interview for Mental Status
Administration Requirement: At every SOC, ROC, and RECERT assessment time point where M1700 is applicable, unless a documented clinical exception requires use of the SAMS pathway.
Validated Administration Protocol:
Step 1 — Introduction (do not skip): Say to the patient: "I am going to ask you some questions about your memory and thinking. Some of these questions will be easy, and some will be harder. Let's start with a short memory test."
Step 2 — Word Repetition Component (Component A — scored 0–3): Say: "I am going to say three words, and I would like you to repeat them back to me right now, and remember them for a few minutes. The three words are: [sock], [blue], [bed]." Use these specific words. Do not substitute. Do not provide multiple repetitions — the words are stated once. Ask the patient to repeat them. Record how many of the three words the patient repeated correctly (0, 1, 2, or 3).
Step 3 — Temporal Orientation Component (Component B — scored 0–4): Ask the following three questions in sequence:
"What year is it right now?" (Score 1 if correct; 0 if incorrect)
"What month is it right now?" (Score 1 if within 5 calendar days of a new month; otherwise 0 if correct, partial credit per OASIS guidance if within 5 days of month end)
"What day of the week is it today?" (Score 1 if correct; 0 if incorrect)
Follow the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual scoring rules for the month question — specific rules apply for responses that are close to a month boundary.
Step 4 — Word Recall Component (Component C — scored 0–3): After completing the temporal orientation questions (a pause of at least several minutes from the word repetition), say: "Now, what were those three words I asked you to remember a few minutes ago?" Record how many of the three original words the patient recalls (0, 1, 2, or 3). Do not provide cues. Do not repeat the words.
Step 5 — Score Calculation: BIMS Total Score = Component A + Component B + Component C (maximum 15)

| Score Range | Cognitive Function | M1700 Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13–15 | Cognitively Intact | Per CMS guidance — see Guidance Manual |
| 8–12 | Moderately Impaired | Per CMS guidance |
| 0–7 | Severely Impaired | Per CMS guidance |

Documentation Requirement: Document the three words used, each component score, and the total score. Example: "BIMS administered. Words: sock, blue, bed. Component A (repetition): 3/3. Component B (orientation): Year correct (1), Month correct (1), Day of week correct (1) = 3/3 total orientation. Component C (recall): 2/3 words recalled (sock, bed). BIMS Total Score: 8. Interpretation: Moderately Impaired."
### 6.2 PHQ-2 and PHQ-9 — Patient Health Questionnaire
Administration Requirement: PHQ-2 at every SOC, ROC, and RECERT assessment where M1730 is applicable. PHQ-9 when PHQ-2 total score is ≥3 or when clinical presentation indicates depression regardless of PHQ-2 score.
Validated PHQ-2 Administration Protocol:
Say to the patient: "I am going to ask you two questions about your mood over the past 2 weeks. Please answer based on how often you have been bothered by each of the following."
PHQ-2 Item 1: "Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by having little interest or pleasure in doing things?"
PHQ-2 Item 2: "Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?"
For each item, use the exact response scale:
"Not at all" = 0
"Several days" = 1
"More than half the days" = 2
"Nearly every day" = 3
PHQ-2 Total Score = Item 1 + Item 2 (maximum 6)
A score of ≥3 is a positive screen requiring PHQ-9 administration.
Validated PHQ-9 Administration Protocol:
Continue from PHQ-2 (use the same 2-week look-back): "Now I have some additional questions about your mood over the past 2 weeks."
Items 3 through 9 (read verbatim using the validated 9-item PHQ-9 protocol per CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual):
"Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much?"
"Feeling tired or having little energy?"
"Poor appetite or overeating?"
"Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down?"
"Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television?"
"Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual?"
"Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself in some way?"
Each item scored 0–3 using the same frequency scale as PHQ-2. PHQ-9 Total Score = Items 1–9 (maximum 27).
Item 9 Special Requirement: When a patient scores ≥1 on PHQ-9 Item 9, the suicidality assessment protocol per CL-SD-022 Section 6.5 is immediately triggered. Document the Item 9 response separately and clearly in the assessment narrative with notation that the suicidality assessment was initiated.
PHQ-9 Score Interpretation:

| Score | Severity | Clinical Significance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–4 | Minimal |  |
| 5–9 | Mild | Physician notification required per CL-SD-022 |
| 10–14 | Moderate | Physician notification and MSW referral required |
| 15–19 | Moderately Severe | Immediate clinical response per CL-SD-022 |
| 20–27 | Severe | Immediate clinical response per CL-SD-022 |

Documentation Requirement: Document each item response (0–3 score for each item), both the PHQ-2 and PHQ-9 total scores, the severity interpretation, and any Item 9 special action taken.
### 6.3 Clinical Exceptions — When Standardized Tools Cannot Be Administered

| Exception Type | Documentation Required | Alternative Pathway |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient is comatose or minimally responsive | Document patient's level of consciousness and the reason BIMS cannot be administered | Code M1700 using the SAMS (Staff Assessment for Mental Status) pathway per CMS guidance |
| Patient has severe aphasia, is non-verbal, or cannot communicate in any mutually understandable way | Document the communication limitation specifically | BIMS: Use SAMS pathway. PHQ-2/PHQ-9: Code M1730/M1750 from behavioral observation per CMS guidance |
| Patient refuses to participate in the standardized tool | Document the patient's refusal and the education provided about the tool's purpose | Code the OASIS item based on clinical observation with a notation that the tool was refused and clinical observation was substituted |
| Patient is too fatigued or medically unstable to complete the tool at the time of the assessment visit | Document the clinical status limiting participation | Attempt administration at the next visit within the OASIS completion window; if the window will close, code from the best available clinical information with documentation |
| Patient does not speak a language in which a validated translation exists | Document the language and the absence of a validated translation | Administer with a qualified interpreter for informal languages; for languages with validated translations, obtain and use the validated translation per CL-SD-022 and OP-PA-003 |

## 7. Quality Review Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | At every SOC Level 2 review, verify that BIMS component scores are documented (not just the total score), that the three words used are identified, and that each temporal orientation response is recorded. An assessment where only the BIMS total score is documented without components raises a protocol validity concern. | At each Level 2 review. |
| 7.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Verify that PHQ-2 item scores are documented individually and that the PHQ-9 was administered when the PHQ-2 total was ≥3. A PHQ-9 not administered when PHQ-2 ≥3 is a protocol compliance failure. | At each Level 2 review. |
| 7.3 | Director of Nursing | Conduct an annual BIMS competency assessment for all authorized assessors — a direct observation of BIMS administration with a simulated patient — per CL-OA-003. Any assessor who cannot correctly administer all three BIMS components in sequence is not authorized to conduct independent OASIS assessments until remediation is completed. | Annually. |

## 8. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BIMS component scores | Component A (word repetition), Component B (orientation — year, month, day), Component C (recall), total score, and interpretation | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment module | At each applicable OASIS time point; retained minimum 7 years |
| PHQ-2 and PHQ-9 item scores | All individual item scores (0–3), total score, severity interpretation | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment module | At each applicable OASIS time point; retained minimum 7 years |
| PHQ-9 Item 9 response and safety action | Item 9 score and documentation of suicidality assessment initiation if score ≥1 | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment module; Communication notes | At each assessment; immediate action documented |
| Clinical exception documentation | Exception type, clinical reason, alternative pathway used | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | At each exception; retained minimum 7 years |
| Annual BIMS competency | Competency assessment form per CL-OA-003 | Director of Nursing | Personnel file | Annually; retained minimum 7 years |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 9. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 9.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BIMS administered and component scores documented at all applicable time points | Monthly OASIS audit | ≥98% of M1700 entries with component-level BIMS documentation |
| PHQ-9 administered when PHQ-2 ≥3 | Monthly audit — cross-reference PHQ-2 scores ≥3 with PHQ-9 documentation | 100% — zero positive PHQ-2 screens without PHQ-9 follow-up |
| PHQ-9 Item 9 triggers safety assessment when ≥1 | Audit of Item 9 scores — cross-reference with safety assessment documentation | 100% |
| Clinical exceptions documented with alternative pathway | Audit of assessments where tool administration was not completed | ≥95% of exceptions with documented alternative pathway |
| Annual BIMS competency assessment completed | Personnel file audit | 100% — no assessors with lapsed BIMS competency |

### 9.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will ask clinical staff to describe how they administer the BIMS. A common finding is that assessors describe an informal assessment of orientation (asking date, place, and person) rather than the validated BIMS protocol (word repetition + temporal orientation + word recall). The absence of the word repetition and word recall components means the assessment is not the BIMS — and M1700 coded from that assessment is coded from a non-validated instrument.
ADR auditors will specifically look for BIMS total scores without component scores — a strong indicator that the tool was not formally administered and the score was estimated. Documentation that reads "BIMS: 12" without component scores will be treated as inadequate substantiation for M1700.
### 9.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BIMS total score documented without components | Suggests informal administration; M1700 substantiation deficiency | EHR assessment template requires individual BIMS component fields; Director of Nursing reviews component documentation at monthly audit |
| PHQ-9 not administered after positive PHQ-2 | M1730/M1750 coding rule violation; behavioral health PDGM classification error | EHR workflow alert when PHQ-2 total is ≥3; OASIS Quality Reviewer validates PHQ protocol compliance at every SOC review |
| BIMS word repetition component omitted — assessor jumps directly to orientation | Validated protocol violation; BIMS score not valid without Component A | Annual BIMS competency includes direct observation of Component A administration; zero tolerance for component omission |

11.1 All authorized OASIS assessors shall demonstrate competency in validated BIMS and PHQ-2/PHQ-9 administration before independent assessment authorization per CL-OA-003. Annual re-competency shall include BIMS administration demonstration as a mandatory component.
11.2 Training shall use actual tool administration practice with role-play scenarios, not just didactic instruction. Assessors must physically administer the BIMS to a simulated patient in the correct protocol sequence to receive competency credit.
11.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, revision, or hire.

# CL-OA-012 — Clinical Reasoning Documentation for Coding Decisions
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-012 |
| Policy Title | Clinical Reasoning Documentation for Coding Decisions |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires that when an OASIS coding decision involves clinical judgment beyond direct observation — because the evidence is ambiguous, the patient's performance varied across the look-back period, the assessment tool could not be administered in full, or the CMS Guidance Manual does not unambiguously resolve the specific clinical scenario — the authorized assessor at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. documents the specific clinical reasoning that supports the selected response. Clinical reasoning documentation is both the compliance defense and the clinical integrity mechanism for judgment-based coding decisions.
Every OASIS item has a defined, correct response for every patient's clinical situation — but some items require clinical judgment to determine what that correct response is. When a patient's performance varies from day to day, and the item requires coding "typical" status, the determination of what is "typical" requires judgment. When a patient can complete 60% of a self-care activity independently but requires physical assistance for the remaining 40%, the selection of the appropriate GG response option requires judgment about the assistance level category. When the CMS Guidance Manual's response option definitions do not cleanly map to the patient's specific presentation, the assessor must apply clinical reasoning to identify the best-fit response.
Clinical reasoning documentation does not excuse inaccurate coding — it documents the reasoning behind accurate coding that required judgment to arrive at. A well-documented reasoning process for a difficult coding decision is a clinical integrity statement. An undocumented judgment call that happens to produce an accurate response is a compliance vulnerability, because it cannot be evaluated or defended.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors, the OASIS Quality Reviewer, and the Director of Nursing.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 When an OASIS coding decision requires clinical judgment beyond the direct application of documented clinical observations to a CMS Guidance Manual response option — specifically, when any of the triggering conditions in Section 5 apply — the assessor shall document the clinical reasoning that supports the selected response before locking the assessment.
4.2 Clinical reasoning documentation is required for judgment-based coding decisions; it is not required for routine coding decisions where the clinical evidence directly maps to the response option without ambiguity. The requirement is triggered by the conditions in Section 5, not applied universally to every item.
4.3 Clinical reasoning documentation shall include: the specific coding question being resolved; the relevant clinical evidence available; the alternative response options considered; the clinical reasoning applied to select among the options; and the selected response with its basis. The documentation shall be specific enough that a qualified OASIS assessor reviewing the record can evaluate whether the reasoning is clinically sound.
4.4 Clinical reasoning documentation does not substitute for clinical evidence. An assessor cannot document reasoning in place of conducting the assessment that would generate the evidence. If a GG item requires direct observation and the patient refused to perform the activity, the appropriate response is to document the refusal and apply the substitute evidence protocol per CL-OA-006 — not to document reasoning about what the patient's performance level "probably is" based on their diagnosis.
4.5 The OASIS Quality Reviewer shall specifically review clinical reasoning documentation during Level 2 quality reviews for all items coded under the triggering conditions in Section 5. Reasoning documentation that is absent, vague, or internally inconsistent shall be treated as an accuracy deficiency per CL-OA-002.
## 5. Triggering Conditions for Clinical Reasoning Documentation
Clinical reasoning documentation is required when any of the following conditions apply to a coding decision:
Condition 1 — Variable Patient Performance Across the Look-Back Period: The patient's performance of an activity or exhibition of a symptom varied significantly across the look-back window — some days better, some days worse — and the assessor must determine which response option best represents "typical" performance. The reasoning documentation shall describe the range of performance observed or reported, the frequency and pattern of better vs. worse days, and the basis for the typical performance determination.
Condition 2 — Partial Activity Completion: The patient completes part of an activity independently and requires physical assistance for another part, and the activity is not sub-divided at that level in the OASIS item. The reasoning documentation shall describe the specific portions of the activity completed independently and with assistance, and the basis for the selected GG response option that most closely represents the overall assistance level.
Condition 3 — Atypical Assessment Day Performance: The assessor has reason to believe that the patient's performance during the assessment visit was atypical — better or worse than their usual performance — due to a transient factor (acute pain, unusual fatigue, anxiety about the assessment, medication timing). The reasoning documentation shall describe the evidence of the atypical performance, the evidence about the patient's typical performance, and the assessment of which more accurately represents the patient's functional level per the CMS coding rules.
Condition 4 — Standardized Tool Partial Administration: The standardized tool could not be administered in full due to a clinical exception per CL-OA-011 Section 6.3, and the assessor must code the OASIS item using an alternative pathway. The reasoning documentation shall describe the specific component(s) not administered, the clinical exception, and the alternative evidence used.
Condition 5 — CMS Guidance Ambiguity: The CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual does not unambiguously resolve the coding decision for the patient's specific clinical situation. The reasoning documentation shall describe the specific ambiguity, the steps taken to resolve it (including any consultation with the Director of Nursing or OASIS contractor per CL-OA-004), and the clinical reasoning applied to the best-fit response.
Condition 6 — Caregiver Performs Activities for Patient: The patient's caregiver routinely performs activities for the patient, making it difficult to assess the patient's actual performance ability versus their habitual assistance level. The reasoning documentation shall describe the evidence about the patient's actual ability (from direct observation, patient self-report, and caregiver report) versus the habitual assistance level, and the basis for the coded response.
Condition 7 — Inferred Coding for Transfer OASIS: The Transfer OASIS is being completed retrospectively without the assessing RN having been present at the time of transfer. The reasoning documentation shall describe the sources used (last available visit note, patient/caregiver contact, hospital contact), the limitations of those sources, and the clinical reasoning applied to each coded response.
## 6. Clinical Reasoning Documentation Structure
The following structured format shall be used for all clinical reasoning documentation:
[Item Code] — Clinical Reasoning Entry:
"[OASIS item code and name]: Clinical judgment required for this coding decision. [Triggering condition]: [Describe the specific triggering condition]. Available evidence: [Describe the specific clinical evidence available — source, content, and evidence hierarchy level per CL-OA-006]. Alternative responses considered: [Identify the response options that were candidates]. Coding reasoning: [Explain why the selected response most accurately represents the patient's status per the applicable OASIS item definition]. Selected response: [State the response selected and confirm it is consistent with the CMS Guidance Manual definition for that response option]."
Example — Condition 1 (Variable Performance):
"GG0170B (Walking 10 Feet) — Clinical Reasoning Entry: Clinical judgment required. Triggering condition: Variable performance across the 7-day look-back. Available evidence (Level 4 — patient self-report corroborated by caregiver): Patient reports that on most days she walks from bedroom to bathroom (approximately 15 feet) without physical assistance, holding the wall for support. However, on two days this week (per caregiver report), patient required hand-holding assistance from the caregiver at the bathroom threshold due to increased dizziness following medication change on 7/3. Direct observation today (7/5): Patient walked 15 feet to the bathroom without physical contact assistance; required verbal cueing at the threshold. Alternative responses considered: 04 (Supervision or Touching Assistance — reflects typical performance most days and direct observation today) vs. 03 (Partial/Moderate Assistance — reflects the two days with hand-holding). Coding reasoning: Per CMS OASIS guidance for GG items, code reflects the patient's usual performance — the level that most commonly describes the patient. Patient performs independently or with supervision/touching on 5 of 7 days. The 2-day variance was associated with a new medication that has now been dose-adjusted. Typical performance is supervision/touching assistance. Selected response: 04 — Supervision or Touching Assistance."
## 7. Procedures
### 7.1 Recognition of Triggering Conditions

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.1.1 | Assessing RN | During the OASIS coding process, evaluate each item being coded against the seven triggering conditions in Section 5. If any triggering condition applies, flag the item for clinical reasoning documentation before proceeding to the next item. | During OASIS coding. |
| 7.1.2 | Assessing RN | Do not code a judgment-based item and then return to add reasoning documentation later — the reasoning should be worked through and documented at the time of coding, reflecting the actual cognitive process of selecting the response. Post-hoc reasoning documentation risks appearing as reverse-engineering and does not accurately capture the assessment-time clinical judgment. | During OASIS coding; before locking. |

### 7.2 Escalation for Unresolvable Judgment Questions

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.2.1 | Assessing RN | If a judgment-based coding question cannot be resolved by the assessor after applying the evidence hierarchy, reviewing the CMS Guidance Manual, and attempting to document the reasoning, escalate to the Director of Nursing for clinical adjudication before locking the assessment. Describe the specific item, the triggering condition, the available evidence, and the response options being considered. | Before locking; within the OASIS completion deadline. |
| 7.2.2 | Director of Nursing | Provide clinical adjudication guidance. If the Director of Nursing also cannot resolve the ambiguity through clinical judgment and Guidance Manual review, initiate the question submission process to the state OASIS contractor per CL-OA-004. Document the adjudication guidance in the patient's clinical record. | Within 24 hours of escalation; within OASIS completion deadline. |
| 7.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Compile all recurring judgment-based coding questions in the agency's Item-Level Ambiguity Log per CL-OA-004 Section 6.2.3. Use recurring patterns to develop pre-emptive guidance for common scenarios and to identify training needs. | Log updated at each recurring question identification; reviewed quarterly. |

### 7.3 Quality Review of Clinical Reasoning Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.3.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | During every Level 2 review per CL-OA-002, identify all items where a triggering condition would be expected to apply based on the patient's clinical presentation and assessment circumstances. For each such item, verify that clinical reasoning documentation is present in the assessment narrative. | At each Level 2 review. |
| 7.3.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Evaluate the quality of each clinical reasoning documentation entry against the structured format in Section 6: (a) Is the triggering condition identified? (b) Is the relevant evidence described? (c) Are alternative responses considered? (d) Is the reasoning clear and clinically sound? (e) Is the selected response consistent with the reasoning provided? | At each Level 2 review. |
| 7.3.3 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | When clinical reasoning documentation is absent for a triggering-condition item, or when the reasoning provided does not support the selected response, treat the item as an accuracy deficiency and initiate the correction process per CL-OA-002. | Within 24 hours of finding. |

## 8. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical reasoning entries per Section 6 format | Structured reasoning documentation for each triggering-condition item | Assessing RN | EHR — Assessment narrative | During OASIS coding; before locking; retained minimum 7 years |
| Director of Nursing adjudication | Adjudication guidance and reasoning | Director of Nursing | EHR — Communication notes | Within 24 hours of escalation |
| Item-Level Ambiguity Log | Log of recurring judgment-based coding questions and their resolutions | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing supervisory file | Updated at each identification; reviewed quarterly |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment — Appendix A | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 9. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 9.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical reasoning documentation present for all triggering-condition items | Monthly OASIS audit — cross-reference triggering conditions with assessment narrative | ≥90% of triggering-condition items with structured reasoning documentation |
| Reasoning documentation meets the structured format in Section 6 | Quality review assessment of reasoning documentation quality | ≥85% of documented reasoning entries meeting all five format criteria |
| Escalation to Director of Nursing for unresolvable judgment questions | Escalation documentation in Director of Nursing communication notes | 100% — no unresolved judgment questions locked without Director of Nursing guidance |

### 9.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Judgment-based coding decisions made without documentation of the reasoning | Coding decisions cannot be evaluated; quality review cannot validate accuracy | Annual training on triggering conditions; OASIS Quality Reviewer specifically audits for reasoning documentation |
| Reasoning documentation is present but supports a different response than the one coded | Internal inconsistency; coding appears arbitrary | Director of Nursing monthly audit includes reasoning-to-response consistency check |
| Assessors avoid clinical reasoning documentation because it is perceived as creating a record of uncertainty | Judgment calls made silently; no audit trail | Train all assessors that clinical reasoning documentation is a demonstration of professionalism, not an admission of uncertainty |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires that prior to finalizing any comprehensive OASIS assessment at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., the assessing registered nurse must reconcile assessment findings against all available documentation sources — including the referral record, physician orders, prior visit notes, medication reconciliation records, discipline-specific evaluations, and any external clinical documentation from referring facilities — to ensure that the completed assessment is internally consistent, externally corroborated where applicable, and free from material contradictions that would undermine its accuracy, integrity, or billing defensibility.
Cross-document verification is the quality control bridge between data collection and submission. Without it, individually accurate OASIS responses may conflict with each other or with the broader clinical record in ways that neither the assessor nor the OASIS Quality Reviewer would detect without a structured side-by-side comparison. A functional status OASIS response that conflicts with the medication list (e.g., a patient coded as independent in medication management who has a documented cognitive impairment severe enough to require supervised medication dispensing), a wound item response that conflicts with the wound care visit note from two days prior, or a discharge summary clinical picture that conflicts with the SOC homebound documentation — each of these represents a cross-document inconsistency that creates survey deficiency risk, ADR audit vulnerability, and clinical care coordination failure simultaneously.
This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.55(b) — requiring the comprehensive assessment to accurately reflect the patient's current health status — and 42 CFR § 484.110 — requiring clinical records to be complete, accurately written, and promptly completed. It is a companion policy to CL-OA-007 (Evidence-Based OASIS Coding Substantiation) and CL-OA-008 (Conflicting Documentation Source Resolution), which establish the substantiation and conflict resolution standards that cross-document verification enforces.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) authorized to conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments per CL-OA-003
The OASIS Quality Reviewer who conducts pre-submission and post-submission accuracy reviews
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager who oversees assessment completeness and accuracy
All clinical disciplines whose documentation outputs are subject to cross-verification against OASIS assessments
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Prior to locking any comprehensive OASIS assessment, the assessing RN shall conduct a structured cross-document verification review using the Cross-Document Verification Checklist (Appendix A) to confirm that the completed assessment is consistent with all available documentation sources and free from material contradictions.
4.2 Cross-document verification shall include comparison of the completed OASIS assessment against each of the following document categories, to the extent each category is available at the time of assessment finalization: (a) referral documentation including hospital discharge summaries, SNF records, and physician office notes; (b) the current physician order set; (c) the plan of care in development or the prior plan of care (for ROC and RECERT time points); (d) the medication reconciliation record per CL-SD-013; (e) all visit notes created during the applicable look-back period; (f) discipline-specific evaluation reports (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) if available; (g) laboratory and diagnostic results available in the clinical record.
4.3 When the cross-document verification identifies a material inconsistency between the completed OASIS assessment and another document in the clinical record, the assessing RN shall resolve the inconsistency before locking the assessment, applying the documentation hierarchy per CL-OA-006 and the conflict resolution process per CL-OA-008. The resolution shall be documented in the assessment narrative per CL-OA-012.
4.4 The cross-document verification checklist (Appendix A) shall be completed and documented in the EHR for every OASIS assessment at every applicable time point. A checklist that is not completed is treated as a missing verification — equivalent to not having performed the verification.
4.5 The OASIS Quality Reviewer shall specifically assess cross-document verification checklist completion and adequacy as part of every Level 2 quality review per CL-OA-002. An assessment where the checklist is absent, incomplete, or where the reviewer identifies an unresolved inconsistency not flagged by the checklist shall be treated as a quality deficiency requiring correction.
4.6 Cross-document verification is not a guarantee of accuracy — it is a structured process for detecting detectable inconsistencies. The verification does not substitute for the underlying evidence-based coding standards of CL-OA-006 and CL-OA-007. Both the evidence quality and the cross-document consistency are required.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Cross-Document Verification | A structured review process in which the assessing RN compares the completed OASIS assessment item responses against all available documentation sources to identify and resolve material inconsistencies before locking the assessment. |
| Material Inconsistency | A discrepancy between an OASIS item response and a document in the clinical record that is clinically significant — meaning it reflects a genuine difference in documented clinical status rather than a difference in documentation style or format. Minor differences in terminology that describe the same clinical finding are not material inconsistencies. |
| Internal Consistency | The property of an OASIS assessment in which all items that logically relate to each other (e.g., functional mobility items, wound items, cognitive function items) produce a coherent clinical picture without contradicting each other. |
| External Consistency | The property of an OASIS assessment in which the item responses are consistent with the clinical information in other documents in the patient's record — including the physician orders, the plan of care, medication lists, and visit notes. |
| Cross-Document Verification Checklist | The structured form (Appendix A) that the assessing RN completes for every OASIS assessment to document that each category of available documentation has been reviewed and compared against the OASIS responses. |
| Assessment Finalization | The process of reviewing, correcting, and locking the completed OASIS assessment in the EHR, making it the definitive submitted record for the applicable assessment time point. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 — Pre-Verification Preparation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assessing RN | Before beginning the cross-document verification, compile all available documentation relevant to the current assessment time point. For SOC assessments, this includes all referral documentation, the initial physician order set, the medication reconciliation worksheet, and any external clinical records received. For ROC assessments, add all internal visit notes from the prior episode and the inpatient facility's discharge documentation. For RECERT assessments, add all visit notes, physician communication records, and updated physician orders from the current certification period. | Before beginning verification; documentation compiled before assessment locking. |
| 6.1.2 | Assessing RN | Open the completed OASIS assessment in the EHR alongside each documentation category to be reviewed. Do not rely on memory of the documentation content — each comparison must be made with the actual document visible. EHR mobile or dual-screen workflow is strongly recommended to enable simultaneous document review. | During verification. |
| 6.1.3 | Assessing RN | Open the Cross-Document Verification Checklist (Appendix A) in the EHR quality review module. The checklist shall remain open throughout the verification process. | Before beginning verification. |

### 6.2 — Core Verification Comparisons

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assessing RN | Functional Status Verification: Compare all GG functional item responses (GG0130, GG0170) against: (a) the referral's discharge functional summary; (b) any PT or OT evaluation reports available; (c) the physician's functional status notation in the discharge summary or office notes; (d) visit notes from the look-back period that describe the patient's functional performance. Identify any response where the OASIS reflects a significantly different functional level than any of these documents without a documented clinical reason for the difference. Document any inconsistency identified and its resolution in the checklist. | During verification. |
| 6.2.2 | Assessing RN | Diagnosis and Clinical History Verification: Compare the diagnoses coded in the plan of care and the diagnoses referenced in OASIS clinical severity items against: (a) the referring physician's diagnosis list; (b) the hospital discharge diagnosis list; (c) the medication list (medications should be consistent with the documented diagnoses — a patient on insulin should have a diabetes diagnosis; a patient on anticoagulants should have a relevant diagnosis explaining the anticoagulation). Flag any diagnosis referenced in the OASIS that does not appear in the physician record, and any diagnosis in the physician record that appears clinically relevant but is not reflected in the OASIS. | During verification. |
| 6.2.3 | Assessing RN | Medication Verification: Compare the medication list used for M2001 (Drug Regimen Review) and M2010 (High-Risk Medication Education) against: (a) the physician's current medication orders; (b) the medication reconciliation worksheet per CL-SD-013; (c) the patient's medication bottles (as documented during the assessment visit). Verify that the medication list used for OASIS coding reflects the actual medications at the time of assessment — not the pre-discharge medication list without modification per the reconciliation findings. Flag any medication in the OASIS list not supported by a current physician order, and any physician-ordered medication not in the OASIS list. | During verification. |
| 6.2.4 | Assessing RN | Wound Status Verification: Compare all wound item responses (M1311–M1350) against: (a) the wound assessment documentation from the SOC/ROC visit; (b) the most recent wound care visit note from the look-back period; (c) the wound photographs if obtained per CL-SD-011; (d) the referral's wound description from the discharging facility. Verify that wound stage, measurements, and character are consistent across the OASIS coding and the narrative wound documentation. Any discrepancy between the OASIS wound response and the concurrent wound narrative documentation is a material inconsistency requiring resolution before locking. | During verification. |
| 6.2.5 | Assessing RN | Behavioral Health Verification: Compare behavioral health item responses (M1700–M1750) against: (a) the BIMS component scores and total score documented in the assessment narrative; (b) the PHQ-2/PHQ-9 item scores documented in the assessment narrative; (c) the physician's notes regarding the patient's cognitive status; (d) the caregiver's report of the patient's behavioral patterns from the look-back period as documented in the assessment narrative. Verify that M1700 responses are consistent with BIMS scores, and that M1730/M1750 responses are consistent with PHQ-2/PHQ-9 scores. | During verification. |
| 6.2.6 | Assessing RN | Homebound Status Verification: Compare the homebound status narrative against: (a) the GG functional item responses — the homebound documentation must be consistent with the functional levels coded in GG items (e.g., a patient coded as independent in all GG mobility items would be difficult to document as homebound without specific clinical justification); (b) the physician's clinical notes documenting the patient's functional status; (c) the patient's stated activity patterns as documented in the assessment narrative. Flag any homebound documentation that is inconsistent with GG functional responses or physician documentation. | During verification. |
| 6.2.7 | Assessing RN | Physician Order Consistency Verification: Compare the services and disciplines listed in the developing plan of care and the OASIS items reflecting services ordered (where applicable) against the current physician order set. Verify that: (a) every discipline ordered has a corresponding physician order; (b) every physician order for a service is reflected in the plan of care; (c) no service is documented as ordered in the OASIS or plan of care without a supporting physician order. | During verification. |

### 6.3 — Internal Consistency Verification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assessing RN | Conduct an internal consistency review of the OASIS assessment itself — independent of external document comparison — verifying that related OASIS items produce a coherent clinical picture: (a) Mobility-Wound Consistency: A patient coded as requiring maximal assistance for all mobility GG items should have wound documentation reflecting pressure injury risk management consistent with that level of immobility. A patient coded as fully independent in mobility should not have documented pressure injuries attributed to immobility without clinical explanation. (b) Cognitive-Medication Consistency: A patient coded as severely cognitively impaired (BIMS 0–7) should have medication management coded as requiring assistance or being unable to manage independently. A patient coded as cognitively intact (BIMS 13–15) whose M2020 (Oral Medication Management) is coded as "Unable" requires clinical explanation. (c) Respiratory-Activity Consistency: A patient with severe dyspnea coded at the highest severity level (significant respiratory symptom at rest) should have GG mobility items that reflect the activity limitation caused by the dyspnea. | During verification. |
| 6.3.2 | Assessing RN | Complete the Internal Consistency section of the Cross-Document Verification Checklist (Appendix A, Section 3) for each of the above consistency pairs. Document any inconsistency identified and the clinical reasoning or correction applied. | During verification. |

### 6.4 — Discrepancy Resolution and Checklist Completion

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assessing RN | For each material inconsistency identified during the cross-document verification, apply the resolution process: (a) Determine which source governs per the documentation hierarchy of CL-OA-006; (b) Correct the OASIS response if the current response is not supported by the governing source; (c) Document the inconsistency, the governing source, and the resolution in the assessment narrative per CL-OA-008 and CL-OA-012; (d) Note the resolution in the corresponding checklist field. | Before locking; within the OASIS completion deadline. |
| 6.4.2 | Assessing RN | If a material inconsistency cannot be resolved by the assessing RN through application of the documentation hierarchy, escalate to the Director of Nursing for clinical adjudication before locking the assessment. Do not lock an assessment with an unresolved material inconsistency. | Before locking; escalation within 24 hours if Director of Nursing adjudication is needed. |
| 6.4.3 | Assessing RN | Upon completing all verification sections, sign and submit the Cross-Document Verification Checklist in the EHR. The checklist submission timestamp constitutes the completion record for this required step. Lock the OASIS assessment only after the checklist is submitted. | Before locking; checklist submitted immediately before or concurrently with locking. |
| 6.4.4 | Assessing RN | If documentation from an important source (e.g., hospital discharge summary, PT evaluation) is not yet available at the time of verification, document in the checklist which source is missing, the reason it is not available, and the plan to obtain it. A missing external document does not automatically prevent assessment locking, but the absence must be documented and the assessment must be based on the best available evidence per CL-OA-006. | At the time of checklist completion. |

### 6.5 — OASIS Quality Reviewer Cross-Document Verification Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | During every Level 2 quality review per CL-OA-002, access and review the Cross-Document Verification Checklist for the assessment being reviewed. Verify that: (a) the checklist was completed and submitted before or concurrent with assessment locking; (b) all applicable document categories were reviewed; (c) all identified inconsistencies have documented resolutions; (d) the resolutions are consistent with the documentation hierarchy of CL-OA-006. | Within the timeline specified in CL-OA-002. |
| 6.5.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Independently perform a targeted cross-document verification of the highest-risk item categories for the reviewed assessment: GG functional items vs. referral functional description; wound items vs. wound narrative documentation; behavioral health items vs. standardized tool scores. If the Quality Reviewer identifies a material inconsistency not flagged or resolved in the checklist, document the finding and initiate the correction process per CL-OA-002. | Within the Level 2 review timeline. |

### 6.6 — Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-document verification checklist not completed for a locked assessment | Director of Nursing identifies during monthly audit | Director of Nursing directs the assessing RN to perform the verification retroactively and document findings. If material inconsistencies are identified during retroactive verification, initiate OASIS correction per CL-OA-002. Corrective counseling provided to the assessing RN. | Retroactive verification within 5 business days; correction within 10 business days. |
| Assessing RN cannot access a required document for cross-verification | Assessing RN documents the access barrier and contacts Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing coordinates document access through appropriate channels (contacting the referring facility, physician office, or prior HHA). If the document cannot be obtained within the OASIS completion window, the assessment may be locked with the access barrier documented and the missing source clearly noted in the checklist. | Document access coordinated within 24 hours of identification. |
| Internal consistency check reveals a clinically significant conflict between GG functional items and documented clinical severity | Assessing RN escalates to Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing conducts clinical review and adjudicates. If the conflict suggests a clinical condition affecting multiple OASIS item categories, Director of Nursing may direct a supplemental assessment visit before locking. | Director of Nursing review within 24 hours; supplemental visit within 48 hours if directed. |
| Cross-document verification reveals that a previously submitted OASIS has a material inconsistency not identified at the time of verification | OASIS Quality Reviewer or Director of Nursing | Initiate OASIS correction process per CL-OA-002. Assess whether the inconsistency affected the PDGM payment group or quality measure calculation. Report to Compliance Officer if payment was affected. | Correction within 5 business days of identification; Compliance Officer within 48 hours if payment is affected. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-Document Verification Checklist completed for every OASIS assessment | EHR checklist completion log audit | ≥98% of locked assessments with completed checklist |
| All identified inconsistencies have documented resolutions | Checklist audit for completeness of resolution fields | 100% of flagged inconsistencies with documented resolution |
| GG functional items consistent with referral documentation or inconsistency documented | Monthly OASIS audit — GG responses vs. referral functional description | ≥95% of post-hospitalization SOC assessments with documented GG-to-referral comparison |
| Medication OASIS items consistent with reconciled medication list | Monthly audit cross-referencing M2001 documentation against medication reconciliation worksheet | ≥95% consistency |
| BIMS/PHQ scores consistent with M1700/M1730 OASIS responses | Monthly audit | 100% — zero assessments with inconsistent tool score-to-item response |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer reviews checklist for all Level 2 reviews | Quality Review Log audit | ≥95% of Level 2 reviews with documented checklist assessment |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors and MAC ADR auditors conducting assessments of OASIS data quality will specifically examine:
1. Internal consistency of the OASIS assessment. Surveyors are trained to identify logical inconsistencies within the OASIS data set — a patient coded as fully independent in all GG mobility items but with a documented pressure injury, for example, or a patient coded as having severe cognitive impairment but coded as independently managing a complex medication regimen. These internal contradictions suggest that the assessor was not applying a coherent clinical picture across the assessment.
2. Consistency between the OASIS and the clinical narrative. Auditors will compare the OASIS item responses against the assessment narrative documentation. The narrative is expected to provide the clinical basis for the OASIS response — when the narrative description of a patient's functional status during the SOC visit is inconsistent with the GG item response, the auditor must determine which is accurate. When neither the narrative nor the OASIS clearly establishes the clinical basis, both are treated as inadequately substantiated.
3. Consistency between the OASIS and the physician documentation. Surveyors will compare the OASIS clinical grouping diagnoses against the physician's current orders and the discharge summary diagnoses. A primary OASIS diagnosis that does not appear in any physician documentation is a documentation integrity concern.
4. Evidence of a systematic verification process. Surveyors are increasingly looking for agencies to demonstrate not just accurate OASIS data, but a process that systematically produces accurate OASIS data. An agency with a documented cross-document verification requirement — and evidence that it is being followed — demonstrates a governance structure that sustains accuracy over time, not just in individual assessments.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No cross-document verification performed — assessors complete OASIS in isolation | Material inconsistencies undetected; quality measure distortion; ADR vulnerability | Mandate checklist completion as a required step before OASIS locking; EHR workflow enforces checklist submission before lock button is enabled |
| Verification performed verbally without checklist documentation | No audit trail of verification; cannot demonstrate compliance to surveyor | Require EHR-based checklist completion; accept no verbal-only verification |
| GG items not compared against referral functional description at SOC | Most common cross-document inconsistency; point-in-time principle violation per CL-OA-009 | Checklist Section 1 specifically requires GG-to-referral comparison for every SOC assessment; OASIS Quality Reviewer validates at Level 2 review |
| Wound OASIS items not compared against concurrent wound narrative | OASIS wound staging inconsistent with wound narrative; quality measure distortion | Checklist Section 2 specifically requires wound item-to-wound narrative comparison; mandatory wound observation documentation per CL-SD-011 |
| Internal consistency check not performed | Logical contradictions within the OASIS data set submitted to CMS | Checklist Section 3 provides item-pair consistency checks; Director of Nursing monthly audit includes internal consistency as a metric |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All authorized OASIS assessors shall receive training on cross-document verification requirements within their initial OASIS Competency Program per CL-OA-003 and at each annual re-competency, including: the purpose and regulatory basis for cross-document verification; the categories of documents to be reviewed; the Cross-Document Verification Checklist structure and completion requirements; the inconsistency resolution process per CL-OA-006 and CL-OA-008; and the internal consistency check pairs.
10.2 Training shall include case-based exercises requiring assessors to identify material inconsistencies across sample clinical record sets — including GG-to-referral discrepancies, wound item-to-narrative discrepancies, and medication OASIS item-to-reconciliation list discrepancies.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001. 11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions shall be archived as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE." 11.3 Substantive revisions require Governing Body approval, re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days, and policy index update per EN-TG-001. 11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with Governing Body notification at the next regular meeting.
