# CL-OA-018 — Clinician Competency Validation for OASIS Assessment
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-018 |
| Policy Title | Clinician Competency Validation for OASIS Assessment |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the complete validated competency assessment process — including all assessment instruments, performance standards, evaluation methodologies, evaluator qualifications, documentation requirements, remediation protocols, and ongoing competency maintenance standards — for all clinicians authorized to independently conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy is the operational companion to CL-OA-003 (OASIS Clinician Authorization & Competency), which defines the authorization structure and the OASIS Competency Program curriculum. CL-OA-018 defines how competency is measured, what tools are used to measure it, what passing standards apply, who is qualified to evaluate, and what happens when an assessor does not meet competency standards.
The distinction between having completed a training program and having demonstrated competency is clinically and legally significant. An assessor who has sat through an OASIS training module has met a training attendance requirement. An assessor who has demonstrated OASIS competency through validated performance evaluation has met a clinical governance standard. Only the latter qualifies an assessor to independently produce OASIS assessments that are submitted to the federal government as the basis for Medicare payment. This policy establishes the standards that distinguish training attendance from demonstrated competency.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all registered nurses who are candidates for OASIS assessor authorization, all currently authorized OASIS assessors, the Director of Nursing who serves as the designated Competency Evaluator, and the OASIS Quality Reviewer who has evaluator responsibilities for certain competency domains.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All clinicians must demonstrate competency across the domains defined in Section 5 before being authorized to independently conduct OASIS assessments. Competency demonstration is distinct from training completion — it requires performance evaluation against defined standards, not merely attendance at or completion of training content.
4.2 Competency shall be evaluated by the Director of Nursing or a designated evaluator who: (a) holds current OASIS assessor authorization; (b) has administered the specific competency evaluation instruments used in this policy for at least 12 months; (c) has been designated in writing by the Director of Nursing as qualified to conduct competency evaluations for the specific competency domain being assessed.
4.3 Competency evaluation results — including all scores, evaluator observations, and determination of pass or fail — shall be documented using the OASIS Competency Validation Record (Appendix A) and filed in each assessor's personnel file per HR-WM-007.
4.4 Annual competency re-validation is required for all authorized assessors. The re-validation process is abbreviated compared to the initial validation but must include all components defined in Section 6.2. An assessor whose annual re-validation is not completed by their authorization anniversary date is in lapsed authorization status per CL-OA-003 and may not independently conduct OASIS assessments until re-validation is completed.
4.5 An assessor who fails any single competency domain during initial or annual validation shall be immediately suspended from independent OASIS assessment pending remediation and re-evaluation of the failed domain. The assessor may conduct OASIS assessments only in a supervised capacity during the suspension period.
4.6 An assessor who fails the same competency domain twice in any 12-month period shall have their OASIS assessor authorization revoked and shall be required to complete the full initial OASIS Competency Program before re-applying for authorization.
## 5. Competency Domains
The following seven competency domains must be demonstrated for initial authorization and maintained through annual re-validation:

| Domain | Description | Evaluation Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain 1: OASIS Regulatory Framework | Understanding of 42 CFR § 484.55, CMS OASIS-E2 requirements, PDGM linkage, and quality measure implications | Written knowledge assessment |
| Domain 2: Assessment Time Points and Deadlines | Knowledge of all OASIS time point triggers, assessment windows, operational targets, and regulatory deadlines | Written knowledge assessment; case scenario questions |
| Domain 3: Standardized Tool Administration | Correct administration of BIMS (all three components in sequence), PHQ-2/PHQ-9 (all items, correct response scale), and MAHC-10 (where applicable) | Direct observation performance evaluation using standardized patient simulation |
| Domain 4: Standardized Tool Scoring | Correct calculation of component scores and totals for BIMS and PHQ-2/PHQ-9; correct score-to-OASIS-response mapping | Written scoring exercise using provided simulated patient response sets |
| Domain 5: OASIS Item-Level Coding | Accurate application of CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual response selection rules for GG functional items, wound items, and behavioral health items | Case study coding exercise with scored response key |
| Domain 6: Documentation and Substantiation | Adequate documentation of clinical findings to support OASIS item responses per CL-OA-007; narrative-OASIS consistency | Documentation review of supervised SOC assessment |
| Domain 7: Supervised OASIS Assessment | Completion of a comprehensive SOC OASIS assessment in the physical presence of the Director of Nursing or designated evaluator | Direct observation with real-time feedback and post-assessment coding review |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 — Initial Competency Validation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Before scheduling initial competency evaluation, verify that the candidate has completed all modules of the OASIS Competency Program per CL-OA-003. Competency evaluation shall not be administered before program completion. | Before scheduling evaluation. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Written Knowledge Assessment covering Domains 1 and 2 (Appendix B). The assessment consists of 50 multiple-choice questions with a time limit of 90 minutes. Each question addresses a specific knowledge area from the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, assessment time point rules, or PDGM linkage concepts. All questions have a single correct answer determined by the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. Passing score: ≥85%. | At the scheduled evaluation session. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Standardized Tool Performance Evaluation for Domain 3 (Appendix C). The candidate demonstrates complete administration of: (a) the BIMS to a standardized patient (simulation model or role-play partner) including the word repetition component, all three temporal orientation questions, a pause activity, and the word recall component in the correct sequence; (b) the PHQ-2 with correct verbatim question reading and correct response scale; (c) the PHQ-9 continuation from PHQ-2 (if PHQ-2 score ≥3 in the scenario). The evaluator rates each step of each tool using the pass/fail tool-specific checklist in Appendix C. Passing standard: all steps rated "Satisfactory" or "Acceptable with Minor Deviation"; any step rated "Unsatisfactory" constitutes a domain failure. | At the evaluation session, following the written assessment. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Standardized Tool Scoring Exercise for Domain 4 (Appendix D). The candidate receives 5 complete simulated patient BIMS response sets and 5 complete simulated PHQ-9 response sets. The candidate calculates component scores and totals for each, and determines the correct OASIS item response for each. Passing standard: ≥90% of scoring exercises completed correctly with correct score-to-response mapping. | At the evaluation session, following the performance evaluation. |
| 6.1.5 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the OASIS Item-Level Coding Case Study Exercise for Domain 5 (Appendix E). The candidate receives 3 complete clinical case vignettes and is required to code specified OASIS items for each case using the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual as the reference. The answer key is derived from the current Guidance Manual. Passing standard: ≥85% of coded items match the answer key. | At the evaluation session. |
| 6.1.6 | Director of Nursing | Arrange the Supervised SOC Assessment for Domains 6 and 7. The candidate conducts a complete SOC assessment on a real patient in the Director of Nursing's or designated evaluator's physical presence. The evaluator observes the entire assessment without intervening unless a patient safety concern arises, and reviews the completed OASIS narrative and item selections immediately following the assessment. The evaluator rates each domain using the Supervised Assessment Rating Form (Appendix F). Passing standard per domain: overall rating of "Meets Standard" or better. | Within 14 calendar days of completing Domains 1–5 with passing scores. |
| 6.1.7 | Director of Nursing | Review all domain evaluation results. If the candidate has passed all 7 domains, authorize the assessor per CL-OA-003. If the candidate has failed any domain, initiate the remediation process per Section 6.3. Complete the OASIS Competency Validation Record (Appendix A) and file in the personnel file. | Within 5 business days of completing all evaluation components. |

### 6.2 — Annual Re-Validation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Director of Nursing | Alert each assessor 60 days before their authorization anniversary date that annual re-validation is required. Schedule the re-validation to be completed before the anniversary date. | 60 days before anniversary date per CL-OA-003. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer the Annual Re-Validation Written Assessment covering: (a) any changes to the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual since the prior re-validation; (b) items where the assessor had documented accuracy deficiencies in the prior year's monthly audit results; (c) high-risk coding areas (GG functional items, wound staging, BIMS scoring). 25-item assessment; minimum 85% passing score. | At the annual re-validation session. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Administer BIMS Direct Observation Re-Demonstration (mandatory annually regardless of prior-year accuracy): the assessor demonstrates the complete BIMS administration to a simulated patient using the Domain 3 evaluation checklist (Appendix C). Passing standard: same as initial. | At the annual re-validation session. |
| 6.2.4 | Director of Nursing | If the assessor had any Domain 4 (scoring accuracy) or Domain 5 (item-level coding) deficiency in the prior year's monthly audits (any item category below 90%): administer the targeted re-validation exercise for the deficient domain(s) using the same instruments as the initial evaluation. If no prior-year deficiency, Domains 4 and 5 re-validation is waived for the current annual cycle. | At the annual re-validation session if deficiency present. |
| 6.2.5 | Director of Nursing | If the assessor had no prior-year deficiencies in Domains 6 and 7 (documentation and supervised assessment), the Supervised SOC Assessment is waived for the annual re-validation. If a Domain 6 or 7 deficiency was identified in the prior year's audits, a supervised assessment is required. | At the annual re-validation session if deficiency present. |
| 6.2.6 | Director of Nursing | Complete the OASIS Competency Validation Record (Appendix A) for the annual re-validation and file in the personnel file. Update the Authorized Assessor Roster per CL-OA-003. | Within 5 business days of re-validation completion. |

### 6.3 — Remediation Protocol for Domain Failure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Immediately upon identifying a domain failure during initial or annual validation: (a) suspend the assessor from independent OASIS assessment; (b) notify the assessor in writing of the specific domain failure, the performance standard not met, and the remediation requirements; (c) arrange supervised assessment coverage for the assessor's caseload. | Within 24 hours of domain failure identification. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Develop a targeted remediation plan for the failed domain: (a) for Domain 1/2 written assessment failure — assign additional reading from the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual chapters covering the failed areas; re-administer the written assessment or a comparable alternate assessment within 14 calendar days; (b) for Domain 3 tool administration failure — provide direct hands-on coaching with repeat demonstration practice; re-evaluate within 14 calendar days; (c) for Domain 4/5 coding failures — provide focused coding practice exercises with answer key review; re-administer the failed exercise within 14 calendar days; (d) for Domain 6/7 documentation/supervised assessment failure — provide documentation standard review and additional supervised assessments before re-evaluation; re-evaluate supervised assessment within 21 calendar days. | Within 5 business days of domain failure; remediation plan documented. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing / Evaluator | Re-administer the failed domain evaluation after remediation. Passing standard is the same as the initial evaluation. If the assessor passes the re-evaluation, restore authorization per CL-OA-003. Document the remediation and re-evaluation in the OASIS Competency Validation Record. | Within 14–21 calendar days of remediation initiation per domain type. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing | If the assessor fails the re-evaluation of the same domain: revoke OASIS assessor authorization. The assessor must complete the full initial OASIS Competency Program before re-applying for authorization. Document the revocation in the OASIS Competency Validation Record and update the Authorized Assessor Roster. Notify HR per HR-ER-002 regarding employment implications. | Within 24 hours of second domain failure; HR notification within 5 business days. |

| Domain failure triggers immediate suspension | Audit trail of suspension and OASIS access restriction | 100% |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Competency validation records not filed in personnel files | Survey deficiency; inability to demonstrate assessor qualification | Personnel file audit quarterly per HR-WM-007; HR Director quarterly cross-check |

# CL-OA-019 — Pre-Submission Quality Review for Comprehensive Assessments
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-019 |
| Policy Title | Pre-Submission Quality Review for Comprehensive Assessments |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the structured pre-submission quality review process that every authorized OASIS assessor at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. must complete for every OASIS assessment at every applicable time point before locking and transmitting the assessment to the CMS repository. The pre-submission quality review is the final quality control gate between the assessor's work product and the federal data system — the last opportunity to identify and correct errors before they become compliance deficiencies, payment classification errors, or quality measure distortions.
The pre-submission quality review is not a post-completion re-read. It is a structured, checklist-driven systematic review that verifies specific, predefined quality criteria for each major OASIS item category. Its purpose is to catch the categories of errors that are most common, most consequential, and most detectable at the pre-submission stage: items left at default values without clinical justification; internal inconsistencies between related item groups; items where the documented evidence does not support the coded response; standardized tool scores that are inconsistent with the coded OASIS item; and homebound status documentation that does not meet the standards of CL-CA-005.
This policy establishes the complete Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A), the required completion standards for each checklist section, the documentation requirements for the completed review, and the escalation process when the review identifies issues that cannot be resolved before the OASIS completion deadline.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all authorized OASIS assessors, the OASIS Quality Reviewer, and the Director of Nursing. The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) is the operative document of this policy — no assessment shall be locked without the checklist being completed.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every OASIS assessment at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall undergo a structured pre-submission quality review using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) before the assessment is locked in the EHR. The review shall be conducted by the assessing RN as a self-review after completing all OASIS item selections and all supporting narrative documentation.
4.2 The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist is a required clinical record document — its completion shall be recorded in the EHR OASIS quality review module with the assessor's electronic signature and the date and time of completion. An OASIS assessment that is locked without a completed, authenticated checklist is a documentation compliance deficiency.
4.3 When the pre-submission quality review identifies a correctable issue — an item response that is not supported by documentation, an internal inconsistency, a missing required element — the assessor shall correct the issue before locking the assessment. Do not lock the assessment with known uncorrected issues.
4.4 When the pre-submission quality review identifies an issue that cannot be immediately resolved by the assessing RN — for example, an ambiguous clinical situation requiring Director of Nursing adjudication, or a missing document that requires clinical judgment about its absence — the assessor shall document the issue in the checklist, escalate to the Director of Nursing, and delay locking until the issue is resolved or the Director of Nursing authorizes locking with the documented limitation.
4.5 The OASIS Quality Reviewer's Level 2 review per CL-OA-002 shall include verification that the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist was completed for the reviewed assessment and that the checklist findings are consistent with the Level 2 reviewer's independent assessment of the assessment quality.
4.6 The pre-submission quality review is the assessor's responsibility and accountability. It is not a substitute for the OASIS Quality Reviewer's Level 2 review — both are required. The pre-submission review catches issues the assessor can self-identify; the Level 2 review provides independent expert validation.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review | The structured, checklist-driven review of a completed OASIS assessment conducted by the assessing RN before locking, using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) to verify completeness, internal consistency, evidence substantiation, and homebound documentation adequacy. |
| Default Value | The pre-populated or default response option that the EHR may apply to an OASIS item before the assessor makes a selection. An item left at its default value without a clinical basis for that value is not a valid assessment response. |
| Internal Inconsistency | A contradiction between two or more OASIS item responses within the same assessment that cannot simultaneously be true given the patient's clinical presentation — for example, coding a patient as requiring maximal assistance for all GG mobility items while coding them as having no pressure injuries, without clinical explanation. |
| Completeness Check | The verification that all OASIS items applicable to the current assessment time point have been addressed with a valid response — either a clinician-selected response or a documented not-applicable designation with clinical basis. |
| Evidence Check | The verification that the clinical narrative in the assessment contains documentation that supports the coded OASIS response for each item reviewed, per the substantiation standards of CL-OA-007. |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist | The structured form (Appendix A) that the assessing RN completes for every OASIS assessment before locking, systematically verifying quality criteria for each major OASIS item category. |

## 6. Pre-Submission Quality Review — Required Review Sections
The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) consists of the following five review sections, each addressing a distinct quality dimension:
### Section 1 — Completeness Check
Purpose: Verify that all applicable OASIS items for the current time point have been addressed with a clinician-selected response.
Required Actions:
Open the CMS OASIS-E2 item applicability table for the applicable time point (SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU, TRN, or DC).
For each applicable item, verify that a response has been selected and that the response is not a default value that was not reviewed.
For any item left blank, not applicable, or at a default value, verify that the clinical record contains a documented basis for that status (the patient's condition makes the item genuinely not applicable; the patient could not complete the required assessment).
Flag and correct any item that appears incomplete without a documented clinical basis.
Checklist Recording: Rate each item category as: ☐ Complete ☐ Incomplete — Issue Identified and Corrected ☐ Incomplete — Director of Nursing Consultation Required
### Section 2 — Internal Consistency Check
Purpose: Verify that logically related OASIS items produce a coherent clinical picture without internal contradictions.
Required Item-Pair Consistency Reviews:

| Item Pair | Consistency Check |
| --- | --- |
| GG0130 (Self-Care) and GG0170 (Mobility) | The overall pattern of self-care and mobility independence should be clinically coherent — a patient who requires maximal assistance for all self-care activities would typically also require assistance for most mobility activities, absent a specific clinical explanation for the discrepancy |
| M1700 (Cognitive Function / BIMS score) and M2020 (Oral Medication Management) | A patient with severe cognitive impairment (BIMS 0–7) would not be expected to independently manage complex oral medication regimens — a discrepancy between high cognitive impairment and high medication management independence requires clinical explanation |
| M1700 (Cognitive Function) and M1710/M1720 (Confusion/Anxiety frequency) | The frequency of confusion/anxiety behavioral items should be consistent with the overall cognitive function rating |
| GG mobility items and M1311 (Pressure Injury presence) | A patient with high GG mobility independence (independent ambulation, transfer) would not typically develop pressure injuries attributable to immobility — any pressure injury in a highly mobile patient requires documented clinical explanation |
| Respiratory severity items and GG0170 mobility activity items | A patient with the highest respiratory impairment (dyspnea at rest) would be expected to have significant GG mobility limitations — a highly mobile patient also coded as having severe resting dyspnea requires clinical documentation of how the patient achieves that mobility level despite the respiratory severity |

Checklist Recording: Rate each pair as: ☐ Consistent ☐ Inconsistency Identified and Resolved (resolution documented in narrative) ☐ Inconsistency — Director of Nursing Consultation Required
### Section 3 — Evidence Substantiation Check
Purpose: Verify that the clinical narrative contains documented evidence supporting the coded OASIS response for each high-risk item category, per CL-OA-007.
Required Evidence Checks:

| OASIS Item Category | Evidence Substantiation Verification |
| --- | --- |
| GG0130 Self-Care items | Narrative contains activity-specific observation descriptions for each sub-item coded (not general mobility statements) |
| GG0170 Mobility items | Narrative contains activity-specific observation descriptions including assistance level and environmental context |
| M1311–M1324 Pressure Injury items | Narrative contains direct wound observation documentation (NPIAP stage, measurements, wound bed, drainage, periwound) — dressing removal confirmed |
| M1340–M1342 Surgical Wound items | Narrative contains surgical wound observation documentation — wound type, stage, character |
| M1700 Cognitive Function | Narrative contains BIMS component scores (A, B, C) and total score — not just total; administration confirmed |
| M1730/M1750 Depressive Feelings | Narrative contains PHQ-2 item scores and total; PHQ-9 item scores and total if PHQ-2 ≥3 |
| M2001 Drug Regimen Review | Narrative documents review methodology, medications reviewed, issues found or not found |
| Homebound Status | Narrative documents both CMS homebound criteria with patient-specific functional language |
| Skilled Need | Narrative documents the clinical justification for each ordered skilled discipline |

Checklist Recording: For each item category: ☐ Adequate substantiation documented ☐ Substantiation gap identified and corrected ☐ Substantiation gap — Director of Nursing Consultation Required
### Section 4 — Standardized Tool Score Consistency Check
Purpose: Verify that standardized tool scores are documented correctly and map to the corresponding OASIS item response.
Required Score-to-Response Verifications:

| Tool | Verification Required |
| --- | --- |
| BIMS total score → M1700 | BIMS total (Component A + B + C = Total) maps to the correct M1700 response: 13–15 = Cognitively Intact; 8–12 = Moderately Impaired; 0–7 = Severely Impaired. Arithmetic verified. |
| PHQ-2 total → PHQ-9 required? | PHQ-2 total ≥3 requires PHQ-9 administration. If PHQ-2 ≥3 and PHQ-9 not documented, flag immediately. |
| PHQ-9 total → M1730/M1750 | PHQ-9 total maps to the correct M1730/M1750 response per CMS guidance. Arithmetic verified (sum of 9 items). |
| PHQ-9 Item 9 | If PHQ-9 Item 9 score ≥1, suicidality assessment documentation present in clinical record. |

Checklist Recording: For each tool: ☐ Score arithmetic correct; response mapping correct ☐ Arithmetic/mapping error identified and corrected ☐ PHQ-9 required but not administered — immediate action required before locking
### Section 5 — Look-Back Period and Time-Point Accuracy Check
Purpose: Verify that look-back periods were correctly applied and that the assessment reflects the correct OASIS time point.
Required Verifications:
Confirm the assessment time point code is correct for the clinical event (SOC, ROC, RECERT, FU, TRN, or DC).
For each look-back item category, verify that the look-back window was measured from the assessment date — not from the discharge date or any other reference date.
For post-hospitalization SOC/ROC assessments, verify that the look-back window correctly encompasses the inpatient period per CL-OA-010.
Verify that point-in-time items (GG items at SOC/ROC) reflect the patient's status at the assessment visit — not at any other time point.
For RECERT assessments, verify the assessment date falls within the Day 56–60 window.
Checklist Recording: For each verification: ☐ Confirmed ☐ Issue identified and corrected ☐ Issue requiring Director of Nursing consultation
## 7. Procedures
### 7.1 — Pre-Submission Review Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.1.1 | Assessing RN | After completing all OASIS item selections and all supporting narrative documentation, open the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) in the EHR. Do not lock the assessment before opening the checklist. | Before locking. |
| 7.1.2 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 1 (Completeness Check) by reviewing each applicable OASIS item for the current time point. Allow a minimum of 5 minutes for this section — it requires opening the CMS item applicability table and reviewing each item. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.3 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 2 (Internal Consistency Check) by reviewing each required item-pair. For each pair, look at both coded responses simultaneously and assess whether they produce a coherent clinical picture. Allow a minimum of 5 minutes for this section. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.4 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 3 (Evidence Substantiation Check) by opening the assessment narrative alongside the OASIS item responses and verifying that each high-risk item category has adequate narrative documentation. Allow a minimum of 10 minutes for this section — it is the most detailed review. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.5 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 4 (Standardized Tool Score Consistency Check) by re-calculating tool totals from the documented component scores and verifying that the calculated totals match the coded OASIS responses. Allow a minimum of 3 minutes for this section. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.6 | Assessing RN | Complete Section 5 (Look-Back Period and Time-Point Accuracy Check) by verifying time point code, look-back windows, and point-in-time application. Allow a minimum of 3 minutes. | During pre-submission review. |
| 7.1.7 | Assessing RN | Review the overall pre-submission quality status. If all sections are rated "Confirmed" or "Issue Identified and Corrected," sign and submit the checklist and proceed to locking. If any section has a "Director of Nursing Consultation Required" flag, notify the Director of Nursing before locking. | After all sections are completed. |
| 7.1.8 | Assessing RN | Lock the OASIS assessment immediately after submitting the checklist and, if required, receiving Director of Nursing authorization. Do not delay locking after the checklist is complete — unnecessary delay beyond the checklist completion creates additional operational target risk per CL-OA-001 and CL-OA-015. | Immediately after checklist submission and Director of Nursing authorization (if required). |

### 7.2 — Issue Resolution During Pre-Submission Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.2.1 | Assessing RN | When a correctable issue is identified during any checklist section: (a) correct the OASIS item response or the narrative documentation as appropriate; (b) re-verify the affected section of the checklist after correction; (c) document the issue and correction in the checklist issue field. | During the pre-submission review. |
| 7.2.2 | Assessing RN | When an issue requiring Director of Nursing consultation is identified: (a) document the issue in the checklist consultation field; (b) notify the Director of Nursing immediately by telephone or secure message; (c) do not lock the assessment pending Director of Nursing response. | Before locking; Director of Nursing notification immediately. |
| 7.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Upon notification of a consultation-required issue: respond within 4 hours during business hours or at the earliest practicable time outside business hours. Provide specific clinical adjudication guidance. Document the guidance provided in the EHR communication notes. | Within 4 hours during business hours. |

### 7.3 — OASIS Quality Reviewer Checklist Validation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7.3.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | During every Level 2 review per CL-OA-002: (a) verify that the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist is present in the EHR for the reviewed assessment; (b) review the checklist for completeness — all five sections completed; (c) assess whether any issues identified in the checklist were appropriately resolved; (d) independently verify Section 2 (internal consistency) and Section 3 (evidence substantiation) using the Quality Reviewer's own assessment. | Within the Level 2 review timeline. |
| 7.3.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | If the Level 2 review identifies issues not flagged in the pre-submission checklist, document the finding in the OASIS Quality Review Log and classify the assessment as having an inadequate pre-submission review — initiate the correction process per CL-OA-002 and provide targeted feedback to the assessing RN. | Within 24 hours of finding. |

### 7.4 — Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment locked without completed Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist | Director of Nursing identifies during monthly audit | Director of Nursing directs the assessing RN to retroactively complete the checklist. If the retroactive review identifies unresolved issues, initiate OASIS correction per CL-OA-002. Document corrective counseling. | Retroactive checklist within 5 business days; correction within 10 business days. |
| Pre-submission review consistently takes less than 15 minutes (below the section-minimum time allocations) | Director of Nursing identifies through EHR timestamp comparison | Director of Nursing assesses whether the review is being conducted with adequate rigor. If the timestamp analysis suggests the review is perfunctory (e.g., under 5 minutes total), provide corrective guidance and consider requiring supervised pre-submission reviews for the affected assessor. | Corrective guidance within 7 calendar days. |
| Pre-submission review identifies a patient safety concern (e.g., unidentified adverse drug reaction, new pressure injury not in the plan of care) | Assessing RN follows applicable clinical protocol simultaneously | Pre-submission review identification of a clinical concern triggers both the clinical response (physician notification per applicable policy) and the OASIS correction/update. The assessment should not be locked until the clinical response has been initiated and the OASIS reflects the current clinical picture. | Clinical response immediately; OASIS update within the applicable deadline. |

## 8. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (Appendix A) | Completed checklist for every OASIS assessment at every time point | Assessing RN | EHR — OASIS quality review module | Completed and authenticated before each OASIS lock; retained minimum 7 years |
| Director of Nursing consultation documentation | Communication notes for all consultation-required issues | Director of Nursing | EHR — communication notes | Within 4 hours of notification; retained minimum 7 years |

## 9. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 9.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist completed and authenticated before every OASIS lock | EHR quality review module completion log | ≥98% of locked assessments with completed, authenticated checklist |
| All five checklist sections completed for each assessment | Checklist completeness audit | ≥98% of checklists with all five sections completed |
| Issues identified in checklist are appropriately resolved before locking | OASIS Quality Reviewer Level 2 review finding correlation | ≥95% of issues identified in checklists have documented resolutions |
| Assessments with consultation-required flags are not locked before Director of Nursing authorization | EHR lock timestamp vs. Director of Nursing communication note timestamp | 100% |
| Level 2 review does not identify material issues absent from pre-submission checklist | Quality Review Log audit — new issues identified at Level 2 not present in pre-submission checklist | ≤5% of Level 2 reviews identify material issues not flagged in pre-submission checklist |

### 9.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting OASIS validation surveys will request evidence of the agency's OASIS quality assurance process. The Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist — when consistently completed and when it demonstrates a pattern of assessors actively identifying and resolving issues before submission — is direct evidence of a functioning OASIS quality governance program. An agency that cannot demonstrate a systematic pre-submission review process has no structural mechanism for preventing OASIS errors that are detectable before submission.
ADR auditors will look for evidence that errors that could have been caught before submission were not caught — particularly internal consistency errors (BIMS score inconsistent with M1700 coding) and substantiation gaps (GG items with no activity-specific observation documentation). These are precisely the errors a properly conducted pre-submission review should catch. When an ADR auditor finds them, the absence of a documented pre-submission review suggests the agency lacked the quality governance to prevent them.
### 9.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-submission review treated as a checkbox exercise without genuine item-by-item review | Errors that should be caught before submission are not caught; Level 2 review finds issues that were reviewable at pre-submission | Time allocation minimums in Section 6; Director of Nursing reviews checklist completion times in monthly audit |
| Section 4 (tool score consistency) skipped because assessor believes scores are correct | PHQ/BIMS scoring errors not caught; M1700/M1730 miscoding | Make Section 4 mandatory with required score recalculation; OASIS Quality Reviewer validates score recalculation at Level 2 |
| Assessor locks assessment before completing Section 3 (evidence substantiation) because the narrative feels adequate | Substantiation gaps not identified; OASIS locked without supporting narrative | EHR workflow requires Section 3 completion rating before lock button is enabled |
| No documentation that the checklist was completed — assessors sign but do not complete | No evidence of compliance with the review requirement | EHR checklist requires each section to be rated before the attestation signature can be applied |

## 11. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
11.1 All authorized OASIS assessors shall receive training on the Pre-Submission Quality Review process within their initial OASIS Competency Program and at each annual re-competency per CL-OA-003, including: the purpose and structure of each checklist section; the minimum time allocations for each section; the issue escalation process; and the consequences of locking an assessment without a completed checklist.
11.2 Training shall include a simulated pre-submission review exercise in which assessors complete the checklist for a case study OASIS assessment that intentionally contains issues in each of the five checklist sections — requiring assessors to identify the issues, document them, and apply the appropriate resolution.
11.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.
11.4 The Director of Nursing shall maintain training completion records for all authorized assessors and shall report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of any training deadline.
## 12. Version Control
12.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
12.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
12.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
12.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

### 1. Policy Header

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for developing, approving, implementing, and maintaining an individualized plan of care (POC) for every patient admitted to home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The plan of care is the foundational clinical document that authorizes, defines, and guides all services delivered to a patient during a certification period. It is simultaneously a clinical roadmap, a legal authorization for skilled services, and a billing instrument — any deficiency in its development, physician approval, or content directly compromises patient safety, regulatory compliance, and reimbursement integrity.
This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.60 — Condition of Participation: Care Planning, Coordination, and Quality of Care, which mandates that a plan of care be established and periodically reviewed by a physician for every patient receiving home health services. It also ensures compliance with CMS PDGM episode management requirements, OASIS data collection obligations, and the agency's documentation and billing alignment standards.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses (RNs) responsible for completing the comprehensive assessment and establishing the plan of care
All clinical disciplines contributing to the plan of care (PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA)
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
All intake and admissions staff who initiate the plan of care process
Physicians and allowed practitioners who review and approve plans of care
The Medical Records and Health Information staff
The Revenue Cycle team responsible for billing based on the approved plan of care
This policy applies at Start of Care (SOC), Resumption of Care (ROC), and Recertification (RECERT) for every patient served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It does not govern individual visit notes, which are governed by CL-CD-001, or OASIS-specific data collection requirements, which are governed by CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019.
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall establish a written, individualized plan of care for every patient admitted to home health services prior to or at the initiation of services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a).
4.2 The plan of care shall be developed by the registered nurse responsible for the patient's care in collaboration with the patient, the patient's caregiver(s), the patient's attending physician or allowed practitioner, and all clinical disciplines involved in the patient's care.
4.3 No skilled home health services shall be provided to a patient without a physician-approved plan of care. Verbal orders for services may be initiated prior to written physician signature, provided the verbal order is received, documented, and authenticated in compliance with policy CL-CP-004 (Verbal Order Receipt & Authentication).
4.4 The plan of care shall be signed and dated by the physician or allowed practitioner before the agency submits a claim for Medicare home health services. For initial certification periods, the physician must sign the plan of care — which may be the OASIS-generated CMS-485 or equivalent — within the timeframe required by CMS.
4.5 The plan of care shall contain all elements required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a), as defined in Section 5 of this policy and detailed in Appendix A.
4.6 The plan of care shall be patient-centered, based on the findings of the comprehensive assessment (CL-CA-001), and shall reflect the patient's goals, functional limitations, and individual clinical needs.
4.7 No services shall be provided that are not authorized by the plan of care and a corresponding physician order. Any service not reflected in the current plan of care requires a new or amended physician order before the service is rendered, except in clinical emergencies where safety requires immediate action followed by immediate physician notification per CL-CP-003.
4.8 The plan of care shall be reviewed, revised, and recertified at least every 60 calendar days and whenever a significant change in the patient's condition warrants modification, per policy CL-CP-002.
4.9 The physician-approved plan of care, the OASIS assessment, the physician orders, and all visit documentation must be internally consistent. Discrepancies between these documents constitute documentation integrity failures governed by policy CO-DC-004.
4.10 Only the most current physician-approved version of a patient's plan of care shall be operative. Superseded plan versions shall be retained in the clinical record but clearly marked as no longer active.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Plan of Care (POC) | The written document, established by the home health agency and approved by the physician, that specifies the patient's diagnosis, functional limitations, types and frequency of services to be furnished, medications, treatments, safety measures, and patient goals. Referred to in CMS documentation as the CMS-485 or Home Health Certification and Plan of Care. |
| Physician | A doctor of medicine (MD) or osteopathy (DO) legally authorized to practice medicine. For home health purposes, the physician responsible for signing the plan of care must not be employed by or have a financial relationship with the agency that would constitute a violation of the Stark Law, per 42 CFR § 424.22. |
| Allowed Practitioner | A nurse practitioner (NP), clinical nurse specialist (CNS), or physician assistant (PA) who is working in collaboration with a physician in accordance with state law, and who is authorized under 42 CFR § 424.22 to certify eligibility for home health services and approve the plan of care. |
| Certification Period | A period of not more than 60 calendar days during which the physician certifies that the patient is eligible for home health services. Each certification period requires a signed plan of care. |
| Start of Care (SOC) | The first billable visit made to a patient who has been admitted for a new episode of home health care. |
| Resumption of Care (ROC) | The first billable visit following a patient's return to the agency after an inpatient facility stay. |
| Recertification (RECERT) | The process of renewing a patient's plan of care for a subsequent 60-day certification period, based on a physician's determination that the patient continues to meet eligibility criteria and requires ongoing skilled services. |
| Verbal Order | An oral communication from a physician or allowed practitioner to a qualified clinician that authorizes a specific clinical action, governed by policy CL-CP-004. |
| CMS-485 | The Home Health Certification and Plan of Care form, or its electronic equivalent in the agency's EHR, that serves as the formal plan of care document for Medicare billing purposes. |
| PDGM | Patient-Driven Groupings Model — the Medicare home health prospective payment system that classifies patients into payment categories based on clinical grouping, functional level, comorbidity adjustments, and admission source, all of which are derived from the plan of care and OASIS assessment. |
| Homebound Status | The condition of a patient who has a condition due to an illness or injury that restricts their ability to leave home except with considerable effort, as defined in 42 CFR § 409.42(a). Homebound status must be certified by the physician and documented in the plan of care. |
| Individualized | Tailored to the specific needs, goals, diagnoses, functional limitations, and living situation of each patient, as opposed to a standardized or template-driven approach without patient-specific modifications. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Initiating the Plan of Care Process at Start of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Intake Staff / Administrator | Upon acceptance of a referral and determination that the patient meets admission criteria per OP-IM-002, assign the case to a qualified registered nurse for the comprehensive assessment and plan of care development. Ensure the patient's attending physician has been identified and contact information is documented in the intake record. | At the time of referral acceptance; assignment made no later than 1 business day before the scheduled SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Prior to the SOC visit, review all available referral documentation including hospital discharge summaries, physician orders, medication lists, recent laboratory results, and any therapy evaluations, to prepare for the comprehensive assessment. Do not pre-populate the plan of care with information that has not been verified through direct patient assessment. | Before the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Conduct the comprehensive assessment at the SOC visit in compliance with policy CL-CA-001, including completion of all required OASIS data elements per policies CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019. The SOC visit must occur within 48 hours of the referral or on the physician-ordered start date, whichever is earlier. | Within 48 hours of referral or on the physician-ordered start date. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | During or immediately following the SOC comprehensive assessment, develop the patient-specific plan of care incorporating: (a) all diagnoses, including the primary diagnosis and relevant secondary diagnoses supported by clinical documentation; (b) patient-specific functional limitations; (c) all skilled services ordered including discipline type, frequency, and duration; (d) medications including a complete medication list with dosages; (e) treatments and procedures; (f) safety measures; (g) patient goals — short-term and long-term, stated in measurable and patient-centered terms; (h) physician-ordered equipment and supplies; (i) patient/caregiver education needs and plan; (j) homebound status narrative. | Developed during or immediately following the SOC visit; documented in the EHR within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Collaborate with the patient and caregiver(s) in developing the plan of care. Document the patient's participation in goal-setting and any patient preferences, cultural considerations, or language access needs that affect the plan. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Identify all clinical disciplines needed based on the assessment findings. If additional disciplines are indicated (PT, OT, SLP, MSW), place orders per the physician referral or secure a verbal order per CL-CP-004 and document the referral to those disciplines within the plan of care. | Within 24 hours of the SOC assessment. |

#### 6.2 Required Elements of the Plan of Care
The plan of care for each patient shall contain, at minimum, all of the following elements as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a) and CMS billing requirements. Absence of any required element constitutes a documentation deficiency subject to correction per CO-DC-003.

| Required Element | Content Standard | Policy Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient identifying information | Full legal name, date of birth, Medicare/Medicaid number, address, emergency contact | CL-CA-001 |
| Attending physician | Name, NPI, address, telephone | CL-CP-003 |
| Certification period | Start and end dates of the 60-day episode | CL-CP-008 |
| Diagnoses | Primary diagnosis (the condition chiefly responsible for the patient's need for home health) and all relevant secondary diagnoses, coded to the highest level of specificity per ICD-10-CM | FN-CM-002 |
| Homebound status | Narrative description of the patient's homebound status with specific functional limitations | CL-CA-005 |
| Types and frequency of services | Each discipline ordered (RN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA), visit frequency per week or month, and estimated duration | CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-008 |
| Medications | Complete medication list including drug name, dose, route, frequency, and purpose | CL-SD-012 |
| Treatments and procedures | All skilled clinical interventions ordered (wound care, IV therapy, etc.) | CL-SD-010, CL-SD-011 |
| Safety measures | Environmental safety, fall risk precautions, high-risk medication monitoring | CL-SD-015, RM-PS-001 |
| Patient goals | Measurable short-term and long-term goals, patient-centered and time-bound | CL-CA-001 |
| Equipment and supplies | DME and supply items ordered | OP-SL-004 |
| Patient/caregiver education | Topics to be addressed and teaching plan | CL-SD-017 |
| Physician signature and date | Must be signed and dated by the certifying physician or allowed practitioner | CL-CP-003 |
| Prognosis | Physician's prognosis for restoration of normal health | 42 CFR § 484.60(a) |

#### 6.3 Physician Approval Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | Within 24 hours of finalizing the plan of care in the EHR, transmit the plan of care to the patient's certifying physician for review, approval, and signature. Transmission shall be via fax, secure electronic transmission, or physician portal. Document the date, method, and recipient of transmission in the clinical record. | Within 24 hours of POC finalization; documented at time of transmission. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | Initiate tracking of the pending physician signature in the agency's physician order tracking system per policy CL-CP-009. Log the date transmitted, the physician's name and fax/contact number, and the expected return date. | At the time of transmission. |
| 6.3.3 | Clinical Coordinator | If no signed plan of care is received within 7 calendar days of transmission, initiate the first follow-up contact. Document the follow-up attempt including date, time, method, and person contacted. | 7 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.4 | Clinical Coordinator | If no signed plan of care is received within 14 calendar days of transmission, escalate to the Director of Nursing for second-level follow-up. The Director of Nursing or designee shall contact the physician's office directly by telephone and document the conversation. | 14 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | If no signed plan of care is received within 21 calendar days of transmission despite documented follow-up, escalate to the Administrator. Assess whether continued services are appropriate pending physician signature. Document all escalation actions. | 21 calendar days after transmission without return. |
| 6.3.6 | Revenue Cycle / Director of Nursing | The agency shall not submit a final claim for a Medicare home health episode until a signed plan of care is on file for that episode. Verbal orders initiating care are permissible, but billing requires a signed plan of care. If the physician signature is not obtained, the episode is not billable and the Director of Nursing and Revenue Cycle Director must determine whether services should be discontinued. | Before claim submission for each episode. |
| 6.3.7 | Medical Records | File the signed plan of care in the patient's clinical record within 3 calendar days of receipt. Verify that the physician signature is dated, legible or accompanied by printed name and NPI, and covers the full certification period. Flag any unsigned, undated, or electronically unsigned plans of care for Director of Nursing review before filing. | Within 3 calendar days of receipt. |

#### 6.4 Multidisciplinary Coordination in Plan of Care Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Ensure that all disciplines providing services to the patient have reviewed the plan of care and that their discipline-specific goals, interventions, and visit frequencies are accurately reflected. No discipline shall provide services that conflict with or exceed what is authorized in the plan of care without a new physician order. | Within 48 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.4.2 | Each Clinical Discipline Provider | Upon receiving a referral for a new patient, review the plan of care within 24 hours of assignment. Confirm that the ordered services are within the discipline's scope of practice, are clinically appropriate based on the OASIS assessment and available records, and are supported by a current physician order. If any ordered service appears clinically inappropriate or outside scope, immediately contact the Director of Nursing. | Within 24 hours of assignment. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Serve as the primary coordinator for the patient's plan of care. Document all clinical communications regarding the plan of care in the patient's clinical record. Any discipline-specific addition, modification, or concern regarding the plan of care shall be communicated to the assigned RN, who will coordinate with the physician per CL-CP-003. | Ongoing throughout the certification period. |
| 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing | Conduct or ensure that a care coordination communication occurs among all disciplines involved in the patient's care no later than 14 calendar days after SOC for patients receiving three or more disciplines. The communication may occur via telephone, secure messaging, or a documented care conference. Document the date, participants, topics discussed, and any plan of care modifications agreed upon. | Within 14 calendar days of SOC for patients receiving three or more disciplines. |

#### 6.5 Patient and Caregiver Engagement in Plan of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, review the plan of care with the patient and caregiver(s) in plain language, ensuring they understand: (a) the services that will be provided and their frequency; (b) the goals of care; (c) their rights related to care decisions, including the right to refuse services; (d) how to contact the agency with questions or concerns; (e) safety measures specific to their condition and home environment. Provide the patient with a written copy of the plan of care or a plain-language summary in the patient's primary language. | During the SOC visit. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | Document the patient's and caregiver's understanding of and participation in the plan of care, including any expressed disagreements with specific goals or services, any modifications made based on patient preference (within physician-ordered parameters), and any language access services provided per OP-PA-003. | In the SOC visit note within 24 hours of the visit. |
| 6.5.3 | Assigned RN | If the patient or caregiver declines a specific ordered service, document the refusal per the agency's informed refusal process, notify the physician, and assess whether the refusal affects the patient's eligibility for continued home health services. | Immediately upon refusal; physician notification within 24 hours. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plan of care is incomplete or missing required elements at the time of the first billable visit | Assigned RN escalates to Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing reviews and requires completion before any claim is submitted. Services may continue if the verbal order is properly documented per CL-CP-004. | Completion required before claim submission. |
| Physician refuses to sign the plan of care as written | Assigned RN and Director of Nursing contact the physician | Director of Nursing engages the physician to resolve clinical disagreements. Modify the plan of care per the physician's direction if clinically appropriate. If the physician declines to certify the patient at all, initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006. | Resolution within 7 calendar days of refusal. |
| Patient refuses to participate in plan of care development | Assigned RN documents refusal and notifies Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing assesses whether the patient's capacity to refuse is intact. Engage the patient's legal representative if capacity is in question. Document refusal, actions taken, and outcome. | Immediate documentation; assessment within 24 hours. |
| Services are being delivered that are not reflected in the plan of care | Director of Nursing identifies the discrepancy | Stop non-authorized services immediately. Obtain a verbal or written physician order for any service that should have been included. Review for billing compliance with Revenue Cycle Director per CO-DC-004. Report to Compliance Officer if billing has already occurred. | Stop services immediately; order obtained within 24 hours; compliance review within 5 business days. |
| Plan of care is submitted to the physician but cannot be located in the record | Clinical Coordinator escalates to Director of Nursing | Conduct a full audit trail review in the EHR. If the plan of care was transmitted but not returned, re-transmit. If there is a gap in the audit trail, assess for data integrity concerns per CO-DC-001 and report to Compliance Officer. | Audit trail review within 3 business days of identification. |

| Physician follow-up documentation | Records of all follow-up contacts for pending signatures | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | EHR — orders tracking module | At each follow-up attempt; retained minimum 7 years |
| Patient/caregiver education and participation | Documentation in the SOC visit note of plan of care review with patient, patient's understanding, and any modifications | Assigned RN | EHR — visit note | Within 24 hours of SOC visit |
| Multidisciplinary care coordination | Documentation of care coordination communications per Section 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing / Assigned RN | EHR — care coordination notes | Within 14 calendar days of SOC for qualifying patients |

| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment of this policy by all personnel within scope (Appendix B) | Each individual (completion); Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of policy effective date, revision, or new hire |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans of care contain all required elements per 42 CFR § 484.60(a) | Monthly audit of a random sample of SOC plans of care using the Documentation Audit Tool (Appendix C) | ≥95% of audited plans contain all required elements; 100% target |
| Plans of care are physician-signed before claim submission | Cross-reference of billing records with physician signature dates in the EHR | Zero claims submitted without a signed plan of care on file |
| Plans of care are developed within 24 hours of SOC visit | Audit of POC finalization dates against SOC visit dates | ≥95% of SOC plans finalized within 24 hours of the SOC visit |
| Physician follow-up is documented for all unsigned plans | Review of the orders tracking module for plans pending signature longer than 7 days | All plans pending signature longer than 7 days have documented follow-up attempts |
| Patient participation in plan of care is documented | Review of SOC visit notes for patient engagement documentation | ≥95% of SOC visit notes document patient/caregiver participation in plan of care review |
| Plan of care is consistent with OASIS assessment and physician orders | Triangulation audit per CO-DC-004 | Zero tolerance for material inconsistencies between POC, OASIS, and orders on audited records |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60):
Evidence that a plan of care exists for every patient. Surveyors will request clinical records and verify that a written, physician-approved plan of care exists for each active patient and for each certification period of sampled past patients. Missing plans of care or unsigned plans are Condition-level deficiency risks.
Evidence that the plan of care contains all required elements. Surveyors will review plans of care for completeness per 42 CFR § 484.60(a). Commonly cited deficiencies include: missing homebound status narrative, vague or unmeasurable goals, incomplete medication lists, and visit frequencies that do not match delivered services.
Evidence that the plan of care is patient-centered and individualized. Surveyors distinguish between plans that are genuinely tailored to the patient and plans that appear to be templated without individualization. Cookie-cutter goal language (e.g., "patient will improve") without patient-specific metrics is a common deficiency.
Evidence of physician approval. Surveyors will verify physician signatures on plans of care and cross-reference with service dates to confirm that signed plans of care predate or accompany the services billed. Surveys will also verify that the certifying physician is eligible (not employed by or financially related to the agency in a prohibited manner).
Evidence that the plan of care is consistent with services delivered. Surveyors will compare ordered visit frequencies against actual visit delivery records. Significant and unexplained variances are cited as documentation integrity failures and potential False Claims Act concerns.
Evidence of patient participation. Surveyors may interview patients and caregivers about their knowledge of their plan of care and whether they were involved in developing their goals.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan of care developed by non-RN staff or templated without individualization | CMS deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.60; potential False Claims Act risk | Require RN development of all SOC plans of care; Director of Nursing conducts quality review of new SOC plans |
| Goals stated in non-measurable terms ("patient will improve ADLs") | Survey citation for inadequate plan of care; inability to demonstrate outcome achievement | Train all RNs on SMART goal-writing; use goal templates with required metrics |
| Services delivered that are not on the plan of care | Billing compliance risk; potential False Claims Act; survey deficiency | Implement visit authorization checking in scheduling system; audit monthly per CO-DC-004 |
| Physician signature obtained but not retained in clinical record | Missing documentation during survey; inability to support billing | Implement document receipt verification workflow; Director of Nursing reviews all unsigned episode records weekly |
| Plan of care not updated following significant change in patient condition | Clinical risk; documentation integrity failure | Train all clinicians on significant change criteria; Director of Nursing reviews mid-episode plan changes quarterly |
| Visit frequency on the plan of care does not match OASIS functional level | PDGM classification error; potential overpayment or underpayment; billing compliance risk | Conduct OASIS-to-POC consistency check at each SOC before claim submission per CO-DC-004 |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All registered nurses responsible for conducting SOC assessments and developing plans of care shall receive competency-validated training on plan of care development requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Training shall be conducted by the Director of Nursing or a qualified designee and shall include: (a) all required elements of the plan of care per 42 CFR § 484.60(a); (b) ICD-10 primary diagnosis selection for PDGM; (c) SMART goal-writing for home health; (d) physician order management and the verbal order process; (e) plan of care transmission and tracking; (f) common survey deficiencies and how to avoid them; (g) the agency's EHR plan of care workflow.
10.2 All other clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) shall receive orientation to plan of care processes relevant to their discipline-specific contributions within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) how to read and confirm the plan of care; (b) their obligation not to deliver services outside the plan of care; (c) how to initiate a discipline-specific order change request through the assigned RN.
10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/appointment.
10.4 The Director of Nursing shall verify training completion and competency for all RNs in plan of care development prior to their independently conducting SOC assessments. Competency shall be documented using the SOC Competency Assessment Tool (Appendix D).
### 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.
