## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the clinical standards, documentation requirements, competency expectations, and discharge criteria for speech-language pathology (SLP) services provided by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. SLP services in the home health setting address communication disorders (aphasia, dysarthria, apraxia, voice disorders), cognitive-linguistic deficits, swallowing disorders (dysphagia), and related safety and functional impairments. SLP is a qualifying skilled service under the Medicare home health benefit. This policy ensures that all SLP services comply with 42 CFR § 484.75, the California Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology Practice Act, and CMS coverage requirements.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all speech-language pathologists providing direct patient care, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, Clinical Coordinators, and Revenue Cycle staff verifying SLP documentation. Note: Speech-language pathology assistants (SLPAs) are not independently billable under Medicare home health and their use is subject to California licensing board restrictions and direct on-site supervision requirements.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 SLP services shall be provided only by speech-language pathologists holding a current California license issued by the Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology and Hearing Aid Dispensers Board per California BPC § 2530 et seq. and holding the Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology (CCC-SLP) from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), or meeting equivalent qualification standards per CMS requirements.
4.2 All SLP services shall be authorized by a physician order and reflected in the physician-approved plan of care per CL-CP-001 and CL-CP-003.
4.3 The SLP shall conduct an initial evaluation within 48 hours of receiving the patient referral, including: (a) review of the patient's medical history, current diagnoses, neurological history, and any imaging or diagnostic reports relevant to communication or swallowing function; (b) assessment of speech articulation, fluency, and voice; (c) language assessment including receptive and expressive language abilities; (d) cognitive-linguistic assessment including attention, memory, problem-solving, and executive function; (e) swallowing assessment including oral motor examination, clinical swallowing evaluation, and determination of whether an instrumental swallowing assessment (MBSS or FEES) is indicated; (f) identification of patient-specific, measurable, time-bound goals; (g) a recommended treatment plan including visit frequency, duration, diet texture and liquid consistency recommendations if applicable, and discharge criteria.
4.4 SLP visit documentation shall be completed within 24 hours and shall demonstrate the skilled nature of the service, patient response to treatment, and measurable progress.
4.5 The SLP shall conduct a re-evaluation at each recertification period, or more frequently when warranted by a significant change in the patient's condition, particularly any change in swallowing status or neurological function.
4.6 Discharge from SLP shall occur when: (a) the patient has met all SLP-specific goals; (b) the patient has plateaued and further skilled SLP will not result in meaningful improvement; (c) the physician orders discontinuation; or (d) the patient declines further services. The SLP shall document a discharge summary including final communication and swallowing status, goals achieved, and recommendations.
4.7 For patients with dysphagia, the SLP shall coordinate all diet texture and liquid consistency recommendations with the assigned RN, the physician, the caregiver, and any other disciplines involved in the patient's nutrition and hydration. All diet modifications must be ordered by the physician.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Aphasia | An acquired language disorder resulting from brain damage that affects the ability to produce and/or comprehend spoken and written language. |
| Dysarthria | A motor speech disorder caused by weakness, paralysis, or incoordination of the speech musculature. |
| Dysphagia | A swallowing disorder characterized by difficulty in oral preparation, oral transit, pharyngeal transit, or esophageal transit of food or liquid. |
| Cognitive-Linguistic Deficit | An impairment in cognitive processes (attention, memory, reasoning, executive function) that affects the patient's ability to communicate effectively and manage daily activities. |
| Clinical Swallowing Evaluation | A bedside/home-based evaluation of swallowing function conducted by the SLP using observation, trial swallows, and oral motor examination. |
| Instrumental Swallowing Assessment | A videofluoroscopic (MBSS) or fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES) conducted in a medical facility to visualize swallowing anatomy and physiology. |
| Diet Texture Modification | A physician-ordered change in the consistency of solid foods and/or liquids to reduce aspiration risk. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Initial SLP Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Speech-Language Pathologist | Review the plan of care, physician orders, OASIS assessment, and all available clinical documentation before the evaluation visit. | Before evaluation. |
| 6.1.2 | Speech-Language Pathologist | Conduct the initial evaluation in the patient's home, completing all elements in Section 4.3. Use standardized assessment tools appropriate to the patient's diagnoses (e.g., Boston Naming Test, WAB-R, BDAE, CLQT, MMSE or MoCA for cognitive screening, clinical swallowing protocol). | Within 48 hours of referral. |
| 6.1.3 | Speech-Language Pathologist | Establish measurable, time-bound goals in collaboration with the patient and caregiver. Goals shall be functionally relevant (e.g., "Patient will safely swallow thin liquids without coughing or wet vocal quality in 80% of trials within 4 weeks"). | During evaluation. |
| 6.1.4 | Speech-Language Pathologist | If the evaluation identifies dysphagia, immediately provide the patient, caregiver, and assigned RN with aspiration precautions and diet recommendations. Contact the physician within 24 hours to obtain orders for any diet texture or liquid consistency modifications. | Aspiration precautions immediately; physician contact within 24 hours. |
| 6.1.5 | Speech-Language Pathologist | If the evaluation reveals that the patient does not require skilled SLP services, document the finding and notify the physician and assigned RN within 24 hours. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.1.6 | Speech-Language Pathologist | Communicate evaluation findings, goals, and the treatment plan to the assigned RN and all other disciplines per CL-CP-005. | Within 48 hours. |

### 6.2 SLP Treatment Visits

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Speech-Language Pathologist | At each visit, document: (a) specific interventions performed (e.g., language therapy tasks, cognitive-linguistic exercises, swallowing exercises, compensatory strategy training, caregiver training); (b) the patient's response including accuracy percentages, cueing levels required, and trial performance data; (c) objective measurements demonstrating progress toward goals; (d) patient and caregiver education; (e) the plan for the next visit. | During each visit; documented within 24 hours. |
| 6.2.2 | Speech-Language Pathologist | For dysphagia patients, assess swallowing status at each visit and document: current diet texture and liquid consistency; patient compliance with diet modifications; any signs or symptoms of aspiration (coughing, wet vocal quality, temperature elevation, respiratory changes); and caregiver adherence to aspiration precautions. | At each visit for dysphagia patients. |
| 6.2.3 | Speech-Language Pathologist | If the patient is not progressing after a reasonable treatment period, conduct a re-evaluation. Notify the physician and assigned RN. | Re-evaluation within 2 weeks of identified non-progression. |

### 6.3 SLP Discharge

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Speech-Language Pathologist | Conduct a final evaluation at or near discharge. Document: final communication and swallowing status using the same assessment tools used at evaluation; comparison of initial and final status; goals achieved and unachieved; final diet recommendations; communication strategies for the caregiver; and recommendations for follow-up. | At the last SLP visit. |
| 6.3.2 | Speech-Language Pathologist | Notify the physician, assigned RN, and all other disciplines of SLP discharge and recommendations. For dysphagia patients, ensure the physician has current diet orders that will remain in effect after SLP discharge. | Within 24 hours of the final visit. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patient shows signs of aspiration pneumonia | SLP immediately notifies RN and physician | RN conducts urgent assessment; physician contacted for immediate medical evaluation; SLP modifies diet recommendations as indicated. | Immediate notification; assessment within 4 hours. |
| Physician orders diet upgrade against SLP clinical recommendation | SLP documents clinical rationale and concern; escalates to Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing facilitates a clinical discussion with the physician; document the physician's final decision and the SLP's clinical documentation of concern. | Discussion within 48 hours. |
| SLP documentation does not support skilled nature | Director of Nursing chart review | Documentation coaching; billing review. | Within 7 calendar days. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements
Same structure as previous discipline policies: initial evaluation, treatment visit notes, re-evaluation notes, discharge summary, and policy acknowledgment — all within 24 hours; retained minimum 7 years.
## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SLP evaluation completed within 48 hours | EHR audit | ≥95% |
| Visit notes include objective performance data (accuracy percentages, cueing levels) | Monthly chart audit | ≥95% |
| Diet modification orders obtained for all dysphagia patients | Audit of physician orders vs. SLP diet recommendations | 100% — zero unordered diet modifications |
| Discharge summaries include functional comparison | Discharge documentation audit | ≥95% |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SLP goals that are impairment-based rather than functional | Claim denial | Train SLPs on functional, measurable goal-writing |
| Diet recommendations given without physician orders | Scope issue; liability | Policy requires physician order for all diet modifications |
| Swallowing assessments without standardized documentation | Survey deficiency | Standardized clinical swallowing evaluation form |

## 9. References

| Citation | Relevance |
| --- | --- |
| 42 CFR § 484.75 | Skilled professional services requirements |
| California BPC § 2530 et seq. | SLP Practice Act |
| CMS Home Health Benefit Manual, Chapter 7, § 40.2 | SLP coverage requirements under Medicare |

### Cross-Referenced Agency Policies
CL-CP-001, CL-CP-003, CL-CP-005, CL-SD-008, CL-CD-001, CL-CD-004, CL-SD-012 (medication management — swallowing considerations).

10.1 All SLPs shall receive training on agency-specific SLP service requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually.
10.2 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days.

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the scope, referral criteria, clinical standards, and documentation requirements for medical social work (MSW) services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Medical social work in home health addresses the psychosocial, emotional, financial, environmental, and community resource needs that affect the patient's ability to participate in and benefit from the medical plan of care. MSW services are a Medicare-covered home health service under 42 CFR § 484.75 when they are necessary to resolve social or emotional problems that are expected to impede the effective treatment of the patient's medical condition. MSW is not a qualifying skilled service for home health admission — it may be provided only in conjunction with a qualifying skilled service (nursing, PT, OT, or SLP).
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all medical social workers (MSWs) providing direct patient services, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, assigned RNs making MSW referrals, and Revenue Cycle staff verifying MSW documentation.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 MSW services shall be provided only by individuals holding a master's degree in social work (MSW) from a Council on Social Work Education (CSWE) accredited program, or a doctoral degree in social work, and who meet the qualifications defined in 42 CFR § 484.115(d).
4.2 MSW services shall be authorized by a physician order and reflected in the plan of care per CL-CP-001 and CL-CP-003. An RN or other discipline identifying a psychosocial need shall request a physician order for MSW services.
4.3 Referral criteria for MSW services include but are not limited to: (a) psychosocial factors interfering with the patient's medical plan of care (depression, anxiety, caregiver stress, social isolation, family conflict); (b) financial barriers to care (inability to afford medications, equipment, or supplies); (c) need for community resource linkage (transportation, meal programs, financial assistance, adult protective services, support groups); (d) advanced care planning needs (advance directive discussions, end-of-life planning, hospice referral counseling); (e) abuse, neglect, or exploitation concerns requiring psychosocial assessment and mandatory reporting per CL-PR-006; (f) substance abuse concerns; (g) grief and bereavement counseling needs.
4.4 The MSW shall conduct a psychosocial assessment within 48 hours of receiving the referral, including: (a) the patient's emotional and psychological status; (b) the patient's social support system; (c) financial status and barriers; (d) community resource needs; (e) advance directive status; (f) caregiver stress and coping; (g) safety concerns including abuse, neglect, or exploitation indicators; (h) cultural and spiritual considerations affecting care.
4.5 MSW visit documentation shall be completed within 24 hours and shall demonstrate the clinical necessity of the social work intervention and its relationship to the medical plan of care. MSW documentation that reads as non-medical counseling or general social conversation does not support Medicare coverage.
4.6 The MSW shall serve as the primary coordinator for community resource referrals per CL-CP-005. All referrals shall be documented with the resource identified, the reason for referral, the date, and the outcome.
4.7 Discharge from MSW services shall occur when: (a) the psychosocial goals have been met; (b) the community resource linkages have been established; (c) the psychosocial barriers to the medical plan of care have been resolved or mitigated; (d) the qualifying skilled service has been discharged; or (e) the patient declines further MSW services.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Psychosocial Assessment | A comprehensive evaluation of the patient's emotional, psychological, social, financial, and environmental factors that affect their ability to participate in and benefit from the medical plan of care. |
| Community Resource Linkage | The process of connecting a patient and/or caregiver with external services and support systems that address identified psychosocial needs. |
| Caregiver Stress Assessment | An evaluation of the caregiver's emotional well-being, coping capacity, support system, and ability to continue in the caregiver role. |
| Advance Care Planning | The process of discussing and documenting the patient's wishes regarding future medical treatment decisions, including advance directives, healthcare proxy, and end-of-life preferences. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 MSW Referral and Initial Assessment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN / Any Discipline | Identify psychosocial needs during patient visits. Document the identified need and request a physician order for MSW referral per CL-CP-003. | Within 24 hours of identifying the need. |
| 6.1.2 | Medical Social Worker | Upon receiving the referral, review the patient's clinical record, plan of care, and referral information. | Before the assessment visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Medical Social Worker | Conduct the psychosocial assessment in the patient's home per Section 4.4. Use validated screening tools as appropriate (PHQ-9 for depression, GAD-7 for anxiety, Zarit Burden Interview for caregiver stress). | Within 48 hours of referral. |
| 6.1.4 | Medical Social Worker | Develop MSW-specific goals in collaboration with the patient and caregiver. Goals shall be measurable, time-bound, and directly linked to the patient's medical plan of care (e.g., "Patient will be connected with Meals on Wheels within 7 calendar days to ensure adequate nutrition supporting wound healing"). | During the assessment visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Medical Social Worker | Communicate findings and recommendations to the assigned RN, Director of Nursing, and physician as indicated per CL-CP-005. If the assessment reveals abuse, neglect, or exploitation concerns, follow the mandatory reporting procedures of CL-PR-006 immediately. | Within 24 hours of assessment; abuse reports immediately per CL-PR-006. |

### 6.2 MSW Treatment Visits

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Medical Social Worker | At each visit, document: (a) the psychosocial intervention provided; (b) the patient's and caregiver's response; (c) community resources explored, referrals made, and referral outcomes; (d) progress toward each MSW goal; (e) the plan for the next visit. | Within 24 hours of each visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Medical Social Worker | Ensure all community resource referrals are documented with: the resource, contact information, the reason for referral, the date, the outcome, and any follow-up needed. | At the time of each referral. |
| 6.2.3 | Medical Social Worker | If the patient's psychosocial situation worsens or new barriers emerge, notify the assigned RN and physician and assess whether additional interventions or plan modifications are needed per CL-CP-002. | Within 24 hours of identifying a new barrier or worsening situation. |

### 6.3 MSW Discharge

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Medical Social Worker | At discharge, document: final psychosocial status; goals achieved and unachieved; community resources established; recommendations for ongoing support; and any advance directive documentation completed. | At or within 24 hours of the final MSW visit. |
| 6.3.2 | Medical Social Worker | Notify the assigned RN and physician of MSW discharge and recommendations. | Within 24 hours. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation | MSW follows CL-PR-006 mandatory reporting | Immediate report to the appropriate state agency; Director of Nursing notification within 2 hours. | Immediate. |
| Patient in acute psychiatric crisis | MSW contacts 911 if imminent danger; otherwise contacts physician and Director of Nursing | Ensure patient safety; coordinate with mental health crisis resources; document all actions. | Immediate for safety; physician notification within 4 hours. |
| Community resources unavailable or patient ineligible | MSW documents barrier and explores alternatives | Identify at least one alternative; if none available, notify Director of Nursing and document the gap in the care record. | Within 5 business days. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements
Same structure as previous policies: initial psychosocial assessment, treatment visit notes, community resource referral documentation, discharge summary, and policy acknowledgment — within 24 hours; retained minimum 7 years.
## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MSW assessment completed within 48 hours of referral | EHR audit | ≥95% |
| Visit notes demonstrate clinical necessity linked to the medical plan of care | Monthly chart audit | ≥95% |
| All community resource referrals documented | Referral documentation audit | ≥95% |
| MSW services only provided when a qualifying skilled service is active | Cross-reference MSW visits with active skilled service episodes | 100% compliance |

# CL-SD-006 — Home Health Aide Services & Supervision
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-006 |
| Policy Title | Home Health Aide Services & Supervision |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the service delivery standards, supervision requirements, and documentation expectations for home health aide (HHA) services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Home health aide services are a Medicare-covered service available only in conjunction with a qualifying skilled service and only when the patient requires personal care assistance as part of the physician-approved plan of care. The HHA provides hands-on personal care, simple health-related services, and assistance with activities that support the skilled care plan — but does not perform skilled clinical services, medication administration, or clinical assessments. The CMS Conditions of Participation impose the most prescriptive supervision requirements on HHA services of any home health discipline, and non-compliance with HHA supervision requirements is one of the most commonly cited deficiencies in CMS surveys. This policy implements 42 CFR § 484.80 — Condition of Participation: Home Health Aide Services.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all home health aides providing direct patient care, all RNs providing HHA supervision, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, Clinical Coordinators managing HHA scheduling, and Operations staff coordinating HHA assignments.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 HHA services shall be provided only by individuals who have completed a home health aide training program meeting the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.80(b) and have passed a competency evaluation per 42 CFR § 484.80(c) and agency policy CL-SD-007.
4.2 HHA services shall be authorized by a physician order and reflected in the plan of care, which shall specify: (a) the type of personal care services to be provided; (b) the frequency and duration of HHA visits; (c) any specific clinical parameters the HHA must observe and report (e.g., skin checks, intake/output monitoring, vital signs — if trained and competency-validated).
4.3 Each patient receiving HHA services shall have a written HHA care plan (also called an HHA assignment sheet or HHA task list) developed by the assigned RN that specifies, for each visit: (a) the specific tasks the HHA is authorized to perform for this patient; (b) the sequence of tasks if clinically relevant; (c) any precautions, safety measures, or clinical observations to make and report; (d) parameters for when to contact the RN immediately (e.g., skin breakdown, vital sign abnormalities, patient complaints, behavioral changes).
4.4 A registered nurse shall make a supervisory visit to the patient's home to observe and assess the HHA's provision of care no less frequently than every 14 calendar days, as required by 42 CFR § 484.80(h). The supervisory visit shall be made while the HHA is providing care, so the RN can directly observe the aide's skills, interaction with the patient, and compliance with the HHA care plan. At minimum every other supervisory visit (i.e., every 28 days), the RN supervisory visit must be conducted on-site with the HHA present.
4.5 The RN supervisory visit shall include: (a) direct observation of the HHA performing assigned tasks; (b) assessment of the patient's satisfaction with HHA services; (c) assessment of whether the HHA care plan remains appropriate; (d) assessment of the HHA's competency in assigned tasks; (e) documentation of the supervisory visit findings, any corrective guidance provided, and any changes to the HHA care plan.
4.6 If the HHA's primary supervising discipline is a therapist (when therapy is the only qualifying skilled service), the therapist shall conduct the supervisory visits per the same 14-day schedule, but an RN shall also make a supervisory visit at least once every 60 calendar days per 42 CFR § 484.80(h)(2).
4.7 The HHA shall not perform any of the following: (a) medication administration; (b) sterile procedures; (c) clinical assessments; (d) any task not assigned in the written HHA care plan; (e) any task for which the HHA has not been trained and competency-validated.
4.8 The HHA shall immediately report to the assigned RN any of the following: (a) changes in the patient's condition; (b) patient complaints; (c) refusal of care by the patient; (d) safety concerns in the home; (e) inability to complete assigned tasks; (f) any incident or injury during the visit.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Home Health Aide (HHA) | A trained and competency-validated individual who provides personal care and simple health-related services to patients in the home under the supervision of a registered nurse or therapist. |
| HHA Care Plan | A written, patient-specific assignment document prepared by the supervising RN that specifies the tasks the HHA is authorized and required to perform at each visit. |
| Supervisory Visit | A visit conducted by a registered nurse (or, in certain circumstances, a therapist) to the patient's home to observe and evaluate the HHA's performance while the HHA is delivering care. |
| Personal Care Services | Hands-on assistance with activities of daily living including bathing, grooming, dressing, toileting, eating, mobility assistance, and light meal preparation directly related to the patient's care plan. |
| Simple Health-Related Services | Non-skilled tasks that may be delegated to the HHA, such as taking vital signs (when competency-validated), assisting with exercises as directed by a therapist, and observing and reporting changes in the patient's condition. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 HHA Assignment and Care Plan Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | When HHA services are ordered in the plan of care, develop a written, patient-specific HHA care plan specifying all tasks per Section 4.3. The HHA care plan shall be consistent with and derived from the physician-approved plan of care. | Within 24 hours of HHA service initiation. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Provide the assigned HHA with the written HHA care plan before the first HHA visit. Review the care plan verbally with the HHA to ensure understanding. Document the orientation. | Before the first HHA visit. |
| 6.1.3 | Clinical Coordinator | Schedule HHA visits per the frequency and duration specified in the physician-approved plan of care. Schedule RN supervisory visits to coincide with HHA visits per the 14-day supervision schedule. | At the time of HHA assignment. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Update the HHA care plan whenever the patient's plan of care changes, new tasks are added, tasks are removed, or the patient's condition changes. Provide the updated care plan to the HHA and document the update. | Within 24 hours of a plan change. |

### 6.2 HHA Visit Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Home Health Aide | At each visit, verify patient identity, perform hand hygiene, review the HHA care plan, and provide only the services authorized in the care plan. | At each visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Home Health Aide | Complete the HHA visit documentation (paper or EHR) including: (a) date and time of the visit; (b) tasks performed; (c) patient's response and condition observations; (d) vital signs if assigned; (e) any concerns, changes, or patient complaints; (f) time in and time out. | At or immediately after each visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Home Health Aide | Immediately contact the assigned RN (or on-call nurse if after hours) if any reportable event occurs per Section 4.8. Do not attempt to manage clinical situations outside the scope of HHA training. | Immediately upon occurrence. |

### 6.3 RN Supervisory Visits

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Track the 14-day supervisory visit schedule for every patient receiving HHA services. Generate alerts when a supervisory visit is due within 3 calendar days. | Ongoing; alerts generated at Day 11. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | Conduct the RN supervisory visit at the patient's home while the HHA is providing care, per the 14-day schedule. Complete all supervisory elements per Section 4.5. | Every 14 calendar days. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Document the supervisory visit in the patient's clinical record using the HHA Supervisory Visit Form (Appendix A). The form shall include: date, patient name, HHA name, tasks observed, patient satisfaction, competency assessment, any corrective guidance provided, and any care plan changes. | Within 24 hours of the supervisory visit. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN | If the supervisory visit reveals deficiencies in the HHA's performance — including failure to follow the care plan, inadequate infection control, or patient complaints — provide immediate on-site corrective guidance, document the deficiency and the corrective action, and notify the Director of Nursing. If the deficiency is serious, remove the HHA from the patient's care and reassign. | Immediate corrective guidance on-site; Director of Nursing notification within 24 hours; reassignment immediately for serious deficiencies. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | Review HHA supervisory visit documentation monthly. Identify patterns of deficiency across HHAs and initiate targeted retraining or disciplinary action per HR-ER-002 as warranted. | Monthly review. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14-day supervisory visit not completed on schedule | Clinical Coordinator alerts Director of Nursing at Day 15 | Director of Nursing directs the assigned RN to complete the supervisory visit immediately. If the lapse is greater than 21 days, document the gap and report to Compliance Officer as a CMS compliance issue. | Supervisory visit within 24 hours of identification; compliance reporting within 48 hours for lapses >21 days. |
| HHA performs tasks not on the HHA care plan | RN identifies during supervisory visit or chart review | Remove the HHA from the patient if the task was outside their scope. Provide retraining. Document corrective action. Assess for patient harm. | Immediate removal if scope violation; retraining within 7 days. |
| Patient complains about HHA care | RN or Director of Nursing receives complaint | Investigate within 48 hours. Conduct an unscheduled supervisory visit. Reassign HHA if complaint is substantiated. Document investigation and outcome. | Investigation within 48 hours. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Written HHA care plan | Patient-specific task assignment | Assigned RN | EHR — HHA care plan | Before first HHA visit; updated as needed |
| HHA visit documentation | Task completion record per visit | HHA | EHR or paper HHA visit log | At or immediately after each visit |
| RN supervisory visit documentation | Supervisory Visit Form (Appendix A) | Assigned RN | EHR — supervisory notes | Within 24 hours; every 14 days |
| Corrective guidance documentation | Record of deficiencies identified and corrective actions | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | EHR — supervisory notes and HR file | At the time of the event |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Written HHA care plan on file for every patient receiving HHA services | Monthly audit of HHA patient records | 100% — zero patients without a current HHA care plan |
| RN supervisory visits completed every 14 calendar days | Supervisory visit tracking log | ≥98% of supervisory visits within the 14-day window |
| At least every other supervisory visit conducted with the HHA present | Supervisory visit log review | 100% compliance with alternating on-site HHA observation |
| HHA visit documentation completed for every visit | HHA documentation audit | ≥98% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors under Tag G270 (42 CFR § 484.80) will specifically: (a) review the 14-day supervisory visit schedule for compliance; (b) verify that written HHA care plans exist for every patient; (c) interview patients about HHA service quality; (d) interview HHAs about their understanding of the care plan and their reporting obligations; (e) verify that supervisory visits are conducted while the HHA is present. HHA supervision non-compliance is one of the top 5 most cited deficiencies nationally.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supervisory visits conducted but not while HHA is present | CMS deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.80(h) | Schedule supervisory visits to coincide with HHA visit times; EHR alert system |
| No written HHA care plan — RN relies on verbal instructions | Condition-level deficiency; HHA performing unauthorized tasks | Require HHA care plan in EHR before HHA visit can be scheduled |
| HHA documentation missing or incomplete | Inability to demonstrate services were provided; billing risk | Require HHA visit log submission within 24 hours; Director of Nursing audits weekly |
| Supervisory visit exceeds 14-day window | CMS deficiency | Automated tracking with Day 11 alert |

# CL-SD-007 — Home Health Aide Competency Evaluation
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-007 |
| Policy Title | Home Health Aide Competency Evaluation |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the initial and ongoing competency evaluation requirements for home health aides (HHAs) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. per 42 CFR § 484.80(c). CMS requires that home health aides demonstrate competency in each of the skills listed in 42 CFR § 484.80(c)(1) before they are permitted to provide direct patient care, and that competency is re-evaluated at minimum annually. Competency evaluation failures that are not identified and remediated represent direct patient safety risks and are a frequent citation in CMS surveys. This policy ensures that every HHA employed by or contracted with the agency has been rigorously evaluated, that competency is maintained through ongoing assessment, and that HHAs who do not meet competency standards are not permitted to deliver patient care until remediation is complete.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all home health aides (employees and contracted staff), the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, all RNs conducting HHA competency evaluations, and HR staff managing competency records in personnel files per HR-WM-007.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every HHA shall complete an initial competency evaluation before being assigned to provide patient care. The initial evaluation shall cover all skill areas required by 42 CFR § 484.80(c)(1) including but not limited to: (a) communication skills; (b) observation, reporting, and documentation of patient status and services delivered; (c) reading and recording temperature, pulse, and respiration; (d) basic infection control procedures; (e) maintenance of a clean, safe, and healthy environment; (f) recognizing emergencies and knowledge of emergency procedures; (g) safe transfer and ambulation techniques; (h) range of motion and positioning; (i) adequate nutrition and fluid intake; (j) personal care services including bathing, skin care, hair care, nail care, oral hygiene, toileting, dressing, and feeding; (k) safe operation of medical equipment as assigned; (l) sensitivity to the patient's rights.
4.2 The competency evaluation shall include both a written (or oral) knowledge assessment and a direct observation of skills performance (return demonstration) conducted by a registered nurse. A passing score of 80% on the knowledge assessment and satisfactory performance on all return demonstration skills is required.
4.3 Competency shall be re-evaluated at minimum annually (every 12 calendar months) for every HHA. The annual re-evaluation shall include direct observation of skills in the home setting (during a supervisory visit) or in a simulated clinical setting, and shall cover all skill areas in Section 4.1.
4.4 If an HHA fails any component of the initial or annual competency evaluation, the HHA shall be immediately removed from patient care for the failed skill area, shall receive remediation training, and shall be re-evaluated within 14 calendar days. The HHA shall not resume patient care in the failed skill area until competency is demonstrated.
4.5 In addition to the annual evaluation, an HHA shall receive a targeted competency evaluation whenever: (a) a supervisory visit reveals a performance deficiency per CL-SD-006; (b) a patient complaint regarding the HHA's care quality is substantiated; (c) a new task is assigned that the HHA has not previously been evaluated on; (d) an incident or adverse event related to the HHA's care occurs.
4.6 All competency evaluation results — initial and ongoing — shall be documented and maintained in the HHA's personnel file per HR-WM-005 and HR-WM-007.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Competency Evaluation | A structured assessment process that measures an HHA's knowledge and skill performance against defined clinical standards. |
| Return Demonstration | A skills performance assessment in which the HHA physically demonstrates a procedure or task while being observed and evaluated by a registered nurse. |
| Remediation | Targeted retraining provided to an HHA who has failed a competency evaluation component, followed by reassessment. |
| Competency Record | The documented results of all competency evaluations, including skill areas assessed, pass/fail determinations, remediation provided, and re-evaluation outcomes. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Initial Competency Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | HR Director / Director of Nursing | Upon hire, verify that the HHA has completed a state-approved HHA training program or equivalent per 42 CFR § 484.80(b). Verify training certificate and document in the personnel file. | At hire, before patient care assignment. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing / Designated RN Evaluator | Administer the written (or oral) knowledge assessment covering all skill areas in Section 4.1. Score the assessment. A passing score is ≥80%. | At hire, before patient care assignment. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing / Designated RN Evaluator | Conduct the return demonstration skills evaluation. The HHA must demonstrate satisfactory performance on each skill area listed in Section 4.1. Use the HHA Competency Evaluation Checklist (Appendix A). Document pass/fail for each skill. | At hire, before patient care assignment. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Review the evaluation results. If the HHA passes all components, certify the HHA as competent and authorize patient care assignments. If the HHA fails any component, proceed to Section 6.3 (Remediation). | Within 24 hours of evaluation completion. |
| 6.1.5 | HR Director | File the completed competency evaluation documentation in the HHA's personnel file per HR-WM-007. | Within 5 business days of evaluation. |

### 6.2 Annual Competency Re-Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Director of Nursing | Maintain a competency evaluation tracking calendar for all HHAs. Generate alerts 30 calendar days before each HHA's annual re-evaluation due date. | Ongoing; alerts at 30 days before due date. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing / Designated RN Evaluator | Conduct the annual competency re-evaluation including: (a) written or oral knowledge assessment; (b) direct observation of skills in the home setting during a supervisory visit, or in a simulated clinical setting. Evaluate all skill areas in Section 4.1. | Before the annual evaluation due date. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Review the re-evaluation results. Certify the HHA as competent if all components are passed. If any component is failed, proceed to Section 6.3. | Within 24 hours of evaluation. |
| 6.2.4 | HR Director | File the completed annual re-evaluation in the HHA's personnel file. | Within 5 business days. |

### 6.3 Remediation Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Immediately remove the HHA from patient care responsibilities for any failed skill area. Notify the HHA and document the removal. | Immediately upon evaluation failure. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing / Designated RN Trainer | Provide targeted remediation training focused on the failed skill area(s). The remediation shall include: (a) review of the correct procedure; (b) demonstration by the trainer; (c) supervised practice by the HHA. Document the remediation training date, content, and trainer. | Within 7 calendar days of evaluation failure. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing / Designated RN Evaluator | Re-evaluate the HHA on the failed skill area(s) using the same evaluation criteria as the initial assessment. | Within 14 calendar days of the original evaluation failure. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing | If the HHA passes the re-evaluation, reinstate the HHA for patient care and document the reinstatement. If the HHA fails the re-evaluation a second time, the Director of Nursing and HR Director shall determine whether continued employment is appropriate per HR-ER-002. | Within 24 hours of re-evaluation; employment determination within 7 calendar days of second failure. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HHA's annual evaluation is overdue | Director of Nursing is alerted at due date | Director of Nursing immediately removes the HHA from patient care until the evaluation is completed. | HHA removed from care immediately; evaluation within 7 calendar days. |
| HHA fails the same skill area repeatedly (3+ times) | Director of Nursing and HR Director | Termination evaluation per HR-ER-002. HHA is not permitted to deliver patient care in the failed skill area. | Employment determination within 7 calendar days. |
| New task is added to a patient's HHA care plan that the HHA has not been evaluated on | Assigned RN identifies | RN provides task-specific training and evaluates competency before the HHA performs the new task. Document. | Before the HHA performs the new task. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial competency evaluation | Completed HHA Competency Evaluation Checklist (Appendix A) | Director of Nursing / RN Evaluator | Personnel file | At hire; retained minimum 7 years |
| Annual competency re-evaluation | Completed re-evaluation checklist | Director of Nursing / RN Evaluator | Personnel file | Annually; retained minimum 7 years |
| Remediation training documentation | Training record including date, content, trainer | Director of Nursing / RN Trainer | Personnel file | At the time of remediation |
| Competency tracking calendar | Master tracking log for all HHAs | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing supervisory file | Updated continuously |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial competency evaluation completed before patient care | Personnel file audit | 100% — zero HHAs assigned before evaluation |
| Annual re-evaluations completed within the 12-month window | Competency tracking calendar audit | 100% |
| Failed evaluations result in immediate removal from affected patient care | Incident and corrective action documentation | 100% |
| Competency records maintained in personnel files | HR audit per HR-WM-007 | 100% |

### What Surveyors Will Look For
CMS surveyors under Tag G276 (42 CFR § 484.80(c)) will request HHA personnel files and verify: (a) that an initial competency evaluation was completed before the HHA began patient care; (b) that the evaluation covers all required skill areas; (c) that annual re-evaluations are documented; (d) that failed evaluations resulted in remediation and re-evaluation before return to care. Surveyors may also directly observe HHA skills during the survey and ask HHAs to describe their training and evaluation experience.

# CL-SD-008 — Clinical Supervision & Oversight
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-008 |
| Policy Title | Clinical Supervision & Oversight |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the requirements for clinical supervision of all professional and paraprofessional staff providing patient care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Clinical supervision is the systematic process by which the agency ensures that all clinical services are delivered safely, competently, and in accordance with the plan of care, professional standards, and regulatory requirements. This policy establishes the supervision structure, frequency, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures for the oversight of RNs, LVNs, PTs, PTAs, OTs, COTAs, SLPs, MSWs, and HHAs. It implements the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.75 (skilled professional services) and 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide services) as they relate to clinical supervision.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, all clinical supervisors (RNs, PTs, OTs), all supervised staff (LVNs, PTAs, COTAs, HHAs), and all professional staff (RNs, PTs, OTs, SLPs, MSWs) subject to administrative and clinical oversight.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager is responsible for the oversight and supervision of all clinical services provided by the agency, as required by 42 CFR § 484.115(b). The Director of Nursing shall be a registered nurse who is currently licensed in California, meets the CMS qualification requirements, and has the authority and accountability to ensure the clinical quality and regulatory compliance of all services.
4.2 The supervision structure shall operate at three levels:
Level 1 — Director of Nursing Oversight: The Director of Nursing provides enterprise-level clinical oversight of all disciplines and clinical functions, including: review of clinical outcomes, quality indicators, documentation compliance, and survey readiness.
Level 2 — Discipline-Specific Professional Supervision: Licensed professionals (PTs, OTs) supervise their respective assistants (PTAs, COTAs) per discipline-specific practice act requirements. RNs supervise LVNs. These supervisory relationships are defined in the discipline-specific service policies (CL-SD-001 through CL-SD-007).
Level 3 — HHA Supervision: RNs (or therapists, when applicable) supervise HHAs per the 14-day supervisory visit schedule defined in CL-SD-006.
4.3 The Director of Nursing shall conduct a supervisory review of each clinical discipline at minimum monthly, covering: (a) documentation quality and timeliness; (b) plan of care adherence; (c) visit frequency compliance; (d) clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction; (e) competency concerns identified.
4.4 The Director of Nursing shall conduct a direct on-site supervisory visit with each clinician at minimum once during their first 60 days of employment and at least annually thereafter. For clinicians with identified performance concerns, the Director of Nursing shall increase the frequency of supervisory visits to no less than monthly until the concern is resolved.
4.5 All supervisory activities shall be documented including: the date, supervisor name, staff member supervised, observations made, findings, any corrective guidance provided, and any follow-up actions required.
4.6 If a supervisor identifies a clinical practice deficiency that poses a risk to patient safety, the supervisor shall: (a) immediately address the safety concern; (b) remove the staff member from the clinical situation if warranted; (c) report the event to the Director of Nursing within 4 hours; (d) initiate incident reporting per RM-ER-002 if patient harm has occurred or was narrowly avoided.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Clinical Supervision | The ongoing process of overseeing, evaluating, and directing the clinical work of staff to ensure safe, competent, and compliant patient care delivery. |
| Supervisory Visit | An on-site visit by a supervisor to observe, assess, and evaluate a staff member's clinical performance during patient care delivery. |
| Administrative Supervision | Oversight of non-clinical aspects of a staff member's performance including scheduling compliance, documentation timeliness, and policy adherence. |
| Clinical Oversight | The Director of Nursing's enterprise-level responsibility for monitoring and ensuring the quality, safety, and compliance of all clinical operations. |
| Corrective Guidance | Verbal or written instruction provided by a supervisor to address identified deficiencies in a staff member's clinical practice. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Director of Nursing Monthly Clinical Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a monthly review of each clinical discipline covering: documentation quality (random chart audit of ≥5% of each discipline's visit notes), plan of care adherence, visit frequency compliance (comparing delivered visits to ordered visits), clinical outcome indicators, patient complaint trending, and competency evaluation status. | Monthly. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | Document findings in a Monthly Clinical Supervision Report. Identify discipline-specific trends, individual performance concerns, and system-level issues. Assign corrective actions with responsible parties and timelines. | Within 5 business days of the review period end. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | Present summary findings to the Administrator and QAPI Committee at least quarterly per QA-PG-003. | Quarterly. |

### 6.2 New Employee Clinical Supervision

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Director of Nursing | Assign every new clinical employee a preceptor or supervisor for the first 60 days. The preceptor shall be a licensed professional in the same discipline with at least 2 years of home health experience. | At hire. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing / Preceptor | Conduct at least one on-site supervisory visit (joint home visit with the new employee and preceptor) within the first 30 days of employment. | Within the first 30 days. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a 60-day competency review including chart review, preceptor feedback, and a direct supervisory visit. Determine whether the employee is approved for independent practice or requires extended supervision. Document the determination. | At Day 60 of employment. |

### 6.3 Ongoing Professional Staff Supervision

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct at minimum one direct on-site supervisory visit with each professional clinician (RN, PT, OT, SLP, MSW) annually. The visit shall include observation of the clinician's assessment technique, patient interaction, clinical judgment, and documentation practices. | Annually; more frequently for performance concerns. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Document the supervisory visit using the Clinical Supervisory Visit Form (Appendix A), including: strengths identified, areas for improvement, corrective guidance provided, and follow-up actions. | Within 24 hours of the visit. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | For clinicians with identified performance concerns, increase the supervisory frequency to at minimum monthly and develop a Performance Improvement Plan in coordination with HR per HR-ER-001. | Increased supervision begins within 7 calendar days of concern identification. |

### 6.4 LVN, PTA, and COTA Supervision

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Supervising RN (for LVNs), Supervising PT (for PTAs), Supervising OT (for COTAs) | Provide discipline-specific supervision per the schedules defined in CL-SD-001 (LVN), CL-SD-002 (PTA), and CL-SD-003 (COTA). Document all supervisory reviews and visits. | Per the schedules in the respective policies. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Audit discipline-specific supervisory compliance monthly. Identify any supervisory lapses and direct immediate corrective action. | Monthly. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supervisory visit reveals unsafe clinical practice | Supervisor immediately intervenes | Remove staff from patient care if safety risk is immediate. Report to Director of Nursing within 4 hours. File incident report per RM-ER-002 if patient harm occurred or was narrowly avoided. Director of Nursing determines next steps including potential suspension pending investigation per HR-ER-002. | Immediate intervention; Director of Nursing notification within 4 hours. |
| Staff member refuses supervisory oversight | Director of Nursing notified | Director of Nursing counsels the staff member on the supervisory requirement. If refusal persists, initiate disciplinary action per HR-ER-002. | Counseling within 48 hours; disciplinary action if refusal continues. |
| Supervisory documentation is missing or incomplete | Director of Nursing identifies during audit | Director of Nursing directs the supervisor to complete the documentation retroactively with a late-entry notation per CO-DC-003. Counsels the supervisor on documentation requirements. | Documentation completed within 7 calendar days; counseling within 5 business days. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly Clinical Supervision Report | Director of Nursing monthly review findings | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing supervisory file | Monthly; retained minimum 7 years |
| New employee supervisory visit | On-site supervisory visit documentation | Director of Nursing / Preceptor | EHR and personnel file | Within first 30 days; retained minimum 7 years |
| 60-day competency review | Competency determination documentation | Director of Nursing | Personnel file | At Day 60 |
| Annual professional staff supervisory visit | Clinical Supervisory Visit Form (Appendix A) | Director of Nursing | EHR and personnel file | Annually; retained minimum 7 years |
| Discipline-specific supervisory documentation | Per CL-SD-001, CL-SD-002, CL-SD-003, CL-SD-006 | Supervising clinician | EHR — supervisory notes | Per respective policy schedule |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly clinical supervision report completed | Director of Nursing file audit | 100% — completed monthly |
| All new employees have on-site supervisory visit within 30 days | Personnel file audit | 100% |
| Annual supervisory visits completed for all professional staff | Supervisory visit tracking log | 100% |
| All discipline-specific supervisory schedules maintained | Monthly audit per discipline | ≥98% |

10.1 The Director of Nursing shall receive training on clinical supervision and oversight requirements at hire and annually.
10.2 All supervisors shall receive training on their supervisory obligations per this policy and the applicable discipline-specific policy at hire and annually.

# CL-SD-009 — Telehealth & Remote Monitoring Services
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-SD-009 |
| Policy Title | Telehealth & Remote Monitoring Services |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | SD — Service Delivery |
| Classification Tier | RECOMMENDED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the standards for the delivery, documentation, and oversight of telehealth services and remote patient monitoring (RPM) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Telehealth and RPM technologies represent supplemental tools that can enhance patient monitoring, improve clinical outcomes, support earlier intervention, and reduce unnecessary hospitalizations — but they do not replace in-person skilled visits. Under current CMS rules, telehealth encounters are not counted as billable home health visits for Medicare payment purposes (though this may evolve with future CMS rulemaking). This policy ensures that telehealth services are used appropriately to complement the plan of care, are properly documented, and do not substitute for required in-person visits.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all clinical staff using telehealth or RPM technology with patients, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, IT staff supporting telehealth platforms, and Operations staff managing telehealth scheduling.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Telehealth services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. include video visits, telephone encounters, and remote patient monitoring (e.g., automated transmission of vital signs, weight, blood glucose, oxygen saturation) used as supplements to the physician-approved plan of care.
4.2 Telehealth encounters shall not be used as a substitute for required in-person skilled visits. The agency shall ensure that all visits counted for Medicare billing purposes are in-person visits conducted in the patient's home. Telehealth encounters may supplement — but not replace — the visit frequencies specified in the plan of care.
4.3 All telehealth services shall be authorized by a physician order, reflected in the plan of care, and documented in the patient's clinical record. The plan of care shall specify the type of telehealth service, frequency, clinical parameters to be monitored, and the responsible clinician.
4.4 Patient consent for telehealth services shall be obtained and documented before initiating telehealth. The consent shall address: (a) the nature of telehealth services; (b) how the patient's data will be transmitted, stored, and used; (c) the patient's right to refuse telehealth and receive in-person services instead; (d) that telehealth does not replace in-person emergency services and the patient should call 911 in an emergency.
4.5 All telehealth technology used by the agency shall comply with HIPAA security requirements per CO-HP-002. Only agency-approved, encrypted platforms shall be used for video visits or data transmission. Consumer-grade, non-encrypted platforms (e.g., standard SMS, non-HIPAA-compliant video apps) shall not be used for clinical communications involving PHI.
4.6 RPM data shall be reviewed by the assigned clinician at minimum daily for actively monitored patients, or per the frequency specified in the plan of care. Clinically significant data (vital signs outside defined parameters, weight changes indicating fluid retention, blood glucose outside target range) shall trigger a same-day clinical response including patient contact, physician notification, and visit scheduling as clinically indicated.
4.7 The Director of Nursing shall ensure that all clinicians using telehealth are trained on the technology, documentation requirements, and clinical protocols specific to telehealth encounters.
4.8 Telehealth and RPM services shall be integrated into the agency's QAPI program per QA-PG-001, with outcome metrics tracked including: patient engagement, alert response times, hospitalization rates for RPM patients, and patient satisfaction.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Telehealth | The use of telecommunications technology to deliver clinical services remotely, including video visits and telephone encounters, as a supplement to in-person care. |
| Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) | The use of electronic devices to collect and transmit patient physiological data (vital signs, weight, blood glucose, oxygen saturation) from the patient's home to the agency for clinical review. |
| Video Visit | A live, synchronous audio-visual encounter between a clinician and a patient conducted via a HIPAA-compliant telehealth platform. |
| Telephone Encounter | A clinical interaction conducted by telephone between a clinician and a patient, typically for follow-up, symptom assessment, or care coordination. |
| Alert Threshold | A predefined clinical parameter (e.g., systolic BP >180, weight gain >3 lbs in 24 hours) that, when exceeded, triggers a clinical response protocol. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Patient Enrollment in Telehealth / RPM

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | Assess the patient's appropriateness for telehealth and/or RPM based on: (a) clinical condition and monitoring needs; (b) patient's or caregiver's ability to use the technology; (c) availability of reliable internet or cellular service; (d) patient's willingness to participate. | At SOC or when telehealth is indicated. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Obtain and document the patient's informed consent for telehealth services using the Telehealth Consent Form (Appendix A). | Before initiating telehealth. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Obtain a physician order for telehealth and/or RPM services per CL-CP-003. | Before initiating telehealth. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN / IT Support | Set up the telehealth and/or RPM equipment in the patient's home. Provide training to the patient and caregiver on how to use the equipment. Document the training and the patient's demonstrated competency. | During an in-person visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Establish patient-specific alert thresholds in the RPM platform based on the physician's orders and the patient's clinical parameters. | At the time of RPM setup. |

### 6.2 Telehealth Visit Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned Clinician | Conduct telehealth visits per the plan of care schedule using the agency-approved HIPAA-compliant platform. | Per plan of care. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned Clinician | Document the telehealth encounter in the patient's EHR within 24 hours including: (a) date, time, and duration of the encounter; (b) platform used; (c) clinical assessment findings (within the limitations of the telehealth modality); (d) patient's reported symptoms and status; (e) interventions provided (education, medication review, care coordination); (f) plan for follow-up. | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned Clinician | Clearly note in the documentation that the encounter was conducted via telehealth and is not counted as an in-person billable visit. | In the visit note. |

### 6.3 RPM Data Review and Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned Clinician | Review RPM data at minimum daily for actively monitored patients. Document the review. | Daily or per the plan of care. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned Clinician | When RPM data exceeds the established alert threshold, contact the patient by telephone within 2 hours to assess the clinical situation. Document the contact and findings. | Within 2 hours of alert. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned Clinician | If the RPM alert indicates a clinically significant change, notify the physician per CL-CP-005, schedule an in-person visit if clinically warranted, and initiate a plan of care modification per CL-CP-002 if indicated. | Same day as alert. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned Clinician | If the patient fails to transmit RPM data for 2 consecutive days without notification, contact the patient by telephone to assess the situation. If the patient is unreachable, schedule an in-person visit. | By the end of the 2nd day of non-transmission. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patient unable to use telehealth technology | Assigned RN assesses alternatives | Provide additional training or involve caregiver. If technology cannot be managed, discontinue telehealth and rely on in-person visits only. Notify physician. | Within 7 calendar days. |
| RPM data reveals a critical clinical value (e.g., BP >200/120, SpO2 <85%) | Assigned Clinician contacts patient and physician immediately | Instruct the patient to call 911 if emergency is indicated. Arrange an immediate in-person visit if non-emergent but critical. | Immediate contact. |
| HIPAA breach via telehealth platform | Report per CO-HP-003 | Suspend use of the affected platform. Complete breach assessment per CO-HP-003. Notify IT Director. | Platform suspended immediately; breach assessment within 24 hours. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Telehealth consent | Telehealth Consent Form (Appendix A) | Assigned RN | EHR — consent forms | Before initiating telehealth |
| Telehealth visit note | Encounter documentation per Section 6.2.2 | Assigned Clinician | EHR — clinical notes | Within 24 hours |
| RPM daily data review | Documentation of daily data review and any actions | Assigned Clinician | EHR — RPM monitoring notes | Daily; retained minimum 7 years |
| RPM alert response documentation | Documentation of alert, patient contact, and clinical actions | Assigned Clinician | EHR — clinical notes | Same day as alert |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Telehealth consent on file for all telehealth patients | Chart audit | 100% |
| Telehealth encounters not billed as in-person visits | Billing audit cross-referencing telehealth notes with claims | Zero telehealth encounters billed as in-person visits |
| RPM data reviewed daily for monitored patients | RPM platform review logs | ≥95% of days with documented review |
| Alert response within 2 hours | RPM alert log with response timestamps | ≥95% |

## 9. References

| Citation | Relevance |
| --- | --- |
| 42 CFR § 484.60 | Plan of care — telehealth must be reflected in the plan of care |
| CMS Home Health Final Rule CY2025 | Current CMS guidance on telehealth in home health (non-billable as visits) |
| HIPAA Security Rule | Telehealth platform security requirements |
| California Telehealth Advancement Act (BPC § 2290.5) | California telehealth practice requirements |

### Cross-Referenced Agency Policies
CL-CP-001, CL-CP-003, CL-CP-005, CO-HP-002, CO-HP-003, IT-SC-003, QA-PG-001.
## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All clinicians using telehealth shall receive training on the agency-approved platform, documentation requirements, and clinical protocols before conducting telehealth encounters.
10.2 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days.
