# CL-CP-007 — Transfer & Referral Procedures
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CP-007 |
| Policy Title | Transfer & Referral Procedures |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for transferring patients from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to inpatient facilities (hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, long-term acute care hospitals), to other home health agencies, to hospice programs, and for receiving incoming transfers from other care settings. Transfer is a high-risk transition event that directly affects patient safety, clinical continuity, OASIS data integrity, billing compliance, and quality measure performance. An improperly executed transfer — where clinical information is incomplete, the receiving facility is not informed of the patient's current clinical status and medications, or the transfer OASIS is not completed — results in fragmented care, medication errors, preventable readmissions, and regulatory deficiencies. This policy ensures that every transfer is clinically coordinated, documented with the required clinical summary, accompanied by a warm handoff to the receiving provider, and compliant with CMS OASIS transfer assessment requirements, 42 CFR § 484.60 (care coordination), and the agency's documentation and billing alignment standards.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses managing active patient caseloads
All clinical disciplines involved in the patient's care at the time of transfer
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
Clinical Coordinators managing transfer scheduling and OASIS documentation
Medical Records staff managing transfer documentation
Revenue Cycle staff managing episode billing affected by transfers
Operations staff coordinating with receiving facilities
The attending physician who must be notified of and, where applicable, order the transfer
This policy governs all outgoing transfers from home health to another care setting and all incoming transfers (resumption of care) from an inpatient setting back to home health. It does not govern discharge (CL-CP-006) unless the transfer constitutes a permanent discharge from home health services.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 When a patient is transferred from home health to an inpatient facility, the agency shall ensure that: (a) the attending physician is notified and, where clinically appropriate, orders or approves the transfer; (b) a comprehensive clinical summary is prepared and transmitted to the receiving facility; (c) a warm handoff (direct clinician-to-clinician communication) occurs with the receiving care team; (d) the transfer OASIS assessment is completed within CMS-required timeframes; (e) the patient's medication list, active diagnoses, current plan of care, and advance directive status are communicated to the receiving facility; (f) the patient and caregiver are informed of the transfer and the reason for it.
4.2 The clinical transfer summary shall include, at minimum: (a) the patient's current diagnoses and relevant medical history; (b) the current, reconciled medication list including recent changes; (c) the reason for transfer; (d) the patient's functional status at the time of transfer; (e) all active treatments and interventions; (f) relevant laboratory and diagnostic results; (g) advance directive status; (h) the attending physician's name and contact information; (i) allergies and adverse drug reactions; (j) the patient's emergency contact information; (k) any known infection or transmission-based precaution status.
4.3 When a patient returns to home health services following an inpatient facility stay, the agency shall treat the return as a Resumption of Care (ROC) event requiring: (a) a new comprehensive assessment including all applicable OASIS items; (b) a medication reconciliation per CL-SD-013; (c) an updated plan of care reflecting the patient's post-facility clinical status; (d) physician orders for resumed services; (e) review and update of all clinical disciplines involved in the patient's care.
4.4 Transfers to other home health agencies shall be coordinated to ensure continuity of care, including transmission of the complete clinical record (or a comprehensive summary with the patient's consent) and direct communication with the receiving agency's clinical leadership.
4.5 Transfers to hospice shall be coordinated per CL-SD-023 and shall include advance directive review, physician discussion regarding prognosis, and patient/caregiver education regarding the hospice benefit.
4.6 All transfers — inpatient, inter-agency, and hospice — shall be documented in the patient's clinical record with the date, time, reason, receiving facility or agency, clinical summary transmitted, warm handoff documentation, and OASIS completion status.
4.7 The transfer OASIS shall be completed on the day of transfer or within the CMS-defined timeframe, and transmitted to the OASIS database per CL-CA-003. Failure to complete the transfer OASIS affects quality measure calculation and billing integrity.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Transfer to Inpatient Facility | A patient move from home health services to an inpatient setting (hospital, SNF, IRF, LTACH) where the patient is admitted as an inpatient. For OASIS and billing purposes, this is distinct from an ED visit that does not result in inpatient admission. |
| Resumption of Care (ROC) | The first billable visit following a patient's return to home health after an inpatient facility stay. ROC requires a new comprehensive assessment and OASIS completion. |
| Transfer OASIS | The OASIS assessment completed at the time a patient is transferred to an inpatient facility, documenting the patient's clinical and functional status at the time of transfer. |
| Warm Handoff | A care transition in which a member of the sending care team directly communicates — by telephone or in person — with a member of the receiving care team to transfer patient care information, as distinct from a written record transfer alone. |
| Clinical Transfer Summary | A comprehensive written document prepared by the agency summarizing the patient's clinical status, active treatments, medications, and relevant history for the receiving care provider. |
| Inter-Agency Transfer | A transfer of a patient's home health services from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to another home health agency, typically due to relocation, patient preference, or service area limitations. |
| Emergency Department Visit Without Admission | A patient visit to the emergency department that does not result in inpatient admission. This is not a transfer for OASIS purposes but must be documented and may require a significant change assessment. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Transfer to Inpatient Facility

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN / Any Clinician | When a patient requires transfer to an inpatient facility — whether due to clinical deterioration, emergent medical need, physician order, or patient/caregiver request — immediately notify the attending physician (if the physician has not already ordered the transfer) and the Director of Nursing. If the transfer is emergent, call 911 first, then notify the physician and Director of Nursing. | Immediately upon identification of transfer need; physician notification within 1 hour for non-emergent transfers. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Prepare the Clinical Transfer Summary (Appendix A) including all elements defined in Section 4.2. The summary shall be generated from the patient's current clinical record and shall reflect the patient's status as of the transfer date. | Before or at the time of transfer; no later than 24 hours after transfer for emergent transfers where pre-transfer summary was not possible. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Conduct a warm handoff with the receiving facility by contacting the receiving nurse, admissions coordinator, or emergency department clinician by telephone. Communicate: (a) the patient's name and identifying information; (b) the reason for transfer; (c) the patient's current clinical status; (d) current medications including recent changes; (e) advance directive status; (f) any transmission-based precaution status; (g) allergies. Document the warm handoff including the date, time, name of the receiving clinician, and information communicated. | At the time of transfer or as soon as the receiving facility is identified. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN / Medical Records | Transmit the Clinical Transfer Summary to the receiving facility by fax, secure electronic transmission, or hand delivery (if the patient is being transported with agency staff present). Document the method and date of transmission. | At the time of transfer; confirmed receipt documented within 24 hours. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Notify all other disciplines involved in the patient's care that the patient has been transferred. Document the notifications. | Within 24 hours of transfer. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Notify the patient's emergency contact and caregiver of the transfer, the receiving facility, and the reason for transfer. Document the notification. | Within 24 hours of transfer; at the time of transfer for planned transfers. |
| 6.1.7 | Assigned RN | Complete the transfer OASIS assessment per CMS requirements. The transfer OASIS shall document the patient's clinical and functional status at the time of transfer, not at the time of the last visit. If the clinician was not present at the time of transfer, the OASIS shall be based on the best available clinical information from the most recent visit and any information obtained from the patient, caregiver, or receiving facility. | On the date of transfer or within CMS-defined completion timeframe; transmitted per CL-CA-003. |
| 6.1.8 | Revenue Cycle | Assess the billing implications of the transfer — determine whether the episode is complete, whether a final claim can be submitted, and whether the transfer affects PDGM payment grouping. Coordinate with the Director of Nursing to ensure all required documentation is on file before claim submission. | Within 5 business days of transfer. |

### 6.2 Resumption of Care (ROC) Following Inpatient Stay

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Clinical Coordinator / Operations | Upon notification that the patient has been discharged from the inpatient facility and is returning to home health services, schedule the ROC visit with the assigned RN within 48 hours of the patient's return home (or per physician order if sooner). | ROC visit within 48 hours of return home. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | Before the ROC visit, obtain the inpatient facility's discharge summary, discharge medication list, and any pending follow-up orders. If the discharge summary is not yet available, contact the facility directly and document the request. | Before the ROC visit; facility contact within 24 hours if documents unavailable. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN | At the ROC visit, conduct a comprehensive assessment including all required OASIS data elements for the ROC time point per CL-CA-001 and CL-OA-001. Assess the patient's current clinical status, compare to pre-transfer status, and identify any new diagnoses, medication changes, or functional changes resulting from the inpatient stay. | At the ROC visit. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | Perform a complete medication reconciliation per CL-SD-013, comparing the facility discharge medication list against the patient's pre-transfer medication list and the patient's actual medications at home. Report all unintentional discrepancies to the physician within 24 hours. | At the ROC visit; physician notification within 24 hours for discrepancies. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN | Update the plan of care to reflect the patient's post-facility clinical status, any new diagnoses, medication changes, new or modified services, and updated goals. Obtain physician orders for all changes per CL-CP-003. | Within 24 hours of the ROC visit. |
| 6.2.6 | Assigned RN | Confirm the patient has a scheduled follow-up appointment with the attending physician within 7–14 days of discharge (or per facility/CMS recommendation). If no appointment is scheduled, assist with scheduling and document. | At the ROC visit. |
| 6.2.7 | Assigned RN | Notify all disciplines involved in the patient's care of the ROC, the updated plan of care, and any changes to their ordered services. | Within 48 hours of the ROC visit. |

### 6.3 Transfer to Another Home Health Agency (Inter-Agency Transfer)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing / Assigned RN | When a patient is being transferred to another home health agency (due to relocation, patient preference, or service area limitations), coordinate with the receiving agency's clinical leadership to ensure a smooth transition. Obtain the patient's written consent (or verbal consent documented per CL-PR-003) to share clinical records with the receiving agency. | As soon as the transfer decision is made. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN / Medical Records | Prepare and transmit to the receiving agency: (a) a comprehensive clinical summary including current plan of care, medication list, active diagnoses, functional status, and current goals; (b) the most recent OASIS assessment; (c) all active physician orders; (d) relevant visit notes from the past 30 calendar days; (e) advance directive documentation; (f) any other records requested by the receiving agency with patient consent. | Before the patient's first visit with the receiving agency; at minimum 3 business days before the intended transfer date. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | Conduct a warm handoff with the receiving agency's assigned clinician. Communicate the patient's current clinical status, active concerns, discharge trajectory, and any care coordination issues. Document the communication. | Before the transfer effective date. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN | Complete the discharge OASIS for the patient's episode with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., documenting the patient's status at the time of transfer. | Per CMS OASIS timing requirements. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | Notify the attending physician that the patient is transferring to another agency, providing the receiving agency's name and contact information. | Within 24 hours of the transfer. |

### 6.4 Transfer to Hospice

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN / Director of Nursing | When a patient's clinical trajectory indicates that the patient may benefit from hospice services, initiate a goals-of-care discussion with the patient, caregiver, and attending physician per CL-SD-023. Document the discussion and the patient's and physician's decisions. | When clinically indicated. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | If the patient and physician agree to hospice referral, coordinate the referral with the hospice provider including: (a) the patient's clinical summary; (b) the physician's prognosis and certification of terminal illness (if applicable); (c) current medication list; (d) advance directive documentation; (e) the patient's and caregiver's preferences. | Within 48 hours of the decision to refer. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Provide the patient and caregiver with education regarding: (a) the hospice benefit, including what services are and are not covered; (b) the difference between home health and hospice; (c) the patient's right to revoke hospice and return to curative care; (d) the election process. Document the education per CL-SD-017. | At the time of the referral discussion. |
| 6.4.4 | Assigned RN | Complete the discharge OASIS and discharge summary for the home health episode. Discharge from home health is effective on the date of hospice election. | Per CMS OASIS timing requirements. |
| 6.4.5 | Assigned RN | Conduct a warm handoff with the hospice agency's admitting clinician. Communicate the patient's clinical status, current symptoms, medication management, and caregiver situation. Document the communication. | Before or on the date of hospice admission. |

### 6.5 Emergency Department Visits Without Admission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Assigned RN | When the agency becomes aware that a patient has visited the emergency department but was not admitted as an inpatient, document the ED visit in the clinical record including: date, reason, facility, and outcome. | Within 24 hours of becoming aware. |
| 6.5.2 | Assigned RN | Contact the patient within 24 hours of the ED visit to assess the patient's current status, obtain the ED discharge instructions, and perform a medication reconciliation if medications were changed. | Within 24 hours of becoming aware of the ED visit. |
| 6.5.3 | Assigned RN | Assess whether the ED visit warrants a significant change in condition assessment, a plan of care modification per CL-CP-002, or a physician notification per CL-CP-005. | Within 24 hours of patient contact. |
| 6.5.4 | Assigned RN | Note: An ED visit without inpatient admission does not trigger a transfer OASIS. The patient remains on the agency's active caseload. However, the ED visit must be documented and clinically addressed. | N/A — no transfer OASIS required. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Transfer occurs but Clinical Transfer Summary not transmitted to the receiving facility | Director of Nursing identifies during review | Director of Nursing directs the assigned RN to complete and transmit the summary immediately. If the patient has already been admitted, contact the facility to transmit. Document the late transmission. | Summary transmitted within 24 hours of identification. |
| Transfer OASIS not completed within required timeframe | Director of Nursing identifies via OASIS tracking | Director of Nursing directs completion based on the best available clinical information. Consult Compliance Officer regarding billing implications. | OASIS completed within 48 hours of identification. |
| Patient transferred to inpatient facility but agency not notified until days later | Assigned RN or Operations discovers the gap | Contact the facility to obtain admission date and clinical information. Complete the transfer OASIS retroactively based on available information. Assess billing impact. Director of Nursing reviews for process improvement. | Transfer documentation completed within 72 hours of discovery. |
| Receiving home health agency does not acknowledge receipt of transfer records | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing contacts the receiving agency directly. Re-transmits records if needed. Documents all communication attempts. | Follow-up within 48 hours. |
| Patient returns from inpatient stay but ROC visit not scheduled within 48 hours | Director of Nursing identifies | Director of Nursing schedules an immediate ROC visit. Assesses the reason for the delay (notification failure, scheduling error). Implements corrective action to prevent recurrence. | ROC visit within 24 hours of identification. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical Transfer Summary | Comprehensive summary per Section 4.2 (Appendix A) | Assigned RN | EHR — transfer documentation | At or before transfer; within 24 hours for emergent transfers |
| Warm handoff documentation | Record of verbal communication with receiving provider | Assigned RN | EHR — communication notes | At the time of transfer |
| Transfer OASIS | OASIS assessment at the time of transfer | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS module | Per CMS timing requirements |
| ROC comprehensive assessment | Full OASIS assessment at resumption of care | Assigned RN | EHR — OASIS module | At the ROC visit |
| Medication reconciliation at ROC | Medication Reconciliation Worksheet per CL-SD-013 | Assigned RN | EHR — medication reconciliation module | At the ROC visit |
| Updated plan of care at ROC | Plan of care reflecting post-facility status | Assigned RN | EHR — plan of care | Within 24 hours of the ROC visit |
| Physician notification | Documentation of physician contact regarding transfer | Assigned RN | EHR — communication notes | Within 1 hour (non-emergent); immediately (emergent) |
| Inter-agency transfer records | Records transmitted to receiving agency with consent | Medical Records / Assigned RN | EHR — transfer documentation | Before the transfer effective date |
| Patient/caregiver notification | Documentation of transfer notification to patient and caregiver | Assigned RN | EHR — clinical notes | At or within 24 hours of transfer |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed acknowledgment (Appendix B) | Each individual; Administrator (collection) | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or hire |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical Transfer Summary transmitted for all transfers to inpatient facilities | Chart audit of transfer events | ≥95% of transfers with documented summary transmission |
| Warm handoff documented for all transfers | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Transfer OASIS completed within CMS-required timeframe | OASIS tracking report | ≥95% |
| ROC visit completed within 48 hours of patient return | Scheduling audit | ≥95% |
| Medication reconciliation completed at every ROC | Chart audit | ≥98% |
| Physician notified of all transfers | Communication note audit | ≥98% |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60):
Evidence that transfers are coordinated with receiving facilities. Surveyors will select patients who have been transferred to inpatient facilities and verify that a clinical summary was transmitted, that a warm handoff occurred, and that the physician was notified. Missing transfer documentation is a care coordination deficiency.
Evidence that the transfer OASIS is completed. Surveyors will compare transfer dates with OASIS completion dates. Missing or late transfer OASIS assessments affect quality measure accuracy and are a documentation compliance deficiency.
Evidence that ROC assessments are comprehensive and timely. Surveyors will select patients who returned from inpatient stays and verify that a full ROC assessment was completed, medications were reconciled, and the plan of care was updated to reflect post-facility status.
Evidence that medication reconciliation occurs at ROC. Surveyors and ADR auditors will specifically examine whether the agency compared the inpatient discharge medication list against the prior home health medication list and the patient's actual medications. Medication discrepancies not identified and resolved at ROC are a patient safety failure.
Evidence that patients who visit the ED without admission are clinically followed up. Surveyors will verify that ED visits are documented and that the agency assessed the patient's status and medications following the ED visit.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transfer occurs but agency not notified for days (patient self-transports to hospital) | Transfer OASIS delayed; medication reconciliation at ROC delayed; quality measure impact | Implement patient/caregiver education at SOC on the importance of notifying the agency of any ER visit or hospitalization; assign operations staff to conduct weekly check-ins with patients who have not had a visit in 7+ days |
| Clinical Transfer Summary is a generic printout without patient-specific detail | Receiving facility lacks actionable clinical information; survey deficiency | Require individualized transfer summary using Appendix A template; Director of Nursing reviews transfer summaries quarterly |
| Warm handoff not performed — records sent by fax only | Fragmented care; critical clinical information not communicated verbally | Train all clinicians: fax alone is not sufficient — verbal communication is required; document the warm handoff recipient |
| Transfer OASIS completed but based on outdated clinical information (last visit was 2 weeks ago) | Inaccurate quality measures; OASIS data integrity failure | Train clinicians to obtain current clinical information from the patient, caregiver, or receiving facility before completing the transfer OASIS if the last visit was >7 days prior to transfer |
| ROC medication reconciliation copies the discharge list without comparison to pre-transfer list | Medication discrepancies not identified; patient safety risk | Enforce three-source comparison methodology per CL-SD-013; Director of Nursing audits ROC reconciliations monthly |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs shall receive training on transfer and referral procedures within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: (a) the Clinical Transfer Summary content requirements; (b) the warm handoff process; (c) the transfer OASIS completion requirement and timing; (d) the ROC assessment and medication reconciliation process; (e) the distinction between transfers, discharges, and ED visits without admission for OASIS and billing purposes; (f) the inter-agency and hospice transfer processes.
10.2 All clinical disciplines shall receive orientation to transfer notification requirements (informing the assigned RN and Director of Nursing of any patient transfer) within 14 calendar days of hire.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or new hire.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

# CL-CP-008 — Physician Recertification Timing Compliance
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Policy ID | CL-CP-008 |
| Policy Title | Physician Recertification Timing Compliance |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |

| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy enforces the 60-day physician recertification timeline with defined escalation protocols, tracking mechanisms, and accountability measures to prevent lapses in physician certification of continued eligibility for home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Under Medicare, a patient's eligibility for home health benefits must be recertified by the physician at least every 60 calendar days. Each 60-day certification period requires a signed physician recertification statement confirming that the patient continues to need skilled services, continues to be homebound, and that a plan of care has been established and is periodically reviewed. A lapse in recertification — where the 60-day period expires without a physician-signed recertification — renders all services delivered after the expiration date unbillable under Medicare, creates a False Claims Act risk if claims are submitted, and constitutes a documentation compliance failure during CMS surveys or ADR audits. This policy establishes a proactive, systematic tracking and escalation process to ensure that no recertification deadline is missed.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses managing active patient caseloads responsible for initiating the recertification assessment
Clinical Coordinators responsible for tracking recertification timelines
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager responsible for oversight of the recertification process
Physicians and allowed practitioners who must review, sign, and date the recertification
Revenue Cycle staff who must verify recertification before claim submission
Medical Records staff who file and manage signed recertification documents
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every patient receiving Medicare home health services shall have a physician-signed recertification on file for each 60-day certification period. The recertification must be signed by the physician before the agency submits a claim for services rendered during that certification period.
4.2 The agency shall maintain a centralized Recertification Tracking System that monitors every active patient's certification period start date, certification period end date, the recertification assessment due date window (Day 56–60), the date the recertification plan of care was transmitted to the physician, and the date the physician signature was received.
4.3 The recertification assessment — including the comprehensive OASIS assessment for the recertification time point — shall be completed between Day 56 and Day 60 of the current certification period per CL-CA-004 and CMS OASIS timing requirements.
4.4 The recertification plan of care shall be transmitted to the physician for signature no later than the last day of the current certification period (Day 60). Earlier transmission is strongly preferred to allow physician review time.
4.5 If the physician-signed recertification is not received within 7 calendar days of transmission, escalation shall be initiated per Section 6.3.
4.6 No claim shall be submitted for a certification period unless a physician-signed recertification is on file. Revenue Cycle shall implement a billing hold for any episode where the recertification signature has not been received.
4.7 If a patient no longer meets Medicare home health eligibility criteria at the time of recertification (no longer homebound, no longer requires skilled services), the clinician shall not seek recertification and shall initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006 instead.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Certification Period | A period of not more than 60 calendar days during which the physician certifies (or recertifies) that the patient meets the eligibility criteria for Medicare home health services. |
| Recertification | The physician's attestation, at the start of each subsequent certification period, that the patient continues to meet the criteria for Medicare home health benefits — specifically: (a) the patient is homebound; (b) the patient requires skilled nursing, PT, OT, or SLP services; (c) the services are reasonable and necessary; (d) a plan of care has been established and is periodically reviewed. |
| Recertification Assessment | The comprehensive clinical assessment, including all applicable OASIS data elements, completed by the assigned RN during the Day 56–60 window of the current certification period to evaluate the patient's continued eligibility and update the plan of care for the next period. |
| Day 56–60 Window | The CMS-defined assessment time period for the recertification OASIS, beginning on the 56th day and ending on the 60th day of the current certification period. |
| Billing Hold | A hold placed on claim submission for a certification period pending receipt of the physician-signed recertification, preventing the submission of claims without required documentation. |
| Recertification Tracking System | The agency's centralized system (within the EHR or a standalone tracking tool) that monitors all active patients' certification period dates, recertification assessment completion, physician signature transmission, and signature receipt status. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Recertification Tracking and Alerting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Maintain the Recertification Tracking System with the following data for each active patient: (a) certification period start date; (b) certification period end date (Day 60); (c) Day 56 date (recertification assessment window opens); (d) assigned RN; (e) recertification assessment status (not started, scheduled, completed); (f) date recertification plan of care transmitted to physician; (g) physician signature status (pending, received, overdue). | Updated continuously; reviewed at minimum weekly. |
| 6.1.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Generate a Recertification Due Report no later than Day 40 of each active certification period, listing all patients whose certification period ends within the next 20 days. Distribute the report to the Director of Nursing and all assigned RNs with patients on the report. | No later than Day 40 of each certification period. |
| 6.1.3 | Clinical Coordinator | At Day 50, verify that the recertification assessment visit has been scheduled for each patient on the report. If not scheduled, escalate immediately to the Director of Nursing. | Day 50 verification. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Review the Recertification Due Report weekly. Identify any patient whose recertification assessment has not been completed by Day 58 and intervene directly to ensure completion before the window closes. | Weekly review; intervention by Day 58 at the latest. |

### 6.2 Recertification Assessment and Plan of Care Transmission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN | Conduct the recertification assessment between Day 56 and Day 60 of the current certification period per CL-CA-004. Complete all required OASIS data elements for the recertification time point. | Between Day 56 and Day 60. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN | Based on the recertification assessment, develop the updated plan of care for the subsequent certification period per CL-CP-002, Section 6.3. The recertification plan of care shall include: (a) updated diagnoses; (b) updated functional status; (c) updated goals; (d) updated service types and frequencies; (e) updated medication list; (f) recertification narrative justifying continued skilled services and homebound status. | Within 24 hours of the recertification assessment. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | Transmit the recertification plan of care to the certifying physician for review, approval, and signature. Document the date, method, and recipient of transmission in the EHR and in the Recertification Tracking System. | No later than Day 60 of the current certification period; earlier transmission strongly preferred. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN | If the recertification assessment reveals that the patient no longer meets Medicare eligibility criteria (no longer homebound, no longer requires skilled services, goals have been met), do not initiate recertification. Instead, notify the physician and initiate discharge planning per CL-CP-006. Document the clinical rationale for non-recertification. | At the time of the recertification assessment. |

### 6.3 Physician Signature Follow-Up and Escalation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Enter the recertification plan of care into the physician order tracking system per CL-CP-009. Log the date transmitted, the physician's name and contact information, and the authentication deadline. | At the time of transmission. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator | If the signed recertification is not received within 7 calendar days of transmission, initiate the first follow-up contact with the physician's office. Document the follow-up: date, time, method, and person contacted. | Day 7 after transmission. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | If the signed recertification is not received within 14 calendar days of transmission, the Director of Nursing shall contact the physician directly by telephone. Document the contact. | Day 14 after transmission. |
| 6.3.4 | Administrator | If the signed recertification is not received within 21 calendar days of transmission despite documented follow-up, the Administrator shall contact the physician's office in writing. The Director of Nursing and Revenue Cycle Director shall assess whether services should continue pending signature and the billing implications. | Day 21 after transmission. |
| 6.3.5 | Revenue Cycle | Implement a billing hold for the new certification period until the physician-signed recertification is on file. Do not submit any claim for the new certification period without a signed recertification. Monitor the billing hold and coordinate with the Director of Nursing for resolution. | Billing hold implemented at the start of each new certification period; released only upon receipt of signed recertification. |

### 6.4 Recertification Documentation and Filing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Medical Records | Upon receipt of the physician-signed recertification, verify that: (a) the physician's signature is present and dated; (b) the signature date covers the applicable certification period; (c) the physician name and NPI are legible or accompanied by a printed name; (d) the recertification covers all ordered services. If any element is deficient, return to the physician for correction before filing. | Within 3 calendar days of receipt. |
| 6.4.2 | Medical Records / Clinical Coordinator | Update the Recertification Tracking System to reflect receipt of the signed recertification, the physician's signature date, and the date filed in the clinical record. Notify Revenue Cycle that the billing hold can be released. | Within 24 hours of filing. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recertification assessment not completed within the Day 56–60 window | Director of Nursing identifies via tracking report | Director of Nursing assesses the reason for the missed window. If the window is narrowly missed (1–3 days), complete the assessment as soon as possible and document the delay. If the window is substantially missed, consult the Compliance Officer regarding OASIS data integrity and billing implications. | Director of Nursing assessment within 24 hours; Compliance Officer consultation within 48 hours for substantial misses. |
| Physician refuses to recertify a patient | Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing discusses the physician's rationale. If the physician determines the patient no longer meets eligibility criteria, initiate discharge per CL-CP-006. If the physician's refusal appears to be administrative rather than clinical, escalate to the Administrator for resolution. | Resolution within 7 calendar days. |
| Recertification signed but signed date does not cover the certification period | Medical Records returns to physician for correction | Physician must re-sign with a date that is within or prior to the start of the certification period it covers. Do not submit the claim until the date discrepancy is resolved. | Correction within 7 calendar days. |
| Claims submitted for a certification period without a signed recertification on file | Revenue Cycle / Compliance Officer | Revenue Cycle immediately halts further claims for the episode. Compliance Officer assesses whether an overpayment has occurred per FN-BC-004. Pursue retroactive recertification signature from the physician if possible. | Claims halted immediately; Compliance assessment within 14 calendar days. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recertification assessments completed within the Day 56–60 window | OASIS assessment date audit vs. certification period dates | ≥95% |
| Recertification plan of care transmitted to physician by Day 60 | Transmission date audit | ≥95% |
| Physician-signed recertification on file for every certification period | Recertification tracking system audit | 100% — zero certification periods without signed recertification |
| No claims submitted without signed recertification | Revenue Cycle pre-bill verification | Zero claims submitted without signed recertification |
| Follow-up initiated for pending signatures within 7 days | Follow-up documentation audit | 100% of pending signatures have documented follow-up at Day 7 |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will request clinical records and verify that a physician-signed recertification exists for every certification period in the survey look-back period. They will cross-reference certification period dates with recertification signature dates and identify any gaps. ADR auditors from the MAC will specifically deny claims where the recertification is missing, unsigned, undated, or dated outside the applicable certification period. The recertification is one of the most frequently audited Medicare home health documentation elements.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recertification assessment completed but plan of care not transmitted to physician before Day 60 | Physician signature delayed; billing hold extends; cash flow impact | Track transmission date separately from assessment completion; Day 50 alert for scheduled assessment |
| Physician signs recertification but date is wrong (backdated or post-dated beyond the certification period) | Claim denial; documentation integrity concern | Medical Records verification of signature date at receipt; return deficient signatures immediately |
| Recertification for patients who no longer meet eligibility criteria | False Claims Act risk; medical necessity audit failure | Train clinicians to evaluate eligibility criteria at each recertification; Director of Nursing reviews 30-day plan of care reviews for discharge readiness |
| No centralized tracking system — reliance on individual clinician memory | Missed deadlines; billing compliance failure | Implement mandatory use of the Recertification Tracking System; Director of Nursing reviews weekly |

# CL-CP-009 — Physician Order Signature Tracking & Escalation
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-CP-009 |
| Policy Title | Physician Order Signature Tracking & Escalation |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | CP — Care Planning |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes a systematic tracking process for all pending physician signatures on orders and plans of care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., with defined follow-up intervals, escalation tiers, and documentation of all outreach attempts. The physician signature is the legal authorization for every service the agency provides and every claim the agency submits. An unsigned order is an unauthorized service. An unsigned plan of care is an unbillable episode. The agency's financial viability, regulatory compliance, and clinical legality depend on a disciplined, relentless tracking system that ensures no physician signature request goes unresolved. This policy is the operational backbone of physician order management — it defines the infrastructure, timelines, responsible parties, and escalation pathways that prevent signature lapses from becoming billing compliance failures, survey deficiencies, or False Claims Act exposures.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
Clinical Coordinators who operate the tracking system daily
All registered nurses who transmit orders and plans of care to physicians
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager who is responsible for escalation oversight
The Administrator who is the final escalation authority
Revenue Cycle staff who must verify signature status before claim submission
Medical Records staff who file and verify signed documents
Physicians and allowed practitioners whose signatures are tracked
This policy applies to all documents requiring physician signature including: initial plans of care (CMS-485), recertification plans of care, verbal order authentications, change orders, and any other physician-authorization document.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The agency shall maintain a centralized Physician Order Signature Tracking System (the "Tracking System") that captures every document requiring a physician signature from the date of transmission through the date of receipt and filing.
4.2 Every document requiring a physician signature shall be entered into the Tracking System at the time of transmission to the physician's office, including: (a) the document type (initial POC, recertification POC, verbal order authentication, change order); (b) the patient's name and medical record number; (c) the physician's name, NPI, and contact information; (d) the date of transmission; (e) the method of transmission (fax, secure portal, mail, hand-delivery); (f) the signature deadline (based on document type); (g) the status (pending, follow-up initiated, received, overdue, escalated).
4.3 The Tracking System shall generate automated alerts at defined follow-up milestones: Day 5 (first follow-up alert), Day 7 (second follow-up and Director of Nursing notification), Day 14 (Director of Nursing direct contact), and Day 21 (Administrator escalation).
4.4 All follow-up attempts shall be documented in the Tracking System including the date, time, method, person contacted, and outcome of each attempt.
4.5 Revenue Cycle shall not submit any claim for any episode or service where the corresponding physician signature has not been received and verified. A pre-bill signature verification step is mandatory before every claim submission.
4.6 The Director of Nursing shall review the Tracking System at minimum weekly and shall report to the Administrator monthly on: (a) total documents pending signature; (b) average turnaround time; (c) documents overdue beyond 14 days; (d) physicians with chronic signature delays; (e) billing hold status for affected episodes.
4.7 For physicians with a pattern of chronic non-response (defined as 3 or more documents overdue beyond 14 days within a 90-day period), the Administrator shall contact the physician practice administration in writing to address the pattern and establish a corrective process.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Physician Order Signature Tracking System | The centralized electronic or manual system used by the agency to track every document transmitted to a physician for signature, including transmission date, follow-up milestones, and receipt status. |
| Signature Deadline | The date by which the physician's signature must be received for the document to be compliant with CMS requirements, agency policy, and billing timelines. Deadlines vary by document type: verbal orders — 7 calendar days; plans of care — before claim submission; recertifications — before claim submission for the new certification period. |
| Follow-Up Milestone | A defined date after transmission at which follow-up action is required if the signature has not been received. |
| Overdue | A document for which the signature has not been received by the applicable deadline. |
| Pre-Bill Signature Verification | The mandatory step in the billing process where Revenue Cycle confirms that all required physician signatures are on file before submitting a claim. |
| Chronic Non-Response | A pattern of 3 or more documents from the same physician that are overdue beyond 14 days within a 90-day period, indicating a systemic issue requiring administrative intervention. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Tracking System Entry and Initial Transmission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | At the time any document requiring physician signature is transmitted to the physician's office, enter the document into the Tracking System with all required data fields per Section 4.2. | At the time of transmission. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN / Clinical Coordinator | Verify the physician's preferred method of receiving documents (fax, secure portal, mail) and ensure the document is transmitted via the preferred method. Document the fax confirmation number, portal submission receipt, or mailing tracking number. | At the time of transmission. |
| 6.1.3 | Clinical Coordinator | Confirm the accuracy of the physician's fax number, portal address, or mailing address before each transmission. Incorrect contact information is a leading cause of delayed signatures. | Before each transmission. |

### 6.2 Follow-Up Milestones

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Day 5 — First Follow-Up: If the signed document has not been received by Day 5, initiate first follow-up contact with the physician's office by telephone or fax. Document the contact: date, time, method, person contacted, and response. | Day 5 after transmission. |
| 6.2.2 | Clinical Coordinator / Director of Nursing | Day 7 — Second Follow-Up + Director of Nursing Notification: If the signed document has not been received by Day 7, the Clinical Coordinator initiates a second follow-up contact and formally notifies the Director of Nursing via the Tracking System alert. For verbal orders, Day 7 is the authentication deadline per CL-CP-004 — unresolved verbal orders at Day 7 require Director of Nursing direct contact with the physician. | Day 7 after transmission. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Day 14 — Director of Nursing Direct Contact: The Director of Nursing shall contact the physician directly by telephone. Document the conversation including the physician's stated reason for delay and the committed return date. If the physician is unreachable, contact the physician's office manager or practice administrator. | Day 14 after transmission. |
| 6.2.4 | Administrator | Day 21 — Administrator Escalation: If the signed document has not been received by Day 21 despite documented follow-up, the Administrator shall contact the physician's practice administration in writing, outlining the document(s) outstanding, the regulatory and billing implications, and requesting immediate resolution. The Administrator and Director of Nursing shall assess whether the document is disputed by the physician (in which case, consult the Compliance Officer). | Day 21 after transmission. |
| 6.2.5 | Revenue Cycle | At any point where a document deadline has passed without signature, Revenue Cycle shall implement a billing hold for the affected episode or service. The billing hold shall remain in place until the signature is received and filed. | Upon expiration of the applicable deadline. |

### 6.3 Receipt and Verification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Medical Records / Clinical Coordinator | Upon receipt of the signed document, verify: (a) the physician's signature is present; (b) the signature is dated; (c) the date is appropriate for the document type (within the certification period for POCs, within 7 days for verbal orders); (d) the physician's name and NPI are legible or printed. If any element is deficient, return the document for correction before filing. | Within 24 hours of receipt. |
| 6.3.2 | Clinical Coordinator | Update the Tracking System to reflect receipt of the signed document, the physician's signature date, and the date filed. Close the tracking entry. | Within 24 hours of filing. |
| 6.3.3 | Clinical Coordinator | Notify Revenue Cycle that the billing hold can be released for the affected episode or service. | At the time of Tracking System update. |

### 6.4 Weekly and Monthly Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Clinical Coordinator | Generate a weekly Pending Signature Report listing all documents with status "pending" or "overdue." Distribute to the Director of Nursing. | Weekly. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Review the weekly report and take action on all overdue items. Document actions taken for each overdue item. | Weekly. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Prepare a monthly Signature Tracking Performance Report for the Administrator including: (a) total documents transmitted; (b) total documents received and filed; (c) average signature turnaround time; (d) number of documents overdue beyond 14 days; (e) physicians with chronic non-response patterns; (f) billing holds in effect and estimated revenue at risk. | Monthly. |
| 6.4.4 | Administrator | Review the monthly report. For physicians with chronic non-response, initiate the administrative intervention per Section 4.7. Report significant signature compliance issues to the Governing Body at the quarterly meeting. | Monthly review; quarterly Governing Body reporting. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Physician disputes having given a verbal order | Director of Nursing contacts physician; Compliance Officer consulted | Director of Nursing reviews the verbal order transcription and clinical circumstances. If the order was legitimately given, document all facts. If the order is in dispute, do not bill for services under the disputed order. Compliance Officer assesses regulatory implications. | Director of Nursing contact within 24 hours; Compliance Officer within 48 hours. |
| Physician practice closes or physician is no longer available | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Coordinate with the patient's new physician to obtain orders and plan of care approval. Assess billing status for any open episodes without physician signatures. | Resolution within 14 calendar days. |
| Physician consistently signs documents but with incorrect dates | Medical Records returns for correction; Director of Nursing contacts physician | Director of Nursing contacts the physician to explain the date requirements. Offer education on acceptable signature dates for each document type. | Contact within 7 calendar days of the second occurrence. |
| Document tracking entry not created at the time of transmission | Director of Nursing identifies during weekly review | Director of Nursing retroactively enters the tracking data and provides corrective coaching to the responsible clinician or coordinator. | Tracking entry created within 24 hours of identification. |
| Billing occurs for an episode without a signed order on file | Revenue Cycle / Compliance Officer | Revenue Cycle immediately reviews the claim. Compliance Officer assesses for potential overpayment per FN-BC-004. If an overpayment is confirmed, process refund within CMS 60-day repayment timeline. | Compliance assessment within 7 calendar days; refund per FN-BC-004. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All transmitted documents entered into the Tracking System | Tracking System audit vs. transmission records | 100% |
| Follow-up initiated at Day 5 for all pending documents | Tracking System milestone documentation | ≥98% |
| Physician signatures received within 14 calendar days of transmission | Monthly turnaround analysis | ≥90% of all documents |
| Zero claims submitted without signed orders/plans of care on file | Pre-bill verification audit | Zero violations |
| Weekly Pending Signature Report generated and reviewed | Report distribution and Director of Nursing review documentation | 100% — generated every week |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will request clinical records and verify that signed physician orders and plans of care are on file for every episode and every service in the survey look-back period. ADR auditors will deny claims where signed orders or plans of care are missing. OIG investigations of home health agencies frequently target unsigned orders as evidence of inadequate physician oversight, which can escalate to False Claims Act allegations. A robust, documented tracking system demonstrating proactive follow-up is a strong compliance defense.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No centralized tracking — signature status tracked informally by individual clinicians | Documents lost; deadlines missed; no accountability | Mandatory Tracking System with all required fields; Director of Nursing weekly review |
| Follow-up consists of re-faxing the document without telephone contact | Physician office may not prioritize fax-only follow-up | Require telephone contact at Day 7 and Day 14 |
| Physician signs the document but it is not received by the agency (fax failure, lost mail) | Document lost in transit; billing delayed | Require transmission receipt confirmation; track receipt separately from transmission |
| Revenue Cycle submits claims during the billing hold period | Billing compliance failure | System-enforced billing hold; Revenue Cycle supervisor approval required to release hold |
| Tracking System not maintained — entries incomplete or not updated | False compliance picture; unresolved documents not identified | Director of Nursing weekly audit of Tracking System completeness |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the assessment, intervention, monitoring, and documentation standards for patients with cardiac conditions at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Cardiac diagnoses — including congestive heart failure (CHF), coronary artery disease (CAD), atrial fibrillation, post-myocardial infarction, post-cardiac surgery, hypertension, and valvular disease — constitute one of the largest clinical populations in Medicare home health. Heart failure alone accounts for the highest rate of 30-day hospital readmissions among Medicare beneficiaries, and the CMS Home Health Compare publicly reports the agency's rehospitalization rate for heart failure patients as a quality measure directly affecting star ratings. Effective cardiac care in the home requires meticulous daily weight and symptom monitoring, complex medication management (including anticoagulants, diuretics, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and antiarrhythmics), dietary sodium restriction education, activity management, and early identification of decompensation signs that, if recognized and treated promptly, can prevent an emergency department visit or hospitalization. This policy ensures that all cardiac patients receive evidence-based, protocol-driven care that reduces rehospitalization, improves functional outcomes, and is documented with the clinical specificity required by CMS and ADR auditors.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to all RNs and LVNs providing skilled nursing to cardiac patients, PTs providing cardiac rehabilitation and activity progression, OTs addressing cardiac-related ADL limitations and energy conservation, the Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager, and Revenue Cycle staff relying on cardiac documentation for coding and billing.
## 4. Policy Statement
4.1 All patients admitted with a primary or secondary cardiac diagnosis shall receive a comprehensive cardiac assessment at SOC including: (a) cardiac history — prior MI, CHF classification (NYHA Class I–IV), surgeries, catheterizations, device implants (pacemaker, ICD, LVAD); (b) current symptoms — dyspnea (at rest and with exertion), orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, edema, fatigue, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, syncope; (c) baseline vital signs including orthostatic blood pressure; (d) baseline weight (obtained on the same scale, at the same time of day, in the same clothing — establish the "dry weight" with physician input); (e) cardiac auscultation — heart sounds, presence of murmurs, gallops (S3, S4); (f) lung auscultation — presence of crackles, wheezing, diminished breath sounds; (g) peripheral edema assessment — location, severity (1+ through 4+), pitting vs. non-pitting; (h) jugular venous distention assessment; (i) skin assessment — color, temperature, capillary refill, cyanosis; (j) current cardiac medication regimen review per CL-SD-012; (k) dietary assessment — sodium intake, fluid restriction compliance; (l) activity tolerance assessment; (m) patient's and caregiver's current knowledge of cardiac self-management.
4.2 A cardiac management plan shall be developed as part of the plan of care including: (a) physician-ordered daily weight monitoring protocol with defined parameters for weight gain notification (typically >2 lbs in 24 hours or >5 lbs in 1 week); (b) physician-ordered vital sign monitoring schedule; (c) medication management plan — including specific attention to diuretics, anticoagulants, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and digoxin; (d) dietary sodium restriction (typically <2,000 mg/day or per physician order) and fluid restriction if ordered; (e) activity progression and exercise tolerance goals (coordinated with PT if involved); (f) symptom monitoring and the "zone system" education (Green/Yellow/Red zones for self-management); (g) self-management education goals; (h) defined parameters for physician notification and emergency response.
4.3 At each skilled nursing visit for a cardiac patient, the RN or LVN shall: (a) assess and document vital signs including blood pressure (lying, sitting, standing if orthostatic assessment ordered), heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and temperature; (b) obtain and record the patient's current weight and compare to baseline and previous visit; (c) assess for heart failure decompensation signs — increased edema, weight gain, increased dyspnea, orthopnea, jugular venous distention, crackles on lung auscultation; (d) review the patient's daily weight log and symptom diary (if applicable); (e) assess medication adherence for all cardiac medications with particular attention to diuretics, anticoagulants, and antihypertensives; (f) assess dietary sodium and fluid intake compliance; (g) assess activity tolerance — compare to prior visit; (h) perform cardiac-specific education per the education plan; (i) assess for medication-related adverse effects — hypotension, bradycardia, electrolyte imbalance symptoms, bleeding (anticoagulants), digoxin toxicity signs.
4.4 The physician shall be notified within 4 hours (or sooner for emergent findings) when any of the following are identified: (a) weight gain >2 lbs in 24 hours or >5 lbs in 1 week; (b) new or worsening edema; (c) new or worsening dyspnea at rest; (d) oxygen saturation <90% (or below the patient's physician-defined threshold); (e) systolic blood pressure >180 or <90 (or per physician parameters); (f) heart rate >120 or <50 (or per physician parameters); (g) new chest pain or angina; (h) new arrhythmia detected; (i) signs of digoxin toxicity (nausea, visual disturbances, bradycardia); (j) signs of bleeding in anticoagulated patients.
4.5 If the patient exhibits signs of acute cardiac emergency (severe chest pain, acute dyspnea at rest, oxygen saturation <85%, acute altered mental status, severe hypotension, suspected MI or stroke), call 911 immediately, initiate emergency nursing interventions within scope (position patient, administer oxygen if available and ordered, aspirin per standing order if applicable), and notify the physician and Director of Nursing within 2 hours.
4.6 All cardiac patients shall receive comprehensive self-management education per CL-SD-017 covering: (a) the "zone system" for symptom self-management — Green Zone (all clear: weight stable, no symptoms), Yellow Zone (caution: weight up 2+ lbs, increased swelling, increased shortness of breath — call the agency), Red Zone (emergency: severe shortness of breath at rest, chest pain, fainting — call 911); (b) daily weight monitoring technique (same scale, same time, same clothing, log daily); (c) sodium restriction — reading food labels, avoiding high-sodium foods, meal planning; (d) fluid restriction management (if ordered); (e) medication purpose, dose, timing, and side effects for all cardiac medications; (f) activity guidelines and energy conservation; (g) when to call the agency, when to call 911; (h) the importance of follow-up appointments.
4.7 For patients on anticoagulation therapy (warfarin, enoxaparin, DOACs), follow the enhanced medication safety protocols defined in RM-PS-005 including INR monitoring schedule for warfarin patients, bleeding risk assessment at each visit, and patient education on signs of bleeding.
4.8 PT involvement shall be initiated per physician order for cardiac patients requiring supervised activity progression, cardiac rehabilitation exercise, and functional mobility training. The PT shall coordinate activity progression with the assigned RN to ensure exercise parameters align with the patient's cardiac status and physician orders.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) | A chronic condition in which the heart does not pump blood as efficiently as it should, leading to fluid accumulation in the lungs, abdomen, and extremities. |
| NYHA Functional Classification | The New York Heart Association classification system for heart failure severity: Class I (no limitation), Class II (slight limitation), Class III (marked limitation), Class IV (symptoms at rest). |
| Dry Weight | The patient's baseline weight when fluid status is optimized — typically the weight at which the patient has no or minimal fluid retention. Established with physician input. |
| Decompensation | A worsening of heart failure symptoms typically indicated by fluid overload (weight gain, edema, dyspnea), representing a clinical deterioration that often precedes hospitalization. |
| Zone System | A patient education framework using Green/Yellow/Red color-coded zones to help patients self-assess their cardiac status and determine appropriate responses. |
| Orthostatic Hypotension | A drop in systolic blood pressure of ≥20 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of ≥10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing from a sitting or lying position, which increases fall risk and may indicate over-diuresis or medication adverse effect. |
| Jugular Venous Distention (JVD) | Visible distention of the jugular veins when the patient is positioned at a 45-degree angle, indicating elevated central venous pressure and right-sided heart failure. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Cardiac Assessment at SOC

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assigned RN | At the SOC visit, complete a comprehensive cardiac assessment per Section 4.1. Document all findings using the Cardiac Assessment Template (Appendix A). | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.2 | Assigned RN | Establish the patient's baseline ("dry") weight in collaboration with the physician. If the patient does not have a reliable scale, coordinate provision of a scale through the agency's equipment process per OP-SL-004. | At the SOC visit; scale provision within 48 hours if needed. |
| 6.1.3 | Assigned RN | Review the patient's complete cardiac medication regimen with the patient and caregiver. Identify all high-risk cardiac medications (anticoagulants, digoxin, antiarrhythmics) and flag them in the medication list per RM-PS-005. | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.4 | Assigned RN | Classify the patient's heart failure severity using NYHA classification (if CHF is a diagnosis) and document the classification. | At the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.5 | Assigned RN | Develop the cardiac management plan per Section 4.2. | Within 24 hours of the SOC visit. |
| 6.1.6 | Assigned RN | Provide the patient and caregiver with the Zone System education materials and a daily weight and symptom log. Begin the zone system education. | At the SOC visit. |

### 6.2 Ongoing Cardiac Monitoring at Each Visit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | Perform all visit assessments per Section 4.3. Document all findings in the visit note with clinical analysis — not just data points but the clinical significance of each finding (e.g., "Weight increased 3 lbs since last visit 3 days ago — patient in Yellow Zone; bilateral lower extremity edema increased from 1+ to 2+; lungs with bibasilar crackles noted — consistent with early decompensation. Physician notified."). | At each visit. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned RN / LVN | Review the patient's daily weight log and symptom diary. Identify trends. If the patient has not been logging daily weights, reinforce the importance and document the non-adherence. | At each visit. |
| 6.2.3 | Assigned RN / LVN | Assess dietary sodium compliance by asking about specific meals and reading food labels with the patient. Document specific findings — not just "diet reviewed" but "Patient reports eating canned soup yesterday — estimated 800mg sodium per serving; patient unaware of sodium content. Provided label-reading education." | At each visit. |
| 6.2.4 | Assigned RN / LVN | If physician notification criteria per Section 4.4 are met, contact the physician within 4 hours and document the notification, information communicated, and physician orders received. | Within 4 hours; immediately for emergent findings. |
| 6.2.5 | Assigned RN / LVN | Provide targeted cardiac education at each visit per the education plan, building sequentially from basic concepts to advanced self-management skills. Use teach-back per CL-SD-017. | At each visit. |

### 6.3 Heart Failure Decompensation Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Assigned RN / LVN | When signs of heart failure decompensation are identified (weight gain, increased edema, worsening dyspnea), immediately assess the severity using the zone system. If the patient is in Yellow Zone, contact the physician within 4 hours. If the patient is in Red Zone, follow Section 4.5 emergency procedures. | Immediately upon identification. |
| 6.3.2 | Assigned RN | Obtain physician orders for decompensation management — which may include: diuretic dose adjustment, fluid restriction modification, additional visit frequency, laboratory orders (BMP for electrolytes, BNP), or referral to the emergency department. | Per physician response. |
| 6.3.3 | Assigned RN | If the physician orders an additional diuretic dose, administer per CL-SD-012 and reassess the patient within 24 hours (either by visit or by telephone per CL-SD-009 if telehealth is in the plan of care). Document the intervention and response. | Within 24 hours of order. |
| 6.3.4 | Assigned RN | Update the plan of care if the decompensation represents a significant change per CL-CP-002. Consider whether increased visit frequency is warranted. | Within 24 hours of the decompensation event. |

### 6.4 Anticoagulation Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Assigned RN | For patients on warfarin, ensure INR monitoring is ordered and tracked per the physician's schedule. Document each INR result, the physician notification, and any dose adjustment ordered. | Per physician-ordered INR schedule. |
| 6.4.2 | Assigned RN | At each visit for anticoagulated patients, assess for signs of bleeding: (a) bruising — new or expanding; (b) gingival bleeding; (c) blood in urine or stool; (d) nosebleeds; (e) headache (potential intracranial bleeding); (f) abdominal pain (potential GI bleeding). Document the assessment. | At each visit. |
| 6.4.3 | Assigned RN | Educate the patient on anticoagulation safety per RM-PS-005 including: avoiding injury, using a soft toothbrush, reporting any bleeding immediately, dietary consistency for warfarin patients (vitamin K foods), and the importance of regular INR testing. | At SOC; reinforced at each visit. |

### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patient's weight increases >5 lbs in 1 week despite interventions | Assigned RN notifies physician and Director of Nursing | Physician assesses for medication adjustment, additional diagnostics, or possible hospitalization. Director of Nursing reviews the case for adequacy of monitoring. | Physician notification within 4 hours; Director of Nursing review within 24 hours. |
| Patient repeatedly non-compliant with sodium restriction or daily weights | Assigned RN documents; notifies Director of Nursing | Director of Nursing reviews the education plan. Consider MSW referral for psychosocial barriers. Increase visit frequency if physician orders. Document non-adherence and interventions. | Director of Nursing review within 7 calendar days. |
| INR critically elevated (>5.0) or patient presents with active bleeding | Assigned RN notifies physician immediately; call 911 if active significant bleeding | Physician orders warfarin hold, possible vitamin K, possible ED referral. Document all actions. Incident report per RM-ER-002. | Immediately. |
| Cardiac documentation does not demonstrate skilled assessment | Director of Nursing chart review | Provide documentation coaching emphasizing clinical analysis of findings, not just data recording. | Within 7 calendar days. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Comprehensive cardiac assessment at SOC | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Weight documented at every cardiac patient nursing visit | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Heart failure decompensation signs assessed at every visit | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Physician notified within 4 hours for notification criteria triggers | Communication note audit | ≥95% |
| Cardiac self-management education documented at each visit | Chart audit | ≥95% |
| Rehospitalization rate for CHF patients | QAPI dashboard | Agency target: below the national average per CMS Home Health Compare |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will verify that cardiac patients have comprehensive assessments, that monitoring is consistent with physician orders, that patient education is individualized and documented, and that clinical changes trigger physician notification. ADR auditors will examine whether cardiac visit documentation supports skilled nursing — a visit that documents only vital signs and weight without clinical analysis does not demonstrate skilled care.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weight documented but no clinical analysis ("Weight 165 lbs" with no comparison or assessment) | Non-skilled documentation; ADR denial | Train clinicians to compare weight to baseline, analyze trend, and document clinical significance |
| Dietary assessment documented as "diet reviewed" without specifics | Non-skilled documentation; education ineffectiveness | Require specific dietary intake documentation; use teach-back for sodium restriction |
| Decompensation signs present in documentation but no physician notification documented | Patient safety failure; survey citation | Mandatory documentation field for physician notification when trigger criteria are met |
| INR monitoring not tracked or delayed | Anticoagulation safety risk; bleeding or clotting events | INR tracking integrated into the medication management plan; Director of Nursing reviews monthly |

## 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All RNs and LVNs providing care to cardiac patients shall receive cardiac care competency training at hire and annually thereafter, including: comprehensive cardiac assessment; heart failure decompensation recognition and response; the zone system; cardiac medication management (including anticoagulants, diuretics, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, digoxin); sodium restriction education techniques; and cardiac documentation standards demonstrating skilled care.
10.2 All PTs providing cardiac rehabilitation services shall receive training on cardiac exercise parameters, activity progression safety, and coordination with nursing per physician orders.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, revision, or hire.
