# POLICY HR-TA-004
# Licensure & Certification Verification
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TA-004 |
| Title | Licensure & Certification Verification |
| Domain | HR — Human Resources |
| Subdomain | TA — Talent Acquisition & Onboarding |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | HR Director / Director of Nursing / Administrator |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory requirements for verifying and continuously monitoring the professional licensure, certification, and registration status of all clinical and licensed personnel employed by or contracted with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Verification of licensure is required by 42 CFR § 484.105 and § 484.115 (Personnel Qualifications), California Health and Safety Code home health agency licensing requirements, and applicable professional practice acts. Employing individuals who do not hold current, valid, unrestricted licensure appropriate to their role exposes the agency to regulatory sanctions, survey deficiencies, malpractice liability, and criminal prosecution for unauthorized practice. This policy ensures that every licensed professional practicing under the agency's authority holds a valid, verified license at all times.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All Registered Nurses (RN), Licensed Vocational Nurses (LVN), Physical Therapists (PT), Physical Therapist Assistants (PTA), Occupational Therapists (OT), Certified Occupational Therapy Assistants (COTA), Speech-Language Pathologists (SLP), Medical Social Workers (MSW), and any other licensed/certified clinical professional employed by or contracted with the agency
Home Health Aides (HHA) — certification verification per 42 CFR § 484.80
All contracted/staffing agency clinical personnel
The HR Director, Director of Nursing, and all personnel responsible for licensure verification
The Administrator
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall verify the current, valid, unrestricted status of every professional license, certification, and registration required for each clinical position prior to the individual performing any clinical duties, and shall continuously monitor licensure status throughout employment.
4.2 Verification shall be conducted through primary source verification — direct confirmation with the issuing state licensing board, certification body, or their authorized electronic verification system. Copies of licenses provided by the applicant or employee are not sufficient as the sole means of verification.
4.3 No individual shall provide clinical services, conduct patient assessments, or perform any task requiring professional licensure until primary source verification is completed and documented as CURRENT and UNRESTRICTED.
4.4 The agency shall maintain a Licensure Expiration Tracking System (Appendix A) to proactively monitor all license expiration dates and initiate renewal verification at least 60 calendar days before expiration.
4.5 Any clinician whose license expires, is suspended, revoked, or subject to restriction shall be immediately removed from clinical duties until the licensure issue is fully resolved. Practice on an expired or restricted license is a violation of California law and agency policy.
4.6 All licensure verification records shall be maintained in the employee's personnel file per HR-WM-005 and HR-WM-007.
4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Primary Source Verification | Confirmation of licensure status directly from the issuing licensing board, certifying body, or their authorized electronic verification system (e.g., California BRN online license lookup, APTA verification, NBCOT verification). |
| Unrestricted License | A license that is current, active, and not subject to any disciplinary limitations, probation, supervision requirements, or practice restrictions imposed by the licensing board. |
| Restricted License | A license that is current but subject to conditions, limitations, probation, or practice restrictions imposed by the licensing board as a result of disciplinary action. |
| License Encumbrance | Any adverse action taken against a license including probation, suspension, revocation, voluntary surrender, or practice restriction. |
| Compact License | A multistate license issued under a nurse licensure compact or therapy compact that authorizes practice in multiple member states. |
| Certification | A credential issued by a professional certifying body (e.g., HHA certification, BLS certification, specialty certification) that validates competency in a defined scope of practice. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Pre-Employment Licensure Verification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | HR Director | Upon receipt of the signed Conditional Offer Letter (HR-TA-001), identify all licenses and certifications required for the position per the approved job description (HR-JD series). | Within 1 business day of conditional offer acceptance. |
| 6.1.2 | HR Director | Conduct primary source verification for each required license/certification: (a) Access the issuing board's electronic verification system; (b) Verify: license number, license type, licensee name, issuance date, expiration date, status (active/inactive/expired), and any disciplinary actions or encumbrances; (c) Print or save a screenshot of the verification result with the date of verification visible. | Within 3 business days of conditional offer acceptance. |
| 6.1.3 | HR Director | Document verification results on the Licensure Verification Record (Appendix B), including: (a) license type and number; (b) issuing state/board; (c) verification method (website URL, phone, written confirmation); (d) verification date; (e) status confirmed (Active/Unrestricted, Active/Restricted, Expired, Suspended, Revoked); (f) expiration date; (g) verifier's name and signature. Attach primary source evidence. | Completed concurrent with verification. |
| 6.1.4 | HR Director | If the license is ACTIVE and UNRESTRICTED: mark the Pre-Employment Screening Checklist (HR-TA-001, Appendix F) as PASS and proceed. | Same day as verification. |
| 6.1.5 | HR Director | If the license is RESTRICTED (active with conditions): notify the Director of Nursing. The DON shall review the specific restrictions and determine whether the individual can perform the essential functions of the position within the restrictions. If yes, document the determination and any practice limitations. If no, rescind the conditional offer. | DON review within 3 business days. |
| 6.1.6 | HR Director | If the license is EXPIRED, SUSPENDED, or REVOKED: the individual is ineligible for employment in the licensed position. Rescind the conditional offer in writing. | Immediate upon verification. |
| 6.1.7 | HR Director | For Home Health Aides: verify HHA certification or training completion per 42 CFR § 484.80. Acceptable documentation includes: (a) state-approved HHA training program completion certificate; (b) competency evaluation documentation; (c) if previously employed as HHA, verification from prior employer of completed training and competency evaluation. | Within 3 business days of conditional offer acceptance. |

### 6.2 Ongoing Licensure Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | HR Director | Maintain a Licensure Expiration Tracking System (Appendix A) listing every licensed/certified employee, their license type(s), license number(s), and expiration date(s). | Ongoing; updated within 5 business days of any hire, separation, or renewal. |
| 6.2.2 | HR Director | At least 90 calendar days before each license expiration date, send a License Renewal Reminder Notice (Appendix C) to the employee reminding them of: (a) the upcoming expiration; (b) their obligation to renew timely; (c) the requirement to provide evidence of renewal to HR; (d) the consequence of practicing on an expired license (immediate removal from clinical duties). | 90 days before expiration. |
| 6.2.3 | HR Director | At 60 calendar days before expiration, if the employee has not yet provided evidence of renewal initiation, send a second reminder with copy to the employee's supervisor and the Director of Nursing. | 60 days before expiration. |
| 6.2.4 | HR Director | At 30 calendar days before expiration, if renewal is still not confirmed, the Director of Nursing shall meet with the employee to confirm renewal status. If the employee indicates they will not or cannot renew, initiate workforce planning per HR-WM-001. | 30 days before expiration. |
| 6.2.5 | HR Director | Upon expiration date: if the employee has not provided evidence of a current, renewed license: (a) immediately remove the employee from all clinical duties; (b) notify the employee in writing that they may not perform any clinical services until the renewed license is verified; (c) the employee may be placed on unpaid administrative leave or reassigned to non-clinical duties (if available) at the Administrator's discretion. | On the expiration date; no exceptions. |
| 6.2.6 | HR Director | When the employee provides a renewed license: conduct primary source verification per Section 6.1.2 and update the Licensure Verification Record (Appendix B) and the Tracking System (Appendix A). Clear the employee to return to clinical duties only upon confirmed verification. | Verification within 2 business days of receiving renewal evidence. |
| 6.2.7 | HR Director | Conduct an annual primary source re-verification of all licenses for all currently employed licensed staff, regardless of expiration dates, to identify any disciplinary actions, restrictions, or encumbrances that may have been imposed since the last verification. | Annually; completed within the first quarter of each calendar year. |

### 6.3 Licensure Adverse Event Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | HR Director / Director of Nursing | If at any time the agency becomes aware that an employee's license has been suspended, revoked, restricted, or subject to disciplinary action: immediately remove the employee from clinical duties. | Immediate upon discovery. |
| 6.3.2 | HR Director | Notify the Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer within 24 hours. Document the finding on the Licensure Adverse Event Report (Appendix D). | Within 24 hours. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Review all patient care provided by the affected clinician during any period of impaired licensure. Identify patients who may have been affected. Coordinate with QAPI per QA-AE-001 if patient harm or quality issues are identified. | Review initiated within 48 hours; completed within 14 calendar days. |
| 6.3.4 | Administrator / HR Director | Determine employment action based on the nature of the licensure issue: (a) suspended license — employee on unpaid administrative leave pending reinstatement, with defined maximum wait period; (b) revoked license — terminate employment per HR-ER-006; (c) restricted license — DON evaluates whether restrictions are compatible with position duties. | Employment determination within 5 business days. |

### 6.4 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clinician found to have performed clinical duties on an expired license | Immediate removal from duties; HR Director notifies DON and Compliance Officer. | Review all care provided during lapsed period. Report to licensing board if required by law. Incident documented per QA-AE-001. | Immediate removal; review within 14 days. |
| Licensing board website unavailable for verification | HR Director documents unavailability; contacts board directly by phone. | Verification obtained through alternative primary source method (phone with documented callback number, written confirmation). Individual may NOT begin clinical duties until verified. | Alternative verification within 5 business days. |
| Employee fails to renew license after 30 days of administrative leave | HR Director notifies Administrator. | Separation per HR-ER-006 unless extenuating circumstances documented and approved by Administrator. | Separation within 5 business days of 30-day mark. |

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Licensure tracking | Licensure Expiration Tracking System (Appendix A) | HR Director | HR records (electronic or physical) | Ongoing; updated within 5 business days of any change. |
| Primary source verification | Licensure Verification Record (Appendix B) with attached evidence | HR Director | Personnel file | Pre-employment; at each renewal; annual re-verification. |
| Renewal reminders | License Renewal Reminder Notices (Appendix C) — copies | HR Director | Personnel file | 90, 60, and 30 days before expiration as applicable. |
| Adverse events | Licensure Adverse Event Report (Appendix D) | HR Director / DON | Personnel file; compliance records | Within 24 hours of discovery. |
| Copies of licenses | Employee-provided copies of current licenses | Employee (provision); HR Director (filing) | Personnel file | At hire and upon each renewal. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100% of clinical staff have primary source verified licenses before providing care | Audit of personnel files for Appendix B dated before or on start date | Zero clinicians providing care without verified licensure. |
| Zero employees practicing on expired licenses | Cross-reference tracking system dates against personnel status | Zero expired licenses in the active workforce at any point. |
| Renewal reminders sent at 90 days for all upcoming expirations | Audit of reminder notices in personnel files | 100% of upcoming expirations receive 90-day notice. |
| Annual re-verification completed for all licensed staff | Audit of Appendix B for annual verification entries | 100% completed within Q1 each year. |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinician practices on expired license (even briefly) | State licensing board violation; CMS survey deficiency; malpractice liability; potential criminal charge | Automated tracking system with alerts at 90/60/30 days; hard-stop at expiration. |
| Primary source verification not performed (reliance on copies) | Fraudulent or altered license copies not detected | Enforce primary source verification for every check; attach screenshot evidence. |
| Staffing agency clinicians not independently verified | Agency liable if contract clinician has invalid license | Enforce independent verification per Section 6.1 for all contract staff per HR-TA-001 § 6.6. |
| Disciplinary action against license not detected between renewals | Clinician practices under impaired/restricted license | Annual re-verification specifically checking for encumbrances. |

## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 HR staff responsible for licensure verification shall receive training on primary source verification methods for each license type, use of state licensing board websites, documentation standards, and the tracking system. Training within 14 days of assignment; refreshed annually.
10.2 All licensed clinical staff shall receive notification during orientation (HR-TA-005) of their personal obligation to maintain current licensure, report any disciplinary action to HR within 24 hours, and provide renewal evidence to HR at least 30 days before expiration.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days of effective date or new assignment.

# POLICY HR-TA-005
# Employee Orientation & Onboarding
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TA-005 |
| Title | Employee Orientation & Onboarding |
| Domain | HR — Human Resources |
| Subdomain | TA — Talent Acquisition & Onboarding |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | HR Director / Administrator |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes mandatory requirements for the orientation and onboarding of all new employees and contracted staff at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A comprehensive, standardized orientation ensures that every individual entering the agency workforce understands the agency's mission, regulatory obligations, clinical standards, compliance requirements, safety protocols, and their role-specific responsibilities before providing any services. This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105 (organization and administration), 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide training), CMS State Operations Manual surveyor expectations, OSHA requirements, and California home health licensure standards.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All newly hired employees (full-time, part-time, per diem) regardless of position
All contracted/staffing agency clinical personnel prior to their first patient assignment
All individuals transitioning to a new role or department within the agency (role-specific orientation component only)
The HR Director, Director of Nursing, department supervisors, and all personnel responsible for conducting or coordinating orientation
The Administrator
This policy does not apply to: Governing Body member orientation, which is addressed in GV-GB-001 § 10. Volunteer orientation is addressed in HR-WM-006.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall provide a mandatory, documented orientation program to every new employee before the employee independently performs any job duties, provides any patient care, or accesses protected health information.
4.2 Orientation shall consist of two components: (a) General Agency Orientation (required for all staff); and (b) Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation (required for clinical staff and position-specific for all other roles).
4.3 General Agency Orientation must be completed within the first 5 business days of employment. Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation must be completed within the first 30 calendar days of employment. Clinical staff may not conduct unsupervised patient visits until both components are satisfactorily completed and documented.
4.4 Orientation content shall be reviewed and updated at least annually by the HR Director (general orientation) and Director of Nursing (clinical orientation) to reflect current regulations, policies, and agency operations.
4.5 Orientation completion shall be documented on the Orientation Completion Checklist (Appendix A for General, Appendix B for Clinical) and retained in the employee's personnel file per HR-WM-005 and HR-WM-007.
4.6 Contracted/staffing agency personnel shall complete an abbreviated orientation (Appendix C) covering patient safety, infection control, HIPAA, emergency procedures, and agency-specific clinical documentation requirements before their first patient assignment.
4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| General Agency Orientation | The standardized orientation program covering agency-wide topics applicable to all employees regardless of position, including mission, compliance, HIPAA, safety, infection control, emergency preparedness, and workplace standards. |
| Role-Specific Orientation | The orientation component tailored to the specific duties, clinical competencies, documentation systems, and supervision requirements of the employee's assigned position. |
| Clinical Orientation | The role-specific orientation for clinical staff including EHR/OASIS training, clinical documentation standards, supervised patient visits, and competency validation. |
| Preceptor | An experienced, competent employee designated to mentor and supervise a new employee during the role-specific orientation period. |
| Supervised Visit | A patient care visit conducted by a new clinical employee under the direct or indirect supervision of a preceptor or clinical supervisor, prior to being cleared for independent practice. |
| Orientation Completion | The point at which all required orientation components have been satisfactorily completed, documented, and signed off by the appropriate supervisor, allowing the employee to perform duties independently. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Pre-Orientation Preparation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | HR Director | Before the new employee's first day, prepare the orientation packet containing: (a) orientation schedule; (b) General Agency Orientation Checklist (Appendix A); (c) Role-Specific Orientation Checklist (Appendix B or C); (d) Employee Handbook; (e) key policy acknowledgment forms (compliance, HIPAA, safety, abuse reporting); (f) IT system access request form per IT-SC-002; (g) benefits enrollment materials; (h) emergency contact form. | At least 2 business days before start date. |
| 6.1.2 | HR Director | Assign a preceptor for clinical staff orientation. The preceptor must: (a) hold the same or supervising licensure/discipline; (b) have at least 1 year of experience with the agency; (c) have no active disciplinary actions. Notify the preceptor and provide the Role-Specific Orientation Checklist. | At least 3 business days before start date. |
| 6.1.3 | Hiring Manager / Supervisor | Prepare the new employee's workspace, equipment, supplies, and system access credentials (coordinated with IT per IT-SC-002). | Completed before start date. |

### 6.2 General Agency Orientation (All Staff — Days 1-5)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | HR Director | Conduct General Agency Orientation covering all topics listed on Appendix A. Orientation may be delivered in-person, via structured e-learning modules, or a combination, but must include opportunity for questions and interaction. | Completed within first 5 business days. |
| 6.2.2 | HR Director | General Agency Orientation must cover, at minimum, the following topics (documented on Appendix A): (a) Agency mission, vision, and values; (b) Organizational structure and reporting relationships (GV-OG-001); (c) Scope of services (GV-OG-003); (d) Corporate compliance program overview (CO-CP-001, CO-CP-004); (e) HIPAA privacy and security (CO-HP-001, CO-HP-002) — including PHI handling, minimum necessary standard, breach reporting; (f) Patient rights and responsibilities (CL-PR-001); (g) Abuse, neglect, and exploitation identification and mandatory reporting (CL-PR-006, HR-ER-009); (h) Infection prevention and control — standard precautions, hand hygiene, PPE (CL-SD-016); (i) Emergency preparedness — agency emergency plan, employee role, communication protocols (OP-FM-005, CL-PR-005); (j) Workplace safety — personal safety during home visits, workplace violence prevention, injury reporting (RM-SS-001, RM-SS-002, HR-WM-004); (k) Anti-harassment and non-discrimination (HR-ER-004); (l) Substance abuse and drug-free workplace (HR-ER-005); (m) Disciplinary process overview (HR-ER-002); (n) Grievance and complaint process (HR-ER-003); (o) IT acceptable use, email, social media policies (IT-UP-001, IT-UP-002, IT-UP-003); (p) Security awareness — password management, phishing, data protection (IT-UP-004); (q) Documentation standards overview; (r) Time and attendance requirements; (s) Benefits overview and enrollment procedures. | Topics delivered across Days 1-5. |
| 6.2.3 | HR Director | Administer the General Orientation Competency Quiz (Appendix D) at the conclusion of general orientation. Passing score: 80% or higher. Employees who do not pass must receive remedial review and retake within 3 business days. | Day 5 of orientation. |
| 6.2.4 | HR Director | Collect all signed policy acknowledgment forms. Verify and file in personnel file. | Completed by end of Day 5. |
| 6.2.5 | HR Director / Employee | Complete and sign the General Agency Orientation Checklist (Appendix A). Both the HR Director (or orientation trainer) and the employee must sign, confirming all topics were covered and the employee had the opportunity to ask questions. | Completed by end of Day 5. |

### 6.3 Role-Specific / Clinical Orientation (Days 1-30)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing / Supervisor | Initiate role-specific orientation using the Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation Checklist (Appendix B). For clinical staff, the checklist must include: (a) EHR system training and proficiency demonstration; (b) OASIS training and assessment (per CL-OA-003, CL-OA-018); (c) Clinical documentation standards (CL-CD-001 through CL-CD-004); (d) Care planning and physician order management (CL-CP-001 through CL-CP-009); (e) Discipline-specific clinical protocols; (f) Medication management (CL-SD-012, CL-SD-013); (g) Fall risk assessment (CL-SD-015); (h) Wound care standards (CL-SD-011, if applicable); (i) Pain assessment (CL-SD-014); (j) Infection prevention — clinical application; (k) Patient identification and verification (OP-PA-002); (l) Homebound status determination (CL-CA-005); (m) Supervised patient visits (minimum 2 for experienced clinicians; minimum 5 for new graduates or clinicians new to home health); (n) Competency validation per HR-TD-003. | Initiated Day 1; completed within 30 calendar days. |
| 6.3.2 | Preceptor | Conduct supervised patient visits with the new clinical employee. Evaluate clinical competency, documentation quality, patient interaction, and safety awareness during each supervised visit. Complete the Supervised Visit Evaluation Form (Appendix E) for each visit. | Per orientation schedule within first 30 days. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Review all Supervised Visit Evaluation Forms. Determine whether the new clinician demonstrates competency to practice independently. If competency concerns are identified, extend the supervised orientation period with a documented remediation plan (maximum extension: 30 additional calendar days). | Within 5 business days of final supervised visit. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing / Supervisor | For non-clinical staff: complete role-specific orientation covering department procedures, systems, workflows, and position-specific competencies. Document on Appendix B (non-clinical version). | Within 30 calendar days. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing / Supervisor / Employee | Complete and sign the Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation Checklist (Appendix B). The supervisor/DON, preceptor (if applicable), and employee must all sign, confirming all components were completed satisfactorily. | By Day 30 (or extended deadline if remediation required). |

### 6.4 Contracted/Staffing Agency Personnel Abbreviated Orientation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | HR Director / Designee | Before any contracted/staffing agency clinician's first patient assignment, conduct an abbreviated orientation using the Contract Staff Orientation Checklist (Appendix C) covering: (a) Agency-specific clinical documentation system/EHR; (b) HIPAA and PHI handling per agency protocols; (c) Patient identification and safety; (d) Infection control — agency protocols; (e) Emergency procedures and communication; (f) Abuse/neglect reporting obligations; (g) Key contact numbers (DON, on-call, office). | Completed before first patient assignment. |
| 6.4.2 | Contract Staff / HR Director | Sign the Contract Staff Orientation Checklist (Appendix C). File in the contract staff file per HR-TA-001, Appendix I. | Same day as orientation. |

### 6.5 Orientation for Internal Transfers / Role Changes

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Receiving Supervisor / DON | When an employee transfers to a new role or department, conduct role-specific orientation for the new position using Appendix B. General agency re-orientation is not required unless more than 12 months have elapsed since the employee's last general orientation or if significant policy changes have occurred. | Within 30 calendar days of transfer effective date. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New clinical employee fails competency assessment after extended orientation period | DON notifies Administrator and HR Director. | Employment may be terminated during probationary period per HR-ER-002. DON documents specific competency deficits and remediation efforts attempted. | Decision within 5 business days of failed extended assessment. |
| Orientation not completed within required timeframe due to scheduling issues | HR Director notifies Administrator. | Orientation completion deadline extended with documented justification. Employee remains under supervision until completed. | Extension approved within 3 business days; orientation completed within 15 additional days. |
| Contract staff refuses abbreviated orientation | HR Director denies assignment clearance; notifies staffing agency. | Individual may not provide services. Staffing agency notified to provide alternate personnel. | Immediate denial; replacement requested same day. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| General orientation completion | General Agency Orientation Checklist (Appendix A) — signed | HR Director and employee | Personnel file | Completed by Day 5; filed within 2 business days. |
| Role-specific/clinical orientation completion | Role-Specific/Clinical Orientation Checklist (Appendix B) — signed | DON/Supervisor, preceptor, and employee | Personnel file | Completed by Day 30; filed within 2 business days. |
| Contract staff orientation | Contract Staff Orientation Checklist (Appendix C) — signed | HR Director and contract staff | Contract staff file | Before first patient assignment. |
| Orientation competency quiz | Completed General Orientation Competency Quiz (Appendix D) with score | HR Director | Personnel file | Day 5; remediation documented if initial fail. |
| Supervised visit evaluations | Supervised Visit Evaluation Forms (Appendix E) for each supervised visit | Preceptor | Personnel file; DON review file | After each supervised visit. |
| Policy acknowledgment forms | Signed acknowledgments for all policies presented during orientation | HR Director (collection) | Personnel file | By Day 5 (general policies); by Day 30 (role-specific policies). |
| Remediation plans (if applicable) | Written remediation plan for orientation competency concerns | DON / Supervisor | Personnel file | Within 3 business days of identifying concern. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100% of new hires complete general orientation within 5 business days | Audit of Appendix A completion dates against hire dates | Zero employees beyond Day 5 without completed general orientation. |
| 100% of clinical staff complete role-specific orientation within 30 days | Audit of Appendix B completion dates | Zero clinical staff practicing independently without completed Appendix B. |
| 100% of contract staff complete abbreviated orientation before first assignment | Audit of Appendix C in contract staff files | Zero contract staff assigned without completed orientation. |
| Orientation competency quiz pass rate ≥ 80% on first attempt | Quiz score tracking | ≥ 90% of employees pass on first attempt; 100% pass after remediation. |
| All required policy acknowledgments collected | Audit of personnel files | 100% of required acknowledgments on file. |

### 8.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical staff sent to patients before orientation is complete | CMS survey deficiency; patient safety risk; liability | Enforce zero-independent-visit rule until Appendix B is signed. DON controls clinical schedule clearance. |
| Orientation content outdated | Employees trained on superseded policies/procedures | Annual content review documented; HR Director and DON sign off on updated curriculum each January. |
| Orientation checklist not signed by employee and trainer | Surveyor treats unsigned orientation as not completed | Both signatures required; HR Director audits within 5 business days of due date. |
| Contract staff orientation skipped due to urgency | Liability; non-compliance with HIPAA and safety training requirements | No patient assignment without Appendix C on file. No exceptions. |

# Job Description & Role Definition

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes requirements for the development, approval, maintenance, and distribution of written job descriptions for all positions at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Job descriptions serve as the foundational document defining the qualifications, scope of authority, essential functions, reporting relationships, and regulatory requirements for each position. CMS surveyors verify that employees meet the qualifications defined in job descriptions per 42 CFR § 484.105 and § 484.115. Written job descriptions also support ADA compliance, performance management, recruitment, disciplinary processes, and workforce planning.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All positions within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. including clinical, administrative, and support roles
All hiring managers, supervisors, and department heads responsible for defining or maintaining job descriptions
The HR Director and Director of Nursing
The Administrator
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Every position at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall have a current, written, approved job description on file with the HR Director.
4.2 Job descriptions shall be developed and approved before any individual is recruited for or appointed to a position per HR-TA-001 § 6.1.2.
4.3 Each job description must contain, at minimum, the following elements: (a) position title; (b) department/discipline; (c) FLSA classification (exempt/non-exempt); (d) reporting relationship (reports to); (e) supervisory responsibilities; (f) position summary; (g) essential functions (ADA-compliant language); (h) minimum qualifications (education, experience, licensure/certification); (i) preferred qualifications; (j) physical requirements and working conditions; (k) regulatory requirements specific to the position; (l) approval signatures and date.
4.4 Job descriptions shall be reviewed at least biennially (every 24 months) or upon: (a) regulatory change affecting the position; (b) significant change in duties; (c) vacancy requiring recruitment; (d) organizational restructuring.
4.5 Each employee shall receive a copy of their current job description at hire, upon any revision, and at each annual performance evaluation, and shall sign an acknowledgment.
4.6 Job descriptions for clinical positions must align with the HR-JD series policies (HR-JD-000 through HR-JD-011) and applicable professional practice acts.
4.7 Only the most current approved version shall be considered valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Essential Functions | The fundamental duties of a position that an employee must be able to perform, with or without reasonable accommodation, as distinct from marginal functions. Essential functions are determined based on: the reason the position exists, the number of employees available to perform the function, and the degree of specialization required. |
| FLSA Classification | The determination of whether a position is exempt or non-exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act, affecting overtime eligibility. |
| Minimum Qualifications | The education, experience, licensure, certification, and competency requirements that a candidate must possess to be considered for the position. |
| Preferred Qualifications | Additional qualifications that enhance a candidate's suitability but are not required for consideration. |
| Physical Requirements | The physical demands of the position including lifting, standing, walking, driving, and environmental exposures, documented in ADA-compliant language. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Job Description Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Hiring Manager / Department Head | When a new position is created or an existing position requires a new/revised job description, draft the job description using the Job Description Template (Appendix A). | Prior to recruitment or upon triggering event. |
| 6.1.2 | HR Director | Review the draft for: (a) ADA-compliant essential functions language; (b) FLSA classification accuracy; (c) alignment with applicable regulatory requirements; (d) consistency with agency organizational structure; (e) appropriate minimum qualifications. | Within 5 business days of receiving draft. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | For clinical positions: review and co-approve ensuring alignment with applicable professional practice acts, CMS CoP requirements, and HR-JD series policies. | Within 5 business days. |
| 6.1.4 | Administrator | Provide final approval. Sign and date the job description. | Within 5 business days of DON/HR review. |
| 6.1.5 | HR Director | File the approved job description in the master job description file. Distribute to the hiring manager. | Within 2 business days of approval. |

### 6.2 Biennial Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | HR Director | Maintain a Job Description Review Tracking Log (Appendix B) listing all positions, current job description version dates, and next review due dates. | Ongoing; reviewed quarterly. |
| 6.2.2 | HR Director | At least 60 days before the biennial review due date, notify the applicable department head/hiring manager that a review is due. Provide the current job description for review. | 60 days before due date. |
| 6.2.3 | Department Head / Hiring Manager | Review the job description for accuracy. Mark any proposed changes. Return to HR Director with: ☐ No changes — current version confirmed, or ☐ Revisions proposed — with tracked changes. | Within 30 calendar days of notification. |
| 6.2.4 | HR Director / DON / Administrator | Process confirmed or revised job descriptions through the approval workflow per Section 6.1. Update the review tracking log. | Within 15 business days of receiving department response. |

### 6.3 Employee Acknowledgment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | HR Director | Provide a copy of the current job description to each new employee during orientation (HR-TA-005). | Day 1 of employment. |
| 6.3.2 | Employee | Sign the Job Description Acknowledgment (Appendix C) confirming receipt, review, and understanding of the essential functions and requirements. | Within 5 business days of hire. |
| 6.3.3 | Supervisor | Provide the current job description to the employee at each annual performance evaluation (HR-ER-001) and upon any revision. Obtain updated acknowledgment signature. | At each annual evaluation; within 14 days of revision. |

### 6.4 Escalation

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Position being recruited for without current job description | HR Director halts recruitment per HR-TA-001 § 6.1.2. | Job description developed on expedited timeline. | Job description completed within 10 business days. |
| Biennial review overdue by more than 30 days | HR Director notifies Administrator. | Department head required to complete review within 14 days. Non-response documented. | Within 14 days of Administrator notification. |

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approved job descriptions | Current job description for every position (Appendix A format) | HR Director | Master job description file | Current at all times. |
| Review tracking | Job Description Review Tracking Log (Appendix B) | HR Director | HR records | Ongoing; reviewed quarterly. |
| Employee acknowledgments | Signed Job Description Acknowledgment (Appendix C) | Employee (signature); HR Director (filing) | Personnel file | At hire; at each revision; at each annual evaluation. |

| Biennial review cycle current | Tracking log audit | Zero overdue reviews exceeding 30 days. |
| Clinical job descriptions align with HR-JD series | Cross-reference audit | 100% alignment. |

# POLICY HR-TD-001
# Annual Mandatory Training Requirements
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TD-001__ |
| Title | Annual Mandatory Training Requirements |
| Domain | HR — Human Resources |
| Subdomain | TD — Training & Development |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | HR Director / Administrator |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director__ |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy defines the agency's annual mandatory training requirements for all employees to ensure continuous compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation, OSHA standards, HIPAA, OIG compliance guidance, California home health licensing requirements, and agency operational standards. Annual training reinforces critical knowledge, addresses emerging risks, fulfills regulatory mandates, and supports the QAPI program's commitment to continuous improvement per 42 CFR § 484.65.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to: All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (full-time, part-time, per diem) regardless of position. Contracted staff training requirements are addressed through staffing agency contractual obligations and verified per HR-TA-001 § 6.6.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an Annual Mandatory Training Program that requires every employee to complete defined training topics each calendar year.
4.2 The Annual Mandatory Training Calendar (Appendix A) shall be established by the HR Director in collaboration with the Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, and Risk Manager by December 15 of each year for the upcoming year.
4.3 All mandatory training must be completed by each employee within the calendar year (January 1 – December 31). New hires who start after July 1 must complete all remaining mandatory training by December 31 of their hire year or within 6 months of hire, whichever is later.
4.4 Training may be delivered through in-person classroom, online/e-learning, competency fairs, simulations, or a combination, provided that: (a) content meets regulatory requirements; (b) completion is individually documented; (c) competency is assessed where required.
4.5 The HR Director shall maintain an Annual Training Compliance Dashboard (Appendix B) tracking completion rates by employee, department, and topic.
4.6 Failure to complete mandatory training within the required timeframe shall result in progressive action: (a) written reminder at 30 days overdue; (b) supervisor notification at 45 days overdue; (c) administrative suspension from clinical duties (clinical staff) or disciplinary action per HR-ER-002 at 60 days overdue.
4.7 Only the most current approved version shall be valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Mandatory Training | Training required by federal or state regulation, CMS Conditions of Participation, OSHA, HIPAA, OIG guidance, or agency policy, that must be completed by all or designated employees on a defined cycle. |
| Competency Assessment | An evaluation method (test, return demonstration, simulation, case study) that measures whether the employee can apply the training content to their job duties. |
| Training Compliance Rate | The percentage of employees who have completed all required training within the defined timeframe. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Annual Training Calendar Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.__ | HR Director | By November 1, solicit input from the Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, Risk Manager, and QAPI Coordinator regarding training needs for the upcoming year based on: (a) regulatory changes; (b) survey findings; (c) incident trends; (d) QAPI data; (e) competency evaluation results (HR-TD-003). | By November 1. |
| 6.1.__ | HR Director | Develop the Annual Mandatory Training Calendar (Appendix A) listing all required topics, applicable staff groups, delivery methods, scheduled dates, and competency assessment requirements. | By December 1. |
| 6.1.3 | Administrator | Review and approve the Annual Mandatory Training Calendar. | By December 15. |
| 6.1.4 | HR Director | Distribute the approved calendar to all department heads and post agency-wide. | By January 1 of the training year. |

### 6.2 Mandatory Training Topics
The following training topics are required annually for ALL employees unless otherwise noted:

| # | Training Topic | Regulatory Basis | Applicable Staff | Competency Assessment Required? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Corporate Compliance Program & Code of Conduct | OIG Guidance; CO-CP-001, CO-CP-004, CO-CP-008 | All | Yes — quiz |
| 2 | Fraud, Waste & Abuse Prevention | OIG; CMS; CO-FA-003 | All | Yes — quiz |
| 3 | HIPAA Privacy & Security | HIPAA; CO-HP-001, CO-HP-002 | All | Yes — quiz |
| 4 | Patient Rights & Responsibilities | 42 CFR § 484.50; CL-PR-001 | All | No |
| 5 | Abuse, Neglect & Exploitation — Identification and Mandatory Reporting | State law; CL-PR-006; HR-ER-009 | All | Yes — quiz |
| 6 | Infection Prevention & Control — Standard Precautions | 42 CFR § 484.70; CL-SD-016; OSHA | All clinical + support staff with patient/facility contact | Yes — return demo (hand hygiene, PPE) |
| 7 | Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure Control | OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030 | All with occupational exposure | Yes — quiz__ |
| 8 | Emergency Preparedness | 42 CFR § 484.102; OP-FM-005; HR-TD-005 | All | No — covered through drills |
| 9 | Fire Safety & Evacuation | OSHA; state fire code | All | No — drill participation__ |
| 10 | Workplace Safety & Injury Prevention | OSHA; HR-WM-004; RM-SS-001 | All | No |
| 11 | Workplace Violence Prevention | OSHA; Cal/OSHA; RM-SS-002 | All | No |
| 12 | Anti-Harassment & Non-Discrimination (2 hours per CA law__ | FEHA; SB 1343; HR-ER-004 | All (supervisors: additional component__ | Yes — quiz |
| 13 | Cultural Competency & Health Equity | CMS; OP-PA-004 | All clinical | No |
| 14 | Pain Assessment & Management | CMS; CL-SD-014 | Clinical only | Yes — case study |
| 15 | Fall Risk Assessment & Prevention | CMS; CL-SD-015 | Clinical only | Yes — case study |
| 16 | Medication Safety & Reconciliation | CMS; CL-SD-012, CL-SD-013 | Clinical only | Yes — quiz |
| 17 | OASIS Updates & Accuracy | CMS; CL-OA series | OASIS-authorized clinicians | Yes — coding exercise__ |
| 18 | IT Security Awareness | HIPAA Security; IT-UP-004 | All | Yes — phishing simulation |
| 19 | Documentation Standards | CL-CD-001; CO-DC series | All clinical | No |
| 20 | Advance Directives | 42 CFR § 484.58; CL-PR-002 | All clinical | No |

### 6.3 Training Delivery and Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | HR Director / Training Coordinator | Deliver training per the approved calendar using approved content and delivery methods. Ensure all training sessions are documented using the Training Attendance Record (Appendix C). | Per calendar schedule. |
| 6.3.2 | Training Instructor | At each training session, collect signatures on the Training Attendance Record (Appendix C) documenting: (a) training topic; (b) date; (c) instructor name; (d) delivery method; (e) each attendee's printed name and signature; (f) competency assessment results (if applicable). | At each training session. |
| 6.3.3 | HR Director | For e-learning modules, ensure the LMS (learning management system) captures: (a) employee name; (b) course title; (c) completion date; (d) assessment score. Export and file completion records. | Ongoing; exported at least quarterly. |
| 6.3.4 | HR Director | Update the Annual Training Compliance Dashboard (Appendix B) at least monthly. Identify employees with incomplete training and initiate the notification/escalation process per Section 4.6. | Monthly by the 15th. |

### 6.4 Non-Compliance Escalation

| Days Overdue | Action | Responsible Party |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 days past deadline | Written reminder to employee with copy to supervisor. | HR Director |
| 45 days past deadline | Second written notice; supervisor meeting with employee to schedule immediate completion__ | Supervisor; HR Director notified.__ |
| 60 days past deadline | Clinical staff: suspended from patient care duties until training complete. All staff: formal corrective action per HR-ER-002. Administrator notified. | HR Director; Administrator |

| Non-compliance notifications | Written reminders and escalation correspondence | HR Director | Personnel file | Per escalation schedule. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring

| Competency assessments administered where required | Audit of personnel files for assessment results | 100% of assessed trainings have documented results. |
| Zero clinical staff providing care with overdue mandatory training >60 days | Cross-reference dashboard with active clinical staff list | Zero non-compliant clinicians providing patient care. |

# POLICY HR-TD-002
# Continuing Education & Professional Development
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TD-002__ |
| Title | Continuing Education & Professional Development |
| Domain | HR — Human Resources |
| Subdomain | TD — Training & Development |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | HR Director / Administrator |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director__ |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for supporting, tracking, and documenting continuing education (CE) and professional development activities for all professional staff at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Continuing education ensures that clinical and professional employees maintain the knowledge and competencies required by their licensing boards, advances evidence-based practice, and supports the agency's commitment to quality patient care and regulatory compliance.
## 3. Scope
All licensed/certified professional staff (RN, LVN, PT, PTA, OT, COTA, SLP, MSW) and any other credentialed staff whose licensure or certification requires continuing education. Administrative staff professional development is encouraged but not mandated by this policy.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All licensed/certified professional employees are responsible for meeting the CE requirements of their respective licensing boards and maintaining proof of compliance.
4.2 The agency shall support continuing education by: (a) providing paid time for approved CE activities up to 16 hours per year for full-time employees (prorated for part-time); (b) maintaining a CE resource library; (c) offering in-house CE opportunities where feasible.
4.3 The agency shall maintain a CE Tracking System (Appendix A) to monitor each employee's CE status relative to their license renewal requirements.
4.4 Employees shall submit documentation of completed CE activities to the HR Director within 30 calendar days of completion using the CE Activity Report Form (Appendix B__
4.5 CE activities must be relevant to the employee's professional role and obtained from providers approved or accredited by the applicable licensing board.
4.6 Failure to maintain CE compliance as required by the licensing board places the employee's license at risk. The agency will coordinate with HR-TA-004 to address any licensure issues arising from CE non-compliance.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Continuing Education (CE) | Structured educational activities designed to maintain, develop, or enhance the knowledge, skills, and professional competence of licensed professionals, as required by their licensing boards. |
| CE Unit / Contact Hour | The standard measurement of continuing education. One contact hour typically equals 50-60 minutes of educational activity. CE requirements vary by profession and state. |
| Approved Provider | An organization or institution accredited or approved by the applicable licensing board or recognized accrediting body to offer continuing education. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 CE Requirement Identification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.__ | HR Director | Maintain a reference table of CE requirements for each license type represented in the agency workforce per applicable California licensing board requirements. | Updated annually by January 31. |
| 6.1.2 | HR Director | During orientation (HR-TA-005) and at each annual performance evaluation (HR-ER-001), inform each professional employee of their specific CE requirements including: (a) total hours required per renewal cycle; (b) any mandatory content areas (e.g., California RN CE requirements for specific topics); (c) approved provider requirements. | At orientation; annually at evaluation. |

### 6.2 CE Activity Approval and Support

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.__ | Employee | Submit a CE Activity Request (Appendix C) to supervisor for any CE activity requiring paid time or agency resources. | At least 14 calendar days before the activity. |
| 6.2.2 | Supervisor | Review the request for relevance and operational coverage feasibility. Approve or deny with documented rationale. | Within 7 business days. |
| 6.2.3 | Employee | Upon completion of CE activity, submit the CE Activity Report Form (Appendix B) with proof of completion (certificate, transcript) to HR Director. | Within 30 calendar days of completion. |

### 6.3 CE Tracking and Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | HR Director | Enter completed CE activities into the CE Tracking System (Appendix A). | Within 10 business days of receiving documentation. |
| 6.3.2 | HR Director | At least 120 days before each employee's license renewal date (coordinated with HR-TA-004 tracking), review their CE status. If the employee is at risk of not meeting CE requirements, notify the employee and supervisor in writing. | 120 days before renewal due date. |
| 6.3.3 | HR Director | Report aggregate CE compliance data to the Director of Nursing quarterly and to QAPI per QA-PI-005 annually. | Quarterly to DON; annually to QAPI. |

### 6.4 Escalation

| Condition | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Employee at risk of CE non-compliance 90 days before renewal | Written notice to employee and supervisor; individualized CE plan developed. | Within 7 days of identification. |
| Employee's license renewal submitted without meeting CE requirements | Licensure issue managed per HR-TA-004. Employee may be at risk of board action. | Per HR-TA-004 procedures. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CE tracking | CE Tracking System (Appendix A) | HR records | Ongoing.__ |
| CE activity reports | CE Activity Report Forms (Appendix B) with certificates | Personnel file | Within 30 days of activity completion. |
| CE requests | CE Activity Request Forms (Appendix C) | Personnel file | As submitted. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All professional staff CE status tracked | Audit of Appendix A | 100% of licensed staff on tracking system. |
| CE documentation current for all staff approaching renewal | Audit 120 days before renewal dates | 100% of staff within 80% of CE requirement at 120-day check. |
| CE completion documentation on file | Personnel file audit | 100% of reported CE activities have supporting certificates on file. |

| California PT Board CE Requirements | PT/PTA CE standards. |

## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 All professional staff informed of CE policy during orientation. 10.2 Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) signed within 14 days.

# POLICY HR-TD-003
# Clinical Staff Competency Evaluation
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TD-003 |
| Title | Clinical Staff Competency Evaluation |
| Domain | HR — Human Resources |
| Subdomain | TD — Training & Development |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | HR Director / Director of Nursing / Administrator |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes requirements for initial and ongoing competency evaluation for all clinical staff at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Competency evaluation ensures that clinical personnel possess and maintain the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to provide safe, effective patient care in compliance with 42 CFR § 484.105, § 484.80 (HHA competency), § 484.115 (personnel qualifications), and applicable California professional practice standards. Competency results are linked to the QAPI program per QA-PI-005 and QA-PI-007 to drive targeted education and performance improvement.
## 3. Scope
All clinical staff: RN, LVN, PT, PTA, OT, COTA, SLP, MSW, HHA, and any other clinical personnel providing direct or indirect patient care. Contracted clinical staff competency is verified per HR-TA-001 § 6.6.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Every clinical employee shall undergo an initial competency evaluation during orientation (HR-TA-005) and an annual competency evaluation thereafter.
4.2 Competency evaluation shall assess both general clinical competencies (applicable to all clinical staff) and discipline-specific competencies (applicable to each profession's scope of practice).
4.3 Competency shall be evaluated using multiple methods: direct observation, skills demonstration (return demonstration), written assessment, case study analysis, clinical record review, and/or simulation.
4.4 Home health aides shall be evaluated per 42 CFR § 484.80 requirements including competency in all required skill areas with supervised performance at least every 12 months.
4.5 Competency deficits shall trigger a documented remediation plan with defined milestones and reassessment timeframe. An employee who fails to achieve competency after remediation shall be referred for employment action per HR-ER-002.
4.6 Competency evaluation results shall be reported to the QAPI program per QA-PI-005 and QA-PI-007 to identify training needs and measure the impact of education on patient outcomes.
4.7 Only the most current approved version shall be valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Competency | The demonstrated ability to apply knowledge, skills, and judgment to perform clinical duties safely and effectively in alignment with established standards of practice and agency protocols. |
| Competency Evaluation | A structured assessment process using defined criteria and tools to determine whether a clinical employee meets the required standard of performance. |
| Remediation Plan | A documented plan specifying the competency deficit, targeted education/training interventions, practice opportunities, reassessment method, timeline, and responsible supervisor. |
| Skills Check-Off | A direct observation evaluation in which the employee demonstrates a specific clinical skill to a qualified evaluator who documents the performance against a defined checklist of required steps. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Initial Competency Evaluation (During Orientation)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Using the Clinical Competency Evaluation Tool (Appendix A), identify the competencies required for the new employee's position based on: (a) job description essential functions; (b) discipline-specific regulatory requirements; (c) agency clinical protocols; (d) current patient population care needs. | Prior to orientation start. |
| 6.1.2 | Preceptor / DON Designee | Evaluate the new employee on all required competencies during the orientation period per HR-TA-005. Methods: (a) Skills check-off for hands-on competencies (Appendix A checklist); (b) Written assessment for knowledge-based competencies; (c) Supervised visit evaluations per HR-TA-005, Appendix E; (d) EHR proficiency demonstration; (e) OASIS competency assessment per CL-OA-003 and CL-OA-018 (for OASIS-authorized clinicians). | Within the 30-day orientation period. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | Review all initial competency evaluation results. Determine: ☐ Competent — cleared for independent practice; ☐ Competency concerns — remediation plan required (Section 6.3); ☐ Not competent — employment action per HR-ER-002. | Within 5 business days of orientation completion. |

### 6.2 Annual Competency Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Director of Nursing / HR Director | By January 31, develop the Annual Competency Evaluation Plan (Appendix B) identifying: (a) competencies to be assessed for each discipline; (b) agency-wide focus competencies based on QAPI data, incident trends, survey findings, and regulatory changes; (c) evaluation methods and tools; (d) schedule. | By January 31 each year. |
| 6.2.2 | Clinical Supervisors / DON Designees | Conduct annual competency evaluations for all clinical staff using the Clinical Competency Evaluation Tool (Appendix A). Evaluate a combination of: (a) core competencies (infection control, medication safety, documentation, patient rights, fall prevention, pain assessment); (b) discipline-specific competencies; (c) agency focus competencies per the annual plan. | Between February 1 and October 31 each year. |
| 6.2.3 | Clinical Supervisor / Evaluator | Document all evaluation results on Appendix A. For each competency: assign a rating (Competent / Needs Improvement / Not Competent); document evidence supporting the rating. | At the time of evaluation. |
| 6.2.4 | Director of Nursing | Compile annual competency evaluation results. Report aggregate data to QAPI per QA-PI-005 and QA-PI-007 including: (a) percentage of staff meeting competency standards; (b) most common competency deficits; (c) correlation with patient outcome data; (d) targeted training recommendations. | By November 30 each year. |

### 6.3 Competency Remediation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Clinical Supervisor | When a competency deficit is identified: meet with the employee to discuss the finding. Develop a written Competency Remediation Plan (Appendix C) specifying: (a) the specific competency deficit; (b) targeted education/training interventions; (c) practice opportunities; (d) reassessment method and criteria; (e) timeline for completion (not to exceed 60 calendar days); (f) responsible supervisor. | Within 7 business days of identifying the deficit. |
| 6.3.2 | Employee | Complete all remediation activities as defined in the plan. | Per plan timeline. |
| 6.3.3 | Clinical Supervisor | Conduct reassessment using the method specified in the plan. Document results on Appendix C. | Upon completion of remediation activities. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing | If the employee achieves competency: document resolution on Appendix C; file in personnel file. If the employee does NOT achieve competency after remediation: refer to Administrator and HR Director for employment action per HR-ER-002. The employee shall be removed from performing the deficient clinical activity until competency is demonstrated. | Within 5 business days of reassessment. |

### 6.4 Home Health Aide Competency (42 CFR § 484.80)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing / RN Supervisor | Evaluate each HHA on all competency areas required by 42 CFR § 484.80(h) at hire and at least every 12 months: (a) Communication skills; (b) Observation, reporting, documentation; (c) Reading/recording vital signs; (d) Basic infection control; (e) Basic body mechanics/safe transfer; (f) Basic nutrition/meal prep; (g) Maintenance of clean/safe/healthy environment; (h) Understanding of patient/family emotional, spiritual, cultural needs; (i) Subject areas specific to patient assignments. Use the HHA Competency Evaluation Form (Appendix D). | At hire and annually. |
| 6.4.2 | RN Supervisor | Conduct a supervised HHA visit at least every 14 days for the first 60 days of employment and at least every 60 days thereafter per 42 CFR § 484.80(h). Document supervision on the HHA Supervisory Visit Form (Appendix E). | Per CMS schedule. |

## 7. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial and annual competency evaluations | Clinical Competency Evaluation Tool (Appendix A) | Personnel file | At orientation; annually. |
| Annual competency evaluation plan | Annual Competency Evaluation Plan (Appendix B) | HR records; DON file | By January 31 each year. |
| Remediation plans and reassessments | Competency Remediation Plan (Appendix C) | Personnel file | As needed; within 7 days of identifying deficit. |
| HHA competency evaluations | HHA Competency Evaluation Form (Appendix D) | Personnel file | At hire; annually. |
| HHA supervisory visits | HHA Supervisory Visit Form (Appendix E) | Personnel file; clinical records | Per CMS schedule. |
| QAPI competency reports | Aggregate data report | QAPI records | Annually by November 30.__ |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100% of clinical staff have completed annual competency evaluation | Audit of personnel files for current Appendix A | 100% by October 31. |
| 100% of HHAs evaluated per 42 CFR § 484.80 schedule | Audit of Appendix D and E | 100% on schedule. |
| Remediation plans documented and resolved | Audit of Appendix C | 100% of identified deficits have documented plans and resolution. |
| Competency data reported to QAPI | QAPI meeting minutes | Annual report documented. |

## 9. References

# POLICY HR-TD-004
# Student & Intern Supervision
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TD-004 |
| Title | Student & Intern Supervision |
| Classification Tier | RECOMMENDED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Biennial |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes requirements for accepting, supervising, and evaluating students and interns completing clinical or administrative fieldwork at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Proper supervision protects patients, maintains regulatory compliance, supports workforce pipeline development, and ensures that student activities are conducted under appropriate professional oversight in compliance with applicable professional practice acts, educational program requirements, and agency standards.
## 3. Scope
All students and interns from accredited educational programs placed at the agency for clinical rotations, fieldwork, or administrative internships. All staff serving as preceptors or supervisors for students/interns. The Director of Nursing, HR Director, and Administrator.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The agency shall only accept students/interns from accredited educational programs with which the agency has a current, signed Affiliation Agreement (Appendix A).
4.2 Students/interns shall not provide any patient care services independently. All patient care activities must be under the direct supervision of a licensed preceptor.
4.3 Students/interns shall complete an abbreviated orientation (per HR-TA-005, Appendix C standards) and sign confidentiality/HIPAA agreements before any patient contact.
4.4 Preceptors must meet minimum qualifications: (a) current unrestricted license in the applicable discipline; (b) minimum 2 years of clinical experience; (c) minimum 1 year with the agency; (d) no active disciplinary actions; (e) completion of preceptor training.
4.5 The agency shall conduct OIG/SAM screening (HR-TA-003) and verify student identity before placement begins.
4.6 Students/interns are not employees and shall not be used to replace or supplement staff for patient care coverage.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Affiliation Agreement | A written contract between the agency and an accredited educational institution defining the terms, responsibilities, liability, and insurance requirements for student placements. |
| Preceptor | A licensed agency employee designated to provide direct supervision, mentorship, and clinical instruction to an assigned student/intern. |
| Direct Supervision | The preceptor is physically present during all patient care activities performed by the student. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Affiliation Agreement and Placement Approval

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | HR Director / Administrator | Review and execute an Affiliation Agreement (Appendix A) with each educational institution prior to accepting any student. The agreement must address: (a) responsibilities of each party; (b) supervision requirements; (c) liability and malpractice insurance; (d) HIPAA compliance; (e) workers' compensation coverage for students; (f) grounds for termination of placement; (g) term and renewal provisions. | Prior to first student placement. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | Evaluate each student placement request for: (a) patient care impact; (b) preceptor availability; (c) operational feasibility. Approve or deny. | Within 14 business days of request. |

### 6.2 Student Onboarding

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | HR Director | Before the student begins: (a) Verify student identity; (b) Conduct OIG/SAM screening per HR-TA-003; (c) Verify current student liability/malpractice insurance; (d) Obtain signed Confidentiality and HIPAA Agreement (Appendix B); (e) Conduct abbreviated orientation per HR-TA-005, Appendix C. | Before first day of placement. |
| 6.2.2 | Assigned Preceptor | Meet with the student to review: (a) learning objectives; (b) schedule; (c) supervision expectations; (d) patient safety requirements; (e) documentation standards; (f) communication/escalation protocols. | First day of placement. |

### 6.3 Supervision and Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Preceptor | Provide direct supervision for all patient care activities. Complete the Student Performance Evaluation Form (Appendix C) at the midpoint and end of the placement. | Midpoint and end of placement. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Review student evaluations. Address any concerns. Provide written evaluation summary to the educational institution per the affiliation agreement. | Within 14 days of placement end. |

### 6.4 Termination of Placement

| Condition | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Student demonstrates unsafe clinical practice | Preceptor immediately suspends patient care activities. DON reviews; may terminate placement with notification to institution. |
| HIPAA violation by student | Immediate termination of placement. Compliance Officer notified per CO-HP-003. |
| Student found on OIG/SAM exclusion list | Immediate termination of placement. |

## 7–8. Documentation & Compliance Monitoring

| Requirement | Document | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Affiliation agreements | Appendix A | Contract files |
| Confidentiality/HIPAA agreements | Appendix B | Student file |
| Performance evaluations | Appendix C | Student file; copy to institution |
| OIG/SAM screening | Per HR-TA-003 | Student file |
| Orientation documentation | Per HR-TA-005 Appendix C | Student file |

## 9. References
42 CFR § 484.105; applicable California professional practice acts; HR-TA-003; HR-TA-005; CO-HP-001; CO-HP-002.

Per standard provisions. Acknowledgment Form = Appendix D.

# POLICY HR-TD-005
# Emergency Preparedness Training & Drills
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | HR-TD-005 |
| Title | Emergency Preparedness Training & Drills |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Policy Owner/Steward | HR Director |
| Status | ACTIVE |

## 2. Purpose
This policy mandates initial and annual emergency preparedness training and drill participation for all staff at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. per 42 CFR § 484.102 (Emergency Preparedness), CMS Emergency Preparedness Rule requirements, and California state emergency preparedness standards. Training ensures all employees understand their roles during emergencies, can execute the agency's Emergency Operations and Business Continuity Plan (OP-FM-005), and can protect patients and themselves during disasters, pandemics, and other emergencies.
## 3. Scope
All employees regardless of position. Coordination with OP-FM-005, CL-PR-005, RM-EP-001, RM-EP-002, and RM-EP-003.
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All new employees shall complete emergency preparedness training during orientation per HR-TA-005.
4.2 All employees shall participate in at least 2 emergency preparedness exercises per year: (a) one community-based exercise (if available) or a tabletop exercise; and (b) one agency-based drill (tabletop, functional, or full-scale). Per CMS requirements, if the agency participates in a community-based exercise, the second exercise may be a tabletop. If not, both must be exercises (at least one being a full-scale or functional exercise).
4.3 Each drill/exercise shall be followed by a documented after-action review (AAR) identifying strengths, gaps, and corrective actions.
4.4 Training and drill completion shall be documented and retained per CO-HP-007.
4.5 Drill results shall be reported to the Governing Body per GV-GB-001 § 6.2.6.2 and to the QAPI program.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Tabletop Exercise | A discussion-based exercise where participants walk through a simulated emergency scenario verbally, testing plans, policies, and communication without actual deployment of resources. |
| Functional Exercise | An exercise that tests specific operations or functions of the emergency plan in a simulated environment with actual deployment of some resources. |
| Full-Scale Exercise | A comprehensive exercise that tests the entire emergency plan with actual resource deployment and real-time coordination. |
| After-Action Review (AAR) | A structured debrief following an exercise or actual emergency that evaluates performance, identifies gaps, and generates corrective action items. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Annual Emergency Preparedness Training

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | HR Director / Risk Manager | Include emergency preparedness training in the Annual Mandatory Training Calendar (HR-TD-001, Appendix A). Content must cover: (a) agency Emergency Operations Plan overview (OP-FM-005); (b) staff roles and responsibilities during emergencies; (c) patient communication and prioritization per RM-EP-003; (d) pandemic/infectious disease protocols per RM-EP-001; (e) evacuation and shelter-in-place procedures; (f) communication systems and contact trees; (g) supply and equipment emergency access; (h) post-emergency procedures and documentation. | Per HR-TD-001 calendar. |
| 6.1.2 | All employees | Complete annual emergency preparedness training. | Per HR-TD-001 schedule. |

### 6.2 Emergency Drills/Exercises

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Administrator / Risk Manager | Plan and schedule at least 2 emergency exercises per year per Section 4.2. Document the exercise plan using the Emergency Exercise Planning Form (Appendix A). | Exercise 1: by June 30. Exercise 2: by December 31. |
| 6.2.2 | Administrator / Risk Manager | Conduct the exercise. Document participation using the Exercise Participation Log (Appendix B). | Per schedule. |
| 6.2.3 | Administrator / Risk Manager | Within 14 calendar days of each exercise, conduct and document an After-Action Review (Appendix C) including: (a) exercise description; (b) participants; (c) objectives met and not met; (d) strengths identified; (e) gaps/weaknesses identified; (f) corrective actions with assigned owners and deadlines. | Within 14 calendar days of exercise. |
| 6.2.4 | Administrator | Report exercise results and AAR findings to the Governing Body per GV-GB-001 § 6.2.6.2 and to QAPI. | At the quarterly meeting following the exercise. |

### 6.3 Corrective Actions from Drills

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Risk Manager | Track all corrective actions from AARs to completion using the AAR Corrective Action Tracker (included in Appendix C). | Ongoing until all actions complete. |
| 6.3.2 | Risk Manager | If corrective actions are not completed by the target date, escalate to the Administrator. | Within 7 days of missed deadline. |

## 7–8. Documentation & Compliance Monitoring

| Requirement | Document | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exercise planning | Appendix A | 2 exercises per year documented. |
| Participation logs | Appendix B | ≥ 80% staff participation per exercise. |
| After-action reviews | Appendix C | AAR completed within 14 days of each exercise. |
| Corrective action tracking | Appendix C tracker | 100% of corrective actions completed or escalated. |
| Governing Body reporting | Meeting minutes | Results reported per GV-GB-001. |

## 9. References
42 CFR § 484.102; CMS Emergency Preparedness Rule; OP-FM-005; CL-PR-005; RM-EP-001; RM-EP-002; RM-EP-003; GV-GB-001 § 6.2.6; HR-TD-001.
## 10–11. Training & Version Control
Per standard provisions. Acknowledgment Form = Appendix D.
