| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for receiving, screening, processing, and managing patient referrals and intake activities at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The referral and intake process is the gateway to all home health services and must ensure timely, accurate, and compliant processing of every referral to support patient access, regulatory compliance, and continuity of care. This policy ensures the agency satisfies applicable requirements of 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration), 42 CFR § 484.50 (Patient Rights — timely acceptance/notification), and 42 CFR § 484.55 (Comprehensive Assessment).
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to:
All intake coordinators, intake nurses, and intake staff
The Operations Director
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Administrator
All clinical staff involved in referral screening or clinical eligibility determination
All contracted or per diem staff performing intake functions
All referral sources communicating with the agency
This policy does not govern clinical assessment content after admission (see CL-CA-001) or billing/authorization processes (see FN-CM-004).
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Referral | A communication from a physician, hospital, skilled nursing facility, patient/family, or other source requesting home health services for a patient. |
| Intake | The administrative and clinical screening process that evaluates a referral for appropriateness, eligibility, and agency capacity prior to acceptance or denial. |
| Referral Source | Any individual or entity that initiates a referral, including physicians, discharge planners, case managers, patients, family members, and community organizations. |
| Clinical Eligibility Screening | The clinical review of referral information to determine whether the patient meets criteria for home health services including homebound status, skilled need, and medical necessity. |
| Intake Coordinator | The designated staff member responsible for receiving, logging, screening, and processing referrals per this policy. |
| Payer Verification | The process of confirming the patient's insurance coverage, benefit eligibility, and authorization requirements prior to admission. |
| Service Area | The geographic boundaries within which the agency is authorized and operationally equipped to provide services, as defined in OP-IM-003. |
| Referral Disposition | The final outcome of intake processing: Accepted, Declined (with reason), or Pending. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a structured referral and intake process that ensures every referral is received, logged, screened, and dispositioned in a timely, accurate, and non-discriminatory manner.
4.2 All referrals shall be processed within defined timeframes to support timely access to care. Urgent referrals shall be triaged within 2 hours of receipt; routine referrals shall be processed within 24 hours of receipt.
4.3 No referral shall be declined on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or diagnosis except where the agency lacks the clinical competency, licensure, or staffing to safely provide the required services.
4.4 Every referral shall be logged in the agency's referral tracking system with a unique referral number, date and time of receipt, referral source, and patient identifying information at the time of initial contact.
4.5 Clinical eligibility screening shall be performed by a licensed clinician (RN or therapist) for all referrals prior to acceptance.
4.6 Payer verification and authorization (where required) shall be completed prior to or concurrent with the first billable visit.
4.7 Referral sources and patients/families shall be notified of the referral disposition (acceptance or declination) within defined timeframes with documentation of all notifications.
4.8 Declined referrals shall include documentation of the reason for declination and evidence that the referral source was offered alternative provider information where available.
4.9 The intake process shall capture all information necessary to support the Start of Care assessment, initial plan of care, and first visit scheduling.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Referral Receipt and Logging

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Intake Coordinator | Receive referral via any approved channel (fax, electronic referral, phone, secure portal, walk-in). Log immediately in the referral tracking system with: (a) unique referral number; (b) date and time of receipt; (c) referral source name, title, organization, and contact information; (d) patient name, date of birth, and contact information; (e) referring physician name and NPI; (f) primary diagnosis and reason for referral; (g) urgency level (Urgent / Routine). | At time of receipt. |
| 5.1.2 | Intake Coordinator | Assign urgency classification: URGENT — patient has immediate clinical need, same-day or next-day SOC required (e.g., post-surgical, wound vac, IV therapy, fall risk); ROUTINE — standard intake processing timeline applies. | Immediately upon logging. |
| 5.1.3 | Intake Coordinator | Acknowledge receipt to the referral source: URGENT referrals — verbal or written acknowledgment within 1 hour; ROUTINE referrals — written acknowledgment within 4 business hours. | Per urgency classification. |

### 5.2 Intake Screening — Administrative

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Intake Coordinator | Verify patient resides within the agency's defined service area per OP-IM-003. If outside the service area, proceed to Section 5.6 (Declination). | Within 2 hours (Urgent) / 8 hours (Routine). |
| 5.2.2 | Intake Coordinator | Verify insurance/payer information: (a) confirm active coverage; (b) verify home health benefit eligibility; (c) identify prior authorization requirements; (d) confirm Medicare beneficiary status if applicable; (e) document verification results in the referral record. | Within 4 hours (Urgent) / 24 hours (Routine). |
| 5.2.3 | Intake Coordinator | Collect and verify all required referral documentation: (a) physician face-to-face encounter documentation (if available); (b) hospital discharge summary (if applicable); (c) current medication list; (d) relevant medical history and diagnoses; (e) any existing orders or plan of care; (f) advance directive status; (g) emergency contact information. Document any missing items and initiate retrieval. | Within 24 hours of receipt. |
| 5.2.4 | Intake Coordinator | Verify that the patient does not have an active episode with another Medicare-certified home health agency. If dual certification is identified, coordinate with the other agency and document resolution. | Within 24 hours. |

### 5.3 Intake Screening — Clinical Eligibility

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Intake RN / Clinical Manager | Perform clinical eligibility screening based on referral information. Evaluate: (a) homebound status indicators; (b) skilled nursing or therapy need; (c) medical necessity for home health services; (d) physician willingness to certify/order services; (e) patient/caregiver willingness to participate; (f) safety of the home environment (based on available information). | Within 4 hours (Urgent) / 24 hours (Routine). |
| 5.3.2 | Intake RN / Clinical Manager | If clinical eligibility cannot be determined from referral documents alone, contact the referral source or physician office to obtain additional clinical information. Document all outreach attempts and outcomes. | Within 24 hours; minimum 2 attempts before escalation. |
| 5.3.3 | Intake RN / Clinical Manager | Document the clinical eligibility determination on the Intake Clinical Screening Form (Appendix A) with rationale. Sign and date the form. | Upon completion of screening. |
| 5.3.4 | Clinical Manager | Review and approve all clinical eligibility determinations for complex or borderline cases including: (a) patients with behavioral health diagnoses as primary condition; (b) patients with homebound status concerns; (c) patients requiring services the agency has limited experience delivering; (d) patients with active wound vac, TPN, or complex infusion needs. | Within 4 hours of escalation. |

### 5.4 Referral Acceptance and Admission Initiation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Intake Coordinator | Upon clinical eligibility confirmation and payer verification, update referral status to ACCEPTED. | Immediately upon approval. |
| 5.4.2 | Intake Coordinator | Notify the referral source of acceptance verbally and in writing. Provide: (a) estimated SOC date; (b) agency contact information; (c) after-hours contact number. | Within 2 hours of acceptance (Urgent) / within 24 hours (Routine). |
| 5.4.3 | Intake Coordinator | Notify the patient and/or family/caregiver of acceptance: (a) introduce the agency; (b) provide the estimated SOC visit date and time window; (c) advise of patient rights notification (to be delivered at SOC); (d) collect any additional information needed for the SOC visit. | Within 4 hours of acceptance (Urgent) / within 24 hours (Routine). |
| 5.4.4 | Intake Coordinator | Prepare and transmit the complete intake packet to the assigned SOC clinician: (a) referral documents; (b) clinical screening results; (c) payer/authorization information; (d) patient demographics and contact information; (e) advance directive status; (f) medication list; (g) any special instructions (interpreter needs, access instructions, safety concerns). | Prior to SOC visit; minimum 12 hours before scheduled visit. |
| 5.4.5 | Operations Director / Scheduling | Schedule the SOC visit per CMS requirements: (a) URGENT — within 24 hours of acceptance or as medically indicated; (b) ROUTINE — within 48 hours of physician order date. Coordinate with the assigned clinician and confirm with the patient. | Per urgency and CMS requirements. |

### 5.5 Referral Pending Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Intake Coordinator | If a referral cannot be accepted or declined within the standard timeframe due to missing information, pending physician orders, or payer verification delays, update status to PENDING with documented reason. | At the point the standard timeframe is exceeded. |
| 5.5.2 | Intake Coordinator | Follow up on all pending items daily. Document each follow-up attempt including date, time, method, and outcome. | Daily until resolved; minimum 1 documented attempt per business day. |
| 5.5.3 | Operations Director | Review all referrals in PENDING status exceeding 72 hours. Escalate to the Administrator if resolution is not achieved within 5 business days. | Every 72 hours; escalation at 5 business days. |
| 5.5.4 | Intake Coordinator | Notify the referral source of pending status and expected resolution timeline. | Within 24 hours of status change to PENDING; updates every 48 hours thereafter. |

### 5.6 Referral Declination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.6.1 | Intake RN / Clinical Manager | Document the specific reason for declining the referral on the Referral Declination Form (Appendix B). Acceptable reasons include: (a) patient outside service area; (b) agency lacks clinical competency or licensure for required services; (c) insufficient staffing to safely provide services; (d) patient does not meet home health eligibility criteria; (e) no valid physician order obtainable; (f) patient/family declines services. Non-acceptable reasons: diagnosis type, payer source (except non-contracted Medicaid managed care with documented non-participation), race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability, or socioeconomic status. | At the time of declination decision. |
| 5.6.2 | Intake Coordinator | Notify the referral source of the declination: (a) provide the specific reason; (b) offer alternative provider information where available; (c) document notification including date, time, method, person notified, and alternative information provided. | Within 24 hours of declination decision. |
| 5.6.3 | Intake Coordinator | Notify the patient and/or family of the declination and provide information about how to access services from other providers or contact the State Home Health Hotline. | Within 24 hours of declination decision. |
| 5.6.4 | Operations Director | Review all declination reports weekly. Analyze declination trends monthly for patterns indicating systemic issues (staffing shortages, service area gaps, training needs). Report findings to the Administrator monthly and to QAPI quarterly. | Weekly review; monthly analysis; quarterly QAPI reporting. |

### 5.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Urgent referral not processed within 2 hours | Intake Coordinator → Operations Director immediately | Operations Director assumes direct management; assigns clinical screener; documents delay and root cause. | Resolution within 4 hours. |
| Routine referral not processed within 24 hours | Intake Coordinator → Operations Director | Operations Director reviews cause, reassigns if needed, notifies referral source of delay. | Resolution within 48 hours. |
| Referral pending > 5 business days without resolution | Operations Director → Administrator | Administrator contacts referral source/physician directly; determination made to accept, decline, or extend with documented justification. | Resolution within 7 business days. |
| Pattern of declinations exceeding 10% of referrals received in any 30-day period | Operations Director → Administrator → QAPI Committee | Root cause analysis initiated; staffing, competency, or service area expansion evaluated; corrective action plan within 30 days. | Analysis within 14 days; corrective plan within 30 days. |
| Allegation of discriminatory referral practices | Any staff → Compliance Officer | Compliance investigation per CO-CP-007; report to Governing Body if substantiated. | Investigation within 7 days of report. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Referral log entry | Referral tracking system entry with all required data points per 5.1.1 | Intake Coordinator | EHR / Referral tracking system | At time of receipt |
| Clinical screening | Intake Clinical Screening Form (Appendix A) | Intake RN | Patient intake record; copy in referral file | Upon completion of screening |
| Payer verification | Insurance verification documentation | Intake Coordinator | Patient intake record | Prior to SOC visit |
| Acceptance notification | Written notification to referral source | Intake Coordinator | Referral file | Within defined timeframe per 5.4.2 |
| Patient notification | Documentation of patient/family notification | Intake Coordinator | Patient intake record | Within defined timeframe per 5.4.3 |
| Declination documentation | Referral Declination Form (Appendix B) | Intake RN / Clinical Manager | Referral file | At time of declination |
| Declination notification | Written notification to referral source with alternatives | Intake Coordinator | Referral file | Within 24 hours |
| Pending referral follow-up | Documented follow-up attempts | Intake Coordinator | Referral tracking system | Daily |
| Monthly declination analysis | Declination trend report | Operations Director | Operations file; QAPI records | Monthly |
| Intake packet to SOC clinician | Complete intake packet per 5.4.4 | Intake Coordinator | Patient record | Minimum 12 hours before SOC |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring
### 7.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All referrals logged at time of receipt with complete data | Monthly audit of referral log (10% random sample or minimum 20 referrals) | ≥ 95% compliance |
| Urgent referrals processed within 2 hours | Referral tracking system timestamps | ≥ 98% compliance |
| Routine referrals processed within 24 hours | Referral tracking system timestamps | ≥ 95% compliance |
| Clinical eligibility screening completed and documented for all referrals | Audit of Appendix A forms | 100% compliance |
| Declination reasons documented and compliant with non-discrimination requirements | Monthly review of Appendix B forms | 100% compliance |
| Referral source and patient notification completed within defined timeframes | Audit of notification documentation | ≥ 95% compliance |
| Pending referrals followed up daily | Referral tracking system documentation | 100% compliance |
| Declination rate monitored and reported to QAPI | Quarterly QAPI reports | Reporting compliance 100% |

### 7.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Referrals received but not logged immediately | Lost referrals; patient safety risk; CMS citation for access issues | Mandate real-time logging; daily reconciliation of all referral channels |
| Clinical screening not performed or not documented | Inappropriate admissions or missed eligibility issues; survey finding | Require Appendix A completion for every referral; weekly audit |
| Declination without documented reason | Appearance of discriminatory practices; complaint investigation | Require Appendix B for every declination; Operations Director weekly review |
| SOC visit not scheduled within required timeframe | Delayed care; patient harm; CMS citation | Daily scheduling review; escalation protocol for unscheduled SOCs |
| Intake packet incomplete or not transmitted to SOC clinician | Clinician unprepared; assessment quality compromised | Checklist verification before transmission; SOC clinician confirmation |

## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 All intake staff shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment to intake functions. Training shall cover: (a) referral logging requirements; (b) urgency classification; (c) clinical screening process; (d) payer verification procedures; (e) non-discrimination requirements; (f) declination documentation and notification requirements; (g) escalation protocols.
10.2 Annual refresher training shall be conducted for all intake staff and documented per HR-TD-001.
10.3 All staff completing this training shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days of training completion or policy revision.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Substantive revisions require: (a) Operations Director review and recommendation; (b) Administrator approval; (c) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days; (d) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections) may be approved by the Operations Director with notification to the Administrator.

# OP-IM-002 — Patient Acceptance & Admission Criteria
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-IM-002 |
| Title | Patient Acceptance & Admission Criteria |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | IM — Intake Management |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines the clinical, operational, and regulatory criteria that must be met for a patient to be accepted for admission to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. This policy ensures that every admission decision is based on objective, non-discriminatory criteria and that the agency only accepts patients for whom it can provide safe, effective, and compliant care per 42 CFR § 484.50 (Patient Rights), 42 CFR § 484.55 (Comprehensive Assessment), and 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration).
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to all intake staff, clinical screeners, the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing/Clinical Manager, the Administrator, and any individual involved in patient acceptance decisions.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Acceptance Criteria | The objective clinical, operational, and regulatory requirements that must be satisfied before a patient is admitted to home health services. |
| Medical Necessity | The requirement that services ordered are reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the patient's illness or injury, consistent with accepted standards of medical practice. |
| Homebound Status | A patient qualifies as homebound if leaving the home requires a considerable and taxing effort due to illness or injury, as defined by CMS and 42 CFR § 484.55. |
| Skilled Need | The requirement for services that can only be safely and effectively provided by or under the supervision of a licensed professional. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall accept patients for admission only when all of the following criteria are met: (a) the patient has a qualifying skilled need; (b) the patient is homebound or expected to meet homebound criteria; (c) a physician is available to certify and order home health services; (d) the services required are within the agency's scope, licensure, and competency; (e) the agency has adequate staffing to deliver services safely; (f) the patient's residence is within the agency's service area; (g) payer coverage has been verified or the patient has agreed to financial responsibility.
4.2 The agency shall not discriminate in patient acceptance decisions based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, diagnosis, or source of payment except where the agency is not a participating provider in the patient's insurance plan.
4.3 The agency shall not refuse admission based solely on the complexity of the patient's condition if the agency has the clinical competency and staffing to provide the required services safely.
4.4 All acceptance decisions shall be documented with the specific criteria evaluated and the rationale for the decision.
4.5 Patients who do not meet acceptance criteria at the time of referral but may qualify in the future (e.g., pending physician orders, pending insurance enrollment) shall be managed under the pending referral process per OP-IM-001.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Acceptance Criteria Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Intake RN | Evaluate the patient against each acceptance criterion using the Patient Acceptance Criteria Checklist (Appendix A). All criteria must be evaluated; no criterion may be omitted. | During clinical eligibility screening per OP-IM-001. |
| 5.1.2 | Intake RN | For each criterion, document one of three findings: MET, NOT MET (with explanation), or PENDING (with action plan). | At time of evaluation. |
| 5.1.3 | Intake RN | If all criteria are MET, recommend acceptance and proceed to admission per OP-IM-001 §5.4. | Immediately upon determination. |
| 5.1.4 | Clinical Manager | If any criterion is NOT MET or if the case involves clinical complexity, the Clinical Manager shall review the determination and make the final acceptance/declination decision. | Within 4 hours of referral. |
| 5.1.5 | Operations Director | If acceptance requires staffing redistribution or service area exception, obtain approval from the Operations Director prior to confirming acceptance. | Within 24 hours. |

### 5.2 Specific Criteria Evaluation Standards

| Criterion | Evaluation Standard | Documentation Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skilled need | At least one qualifying skilled service (SN, PT, OT, ST) must be identified from referral documentation. If MSW or HHA only, must have a qualifying skilled service ordered concurrently. | Specific skilled need documented on Appendix A. |
| Homebound status | Indicators of homebound status present in referral information (e.g., mobility limitations, cognitive impairment, assistive device use, medical restrictions). Full homebound determination completed at SOC assessment. | Homebound indicators documented; full determination deferred to SOC per CL-CA-005. |
| Physician certification | Referring or attending physician identified and willing to certify the home health plan of care. Physician must be a Medicare-enrolled provider (for Medicare patients). | Physician name, NPI, and contact documented. |
| Agency competency | The required services are within the agency's approved scope of services (GV-OG-003) and the agency has clinicians with appropriate training and credentials. | Verification against scope of services; competency confirmation. |
| Staffing adequacy | The agency has available clinical staff within the patient's geographic area to initiate and maintain the ordered visit frequency. | Scheduling confirmation or Operations Director approval. |
| Service area | Patient's residence is within the agency's defined service area per OP-IM-003. | Address verified against service area map. |
| Payer coverage | Insurance verification completed; coverage for home health confirmed; authorization obtained if required. Self-pay patients must acknowledge financial responsibility. | Payer verification documentation; authorization number if applicable. |
| Patient/caregiver consent | Patient (or legal representative) has been informed of services and has consented to receive home health care from the agency. | Verbal consent documented; written consent obtained at SOC. |

### 5.3 Non-Discrimination in Admissions

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | All Intake Staff | At no point during the acceptance evaluation process shall a patient be declined based on a prohibited factor (Section 4.2). If an intake staff member is uncertain whether a declination reason is compliant, the matter shall be escalated to the Clinical Manager before any declination communication. | At the point of any declination consideration. |
| 5.3.2 | Operations Director | Review all declinations monthly to verify compliance with non-discrimination requirements. Any declination that cannot be clearly linked to a permissible criterion shall be investigated per CO-CP-007. | Monthly review. |

### 5.4 Admission Initiation Upon Acceptance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Intake Coordinator | Upon acceptance, initiate the patient record in the EHR including all demographic, clinical, payer, and referral information collected during intake. | Within 4 hours of acceptance. |
| 5.4.2 | Intake Coordinator | Verify and upload all supporting documents (F2F documentation, discharge summary, medication list, orders, advance directive information). | Prior to SOC visit. |
| 5.4.3 | Operations Director / Scheduling | Schedule SOC visit within CMS-required timeframes: (a) within 48 hours of physician order date for routine admissions; (b) within 24 hours or as medically indicated for urgent admissions. | Per CMS requirements. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Acceptance criteria evaluation | Patient Acceptance Criteria Checklist (Appendix A) | Intake RN | Patient intake record | At time of evaluation |
| Declination with non-discrimination attestation | Referral Declination Form (OP-IM-001 Appendix B) | Intake RN / Clinical Manager | Referral file | At time of declination |
| Monthly declination review | Monthly declination compliance review log | Operations Director | Operations file | Monthly |
| Patient consent documentation | Verbal consent documented; written consent at SOC | Intake Coordinator / SOC Clinician | Patient record | At intake/SOC |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Acceptance Criteria Checklist completed for all admissions | Quarterly audit (10% sample) | 100% |
| No declination based on prohibited factors | Monthly declination review | 100% |
| SOC scheduled within CMS-required timeframes | Monthly scheduling audit | ≥ 95% |
| Clinical Manager review completed for complex/borderline cases | Case review audit | 100% |

## 8. Regulatory References

| 42 CFR § 484.55 | Comprehensive assessment requirements |

| Title VI, Civil Rights Act | Non-discrimination in federally funded programs |

## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 All intake and clinical screening staff shall receive training on acceptance criteria within 14 calendar days of hire or role assignment.
10.2 Training shall include: (a) each acceptance criterion and evaluation standard; (b) non-discrimination requirements and prohibited factors; (c) escalation procedures for complex cases; (d) documentation requirements.
10.3 All staff shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days.

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines the geographic boundaries within which Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. provides home health services and establishes standards for ensuring adequate coverage throughout the defined service area. CMS requires that a home health agency serve patients within a defined geographic area and that the agency be operationally capable of providing timely, consistent services throughout that area per 42 CFR § 484.105.
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to the Governing Body, Administrator, Operations Director, all intake staff, scheduling staff, and clinical staff.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Service Area | The geographic region, defined by counties, ZIP codes, or other boundaries, within which the agency provides home health services as identified in its Medicare enrollment and state licensure. |
| Primary Service Area | The core geographic zone where the agency maintains consistent staffing and can meet all visit frequency and timeliness requirements. |
| Extended Service Area | Geographic zones outside the primary area that the agency may serve on a case-by-case basis subject to staffing availability and Operational Director approval. |
| Service Area Exception | An approved deviation from the standard service area for a specific patient, documented and time-limited. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a clearly defined service area that is: (a) documented and approved by the Governing Body; (b) consistent with the agency's Medicare enrollment application (CMS-855A); (c) consistent with the agency's California state home health license; (d) supported by adequate staffing to serve the entire area.
4.2 The service area shall be reviewed annually by the Operations Director and approved by the Administrator. Any changes to the service area require Governing Body notification.
4.3 The agency shall not accept patients residing outside the defined service area unless a service area exception is approved by the Operations Director.
4.4 The agency shall monitor service delivery performance across the service area to identify gaps in coverage and address them through staffing adjustments, scheduling optimization, or service area modification.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Service Area Definition

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Operations Director | Maintain the current service area map and boundary list (Appendix A). The service area shall be defined by: (a) county boundaries; (b) ZIP code list; (c) maximum travel radius from agency office (if applicable). | Continuous; updated as changes occur. |
| 5.1.2 | Operations Director | Submit the service area definition to the Administrator for approval annually. Present to the Governing Body at the second quarterly meeting. | Annually. |
| 5.1.3 | Operations Director | Ensure the service area on file with CMS (Form CMS-855A) and the California HCAI matches the agency's operational service area. Notify the Administrator immediately of any discrepancy. | Verified annually; discrepancy reported immediately. |

### 5.2 Service Area Exception Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Intake Coordinator | When a referral is received for a patient outside the defined service area, document the request and escalate to the Operations Director. | Within 4 hours of identifying out-of-area status. |
| 5.2.2 | Operations Director | Evaluate the exception request considering: (a) distance from nearest agency clinician; (b) staffing availability; (c) ability to meet visit frequency requirements; (d) after-hours coverage feasibility; (e) patient acuity and safety. | Within 24 hours. |
| 5.2.3 | Operations Director | Approve or deny the exception using the Service Area Exception Request Form (Appendix B). If approved, specify the duration and any conditions. | Within 24 hours of evaluation. |
| 5.2.4 | Operations Director | Track all exceptions quarterly. If exceptions for a geographic zone exceed 5 per quarter, evaluate whether the service area should be formally expanded. | Quarterly tracking; expansion evaluation at threshold. |

### 5.3 Coverage Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Operations Director | Monitor SOC timeliness by ZIP code monthly. Identify any area where SOC timeliness falls below 95% within 48 hours of order date. | Monthly. |
| 5.3.2 | Operations Director | Monitor missed visit rates by geographic zone monthly. If any zone exceeds a 5% missed visit rate, initiate staffing analysis. | Monthly. |
| 5.3.3 | Operations Director | Report coverage performance to the Administrator monthly and to QAPI quarterly. | Monthly/Quarterly. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Service area map and ZIP code list | Service Area Definition (Appendix A) | Operations Director | Operations file; intake reference | Annual update |
| Service area exceptions | Service Area Exception Request Form (Appendix B) | Operations Director | Referral file | At time of request |
| Coverage performance reports | Monthly coverage report | Operations Director | Operations file; QAPI | Monthly |
| Governing Body notification | Meeting minutes documenting service area review | Administrator | Governance file | Annually |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Service area definition current and approved | Annual review of documentation | Current within 12 months |
| CMS-855A service area matches operational area | Annual comparison | 100% match |
| All out-of-area admissions have approved exceptions | Quarterly audit of exception forms | 100% |
| SOC timeliness by geographic zone | Monthly ZIP code analysis | ≥ 95% within 48 hours |

# OP-SL-001 — Scheduling & Visit Management
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-001 |
| Title | Scheduling & Visit Management |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for scheduling, managing, tracking, and documenting patient visits at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective scheduling is essential for ensuring physician-ordered visit frequencies are met, patient care is timely, LUPA risk is minimized, and CMS visit compliance is maintained per 42 CFR § 484.60 (Care Planning) and 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration__
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to all scheduling staff, the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing/Clinical Manager, all clinical staff assigned patient visits, and any contracted or per diem staff delivering visits.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Visit Frequency | The number, type, and schedule of visits ordered by the physician in the plan of care. |
| LUPA | Low Utilization Payment Adjustment — a reduced payment applied when the number of visits in a 30-day period falls below the CMS threshold.__ |
| Missed Visit | A scheduled visit that was not completed on the scheduled date due to any cause (clinician, patient, or operational). |
| Visit Compliance Rate | The percentage of physician-ordered visits that are actually delivered within the ordered timeframe. |
| SOC Window | The CMS-defined timeframe within which the Start of Care assessment must be completed (within 5 calendar days of the referral date or within 5 calendar days of the patient's return home). |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All patient visits shall be scheduled in accordance with the physician-ordered visit frequency and disciplines specified in the plan of care.
4.2 The agency shall maintain a centralized scheduling system that provides real-time visibility into all scheduled, completed, and missed visits.
4.3 SOC visits shall be scheduled within 48 hours of the physician order date (routine) or within 24 hours (urgent) to comply with CMS timely initiation requirements.
4.4 All visits shall be scheduled with patient notification at least 24 hours in advance (except for same-day urgent visits). The patient shall be informed of the expected visit date and approximate time window.
4.5 Visit compliance shall be monitored daily. Any variance from the ordered frequency shall be identified, documented, and corrected within 24 hours.
4.6 The scheduling process shall incorporate LUPA risk monitoring per FN-CM-005 and QA-PI-006.
4.7 Clinician assignments shall consider: (a) clinical competency matched to patient needs; (b) geographic proximity; (c) continuity of care (same clinician where feasible); (d) caseload balance.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Visit Scheduling

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Scheduling Coordinator | Upon patient acceptance, enter all ordered visits into the scheduling system based on the plan of care. Include: (a) visit type (SN, PT, OT, ST, MSW, HHA); (b) frequency (visits per week/period); (c) duration of episode; (d) any specific scheduling instructions. | Within 4 hours of POC receipt. |
| 5.1.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | Assign clinicians to visits based on: (a) clinical competency match; (b) geographic zone; (c) caseload capacity; (d) patient preference for continuity where feasible. | At time of scheduling. |
| 5.1.3 | Scheduling Coordinator | Notify the assigned clinician of the visit assignment including: (a) patient name and address; (b) visit type and purpose; (c) any special instructions (interpreter, access codes, safety concerns, infection precautions); (d) required assessment tools. | At time of scheduling; minimum 12 hours before visit. |
| 5.1.4 | Scheduling Coordinator | Notify the patient/caregiver of the scheduled visit: (a) date and approximate time window (2-hour window maximum); (b) name of the assigned clinician; (c) any preparation needed. | Minimum 24 hours before visit (except urgent).__ |
| 5.1.5 | Scheduling Coordinator | For recertification episodes, enter all visits from the new POC within 48 hours of physician recertification. Verify continuity of services during the transition__ | Within 48 hours of recertification. |

### 5.2 Daily Schedule Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Scheduling Coordinator | Generate and review the daily schedule each business day by 6:00 AM. Verify: (a) all scheduled visits have assigned clinicians; (b) no scheduling conflicts exist; (c) travel time between visits is reasonable. | Daily by 6:00 AM. |
| 5.2.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | By end of each business day, reconcile the daily schedule: (a) confirm all visits are marked as completed, rescheduled, or missed; (b) identify any documentation not yet submitted; (c) flag any missed visits for immediate follow-up. | Daily by end of business.__ |
| 5.2.__ | Operations Director | Review the daily schedule reconciliation report. Address any unresolved variances. Escalate patterns of missed visits or scheduling failures to the Clinical Manager and Administrator__ | Daily. |

### 5.3 Visit Frequency Compliance Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.__ | Scheduling Coordinator | Run a weekly visit compliance report comparing ordered frequency vs. actual visits delivered for each patient__ | Weekly (every Monday). |
| 5.3.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | Identify any patient with a visit compliance rate below 100%. For each variance, document: (a) reason for variance; (b) corrective scheduling action taken; (c) whether additional visits can be made up within the period__ | Weekly. |
| 5.3.3 | Operations Director | Review the weekly compliance report. Any patient with visit compliance below 90% for two consecutive weeks shall trigger: (a) clinician counseling; (b) scheduling adjustment; (c) notification to the Clinical Manager. | Weekly. |
| 5.3.4 | Operations Director | Provide a monthly visit frequency compliance report to the Clinical Manager and QAPI committee. Report must include: (a) overall compliance rate; (b) compliance by discipline; (c) most common reasons for non-compliance; (d) corrective actions taken. | Monthly; QAPI quarterly. |

### 5.4 LUPA Risk Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Scheduling Coordinator | At the start of each 30-day period, identify the LUPA threshold for each patient based on PDGM classification. Flag all episodes where the ordered visits are at or near the LUPA threshold. | At start of each 30-day period. |
| 5.4.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | Generate a weekly LUPA risk report identifying patients at risk of LUPA (visits delivered < threshold with ≤ 10 days remaining in the period). | Weekly. |
| 5.4.3 | Operations Director / Clinical Manager | Review the LUPA risk report and coordinate clinical and scheduling responses per FN-CM-005 and QA-PI-006. | Weekly. |

### 5.5 Missed Visit Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Assigned Clinician | If a scheduled visit cannot be completed (patient not home, patient refusal, clinician illness, travel hazard, or other cause), notify the scheduling coordinator immediately and document the reason. | Within 1 hour of the missed visit. |
| 5.5.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | Reschedule the missed visit within 24 hours. If the patient refused the visit, document the refusal and notify the Clinical Manager. | Within 24 hours. |
| 5.5.3 | Scheduling Coordinator | Log the missed visit in the Missed Visit Log (Appendix A) including: (a) patient; (b) date; (c) reason; (d) reschedule date; (e) notification to patient. | At time of missed visit. |
| 5.5.4 | Clinical Manager | If a patient refuses 2 or more consecutive visits, conduct a clinical review to evaluate: (a) patient understanding of service necessity; (b) potential discharge consideration; (c) documentation per CL-SD-024__ | Within 48 hours of second refusal. |
| 5.5.5 | Operations Director | Review the missed visit log weekly. If any clinician has a missed visit rate exceeding 5% of assigned visits in a month, initiate a performance discussion__ | Weekly review; monthly threshold evaluation. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visit scheduling entries | Scheduling system records | Scheduling Coordinator | EHR/Scheduling system | At time of scheduling |
| Daily schedule reconciliation | Daily reconciliation report | Scheduling Coordinator | Operations file | Daily |
| Weekly visit compliance report | Compliance report | Scheduling Coordinator | Operations file | Weekly |
| Weekly LUPA risk report | LUPA risk report | Scheduling Coordinator | Operations/Finance file | Weekly |
| Missed visit documentation | Missed Visit Log (Appendix A) | Scheduling Coordinator | Operations file | At time of occurrence__ |
| Monthly compliance report to QAPI | Monthly scheduling performance report | Operations Director | QAPI records | Monthly |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overall visit frequency compliance rate | Weekly compliance report | ≥ 95% |
| SOC visit within 48 hours of order date | Monthly audit | ≥ 95%__ |
| Missed visits rescheduled within 24 hours | Weekly audit of missed visit log | ≥ 98% |
| LUPA rate (agency-wide__ | Monthly financial analysis | ≤ 10% of episodes__ |
| Daily schedule reconciliation completed | Daily verification | 100% |
| Patient notification minimum 24 hours before visit | Quarterly audit | ≥ 95% |

# OP-SL-002 — After-Hours & On-Call Services
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-002 |
| Title | After-Hours & On-Call Services |
| Domain | OP — Operations__ |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes the agency's requirement to provide 24-hour, 7-day-a-week availability of services as required by 42 CFR § 484.50(a) and 42 CFR § 484.105. Patients have the right to receive care and services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The agency must ensure after-hours clinical response capability for all patients on active service.
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing/Clinical Manager, all clinical staff participating in on-call rotations, the scheduling coordinator, and the Administrator.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| After-Hours | Any time outside the agency's standard business hours, including weekends and holidays. |
| On-Call | A designated period during which a qualified clinician is available by telephone and, when necessary, available to make home visits within defined response timeframes. |
| On-Call Clinician | A licensed registered nurse or therapist designated to provide after-hours triage, telephonic guidance, and emergency home visits. |
| Clinical Triage | The process of evaluating a patient's symptoms and needs via telephone to determine appropriate response (telephonic guidance, scheduled visit, urgent visit, or emergency referral). |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall provide 24-hour, 7-day-a-week availability of clinical services to all patients on active service, including weekends and holidays, per 42 CFR § 484.50(a).
4.2 After-hours availability shall include: (a) a live-answer or prompt call-back telephone response (call-back within 30 minutes maximum); (b) telephonic clinical triage by a licensed clinician; (c) the ability to dispatch a clinician for an in-person visit when clinically indicated.
4.3 All patients and caregivers shall be informed of the agency's after-hours contact number at the time of admission and at each subsequent visit. The after-hours number shall be prominently documented in the patient's home health folder.
4.4 On-call clinicians shall have access to patient clinical records sufficient to provide safe, informed clinical guidance and care.
4.5 All after-hours contacts, triage decisions, and interventions shall be documented in the patient's clinical record.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 On-Call Schedule and Staffing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.__ | Operations Director | Establish and maintain the on-call rotation schedule. The schedule must ensure: (a) a licensed RN is available on call at all times; (b) therapy on-call is available based on active caseload needs; (c) no clinician is assigned more than 7 consecutive on-call days without relief__ | Monthly schedule published by the 20th of the prior month. |
| 5.1.2 | Operations Director | Distribute the on-call schedule to: (a) all clinical staff; (b) the answering service or call routing system; (c) the Administrator__ | Upon publication and with any changes. |
| 5.1.3 | On-Call Clinician | Verify access to: (a) the on-call phone/device; (b) the EHR for patient records; (c) the emergency supply kit; (d) agency emergency contact list before each on-call shift begins__ | At start of each on-call shift. |

### 5.2 After-Hours Call Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Answering Service / On-Call System | Receive after-hours calls and connect the caller to the on-call clinician. If the on-call clinician does not answer, leave an urgent message and continue attempting contact__ | Initial contact within 15 minutes; callback within 30 minutes maximum. |
| 5.2.2 | On-Call Clinician | Perform clinical triage using the After-Hours Clinical Triage Protocol (Appendix A). Determine the appropriate response level: LEVEL 1 — Telephonic guidance (education, reassurance, comfort measures); LEVEL 2 — Next-business-day visit scheduling (non-urgent but requires clinical follow-up); LEVEL 3 — Urgent on-call visit (within 2 hours); LEVEL 4 — Emergency referral (instruct to call 911 immediately, remain on line until EMS dispatched). | Triage initiated within 30 minutes of call receipt. |
| 5.2.3 | On-Call Clinician | For Level 3 responses, make an in-person home visit. Conduct assessment, provide treatment within scope, and coordinate with the attending physician as needed. | Visit within 2 hours of triage decision. |
| 5.2.4 | On-Call Clinician | For all after-hours contacts, document in the After-Hours Contact Log (Appendix B) and in the patient's clinical record: (a) date and time of call; (b) caller identity; (c) nature of concern; (d) triage assessment and level assigned; (e) interventions provided; (f) physician notification if applicable; (g) follow-up plan__ | Documentation completed within 2 hours of contact resolution. |
| 5.2.5 | On-Call Clinician | Notify the patient's assigned clinician and the Clinical Manager of all Level 2, 3, and 4 contacts by the start of the next business day. | By 8:00 AM next business day. |

### 5.3 Physician Notification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | On-Call Clinician | Notify the attending physician for: (a) any significant change in patient condition; (b) any emergency referral (Level 4); (c) any intervention requiring a physician order; (d) any new verbal order obtained after hours. | During the after-hours contact or within 1 hour of clinical decision. |
| 5.3.2 | On-Call Clinician | Document physician notification including: (a) physician contacted; (b) date/time; (c) information communicated; (d) orders received (if any); (e) read-back confirmation for verbal orders per CL-CP-004__ | At time of contact. |

### 5.4 After-Hours Visit Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | On-Call Clinician | Complete a full clinical visit note in the EHR for all in-person after-hours visits. The note must meet the same documentation standards as a regular visit per CL-CD-001. | Within 24 hours of the visit. |
| 5.4.2 | On-Call Clinician | If the after-hours visit results in a new order, change in plan of care, or referral, communicate this to the patient's assigned care team by the start of the next business day. | By 8:00 AM next business day. |

### 5.5 Monitoring and Quality Assurance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Clinical Manager | Review the After-Hours Contact Log (Appendix B) weekly. Evaluate: (a) response timeliness; (b) appropriateness of triage level; (c) documentation completeness; (d) physician notification compliance__ | Weekly. |
| 5.5.2 | Operations Director | Report after-hours utilization to QAPI quarterly including: (a) volume of calls by triage level; (b) response time metrics; (c) trends in after-hours needs; (d) any adverse events related to after-hours care. | Quarterly. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| On-call schedule | Monthly on-call rotation | Operations Director | Operations file | Monthly |
| After-hours contact documentation | After-Hours Contact Log (Appendix B) + clinical record entry | On-Call Clinician | Operations file; patient record | Within 2 hours of resolution |
| After-hours visit note | Full clinical visit note in EHR | On-Call Clinician | Patient record | Within 24 hours |
| Weekly after-hours review | Clinical Manager review documentation | Clinical Manager | Operations file | Weekly |
| Quarterly after-hours report | QAPI report | Operations Director | QAPI records | Quarterly |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Callback within 30 minutes of after-hours call | After-hours log timestamp review | ≥ 98% |

## Appendix A — After-Hours Clinical Triage Protocol
CARE INDEED HOME HEALTH CARE, INC. After-Hours Clinical Triage Protocol Policy Reference: OP-SL-002 | Version: 6.0
Instructions: Use this protocol to guide triage decisions for all after-hours patient contacts. Document the triage level and rationale in the After-Hours Contact Log (Appendix B) and patient record.
### Triage Decision Matrix

| Triage Level | Description | Response | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LEVEL 1 — Telephonic Guidance | Non-urgent concern that can be addressed with education, reassurance, or self-care instructions | Provide telephonic guidance; no visit needed; follow up next scheduled visit | Medication questions, mild symptom management, emotional support, general information |
| LEVEL 2 — Next-Business-Day Visit | Non-emergency clinical concern requiring in-person assessment but not posing immediate danger | Schedule next-business-day visit; notify assigned clinician; advise patient of monitoring plan | New but stable symptoms, mild wound changes, non-acute pain increase, equipment concerns, dressing change needed__ |
| LEVEL 3 — Urgent On-Call Visit | Acute clinical concern requiring timely in-person assessment and intervention | On-call clinician visits within 2 hours; notify attending physician; document fully | Acute symptom change, moderate-severe pain, wound complication, fall with possible injury, medication error, catheter malfunction |
| LEVEL 4 — Emergency Referral (911__ | Life-threatening or potentially life-threatening condition | Instruct caller to call 911; remain on line until EMS dispatched; notify attending physician; document fully | Chest pain, stroke symptoms, severe respiratory distress, uncontrolled hemorrhage, loss of consciousness, severe allergic reaction |

### Triage Assessment Questions (Minimum Required)
What is the patient's current symptom or concern?
When did the symptom begin?
How severe is it on a 0-10 scale?
Has anything been done to address it?
What is the patient's current mental status and level of consciousness?
Does the patient have any known allergies relevant to the concern?
What are the patient's current vital signs (if available)?
Is there a caregiver present?

# OP-SL-003 — Vehicle & Transportation Safety
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-003 |
| Title | Vehicle & Transportation Safety |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL__ |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for safe vehicle operation, mileage documentation, insurance verification, and accident reporting for all Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. staff who use personal or agency vehicles to travel to patient homes in the course of providing home health services.
## 2. Scope
All staff who use a vehicle (personal or agency-provided) for agency business including patient visits, travel to meetings, supply pick-up, or any other agency-related purpose.
## 3. Policy Statements
3.1 All staff using a vehicle for agency business shall maintain: (a) a valid, unrestricted California driver's license; (b) current vehicle registration; (c) automobile liability insurance meeting minimum requirements established by the agency (minimum $100,000/$300,000 bodily injury, $50,000 property damage or equivalent combined single limit).
3.2 Staff shall operate vehicles safely and in compliance with all traffic laws. Use of handheld devices while driving is strictly prohibited.
3.3 All vehicle accidents occurring during agency business shall be reported to the Operations Director within 2 hours regardless of severity.
3.4 Insurance and driver's license verification shall be completed at hire and annually thereafter.
3.5 Staff shall document mileage for all agency-related travel per the agency's mileage reimbursement policy.
## 4. Procedures
### 4.1 Pre-Employment and Annual Verification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | HR Director / Operations Director | Verify at hire: (a) valid California driver's license; (b) vehicle registration; (c) insurance declaration page meeting agency minimums. | Prior to first day of employment. |
| 4.1.2 | HR Director | Re-verify all documents annually. Staff must submit updated documents within 14 calendar days of request. Failure to provide documentation results in suspension from field assignments. | Annually; 14-day compliance window. |
| 4.1.3 | Operations Director | Maintain a Vehicle/Driver Verification Log (Appendix A) documenting all verifications. | Continuous. |

### 4.2 Safe Driving Standards

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.2.1 | All Field Staff | Comply with all traffic laws. Prohibited behaviors include: (a) handheld device use while driving; (b) driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs; (c) driving while fatigued; (d) transporting patients in personal vehicles (except with explicit prior authorization). | At all times during agency business. |
| 4.2.2 | All Field Staff | Conduct a brief vehicle safety check before each shift: (a) tires, lights, mirrors; (b) fuel level; (c) emergency kit accessible. | Before each shift. |
| 4.2.3 | All Field Staff | Plan travel routes to minimize driving time and risk. Check weather and road conditions before departing for visits, particularly during inclement weather per OP-SL-007. | Before each trip. |

### 4.3 Vehicle Accident Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.3.__ | Involved Staff Member | In the event of any vehicle accident during agency business: (a) ensure personal safety; (b) call 911 if injuries or significant damage; (c) exchange information with other parties; (d) take photographs of the scene; (e) do not admit fault. | At time of accident. |
| 4.3.2 | Involved Staff Member | Notify the Operations Director immediately and complete the Vehicle Accident Report Form (Appendix B) within 24 hours. | Verbal notification within 2 hours; written report within 24 hours. |
| 4.3.3 | Operations Director | Investigate the accident. Determine: (a) cause; (b) any policy violations; (c) corrective action needed; (d) whether the incident is reportable to the agency's insurance carrier. Notify the Risk Manager per RM-ER-002. | Investigation within 72 hours. |
| 4.3.4 | Operations Director | Report all accidents to the Administrator and Risk Manager. If the accident results in personal injury, workers' compensation reporting per HR-WM-004 applies concurrently. | Within 24 hours of incident. |

### 4.4 Mileage Documentation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.4.1 | All Field Staff | Record daily mileage for all agency-related travel using the Mileage Log (Appendix C) or agency-approved electronic mileage tracking tool. Log must include: (a) date; (b) starting and ending locations; (c) purpose; (d) miles driven. | Daily. |
| 4.4.__ | Operations Director / Finance | Review and approve mileage submissions monthly. Audit for reasonableness and compliance. | Monthly. |

## 5. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Driver/vehicle verification | Vehicle/Driver Verification Log (Appendix A) | Operations Director | HR/Operations file | At hire; annually |
| Accident reports | Vehicle Accident Report Form (Appendix B) | Involved Staff | Operations/Risk file | Within 24 hours |
| Mileage records | Mileage Log (Appendix C) or electronic log | All Field Staff | Finance/Operations | Daily/Monthly |

## 6. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Driver's license, registration, and insurance current for all field staff | Annual verification audit | 100% |
| All accidents reported within 2 hours (verbal) | Incident report timestamps | 100% |
| Mileage logs complete and submitted monthly | Monthly finance review | 100% |

# OP-SL-004 — Equipment & Supply Management
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-004 |
| Title | Equipment & Supply Management |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines procedures for the procurement, inventory management, distribution, maintenance, calibration, and replacement of medical equipment and clinical supplies used in the delivery of home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
## 2. Scope
All clinical staff, the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing, office staff involved in supply management, and contracted vendors providing equipment or supplies.
## 3. Policy Statements
3.1 The agency shall maintain an adequate inventory of medical supplies and equipment necessary to support the delivery of all services within its defined scope of services.
3.2 All medical equipment used in patient care shall be properly maintained, calibrated (where applicable), and in safe working order.
3.3 Equipment and supply procurement shall follow established vendor management standards per OP-FM-003 and cost management guidelines per FN-FP-006.
3.4 Staff shall be trained on the proper use, care, and safety precautions for all equipment they are expected to use.
3.5 Any defective, expired, or recalled equipment or supplies shall be removed from service immediately and reported per RM-PS-003.
## 4. Procedures
### 4.1 Procurement

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | Operations Director | Maintain an approved vendor list for medical supplies and equipment. Vendors must meet agency qualification standards per OP-FM-003. | Continuous; reviewed annually. |
| 4.1.2 | Operations Director / Designee | Process supply orders based on inventory levels, par levels, and clinical demand. Maintain par levels for high-use items (blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, wound care supplies, PPE, phlebotomy supplies). | Weekly ordering; urgent orders within 24 hours. |
| 4.1.3 | Operations Director | Review all equipment purchases exceeding $500 with the Administrator before procurement. | Prior to purchase. |

### 4.2 Inventory Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.2.1 | Designated Supply Coordinator | Conduct physical inventory count monthly. Reconcile against purchase records and distribution logs. | Monthly. |
| 4.2.2 | Designated Supply Coordinator | Check all supplies for expiration dates monthly. Remove and dispose of expired supplies per biohazardous waste procedures (RM-PS-002 if applicable). | Monthly. |
| 4.2.3 | Designated Supply Coordinator | Maintain the Equipment Inventory Log (Appendix A) for all durable medical equipment owned by the agency including: (a) item description; (b) serial number; (c) purchase date; (d) warranty status; (e) maintenance/calibration schedule; (f) assigned location. | Continuous. |

### 4.3 Equipment Maintenance and Calibration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.3.1 | Operations Director | Establish maintenance and calibration schedules for all equipment requiring periodic servicing (e.g., scales, blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters). Follow manufacturer recommendations. | At time of purchase; annual review. |
| 4.3.2 | Designated Staff | Perform or arrange maintenance/calibration per schedule. Document on the Equipment Maintenance Log (Appendix B). | Per manufacturer schedule. |
| 4.3.3 | All Clinical Staff | Report any malfunctioning, damaged, or suspected defective equipment immediately to the Operations Director. Do not use defective equipment. Tag as "OUT OF SERVICE" and remove from clinical use. | Immediately upon identification. |

### 4.4 Supply Distribution to Clinicians

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.4.1 | Designated Supply Coordinator | Prepare and distribute clinical supply kits/bags for field clinicians. Kits must include: (a) standard wound care supplies; (b) PPE (gloves, masks, gowns); (c) phlebotomy supplies; (d) vital sign equipment; (e) hand sanitizer; (f) sharps container. | At hire; replenished weekly or as requested. |
| 4.4.2 | All Clinical Staff | Inspect supply bags before each shift. Report any missing, expired, or inadequate supplies. | Before each shift. |

### 4.5 Product Recall Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.5.1 | Operations Director | Monitor FDA MedWatch and manufacturer recall notices. Upon notification of a recall affecting agency equipment or supplies: (a) immediately identify all affected items; (b) remove from use; (c) notify all staff who may have used the item; (d) follow manufacturer return/disposal instructions; (e) document per RM-PS-003. | Within 24 hours of recall notification. |

## 5. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Physical inventory reconciliation completed monthly | Inventory count records | 100% |
| Equipment maintenance/calibration current | Equipment Maintenance Log audit | 100% |
| No expired supplies in inventory | Monthly expiration check | 100% |
| Recall response within 24 hours | Recall response documentation | 100% |

# OP-SL-005 — Communication & Documentation Systems
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-005 |
| Title | Communication & Documentation Systems |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines requirements for communication and documentation systems that support the clinical and operational functions of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective communication systems are essential for care coordination, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency.
## 2. Scope
All agency staff, the Operations Director, the IT Director/CISO, and the Administrator.
## 3. Policy Statements
3.1 The agency shall maintain reliable communication systems that enable: (a) real-time communication between office staff and field clinicians; (b) secure transmission of PHI in compliance with HIPAA; (c) after-hours contact per OP-SL-002; (d) emergency communication per OP-FM-005 and RM-EP-003.
3.2 The agency shall maintain an Electronic Health Record (EHR) system that meets all CMS, HIPAA, and state requirements per IT-SA-001.
3.3 All communication systems used for PHI must be encrypted and HIPAA-compliant per CO-HP-002 and IT-SC-003.
3.4 Staff shall not use personal, non-approved communication channels (personal email, personal text messaging, social media) to communicate PHI.
3.5 The agency shall maintain a backup communication plan in the event of primary system failure.
## 4. Procedures
### 4.1 Communication Systems Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | Operations Director / IT Director | Maintain the following communication systems: (a) agency landline telephone system; (b) secure mobile communication (HIPAA-compliant messaging/calling); (c) secure email (encrypted); (d) after-hours answering service or automated routing system; (e) fax (encrypted/HIPAA-compliant); (f) electronic referral portal (if applicable). | Continuous. |
| 4.1.2 | IT Director | Ensure all communication systems meet HIPAA encryption and security requirements per CO-HP-002 and IT-SC-003. Conduct annual security assessment. | Annual assessment; continuous monitoring. |
| 4.1.3 | Operations Director | Establish and maintain a Communication System Directory (Appendix A) listing all agency communication systems, contact numbers, access procedures, and backup contacts. Distribute to all staff. | Maintained continuously; redistributed at any change. |

### 4.2 EHR System Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.2.1 | IT Director / Operations Director | Maintain the EHR system per IT-SA-001 including: (a) OASIS data entry and transmission capability; (b) plan of care documentation; (c) visit note documentation; (d) physician order management; (e) scheduling integration; (f) audit trail per CO-DC-001. | Continuous. |
| 4.2.2 | IT Director | Ensure all clinicians have mobile EHR access for point-of-care documentation, with secure login and device management per IT-UP-001. | Continuous. |
| 4.2.3 | Operations Director | Monitor EHR system uptime. If system downtime exceeds 2 hours during business hours, activate the downtime procedure (paper documentation backup per Appendix B). | Activated when downtime > 2 hours. |

### 4.3 Backup Communication Plan

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.3.1 | Operations Director / IT Director | Maintain a communication backup plan including: (a) backup phone numbers for all key staff; (b) alternative messaging platform; (c) paper documentation forms for EHR downtime; (d) manual scheduling board procedure. | Documented and tested annually. |
| 4.3.2 | IT Director | Test backup communication systems annually. Document test results and any gaps requiring remediation. | Annually. |

## 5. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Communication systems HIPAA-compliant | Annual security assessment | 100% |
| EHR system uptime | Monthly uptime tracking | ≥ 99.5% |
| Communication directory current | Semi-annual review | Current within 30 days |
| Backup plan tested annually | Test documentation | Annual test completed |

## Appendix B — EHR Downtime Procedures
CARE INDEED HOME HEALTH CARE, INC. EHR Downtime Procedures Policy Reference: OP-SL-005 | Version: 6.0
When EHR system is unavailable for more than 2 hours during business hours:
Notification: IT Director notifies Operations Director and all clinical staff of downtime and estimated recovery time.
Paper Documentation: Clinicians shall use the agency's standardized paper visit documentation forms (maintained in each clinician's supply bag and in the office).
Scheduling: Scheduling Coordinator maintains a manual scheduling board or spreadsheet for the duration of downtime.
Physician Orders: All verbal and new orders received during downtime shall be documented on paper order forms and entered into the EHR within 4 hours of system restoration.
OASIS: OASIS documentation delayed during downtime must be completed and transmitted within CMS-required timeframes from the assessment date (not the system restoration date).
Data Entry: All paper documentation must be entered into the EHR within 24 hours of system restoration.
Verification: Operations Director verifies all paper documentation has been entered within 48 hours of restoration.
