# QA-SM-004 — Home Health Compare & Star Rating Monitoring
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | QA-SM-004 |
| Title | Home Health Compare & Star Rating Monitoring |
| Domain | QA — Quality Assurance & Performance Improvement |
| Subdomain | SM — Surveillance & Monitoring |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | QAPI Coordinator |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy establishes systematic monitoring, analysis, and response procedures for the agency's Home Health Compare publicly reported quality measures and Star Ratings at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Home Health Compare data represents the agency's public quality profile — the information that patients, caregivers, referral sources, payers, and surveyors use to evaluate and compare the agency. Declining Star Ratings and below-average publicly reported quality measures have direct impacts on referral volume, competitive positioning, Governing Body accountability, and regulatory scrutiny. This policy ensures that the agency continuously monitors its public quality profile, understands the drivers of its ratings, and implements targeted improvement initiatives when ratings decline or fall below acceptable levels. This policy satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program data use including publicly reported measures) and supports the benchmarking requirements of QA-PI-003.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The QAPI Coordinator
The Administrator
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
All QAPI Committee members
The CFO / Revenue Cycle Director
The Governing Body
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall actively and continuously monitor all publicly reported Home Health Compare quality measures and Star Ratings, with formal analysis conducted at each quarterly release of updated data.
4.2 Home Health Compare data shall be a standing component of the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002, the quarterly QAPI Performance Report per QA-PG-001, and the quarterly Governing Body report per GV-GB-001.
4.3 The agency shall maintain a Star Rating target of 4 stars or higher on both the Quality of Patient Care Star Rating and the Patient Survey Star Rating, and shall develop a documented improvement plan any time either rating falls below 4 stars.
4.4 For every publicly reported quality measure on which the agency performs below the national average for 2 consecutive reporting periods, the QAPI Committee shall direct a documented corrective action plan per QA-AE-003.
4.5 The Administrator and QAPI Coordinator shall verify the accuracy of the agency's Home Health Compare data within each quarterly release window and initiate the CMS data correction process if inaccuracies are identified.
4.6 Home Health Compare performance shall be reported publicly within the agency's marketing and referral source materials only as accurately as permitted by CMS guidelines, and shall not be misrepresented.
4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Home Health Compare | The CMS public reporting website (now part of Care Compare at Medicare.gov) that displays quality measures, patient survey results, and Star Ratings for Medicare-certified home health agencies. |
| Quality of Patient Care Star Rating | A CMS-calculated composite Star Rating (1–5 stars) based on OASIS-derived outcome and process quality measures submitted to CMS. |
| Patient Survey Star Rating | A CMS-calculated composite Star Rating (1–5 stars) based on HHCAHPS results. |
| Home Health Quality Reporting Program (HH QRP) | The CMS program requiring home health agencies to submit quality measure data; non-participation results in a 2% payment penalty. |
| OASIS-Based Quality Measures | Quality measures derived from OASIS data submitted by the agency, reflecting patient outcomes and process compliance (e.g., improvement in ambulation, timely initiation of care). |
| Process Measures | Quality measures reflecting whether specific care processes were followed (e.g., influenza vaccination screening, depression screening). |
| Outcome Measures | Quality measures reflecting patient health status changes over the course of the episode (e.g., improvement in bathing, reduction in hospitalizations). |
| Star Rating Target | The agency's defined minimum acceptable Star Rating per Section 4.3 of this policy (4 stars or higher). |
| CMS Data Correction Window | The defined period following each data release during which agencies may submit corrections to reported data through the CMS iQIES system. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 Monitoring Infrastructure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Establish and maintain access to the following data systems used for Home Health Compare monitoring: (a) CMS Care Compare website (public-facing); (b) CMS iQIES (internal quality improvement reports, agency-specific data previews, data correction submissions); (c) CASPER (Certification and Survey Provider Enhanced Reports); (d) HHCAHPS vendor reports (per QA-SM-003). Document all access credentials and system URLs in the QAPI Data Source Inventory per QA-PG-001 Section 6.4.4. | At program establishment; reviewed annually. |
| 6.1.2 | QAPI Coordinator | Monitor the CMS Home Health Quality Reporting Program (HH QRP) participation and submission requirements calendar. Ensure the agency submits all required OASIS data and public reporting data within required timeframes to avoid the 2% payment penalty. | Ongoing per CMS HH QRP calendar. |
| 6.1.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Subscribe to CMS mailing lists, CASPER notifications, and the agency's HHCAHPS vendor alerts to receive notification of each new data release and preview window. | At program establishment; maintain subscriptions continuously. |

### 6.2 Quarterly Data Review and Analysis

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Upon each quarterly CMS data release, download the agency's current publicly reported quality measure data from iQIES and Home Health Compare. Prepare the Home Health Compare Quarterly Analysis Report (Appendix A) within 10 business days of data release. The report must include: (a) all reported quality measures with agency score, national average, and state average; (b) Quality of Patient Care Star Rating — current and trend; (c) Patient Survey Star Rating — current and trend; (d) measures below national average; (e) measures below state average; (f) measures trending in the wrong direction (declining over 3+ periods, even if still above average); (g) comparison to agency Star Rating target (4 stars); (h) prior 4 quarters of data for trend analysis; (i) recommended actions. | Within 10 business days of each quarterly CMS data release. |
| 6.2.2 | QAPI Coordinator | Verify the accuracy of the agency's reported data during the CMS data preview window (prior to public release). If inaccurate data is identified, submit a correction request through iQIES within the correction window. Document all data verification activities and any corrections submitted. | During each CMS data preview window (per CMS calendar). |
| 6.2.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Present the Home Health Compare Quarterly Analysis Report to the QAPI Committee at the next monthly meeting following data release. | At next QAPI Committee meeting following report completion. |

### 6.3 QAPI Committee Review and Action

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | QAPI Committee | Review the Quarterly Analysis Report and take the following actions: (a) For measures at or above national average — acknowledge; identify and document sustaining practices; (b) For measures below national average but in improving trend — acknowledge improvement; continue monitoring; (c) For measures below national average with flat or declining trend — assign contributing factor analysis; determine if existing PIP or CAP addresses the issue; (d) For measures below national average for 2 consecutive periods — mandate new or enhanced CAP per QA-AE-003; (e) For either Star Rating below target (4 stars) — escalate to Governing Body and initiate comprehensive improvement plan per Section 6.4. Document all decisions and assigned actions in committee minutes. | At QAPI Committee meeting where report is presented. |
| 6.3.2 | QAPI Coordinator | Maintain a Home Health Compare Action Tracker (Appendix B) documenting all measures below threshold, associated corrective actions, assigned leads, deadlines, and current status. Present the tracker at each QAPI Committee meeting. | Updated quarterly following each data release; presented monthly. |

### 6.4 Comprehensive Star Rating Improvement Plan

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | QAPI Coordinator | When either Star Rating falls below 4 stars, prepare a Star Rating Improvement Plan (Appendix C) within 30 calendar days. The plan must: (a) identify each contributing quality measure that is below national average or declining; (b) analyze the root cause of underperformance for each measure (OASIS accuracy issue, care delivery issue, documentation issue, or systemic care quality issue); (c) assign specific, measurable improvement interventions for each measure; (d) define measurable targets (e.g., "improve improvement in ambulation rate from 64% to 72% within 2 quarters"); (e) identify responsible leads for each intervention; (f) establish a monitoring schedule; (g) define the timeline for achieving target Star Rating. | Within 30 calendar days of Star Rating falling below 4 stars. |
| 6.4.2 | Governing Body | Review and approve the Star Rating Improvement Plan at the next Governing Body meeting or at a special meeting if the rating has fallen to 3 stars or below. | At next Governing Body meeting; special meeting if ≤ 3 stars. |
| 6.4.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Report Star Rating Improvement Plan progress to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting until the target rating is achieved and sustained for 2 consecutive quarters. | Quarterly until resolution. |

### 6.5 Governing Body Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Include Home Health Compare summary in the quarterly QAPI Performance Report to the Governing Body per QA-PG-001 Section 6.3.1. Report must include: (a) current Quality of Patient Care Star Rating and trend; (b) current Patient Survey Star Rating and trend; (c) top 3 and bottom 3 publicly reported measures by relative agency performance; (d) measures with active corrective action plans and their status; (e) any data corrections submitted; (f) comparison to agency Star Rating target; (g) recommendations for Governing Body action. | Quarterly per GV-GB-001 schedule. |
| 6.5.2 | Governing Body | Review Home Health Compare data and direct corrective action. If either Star Rating falls to 3 stars or below and does not improve within 2 consecutive quarters with documented corrective action, the Governing Body shall convene a special session to evaluate whether additional resources, leadership action, or structural changes are required. | At each quarterly meeting. |

### 6.6 Benchmarking Integration

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Integrate Home Health Compare quarterly analysis into the agency's clinical outcome benchmarking process per QA-PI-003. Ensure that all publicly reported measures are included in the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002 with thresholds set at or above national averages. | At each quarterly release; integrated in annual QAPI plan development. |
| 6.6.2 | QAPI Coordinator | Annually, during QAPI plan development (per QA-PG-002), use the most recent Home Health Compare data to identify quality priority areas for the upcoming plan year and to set QAPI plan goals aligned with publicly reported measure improvement. | During annual planning cycle (October–December). |

### 6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Either Star Rating falls to 3 stars or below. | QAPI Coordinator notifies Administrator and Governing Body immediately. | Star Rating Improvement Plan per Section 6.4.1 within 30 days; Governing Body oversight until 4 stars restored. | Plan within 30 days; monthly Governing Body updates. |
| Agency falls below national average on 5 or more publicly reported measures simultaneously. | QAPI Coordinator escalates to Administrator and Governing Body. | Comprehensive QAPI plan review and possible special Governing Body session to reassess resources and priorities. | Within 30 days of identification. |
| CMS data correction not submitted within the preview window for identified inaccurate data. | QAPI Coordinator notifies Administrator. | Administrator and Compliance Officer assess corrective options; document the gap and root cause. | Within 5 business days of window closing. |
| HH QRP participation penalty applied (2% payment reduction). | QAPI Coordinator notifies CFO and Administrator. | Immediate assessment of submission compliance; corrective action to restore full participation per CO-RA-001. | Within 5 business days of penalty notification. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quarterly analysis report prepared. | Review of report files. | 4 reports per year; completed within 10 business days of each release. |
| Data accuracy verified each quarter. | Review of data verification records and any iQIES correction submissions. | Verification completed each quarter; corrections submitted within the preview window. |
| HHC data reviewed at QAPI Committee. | Review of committee minutes. | HHC data reviewed at each quarterly QAPI Committee meeting following release. |
| Action Tracker maintained and current. | Review of tracker. | All below-average measures tracked; status current. |
| Star Rating Improvement Plan initiated when rating < 4 stars. | Review of plan documents. | Plan initiated within 30 days of rating falling below 4 stars. |
| HHC data reported to Governing Body quarterly. | Review of QAPI Performance Report. | Included in all quarterly reports. |
| HH QRP submissions completed per CMS calendar. | Review of iQIES submission confirmations. | 100% of required submissions completed; no payment penalty incurred. |

### 8.2 Surveyor Expectations
Surveyors will: (1) ask whether the agency monitors its publicly reported quality measures; (2) request evidence of quarterly analysis and QAPI Committee review; (3) verify the agency acts on below-average measures; (4) assess whether the Governing Body is aware of the agency's public quality profile; (5) cross-reference survey findings with publicly reported measures to assess consistency.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agency does not monitor Home Health Compare between CMS surveys. | Declining measures not addressed until surveyor finds them. | Mandate quarterly analysis per Section 6.2.1. |
| Star Ratings declining but no QAPI-directed corrective action. | Continued decline; reputational and referral impact; survey risk. | Enforce corrective action triggers per Section 6.3.1. |
| Data inaccuracies not identified or corrected during preview window. | Incorrect publicly reported data; payment and reputation impact. | Mandate data verification per Section 6.2.2 each quarter. |
| Governing Body not aware of agency's Star Rating. | Governance failure; surveyor concern. | Include Star Ratings in every quarterly Governing Body report per Section 6.5.1. |

## 9. References
References: 42 CFR § 484.65; CMS Home Health Quality Reporting Program regulations and guidance; CMS Care Compare methodology documents; cross-references QA-PG-001, QA-PG-002, QA-PI-002, QA-PI-003, QA-AE-003, QA-SM-003, CL-OA-001–CL-OA-019, GV-GB-001, FN-BC-001, EN-TG-001.
## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 The QAPI Coordinator shall receive training on iQIES system access, CASPER report interpretation, HH QRP submission requirements, and Home Health Compare data methodology within 30 days of appointment and annually thereafter.
10.2 All QAPI Committee members shall receive annual training on Home Health Compare measure definitions, Star Rating calculation methodology, and quality improvement strategies for commonly below-average measures.
10.3 The DON and clinical supervisors shall receive annual training on the relationship between OASIS accuracy, clinical documentation quality, and publicly reported outcome measures.
10.4 Policy acknowledgment within 14 calendar days per standard.
## 11. Version Control
Per standard enterprise version control (EN-LC-001).

# QA-SM-005 — Policy Effectiveness Monitoring and Outcome Validation
## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | QA-SM-005 |
| Title | Policy Effectiveness Monitoring and Outcome Validation |
| Domain | QA — Quality Assurance & Performance Improvement |
| Subdomain | SM — Surveillance & Monitoring |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | QAPI Coordinator |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 2. Purpose
This policy requires Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to systematically measure whether its policies are achieving their intended outcomes through defined compliance metrics, outcome indicators, and incident correlation analysis. Policies are the foundational mechanism through which the agency operationalizes regulatory requirements, best practices, and quality standards. A policy that exists in writing but does not change behavior or achieve measurable outcomes provides no quality assurance value and may create false compliance assurance. This policy ensures that the agency's policy framework is evaluated not merely for existence and acknowledgment, but for actual effectiveness — measured through outcomes data, compliance audit results, incident trends, and staff behavior indicators. This policy supports compliance with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program data-driven improvement) and the agency's enterprise policy governance framework per EN-TG-001.
## 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Compliance Officer
The QAPI Coordinator
The Administrator
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
All QAPI Committee members
All department heads and supervisors responsible for policy implementation in their domains
## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal Policy Effectiveness Monitoring (PEM) program that evaluates whether REQUIRED and ESSENTIAL-tier policies are achieving their intended compliance and quality outcomes.
4.2 For each REQUIRED-tier policy, at least one defined outcome indicator shall be established that, when measured, provides evidence of whether the policy is being implemented as intended and achieving its stated purpose.
4.3 Policy effectiveness shall be evaluated through three complementary mechanisms: (a) compliance audit results per CO-RA-002 and CO-DC-002; (b) defined outcome indicators monitored through the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002; (c) incident and adverse event correlation analysis — identifying whether adverse events are linked to policy non-compliance.
4.4 Any REQUIRED-tier policy that demonstrates persistent non-compliance (below defined threshold for 2 or more consecutive audit cycles) or persistent adverse outcome correlation shall be reviewed for revision, enhanced communication, training improvement, or structural redesign.
4.5 The Policy Effectiveness Monitoring program shall be reported to the QAPI Committee semiannually and to the Governing Body annually as part of the year-end QAPI evaluation per QA-PG-002.
4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.
## 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Policy Effectiveness Monitoring (PEM) | The systematic process of measuring whether a policy achieves its stated purpose through defined compliance metrics, outcome indicators, and incident correlation analysis. |
| Policy Outcome Indicator | A quantifiable measure that provides evidence of whether a policy is being implemented as intended and is achieving its stated quality or compliance goal. |
| Compliance Metric | A measurable indicator of adherence to a policy's specific requirements, typically derived from documentation audits, observation, or process tracking. |
| Incident Correlation Analysis | The process of examining adverse event data to determine whether incidents are linked to policy non-compliance, policy gaps, or policy design failures. |
| Policy Non-Compliance Pattern | A recurring failure to meet a policy's compliance metric across 2 or more consecutive audit cycles, indicating a systemic implementation problem rather than an isolated deviation. |
| Policy Revision Trigger | A defined condition — persistent non-compliance, adverse outcome correlation, regulatory change, or QAPI Committee directive — that initiates a formal policy review and potential revision process. |

## 6. Procedures
### 6.1 PEM Program Structure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | QAPI Coordinator / Compliance Officer | Formally establish the Policy Effectiveness Monitoring program as a defined component of the QAPI and compliance programs. Document in the QAPI Program Description per QA-PG-001 Section 6.1.3. The program must define: (a) scope (minimum: all REQUIRED-tier policies); (b) evaluation mechanisms (audit, outcome indicator, incident correlation); (c) reporting frequency and format; (d) governance reporting structure. | At program establishment; reviewed annually. |
| 6.1.2 | QAPI Coordinator / Compliance Officer | For each REQUIRED-tier policy, complete the Policy Effectiveness Profile (Appendix A) documenting: (a) the policy's stated purpose; (b) the primary compliance metric (what should be measurably different because of this policy); (c) the defined outcome indicator (the quality or safety outcome the policy is intended to influence); (d) the data source for measurement; (e) the performance threshold; (f) the measurement frequency; (g) the incident correlation variable (what type of adverse event or incident would suggest this policy is not being followed). | Within 90 days of program establishment; updated annually or when a policy is revised. |
| 6.1.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Develop and maintain the Policy Effectiveness Master Registry (Appendix B) — a comprehensive log of all REQUIRED-tier policies with their associated compliance metrics, outcome indicators, and current effectiveness status. | Within 90 days of establishment; updated semiannually. |

### 6.2 Compliance Metric Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Compliance Officer | Ensure that the annual internal audit schedule per CO-RA-002 includes compliance audits for all REQUIRED-tier policies within the audit cycle. Each audit must generate a documented compliance rate for the policy's primary compliance metric. | Per annual audit schedule; all REQUIRED-tier policies audited at least annually. |
| 6.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Report compliance audit results to the QAPI Coordinator within 14 calendar days of audit completion. The report must include: (a) policy ID and title; (b) compliance metric measured; (c) sample size; (d) compliance rate; (e) prior cycle comparison; (f) items of non-compliance with root cause; (g) recommended corrective action. | Within 14 calendar days of each audit. |
| 6.2.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Integrate audit compliance data into the Policy Effectiveness Master Registry. Flag any policy with a compliance rate below the defined threshold for 2 consecutive audit cycles as "Non-Compliant Pattern — Policy Review Required." | Within 5 business days of audit report receipt. |

### 6.3 Outcome Indicator Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Ensure that the policy outcome indicator for each REQUIRED-tier policy is included in the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002 or monitored through an equivalent tracking mechanism. Outcome indicator data must be reviewed at least quarterly. | Ongoing per QA-PI-002 monitoring schedule. |
| 6.3.2 | QAPI Coordinator | For each policy outcome indicator, assess quarterly whether the indicator trend is consistent with the policy being effectively implemented. If the indicator is declining or below threshold while the compliance metric appears adequate, investigate whether: (a) the compliance metric is measuring the right behavior; (b) the policy design itself is flawed; (c) the training approach is insufficient; (d) external factors are confounding the result. | Quarterly as part of QA-PI-002 dashboard review. |

### 6.4 Incident Correlation Analysis

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Semiannually, conduct an Incident Correlation Analysis reviewing all adverse events and near-misses reported in the prior 6 months per QA-AE-001. For each incident category, determine: (a) whether the incident could have been prevented if the related policy had been followed; (b) whether the related policy was in fact followed (review clinical documentation and staff accounts); (c) whether the policy exists, is current, and addresses the incident type; (d) whether staff were trained on the policy. | Semiannually (January and July). |
| 6.4.2 | QAPI Coordinator | Categorize each analyzed incident into one of the following: (a) Policy Followed — no policy-related contributing factor; (b) Policy Not Followed — the policy existed but was not adhered to; (c) Policy Gap — no policy addresses this incident type; (d) Policy Design Failure — the policy exists and was followed, but the policy itself did not prevent the outcome; (e) Training Gap — staff were unaware of or did not understand the applicable policy. | At time of semiannual analysis. |
| 6.4.3 | QAPI Coordinator | For incidents categorized as "Policy Not Followed," "Policy Gap," or "Policy Design Failure," recommend to the QAPI Committee: (a) targeted re-education (for "Not Followed" with isolated occurrence); (b) policy development (for "Policy Gap"); (c) policy revision (for "Design Failure" or "Not Followed" with pattern). | At next QAPI Committee meeting following semiannual analysis. |

### 6.5 Policy Revision Triggers and Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | QAPI Coordinator / Compliance Officer | Initiate a formal policy review and potential revision process when any of the following Policy Revision Triggers are met: (a) Compliance rate below threshold for 2 consecutive audit cycles; (b) Outcome indicator below threshold for 3 consecutive monitoring periods despite adequate compliance audit rate; (c) Incident correlation analysis identifies 3 or more incidents in a 12-month period categorized as "Policy Not Followed" for the same policy; (d) Incident categorized as "Policy Design Failure" with patient harm at Level 3 or above (per QA-AE-001); (e) Regulatory change requiring policy update; (f) QAPI Committee or Governing Body directive for revision; (g) CMS survey finding related to the policy's subject matter. | Per trigger; initiation documented in Policy Effectiveness Master Registry within 7 calendar days. |
| 6.5.2 | Compliance Officer | Manage the policy revision process per EN-LC-001 (policy lifecycle management) and GV-PM-001 (policy development and approval process). Ensure the revised policy is: (a) reviewed against current regulatory requirements; (b) reviewed by subject matter experts; (c) approved by the Governing Body for REQUIRED-tier policies; (d) re-acknowledged by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date. | Per policy development timeline; Governing Body approval at next regular meeting or special meeting if urgent. |
| 6.5.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Following policy revision, re-establish baseline measurements for the revised policy's compliance metric and outcome indicator. Monitor for improvement within 2 audit cycles following the revision. If no improvement is observed, conduct deeper analysis of barriers to effective implementation. | Baseline re-established within 60 days of revised effective date; monitored for 2 audit cycles. |

### 6.6 QAPI Committee and Governing Body Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.6.1 | QAPI Coordinator | Present the Policy Effectiveness Monitoring Summary (Appendix C) to the QAPI Committee semiannually (at the first meeting following the January and July incident correlation analyses). The summary must include: (a) overall compliance metric status for all REQUIRED-tier policies; (b) policies with non-compliant patterns; (c) incident correlation findings; (d) policies with active revision triggers; (e) policies revised in the prior 6 months and effectiveness follow-up data; (f) recommended actions. | Semiannually at QAPI Committee; first meeting in February and August. |
| 6.6.2 | QAPI Coordinator | Include the annual Policy Effectiveness Monitoring Report (Appendix D) in the year-end QAPI evaluation submitted to the Governing Body per QA-PG-002 Section 6.4.1. | Annually as part of year-end QAPI evaluation. |
| 6.6.3 | Governing Body | Review the annual PEM report and direct: (a) additional resources for policies with persistent non-compliance; (b) structural or leadership changes if systemic policy adherence failures are identified; (c) revision priorities for the upcoming plan year. | At Q1 Governing Body meeting during year-end QAPI presentation. |

### 6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| More than 25% of REQUIRED-tier policies in a single domain show non-compliant patterns simultaneously. | QAPI Coordinator escalates to Administrator and Compliance Officer. | Domain-level review; enhanced training; possible external audit. Reported to Governing Body at next meeting. | Domain review within 30 days. |
| Incident correlation identifies Policy Design Failure with sentinel event. | QAPI Coordinator escalates to Administrator and Governing Body immediately. | Immediate policy suspension if risk of further harm exists; urgent revision per Governing Body directive; special Governing Body meeting if needed. | Within 48 hours of identification. |
| PEM program reports not generated for a semiannual cycle. | Compliance Officer notifies Administrator. | Reports generated and presented retroactively. Root cause of gap addressed per QA-AE-003. Reported to Governing Body. | Retroactive reports within 30 days; root cause addressed within 14 days. |

## 8. Compliance Monitoring
### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Policy Effectiveness Profile completed for all REQUIRED-tier policies. | Review of profiles in QAPI records. | 100% of REQUIRED-tier policies have current profile. |
| Policy Effectiveness Master Registry maintained. | Review of registry currency. | Updated within 30 days of each semiannual PEM cycle. |
| Compliance audits completed for all REQUIRED-tier policies annually. | Review of audit schedule vs. audit reports. | 100% of REQUIRED-tier policies audited within the annual cycle. |
| Semiannual incident correlation analysis completed. | Review of analysis reports. | 2 analyses per year; completed in February and August. |
| Policies with non-compliant patterns have documented revision triggers. | Review of Master Registry and QAPI Committee minutes. | 100% of policies with 2+ consecutive non-compliant audit cycles have documented revision trigger. |
| Semiannual PEM summary presented to QAPI Committee. | Review of committee minutes. | 2 presentations per year; documented in minutes. |
| Annual PEM report included in Governing Body year-end review. | Review of year-end QAPI evaluation and Governing Body minutes. | Included in annual Q1 Governing Body presentation. |

### 8.2 Surveyor Expectations
Surveyors will: (1) ask whether the agency monitors whether its policies are actually followed and effective; (2) look for evidence that the agency uses audit and outcome data to evaluate policies, not just to document them; (3) assess whether policy non-compliance is identified and addressed systematically; (4) verify that the QAPI program integrates policy compliance as a data input; (5) look for evidence that the Governing Body is aware of policy effectiveness.
### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agency has comprehensive policies but does not measure whether they are followed. | False compliance assurance; surveyor finds practice diverging from policy. | Mandate compliance metrics per Section 6.2. |
| Adverse events occur but are not analyzed for policy non-compliance contributing factors. | Root causes not identified; policy gaps not closed. | Mandate incident correlation analysis per Section 6.4. |
| Policy non-compliance identified in audit but policy is not revised or training not enhanced. | Pattern of non-compliance persists indefinitely. | Enforce policy revision triggers per Section 6.5.1. |
| PEM program exists but is never reported to the Governing Body. | Governance failure; systemic policy problems unseen at the top. | Mandate annual Governing Body reporting per Section 6.6.2. |

## 9. References
References: 42 CFR § 484.65; cross-references QA-PG-001, QA-PG-002, QA-PI-002, QA-PI-004, QA-AE-001, QA-AE-003, CO-RA-002, CO-DC-002, GV-PM-001, GV-PM-002, EN-LC-001, EN-LC-004, EN-TG-001, GV-GB-001.
## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 The QAPI Coordinator and Compliance Officer shall receive training on policy effectiveness measurement methodology, compliance metric design, and incident correlation analysis within 30 days of assignment.
10.2 All department heads and supervisors shall receive training on their responsibility for policy implementation in their domain and how compliance metrics are measured within 14 calendar days of policy effective date.
10.3 Policy acknowledgment within 14 calendar days per standard.
## 11. Version Control
Per standard enterprise version control (EN-LC-001).

# POLICY: RM-ER-001 — Enterprise Risk Management Program

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes the comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The ERM program provides a systematic, agency-wide approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, monitoring, and reporting risks across all operational domains. This policy ensures that risk management is integrated into the agency's governance structure, strategic planning, and daily operations, supporting compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, OSHA requirements, state licensure standards, and OIG Compliance Program Guidance.
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to:
All members of the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
The Agency Administrator
The Risk Manager
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager
The Compliance Officer
All department directors and supervisory personnel
All clinical and administrative staff responsible for identifying and reporting risks
All contracted entities performing services on behalf of the agency
This policy does not replace domain-specific risk management activities (e.g., clinical risk managed under CL domain, financial risk under FN domain) but provides the overarching governance framework within which all domain-specific risk activities operate.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) | A structured, agency-wide process for identifying, assessing, prioritizing, mitigating, and monitoring risks that may affect the agency's ability to achieve its mission, maintain regulatory compliance, ensure patient safety, or sustain financial viability. |
| Risk | Any event, condition, or circumstance that, if it occurs, could have a negative impact on patient safety, staff safety, regulatory compliance, financial performance, or organizational reputation. |
| Risk Register | The centralized repository documenting all identified risks, their assessed severity and likelihood, assigned mitigation strategies, responsible parties, status, and review dates. |
| Risk Appetite | The level and type of risk the Governing Body is willing to accept in pursuit of the agency's mission and strategic objectives. |
| Risk Tolerance | The acceptable variation in outcomes related to specific risks, defined by measurable thresholds. |
| Mitigation | Actions taken to reduce the likelihood or impact of an identified risk. |
| Residual Risk | The level of risk remaining after mitigation strategies have been implemented. |
| Risk Owner | The individual assigned accountability for monitoring and managing a specific risk, including implementation of mitigation strategies and reporting on status. |
| Sentinel Event | An unexpected occurrence involving death or serious physical or psychological injury, or the risk thereof. |
| Near Miss | An event or situation that did not produce patient or staff injury but had the potential to do so. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal Enterprise Risk Management program that provides a systematic approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, and monitoring risks across all agency operations.
4.2 The Governing Body shall have ultimate oversight of the ERM program and shall receive quarterly risk reports from the Risk Manager, per policy GV-GB-001 §6.2.
4.3 The Risk Manager shall be designated as the agency's ERM program leader, with authority to access all operational domains for risk identification and assessment purposes.
4.4 A centralized Risk Register shall be maintained as the single authoritative source for all identified enterprise risks. The Risk Register shall be reviewed and updated no less than quarterly.
4.5 All agency personnel shall be responsible for identifying and reporting potential risks through the agency's incident reporting system per policy RM-ER-002.
4.6 The ERM program shall be integrated with the agency's QAPI program (QA-PG-001), compliance program (CO-CP-001), and financial oversight processes (FN-FP-007) to ensure coordinated risk governance.
4.7 Risk assessments shall be conducted annually at minimum, and additionally upon any significant operational change, regulatory change, adverse event, or external threat.
4.8 The Governing Body shall formally define the agency's risk appetite and risk tolerance thresholds. Risk tolerance thresholds shall be documented and reviewed annually.
4.9 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 ERM Program Structure and Governance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Governing Body | Approve the ERM program charter, including the program's scope, objectives, governance structure, and reporting requirements. | Prior to initial implementation; reviewed annually at Q1 meeting. |
| 5.1.2 | Administrator | Designate a qualified Risk Manager with defined authority, responsibilities, and reporting relationships. Document designation in writing with copy to Governing Body. | Prior to program operation; within 30 calendar days of any vacancy. |
| 5.1.3 | Risk Manager | Develop and maintain the ERM Program Manual documenting: (a) program structure and governance; (b) risk identification methodology; (c) risk assessment criteria (likelihood and impact scales); (d) risk categorization taxonomy; (e) mitigation planning standards; (f) monitoring and reporting schedules; (g) escalation protocols. | Within 60 calendar days of designation; updated annually. |
| 5.1.4 | Risk Manager | Establish a Risk Management Committee comprising, at minimum: Risk Manager (chair), Administrator, Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, and QAPI Coordinator. | Within 30 calendar days of program establishment. |
| 5.1.5 | Risk Management Committee | Convene meetings no fewer than quarterly. Additional meetings shall be convened within 48 hours of any sentinel event or significant risk emergence. | Quarterly; ad hoc as required. |
| 5.1.6 | Risk Manager | Prepare and distribute meeting agendas no fewer than 5 calendar days before each scheduled Risk Management Committee meeting. | 5 calendar days before each meeting. |
| 5.1.7 | Risk Manager | Record formal minutes for all Risk Management Committee meetings documenting: (a) attendees; (b) risks reviewed; (c) risk register updates; (d) mitigation status; (e) new risks identified; (f) escalation decisions; (g) action items with responsible parties and deadlines. | Draft within 7 calendar days of meeting. |

### 5.2 Risk Identification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Risk Manager | Implement a multi-source risk identification process that incorporates: (a) incident and near-miss reports (RM-ER-002); (b) complaint and grievance data (OP-PA-001); (c) QAPI findings (QA-PG-001); (d) compliance audit results (CO-RA-002); (e) financial variance analysis (FN-FP-003); (f) staff safety reports (RM-SS-001); (g) patient safety data (QA-AE-004); (h) regulatory change monitoring (CO-RA-001); (i) environmental safety assessments (RM-PS-001); (j) external benchmarking data. | Continuous; formally compiled quarterly. |
| 5.2.2 | All Staff | Report identified or suspected risks through the agency's incident reporting system within 24 hours of identification, per RM-ER-002. | Within 24 hours of identification. |
| 5.2.3 | Department Directors | Submit a departmental risk identification summary to the Risk Manager at the close of each quarter, documenting all risks identified within their domain during the period. | Within 10 calendar days of quarter end. |
| 5.2.4 | Risk Manager | Conduct an annual comprehensive risk assessment (enterprise-wide risk survey) across all 10 policy domains, engaging department directors and key personnel. | Annually; completed within 60 calendar days of fiscal year start. |
| 5.2.5 | Risk Manager | Conduct an ad hoc risk assessment within 72 hours of any of the following triggering events: (a) sentinel event; (b) CMS survey deficiency at Condition level; (c) significant regulatory change; (d) natural disaster or public health emergency; (e) data breach or security incident; (f) key leadership vacancy; (g) significant financial variance. | Within 72 hours of triggering event. |

### 5.3 Risk Assessment and Prioritization

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Risk Manager | Assess each identified risk using the agency's standardized Risk Assessment Matrix (Appendix A) evaluating: (a) Likelihood of occurrence (1–5 scale); (b) Severity of impact (1–5 scale); (c) Risk Score = Likelihood × Severity. | Within 14 calendar days of risk identification. |
| 5.3.2 | Risk Manager | Categorize each assessed risk by domain: Clinical, Compliance/Regulatory, Financial, Operational, Technology, Human Resources, Reputational, Legal/Litigation, Environmental/Safety. | Concurrent with assessment. |
| 5.3.3 | Risk Manager | Classify each risk by priority level per the Risk Assessment Matrix: Critical (20–25), High (12–19), Moderate (6–11), Low (1–5). | Concurrent with assessment. |
| 5.3.4 | Risk Management Committee | Review and validate all Critical and High priority risk assessments. Validate that risk scores, categorizations, and priority classifications are accurate and consistent. | At each quarterly meeting; within 48 hours for Critical risks. |
| 5.3.5 | Risk Manager | Escalate all Critical priority risks to the Administrator immediately upon identification and to the Governing Body within 72 hours, with a preliminary mitigation recommendation. | Immediately to Administrator; within 72 hours to Governing Body. |

### 5.4 Risk Mitigation Planning

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Risk Manager | Develop a Risk Mitigation Plan (Appendix B) for each Critical and High priority risk, documenting: (a) risk description and root cause; (b) current controls in place; (c) proposed mitigation actions; (d) responsible party (Risk Owner); (e) implementation timeline; (f) success metrics; (g) residual risk assessment; (h) monitoring frequency. | Within 7 calendar days for Critical; within 14 calendar days for High. |
| 5.4.2 | Risk Owner (Assigned) | Implement approved mitigation actions per the plan timeline and report progress to the Risk Manager at defined intervals. | Per plan timeline; progress reports at minimum monthly. |
| 5.4.3 | Risk Manager | Develop mitigation recommendations for Moderate priority risks. Low priority risks shall be documented in the Risk Register with accepted status and monitored for escalation. | Within 30 calendar days of assessment for Moderate risks. |
| 5.4.4 | Risk Management Committee | Review and approve all Critical and High priority mitigation plans. Approve or modify Risk Owner assignments. | At next scheduled meeting; within 48 hours for Critical risks. |
| 5.4.5 | Governing Body | Review and approve mitigation plans for Critical priority risks. Confirm risk appetite alignment. | At next quarterly meeting; within 7 calendar days for imminent patient safety risks. |

### 5.5 Risk Monitoring and Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Risk Manager | Maintain the centralized Risk Register (Appendix C) with current status for all identified risks. The Risk Register must document: (a) Risk ID; (b) date identified; (c) risk description; (d) category; (e) likelihood score; (f) severity score; (g) risk score; (h) priority; (i) Risk Owner; (j) mitigation status; (k) residual risk; (l) last review date; (m) next review date. | Updated continuously; formally reviewed quarterly. |
| 5.5.2 | Risk Manager | Prepare and submit a quarterly Enterprise Risk Report (Appendix D) to the Risk Management Committee and Administrator, documenting: (a) Risk Register summary with trending; (b) new risks identified; (c) risks closed/resolved; (d) mitigation plan status for all Critical and High risks; (e) risk score trending analysis; (f) domain-level risk heat map; (g) recommendations. | 7 calendar days before each quarterly Risk Management Committee meeting. |
| 5.5.3 | Risk Manager | Prepare and submit an annual Enterprise Risk Report to the Governing Body including: (a) year-in-review risk summary; (b) risk trending analysis; (c) mitigation effectiveness evaluation; (d) risk appetite/tolerance review recommendations; (e) ERM program effectiveness assessment; (f) next-year risk priorities. | Annually; presented at Q4 Governing Body meeting. |
| 5.5.4 | Administrator | Present the quarterly risk summary to the Governing Body as a standing agenda item per GV-GB-001 §6.2. | At each quarterly Governing Body meeting. |
| 5.5.5 | Risk Manager | Monitor all open mitigation plans for adherence to timelines. Escalate overdue mitigation actions to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of missed deadline. | Ongoing; escalation within 7 calendar days. |
| 5.5.6 | Risk Manager | Conduct an annual ERM program effectiveness review evaluating: (a) risk identification completeness; (b) assessment timeliness; (c) mitigation plan closure rates; (d) incident trending correlation; (e) staff reporting compliance; (f) Governing Body engagement. Document findings and improvement recommendations. | Annually; completed within 30 calendar days of fiscal year end. |

### 5.6 Integration with QAPI and Compliance Programs

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.6.1 | Risk Manager | Coordinate with the QAPI Coordinator to ensure all risks with patient safety or quality implications are reported to the QAPI Committee per QA-PG-003. | Ongoing; formal coordination at each quarterly meeting. |
| 5.6.2 | Risk Manager | Coordinate with the Compliance Officer to ensure all risks with regulatory or compliance implications are reported to the Compliance Committee per CO-CP-003. | Ongoing; formal coordination at each quarterly meeting. |
| 5.6.3 | Risk Manager | Ensure that corrective actions arising from risk mitigation are tracked in alignment with the QAPI corrective action process per QA-AE-003. | Ongoing. |
| 5.6.4 | Risk Manager | Participate in the QAPI Committee as a standing member and present the risk management perspective at each meeting. | At each QAPI Committee meeting. |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement
### 7.1 Compliance Indicators

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ERM program charter approved by Governing Body | Review of Governing Body minutes | Current approval documented; reviewed annually. |
| Risk Manager designated and documented | Review of personnel file and designation letter | Current appointment on file; no vacancy >30 days. |
| Risk Management Committee convenes quarterly | Review of meeting minutes with dates and attendance | 4 or more meetings per calendar year. |
| Risk Register is current and maintained | Review of Risk Register with last update date | Updated within 30 calendar days; no stale entries >90 days. |
| Critical risks escalated to Governing Body | Review of Governing Body minutes and risk reports | 100% of Critical risks reported within 72 hours. |
| Quarterly Enterprise Risk Reports completed | Review of report files | 4 reports per year; submitted 7 days before meetings. |
| Annual comprehensive risk assessment completed | Review of assessment documentation | Completed within 60 days of fiscal year start. |
| Risk mitigation plans completed for Critical/High risks | Review of mitigation plans vs. Risk Register | 100% coverage; no Critical risk without plan >7 days. |
| Policy acknowledgments current | Review of signed Appendix E forms | 100% completion within 14 days. |

### 7.2 Surveyor Expectations
CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey will verify:
Evidence of a structured risk management program. Surveyors will request the ERM charter, program manual, and Risk Register.
Evidence of Governing Body oversight of risk. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes for documented risk report presentation and action.
Evidence that risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated. Surveyors will select specific risks from the Register and trace through identification, assessment, mitigation plan, and resolution.
Integration with QAPI. Surveyors will verify that risk data informs the QAPI program and that adverse event data flows into the risk management process.
Incident reporting processes. Surveyors will verify the existence and functioning of the incident reporting system per RM-ER-002.
Staff awareness. Surveyors may interview staff regarding their understanding of how to report risks and incidents.
### 7.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No formal ERM program exists; risk management is ad hoc. | Survey deficiency; unidentified risks accumulate without mitigation. | Implement this policy; maintain charter, manual, and Risk Register. |
| Risk Register exists but is not updated or reviewed. | Stale data provides false assurance; emerging risks missed. | Enforce quarterly review; assign Risk Manager accountability. |
| Governing Body does not receive or act on risk reports. | Failure of governance oversight; per GV-GB-001. | Enforce quarterly reporting as standing Governing Body agenda item. |
| Risks identified but no mitigation plans developed. | Known risks remain unmitigated; liability exposure increases. | Enforce mitigation plan timelines per §5.4. |
| No integration between risk management and QAPI. | Siloed programs; duplicated efforts; gaps in patient safety oversight. | Enforce §5.6 coordination requirements. |
| Staff do not report risks or incidents. | Underreporting leads to incomplete Risk Register. | Enforce training requirements; maintain anonymous reporting option per RM-ER-002. |

## 9. Training Requirements
9.1 The Risk Manager shall receive comprehensive training on ERM methodology, risk assessment tools, and program governance within 30 calendar days of designation.
9.2 All Risk Management Committee members shall receive orientation to this policy and the ERM program within 14 calendar days of appointment.
9.3 All department directors and supervisory personnel shall receive annual training on risk identification, reporting obligations, and their role within the ERM framework.
9.4 All clinical and administrative staff shall receive annual training on incident and risk reporting per RM-ER-002, including how to access the reporting system and what constitutes a reportable event.
9.5 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.
9.6 The Risk Manager shall maintain a training completion tracking log and report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of the completion deadline.
## 10. Version Control
10.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.
10.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. All superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
10.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body; (b) re-acknowledgment by all in-scope personnel within 14 calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
10.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.
## Appendix A — Risk Assessment Matrix

# POLICY: RM-ER-002 — Incident Reporting & Investigation
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | RM-ER-002 |
| Title | Incident Reporting & Investigation |
| Domain | RM — Risk Management & Safety |
| Subdomain | ER — Enterprise Risk |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 3 — Confidential |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Risk Manager |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements for reporting, documenting, and investigating all incidents, near-misses, and adverse events occurring in connection with the operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A robust incident reporting system is essential for identifying risks, preventing recurrence, improving patient and staff safety, and supporting compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, OSHA requirements, and state mandatory reporting obligations.
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to:
All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (clinical and administrative)
All contracted and per diem staff providing services on behalf of the agency
All supervisory and management personnel
All volunteers performing activities under agency direction
The Risk Manager, Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Incident | Any event or occurrence that results in, or has the potential to result in, harm to a patient, staff member, visitor, or third party, or damage to property, or disruption to agency operations. |
| Adverse Event | An incident that results in actual harm or injury to a patient or staff member, including physical injury, psychological harm, or death. |
| Near Miss | An event or situation that did not result in harm but, under slightly different circumstances, could have resulted in an adverse event. |
| Sentinel Event | An unexpected occurrence involving death or serious physical or psychological injury, or the risk thereof. Sentinel events signal the need for immediate investigation and response. |
| Incident Report | The standardized document (Appendix A) used to record the facts, circumstances, and initial assessment of an incident. |
| Reportable Event | An incident that meets criteria for mandatory external reporting to state agencies, CMS, law enforcement, or other regulatory bodies. |
| Contributing Factor | A condition, action, or inaction that, while not the primary cause, increased the likelihood or severity of an incident. |
| Root Cause | The fundamental underlying reason(s) an incident occurred, which, if corrected, would prevent recurrence. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All employees, contractors, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall immediately report any incident, adverse event, near miss, or unsafe condition through the agency's incident reporting system.
4.2 The agency shall maintain a no-retaliation policy for good-faith incident reporting. No employee shall face disciplinary action for reporting an incident, per policy CO-CP-005.
4.3 Incident reports are confidential risk management documents. They shall not be filed in the patient's clinical record and shall be maintained in the risk management file.
4.4 All incidents shall be classified by severity level and investigated according to a tiered investigation protocol proportional to severity.
4.5 Mandatory external reporting obligations (to state agencies, CMS, law enforcement, adult protective services) shall be fulfilled within the timeframes required by applicable law, regardless of internal investigation status.
4.6 All sentinel events shall trigger an immediate investigation and root cause analysis per policy QA-AE-002.
4.7 Incident data shall be aggregated, trended, and reported to the Risk Management Committee quarterly per RM-ER-005, and to the QAPI Committee per QA-PG-003.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Immediate Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Reporting Staff Member | Ensure immediate safety of all persons involved. Provide first aid or emergency medical care as needed. Call 911 if life-threatening emergency exists. | Immediately upon incident occurrence. |
| 5.1.2 | Reporting Staff Member | Notify the immediate supervisor verbally of the incident. | Within 1 hour of incident occurrence. |
| 5.1.3 | Supervisor | For sentinel events or serious adverse events: Notify the Risk Manager, Director of Nursing, and Administrator immediately by phone. | Within 1 hour of notification. |
| 5.1.4 | Director of Nursing | For patient-related incidents: Assess the patient's current condition and ensure appropriate clinical intervention is initiated. Notify the attending physician as clinically indicated. | Within 2 hours of notification. |

### 5.2 Incident Report Completion

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Reporting Staff Member | Complete the Incident Report Form (Appendix A) documenting: (a) date, time, and location of incident; (b) persons involved (patient, staff, visitor); (c) factual description of what occurred (objective, non-judgmental language); (d) witnesses; (e) immediate actions taken; (f) injuries or harm observed; (g) equipment involved (if applicable); (h) environmental conditions. | Within 24 hours of incident occurrence. |
| 5.2.2 | Reporting Staff Member | Submit the completed Incident Report to the immediate supervisor for review. | Concurrent with completion (within 24 hours). |
| 5.2.3 | Supervisor | Review the Incident Report for completeness and accuracy. Obtain additional information from witnesses if needed. Forward to the Risk Manager. | Within 48 hours of incident occurrence. |
| 5.2.4 | Risk Manager | Log the incident in the Incident Tracking Log (Appendix B). Assign an Incident ID number. | Within 72 hours of incident occurrence. |

### 5.3 Incident Classification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Risk Manager | Classify the incident severity using the Incident Severity Classification Scale (Appendix C): Level 1 — No Harm/Near Miss: Event occurred but no injury or harm resulted. Level 2 — Minor Harm: Temporary, minor injury requiring minimal intervention (e.g., first aid). Level 3 — Moderate Harm: Injury requiring medical treatment or resulting in temporary impairment. Level 4 — Serious Harm: Significant injury requiring hospitalization, surgery, or resulting in permanent impairment. Level 5 — Sentinel Event: Death, or serious physical or psychological injury, or risk thereof. | Within 72 hours of report receipt. |
| 5.3.2 | Risk Manager | Classify the incident by type: ☐ Patient fall ☐ Medication error ☐ Infection ☐ Equipment malfunction ☐ Staff injury ☐ Vehicle accident ☐ Verbal/physical threat ☐ Property damage ☐ HIPAA breach ☐ Documentation error ☐ Missed visit impacting care ☐ Other | Concurrent with severity classification. |
| 5.3.3 | Risk Manager | Determine investigation tier: Level 1–2: Manager-level review and documentation. Level 3: Risk Manager investigation with written report. Level 4–5: Full investigation with root cause analysis (per QA-AE-002). | Concurrent with classification. |

### 5.4 Investigation Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Risk Manager | For Level 3–5 incidents, initiate a formal investigation. Preserve all relevant evidence including: (a) clinical records; (b) staff schedules; (c) equipment involved; (d) photographs (if applicable); (e) witness statements; (f) electronic system logs. | Investigation initiated within 24 hours for Level 4–5; within 72 hours for Level 3. |
| 5.4.2 | Risk Manager | Interview all involved parties and witnesses. Document interviews using the Witness Statement Form (Appendix D). Interviews shall be conducted individually in a private setting. | Within 7 calendar days of incident for Level 3; within 48 hours for Level 4–5. |
| 5.4.3 | Risk Manager | For Level 4–5 incidents, convene an Investigation Team comprising: Risk Manager (lead), Director of Nursing (for clinical incidents), department director of involved area, and Compliance Officer (if regulatory implications). | Within 48 hours of incident. |
| 5.4.4 | Investigation Team | Conduct root cause analysis per QA-AE-002 for all Level 4–5 incidents. Document findings using the Root Cause Analysis template. | Completed within 30 calendar days of incident. |
| 5.4.5 | Risk Manager | Complete the Investigation Summary Report (Appendix E) for all Level 3–5 incidents, documenting: (a) incident summary; (b) investigation methodology; (c) findings of fact; (d) root cause(s) identified; (e) contributing factors; (f) recommendations; (g) corrective actions required. | Within 14 calendar days for Level 3; within 30 calendar days for Level 4–5. |
| 5.4.6 | Risk Manager | For Level 1–2 incidents, the supervisor completes a brief investigation summary on the Incident Report Form (Appendix A, Section 3) and submits to Risk Manager for trending. | Within 7 calendar days of incident. |

### 5.5 Mandatory External Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Risk Manager | Determine whether the incident triggers mandatory external reporting obligations including: (a) State health department notification; (b) Adult/Child Protective Services report (per CL-PR-006); (c) OSHA injury/illness report (per 29 CFR § 1904); (d) CMS adverse event reporting; (e) Law enforcement notification; (f) HIPAA breach notification (per CO-HP-003); (g) Coroner/medical examiner notification (if applicable). | Within 24 hours of incident classification. |
| 5.5.2 | Risk Manager / Compliance Officer | Complete and submit all mandatory external reports within required timeframes. Document the report, recipient, date, and method of submission. | Per applicable regulatory timeframes (see Appendix F). |
| 5.5.3 | Risk Manager | Notify the Administrator and Compliance Officer of all mandatory external reports filed. | Within 24 hours of filing. |
| 5.5.4 | Administrator | Notify the Governing Body of all Level 4–5 incidents and all mandatory external reports filed, per GV-GB-001 §6.5. | Within 72 hours; at next Governing Body meeting for full report. |

### 5.6 Corrective Action and Follow-Up

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.6.1 | Risk Manager | For all Level 3–5 incidents, develop corrective action recommendations based on investigation findings. Submit to Risk Management Committee for approval. | Within 7 calendar days of investigation completion. |
| 5.6.2 | Risk Management Committee | Review and approve corrective action plans per QA-AE-003. Assign responsible parties and deadlines. | At next scheduled meeting; within 48 hours for Level 4–5. |
| 5.6.3 | Assigned Responsible Party | Implement corrective actions per approved plan. Document implementation evidence. | Per plan timeline. |
| 5.6.4 | Risk Manager | Monitor corrective action implementation. Verify effectiveness through follow-up audit or review. | At 30, 60, and 90 days post-implementation. |
| 5.6.5 | Risk Manager | Close the incident in the Incident Tracking Log when: (a) investigation is complete; (b) corrective actions are implemented and verified; (c) any external reporting obligations have been fulfilled. | Upon completion of all required actions. |

### 5.7 Trending and Analysis

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.7.1 | Risk Manager | Aggregate incident data monthly for trending analysis. Track: (a) incident volume by type; (b) incident volume by severity; (c) incident volume by department/service; (d) staff involved (de-identified for trending); (e) time of day/day of week patterns; (f) corrective action effectiveness. | Monthly. |
| 5.7.2 | Risk Manager | Present quarterly incident trending report to Risk Management Committee and QAPI Committee per RM-ER-005 and QA-SM-001. | Quarterly. |
| 5.7.3 | Risk Manager | Escalate any identified patterns or clusters (3 or more similar incidents within 30 days) to the Administrator and Director of Nursing for immediate review. | Within 48 hours of pattern identification. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document/Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Incident Report | Completed Appendix A for each incident | Reporting staff member / Supervisor | Risk Management file (NOT patient clinical record) | Within 24 hours of incident; retained 7 years. |
| Incident Tracking Log | Appendix B — centralized log | Risk Manager | Risk Management electronic system | Updated within 72 hours of each incident; retained 7 years. |
| Witness Statements | Completed Appendix D | Risk Manager / Investigator | Risk Management file | Within 7 days (Level 3); within 48 hours (Level 4–5); retained 7 years. |
| Investigation Summary Report | Completed Appendix E (Level 3–5) | Risk Manager / Investigation Team | Risk Management file | Per §5.4.5 timelines; retained 7 years. |
| Corrective Action Plans | Per QA-AE-003 | Risk Manager / Committee | Risk Management file; QAPI file | Per plan timeline; retained 7 years. |
| Mandatory external reports | Copies of all filed reports | Risk Manager / Compliance Officer | Risk Management file; Compliance file | Retained 7 years. |
| Quarterly trending reports | Aggregated analysis | Risk Manager | Risk Management file; QAPI file | Quarterly; retained 7 years. |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed Appendix G | All in-scope personnel | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 calendar days; retained 7 years. |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Incident reports completed within 24 hours | Audit of report timestamps vs. incident time | ≥95% compliance. |
| All incidents logged in tracking system within 72 hours | Audit of Incident Tracking Log dates | 100% compliance. |
| All Level 4–5 incidents investigated with RCA | Review of investigation reports | 100% completion within 30 days. |
| Mandatory external reports filed within required timeframes | Audit of filing dates vs. regulatory deadlines | 100% compliance. |
| Corrective actions implemented per plan | Review of implementation evidence | ≥90% on-time completion. |
| Quarterly trending reports completed | Review of report files | 4 per year; submitted before meetings. |
| Staff training on incident reporting current | Training completion log review | 100% completion within 30 days of hire; annual refresher. |
| No retaliation for reporting | Review of HR records; staff survey results | Zero substantiated retaliation findings. |

### Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Staff do not report incidents or near misses due to fear of blame. | Underreporting; unknown risks accumulate. | Enforce no-retaliation policy; provide anonymous reporting option; emphasize culture of safety in training. |
| Incident reports are placed in patient clinical records. | Legal discovery exposure; breach of risk management privilege. | Train all staff that incident reports go ONLY to Risk Management file. |
| Investigation is not conducted or is superficial. | Root causes not identified; recurrence likely. | Enforce tiered investigation protocol with defined timelines. |
| Mandatory external reporting deadlines missed. | Regulatory violations; fines; survey deficiencies. | Maintain Appendix F (External Reporting Reference); Risk Manager tracks all deadlines. |
| Incident data not trended or analyzed. | Patterns missed; systemic issues persist. | Enforce monthly aggregation and quarterly reporting per §5.7. |

## 9. Training Requirements
9.1 All new employees shall receive incident reporting training during orientation, within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) what constitutes a reportable incident; (b) how to complete the Incident Report Form; (c) to whom and when to report; (d) non-retaliation protections; (e) distinction between incident report and clinical documentation.
9.2 All staff shall receive annual refresher training on incident reporting.
9.3 All supervisory staff shall receive additional training on: (a) Incident Report review and completion oversight; (b) immediate response and escalation protocols; (c) evidence preservation.
9.4 The Risk Manager and Investigation Team members shall receive training on investigation methodology and root cause analysis.
9.5 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix G) within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or new hire.
## 10. Version Control
Per RM-ER-001 §10. Only the most current approved version is valid.

# POLICY: RM-ER-003 — Risk Assessment & Prioritization
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Subdomain | ER — Enterprise Risk |

| Access Tier | Tier 3 — Confidential |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
