### 9. Training Requirements
9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on environmental safety assessment during orientation within 14 calendar days of hire.
9.2 Annual refresher training on environmental safety assessment, including common hazards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.
9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

# POLICY: RM-PS-002 — Hazardous Materials & Waste Management
### Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | RM-PS-002 |
| Title | Hazardous Materials & Waste Management |
| Domain | RM — Risk Management & Safety |
| Subdomain | PS — Patient & Environmental Safety |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Risk Manager |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 1. Purpose
This policy defines procedures for the safe handling, storage, transport, and disposal of biohazardous materials, sharps, pharmaceutical waste, and other regulated medical waste generated during home health service delivery by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Compliance with OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, California Medical Waste Management Act, and EPA regulations is required to protect staff, patients, and the community.
### 2. Scope
This policy applies to all clinical staff, home health aides, and any personnel who handle, transport, or dispose of medical waste, sharps, biohazardous materials, or pharmaceutical waste during agency operations.
### 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Biohazardous Waste | Waste containing blood, body fluids, or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM) that may pose a risk of infection. |
| Sharps | Any object that can penetrate the skin, including needles, syringes with needles, lancets, scalpel blades, and broken glass contaminated with blood or OPIM. |
| Sharps Container | A puncture-resistant, leak-proof, closable container labeled with the biohazard symbol, used for the disposal of sharps. |
| Pharmaceutical Waste | Expired, unused, or contaminated medications requiring special disposal to prevent environmental contamination or misuse. |
| Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) | Gloves, gowns, masks, eye protection, and other equipment used to create a barrier between the worker and infectious material. |
| Standard Precautions | Infection control practices applied to all patients regardless of known infection status, including hand hygiene, PPE use, and safe injection practices. |
| Exposure Incident | A specific eye, mouth, mucous membrane, non-intact skin, or parenteral contact with blood or OPIM resulting from the performance of an employee's duties. |

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All staff shall follow Standard Precautions when handling blood, body fluids, or other potentially infectious materials per CL-SD-016 and OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030.
4.2 Sharps shall be disposed of immediately after use in an approved sharps container at the point of use. Recapping of needles is prohibited.
4.3 Biohazardous waste generated in the patient's home shall be managed and disposed of in compliance with California Medical Waste Management Act (Health & Safety Code § 117600 et seq.) and agency procedures.
4.4 All staff shall have access to appropriate PPE and shall be trained on its proper use, removal, and disposal.
4.5 Exposure incidents shall be reported and managed per the agency's Exposure Control Plan and RM-ER-002.
4.6 Pharmaceutical waste shall be disposed of per FDA and EPA guidelines, with controlled substances disposed of per DEA requirements.
### 5. Procedures
#### 5.1 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Agency (Risk Manager / Operations Director) | Provide all clinical staff with appropriate PPE including: (a) gloves (non-latex available); (b) gowns; (c) face masks; (d) eye protection/face shields; (e) CPR pocket masks. Ensure sufficient supply for all visits. | Continuous; supply checked monthly. |
| 5.1.2 | All Clinical Staff | Use appropriate PPE when exposure to blood, body fluids, or OPIM is anticipated. Select PPE based on the anticipated exposure per Standard Precautions. | At each applicable patient encounter. |
| 5.1.3 | All Clinical Staff | Remove and dispose of contaminated PPE before leaving the patient's home. Dispose in a plastic bag that is sealed and placed in the patient's household waste unless visibly saturated with blood (in which case, treat as biohazardous waste per §5.3). | At completion of each encounter. |

#### 5.2 Sharps Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | All Clinical Staff | Carry an approved, labeled sharps container to every visit where sharps may be used. | At each applicable visit. |
| 5.2.2 | All Clinical Staff | Dispose of sharps immediately after use directly into the sharps container at the point of use. Do NOT recap, bend, break, or remove needles from syringes. | Immediately after use. |
| 5.2.3 | All Clinical Staff | When sharps container is ¾ full, close and seal it. Do not overfill. Replace with a new container. | When ¾ full. |
| 5.2.4 | All Clinical Staff | Transport sealed sharps containers to the agency office for proper disposal through the agency's contracted medical waste hauler. Transport in a secondary leak-proof container in the vehicle. | At next return to office; at least weekly. |
| 5.2.5 | All Clinical Staff | Educate patients and caregivers who self-administer injections on proper sharps disposal. Provide or arrange for a sharps container for the home. Instruct on community sharps disposal options. | At SOC and as needed. |
| 5.2.6 | Operations Director | Contract with a licensed medical waste hauler for regular sharps and medical waste pick-up from the agency office. Maintain the Waste Hauler Agreement (Appendix A) and disposal manifests. | Continuous; contract reviewed annually. |

#### 5.3 Biohazardous Waste Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | All Clinical Staff | Items saturated or dripping with blood or OPIM (dressings, gauze, wound packing) shall be placed in a red biohazard bag or bag marked with the biohazard symbol. | At time of generation. |
| 5.3.2 | All Clinical Staff | In the patient's home, if a biohazard bag is not available, place contaminated items in a sealed plastic bag labeled "BIOHAZARD" and transport to the agency office for proper disposal. | At each applicable visit. |
| 5.3.3 | All Clinical Staff | Small amounts of blood or body fluid on surfaces may be cleaned using a 1:10 bleach solution or EPA-registered disinfectant. Staff shall wear gloves during cleanup. | At time of spill. |
| 5.3.4 | Operations Director | Ensure the agency office maintains a designated, secure area for temporary storage of biohazardous waste awaiting hauler pick-up. Area must be labeled with biohazard symbol and inaccessible to unauthorized persons. | Continuous. |

#### 5.4 Pharmaceutical Waste Disposal

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | All Clinical Staff | Educate patients and caregivers on safe disposal of unused or expired medications per FDA guidelines: (a) medication take-back programs; (b) DEA-authorized collection sites; (c) FDA flush list (select medications); (d) household trash method (mix with coffee grounds/kitty litter, seal in container). | At SOC; at discharge; as needed. |
| 5.4.2 | All Clinical Staff | Do not accept or transport patient medications. If medication disposal is necessary during a visit (e.g., contaminated medication), document the disposal, amount, and method. | As needed. |
| 5.4.3 | Director of Nursing | For controlled substance disposal witnessed in the home, ensure two staff members are present and both sign the disposal documentation. | As applicable. |

#### 5.5 Exposure Incident Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Exposed Employee | Immediately following an exposure incident: (a) wash the affected area with soap and water (needlestick: allow to bleed, then wash; splash: flush eyes/mucous membranes with water for 15 minutes); (b) notify the supervisor. | Immediately. |
| 5.5.2 | Supervisor | Direct the employee to seek post-exposure medical evaluation from a designated healthcare provider or emergency department. | Within 2 hours. |
| 5.5.3 | Exposed Employee | Complete an Incident Report per RM-ER-002. | Within 24 hours. |
| 5.5.4 | Risk Manager | Ensure post-exposure evaluation and follow-up per OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR § 1910.1030(f)) including: (a) documentation of route and circumstances of exposure; (b) identification of source individual (if possible and with consent); (c) blood testing of exposed employee (with consent); (d) post-exposure prophylaxis as recommended by healthcare provider; (e) counseling. | Within 24 hours; follow-up per medical provider. |
| 5.5.5 | Risk Manager | Investigate the incident to determine if controls or work practices can be improved to prevent recurrence. | Within 14 calendar days. |
| 5.5.6 | Risk Manager | Maintain the Sharps Injury Log (Appendix B) as required by OSHA, recording: (a) type and brand of device; (b) department/work area; (c) description of incident. Employee identity is kept confidential. | Within 14 days of incident; log retained 5 years. |

### 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document/Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Waste hauler contract | Appendix A | Operations Director | Operations file | Annual review; retained 7 years. |
| Waste disposal manifests | Hauler-provided manifests | Operations Director | Operations file | At each pick-up; retained 7 years. |
| Sharps Injury Log | Appendix B | Risk Manager | Risk Management file (confidential) | Per incident; retained 5 years per OSHA. |
| Exposure Incident Reports | Per RM-ER-002 | Exposed employee / Risk Manager | Risk Management file; OSHA records | Within 24 hours; retained per OSHA (duration of employment + 30 years). |
| Post-exposure medical records | Medical evaluation records | Risk Manager | Confidential medical file | Retained per OSHA (duration of employment + 30 years). |
| PPE inventory records | Supply logs | Operations Director | Operations file | Monthly; retained 3 years. |
| Training records | Training completion documentation | HR Director | Personnel files | Per training schedule; retained per HR-WM-005. |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed Appendix C | All clinical staff | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 days; retained 7 years. |

### 7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Staff use PPE appropriately | Supervisory observation; staff self-report; patient feedback | Zero observed non-compliance. |
| Sharps disposed of in approved containers | Audit of supply usage; incident reports | Zero sharps injuries from improper disposal. |
| Biohazardous waste properly contained and labeled | Audit of waste storage area | 100% compliance. |
| Exposure incidents reported within 24 hours | Incident report timestamps | 100% compliance. |
| Post-exposure medical evaluation completed | Medical records review | 100% of exposed employees evaluated. |
| Waste hauler contract current | Contract file review | Current at all times; no lapse. |
| Sharps Injury Log maintained | Log review | Current; entries within 14 days of incident. |
| Training current for all staff | Training log review | 100% within 14 days of hire; annual refresher. |

#### Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recapping of needles by staff. | Needlestick injury; bloodborne pathogen exposure. | Enforce prohibition; include in annual training; zero tolerance. |
| No sharps container carried to visit. | Improper sharps disposal; injury risk. | Supply management; pre-visit checklist; supervisory monitoring. |
| Exposure incident not reported. | No medical evaluation; compliance violation. | Enforce reporting; emphasize in training; non-punitive reporting culture. |
| Medical waste disposed in household trash. | Environmental contamination; regulatory violation. | Train on proper segregation; supply biohazard bags. |
| Waste hauler contract lapsed. | Medical waste accumulation; regulatory violation. | Risk Manager/Operations Director tracks expiration; 90-day renewal lead time. |

### 8. Regulatory References

| Citation | Relevance |
| --- | --- |
| 29 CFR § 1910.1030 | OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard. |
| California Health & Safety Code § 117600 et seq. | Medical Waste Management Act. |
| 42 CFR § 484.70 | CMS CoP: Infection Prevention and Control. |
| EPA 40 CFR Parts 239–282 | Solid and hazardous waste disposal. |
| 21 CFR Part 1317 | DEA regulations for drug disposal. |

#### Cross-Referenced Policies

| Policy ID | Title | Relationship |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CL-SD-016 | Infection Prevention & Control | Standard Precautions; infection control program. |
| RM-ER-002 | Incident Reporting & Investigation | Exposure incident reporting. |
| RM-PS-001 | Environmental Safety Assessment | Home environment hazardous materials assessment. |
| HR-WM-003 | Employee Health & Immunization | Hepatitis B vaccination; post-exposure medical. |
| HR-WM-004 | Workplace Safety & Injury Prevention | Workplace injury including needlestick. |

### 9. Training Requirements
9.1 All clinical staff shall receive Bloodborne Pathogens training within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter per OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030(g)(2).
9.2 Training shall cover: (a) OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard; (b) agency Exposure Control Plan; (c) PPE selection, use, removal, and disposal; (d) sharps safety; (e) biohazardous waste handling; (f) pharmaceutical waste disposal; (g) exposure incident response; (h) Hepatitis B vaccination availability.
9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.
### 10. Version Control
Per RM-ER-001 §10.

# POLICY: RM-PS-003 — Product & Equipment Safety Recall Management
### Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | RM-PS-003 |
| Title | Product & Equipment Safety Recall Management |
| Domain | RM — Risk Management & Safety |
| Subdomain | PS — Patient & Environmental Safety |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Risk Manager |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Triggered |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 1. Purpose
This policy defines procedures for monitoring, responding to, and documenting medical product, medical device, and equipment safety recalls and alerts affecting patients or operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Timely identification and response to recalls protects patients from harm due to defective products and ensures regulatory compliance.
### 2. Scope
This policy applies to the Risk Manager, Operations Director, Director of Nursing, all clinical staff, and all personnel responsible for procuring, distributing, or using medical products, devices, or equipment on behalf of the agency.
### 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Product Recall | A notification from a manufacturer, the FDA, or other regulatory body that a medical product, device, or equipment has been found to be defective, dangerous, or non-compliant and must be removed from use, returned, repaired, or replaced. |
| FDA Safety Alert | A notification issued by the FDA regarding safety concerns with a specific product or device that may not require recall but warrants monitoring and precautions. |
| Class I Recall | A recall where there is a reasonable probability that the use of or exposure to a product will cause serious adverse health consequences or death. |
| Class II Recall | A recall where the use of or exposure to a product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences. |
| Class III Recall | A recall where the use of or exposure to a product is not likely to cause adverse health consequences. |
| Affected Product | Any product, device, or equipment in the agency's possession or in use by agency patients that is subject to a recall or safety alert. |

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The Risk Manager shall monitor FDA recall and safety alert databases weekly to identify recalls that may affect agency operations or patients.
4.2 Upon identification of a recall affecting agency products or patient-in-use products, the agency shall respond according to the recall classification and urgency per the procedures in this policy.
4.3 All Class I recalls affecting products in agency possession or patient use shall be treated as emergent and responded to within 24 hours.
4.4 All recall actions shall be documented in the Recall Tracking Log (Appendix A) and retained for a minimum of 7 years.
4.5 Products subject to recall shall be immediately removed from use, segregated, and labeled "DO NOT USE — RECALL" pending disposition per manufacturer/FDA instructions.
### 5. Procedures
#### 5.1 Recall Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Risk Manager | Subscribe to and monitor the following recall/alert sources: (a) FDA MedWatch Safety Alerts; (b) FDA Medical Device Recalls; (c) CDC Health Alert Network; (d) manufacturer notifications; (e) DME supplier notifications. | Weekly monitoring; immediate review of direct notifications. |
| 5.1.2 | Risk Manager | Maintain a list of all medical products, devices, and equipment commonly used or prescribed by the agency (Product Inventory List). | Maintained continuously; updated quarterly. |
| 5.1.3 | All Staff | Upon receiving any recall notice, product safety alert, or product complaint from a patient, immediately notify the Risk Manager. | Within 24 hours of receipt. |

#### 5.2 Recall Response — Agency-Held Products

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Risk Manager | Upon identification of a recall affecting products in agency inventory: (a) determine the recall classification (Class I, II, or III); (b) identify all affected product by lot number, serial number, or model; (c) log the recall in the Recall Tracking Log (Appendix A). | Within 24 hours for Class I; within 72 hours for Class II/III. |
| 5.2.2 | Risk Manager / Operations Director | Immediately remove all affected products from active inventory. Segregate and label "DO NOT USE — RECALL." Secure in a designated area. | Within 24 hours for Class I; within 72 hours for Class II/III. |
| 5.2.3 | Operations Director | Follow manufacturer/FDA instructions for disposition: (a) return to manufacturer; (b) repair/replacement; (c) destroy per instructions. Document disposition. | Per manufacturer/FDA instructions. |
| 5.2.4 | Risk Manager | Notify the Director of Nursing and Administrator of the recall and actions taken. | Within 24 hours for Class I; within 72 hours for Class II/III. |

#### 5.3 Recall Response — Patient-In-Use Products

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Risk Manager | Identify all patients currently using the affected product by cross-referencing the Product Inventory List, patient care records, and DME supplier records. | Within 24 hours for Class I; within 72 hours for Class II/III. |
| 5.3.2 | Director of Nursing | For Class I recalls: Contact each affected patient by phone immediately. Instruct the patient/caregiver to discontinue use of the product (unless discontinuation poses a greater risk). Arrange for replacement or clinical intervention as needed. | Within 24 hours. |
| 5.3.3 | Director of Nursing | For Class II/III recalls: Notify each affected patient at the next scheduled visit or by phone within 7 calendar days. Provide instructions per manufacturer/FDA guidance. | Within 7 calendar days. |
| 5.3.4 | Visiting Clinician | Document the recall notification in the patient's clinical record including: (a) product identified; (b) recall classification; (c) instructions provided; (d) patient response; (e) replacement/alternative arranged. | At time of notification. |
| 5.3.5 | Risk Manager | Coordinate with DME suppliers to arrange product replacement for affected patients. | Within 72 hours for Class I; within 14 calendar days for Class II/III. |
| 5.3.6 | Risk Manager | If any patient has experienced adverse effects from the recalled product, complete an incident report per RM-ER-002 and file an FDA MedWatch report. | Within 24 hours of identification. |

#### 5.4 Recall Closure

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Risk Manager | Close the recall in the Tracking Log when: (a) all agency-held affected products are disposed of per instructions; (b) all affected patients have been notified and product replaced; (c) all documentation is complete. | Upon completion of all actions. |
| 5.4.2 | Risk Manager | Report all Class I and Class II recalls and response actions to the Risk Management Committee at the next quarterly meeting. | Quarterly. |

### 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document/Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recall Tracking Log | Appendix A | Risk Manager | Risk Management file | Per recall; retained 7 years. |
| Recall notices received | Original notices | Risk Manager | Risk Management file | Retained 7 years. |
| Product Inventory List | Agency product/device list | Operations Director | Operations file | Updated quarterly; retained 7 years. |
| Patient notification documentation | Clinical record entries | Visiting Clinician | Patient clinical record | At notification; retained per CO-HP-007. |
| Disposition records | Returns, destruction documentation | Operations Director | Operations file | Retained 7 years. |
| FDA MedWatch reports filed | Copies of filed reports | Risk Manager | Risk Management file | If applicable; retained 7 years. |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed Appendix B | In-scope personnel | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 days; retained 7 years. |

### 7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly recall monitoring performed | Log of monitoring activities | 52 reviews per year; no gaps >14 days. |
| Class I recalls responded to within 24 hours | Recall Tracking Log timestamps | 100% compliance. |
| All affected patients notified per timelines | Patient notification documentation audit | 100% compliance. |
| All affected products removed and disposed | Disposition records review | 100% within defined timelines. |
| Recall Tracking Log current and complete | Log review | 100% entries complete. |

#### Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No systematic recall monitoring. | Recalled products remain in use; patient harm. | Enforce §5.1.1 weekly monitoring; subscribe to FDA alerts. |
| Affected patients not identified. | Patients continue using recalled product. | Maintain Product Inventory List; cross-reference with patient records. |
| Recall response delayed. | Ongoing patient exposure to defective product. | Enforce classification-based timelines; escalate Class I immediately. |
| No documentation of patient notification. | Inability to demonstrate response; survey risk. | Enforce clinical record documentation per §5.3.4. |

# POLICY: RM-PS-004 — Patient Elopement & Wandering Risk
### Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | RM-PS-004 |
| Title | Patient Elopement & Wandering Risk |
| Domain | RM — Risk Management & Safety |
| Subdomain | PS — Patient & Environmental Safety |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Risk Manager |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 1. Purpose
This policy defines risk assessment and intervention protocols for patients at risk of elopement or unsafe wandering served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Patients with cognitive impairment, dementia, delirium, behavioral health conditions, or developmental disabilities may be at risk of leaving their home environment unsafely, resulting in injury, exposure, or death. Systematic identification, documentation, and care planning reduce this risk.
### 2. Scope
This policy applies to all clinical staff who assess, plan, and deliver care to patients with identified or suspected elopement/wandering risk, their supervisors, and the Director of Nursing.
### 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Elopement | A patient's unauthorized or unsafe departure from their place of residence, particularly when the patient lacks the cognitive capacity to navigate safely or is at risk of harm. |
| Wandering | Aimless or repetitive locomotion, often associated with cognitive impairment, that may lead to elopement if not monitored. |
| Elopement Risk Assessment | A clinical evaluation of a patient's likelihood of engaging in elopement or unsafe wandering, considering cognitive status, behavioral history, environment, and supervision. |

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 All patients shall be screened for elopement/wandering risk at SOC/ROC as part of the comprehensive assessment.
4.2 Patients identified as at risk shall have an individualized Wandering/Elopement Safety Plan documented in the plan of care.
4.3 Caregivers of at-risk patients shall be educated on elopement prevention strategies, monitoring techniques, and emergency response.
4.4 Elopement events shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and investigated.
4.5 The agency shall not physically restrain patients per CL-PR-004 but shall implement environmental, educational, and monitoring interventions.
### 5. Procedures
#### 5.1 Elopement/Wandering Risk Screening

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Admitting Clinician | Screen all patients for elopement/wandering risk at SOC/ROC using the Elopement Risk Screening Tool (Appendix A), evaluating: (a) cognitive status (BIMS, orientation, diagnosis of dementia/Alzheimer's); (b) history of wandering or elopement; (c) behavioral agitation or restlessness; (d) exit-seeking behavior; (e) level of supervision in the home; (f) home security features (locked doors, alarms, fencing); (g) proximity to hazards (roads, water, extreme weather exposure). | At SOC/ROC; documented within 24 hours. |
| 5.1.2 | Admitting Clinician | Classify patient risk: ☐ Low Risk — No indicators present. ☐ Moderate Risk — 1–2 risk factors; adequate supervision typically present. ☐ High Risk — 3+ risk factors; history of elopement; inadequate supervision. | Concurrent with screening. |
| 5.1.3 | Admitting Clinician | For Moderate and High Risk patients, complete the Elopement/Wandering Safety Plan (Appendix B) and incorporate interventions into the plan of care. | Within 48 hours of screening. |

#### 5.2 Safety Plan Development

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Develop the Elopement/Wandering Safety Plan (Appendix B) addressing: (a) specific risk factors identified; (b) environmental modifications recommended (door alarms, locks, secure fencing, identification bracelet); (c) supervision recommendations (level of supervision needed; caregiver schedule); (d) patient/caregiver education provided; (e) referrals (community resources, Alzheimer's Association Safe Return, GPS device); (f) emergency response plan if elopement occurs; (g) physician notification; (h) monitoring frequency. | Within 48 hours of risk identification. |
| 5.2.2 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Educate the patient (to the extent of comprehension) and caregiver on: (a) wandering/elopement risk and potential consequences; (b) environmental safety modifications; (c) monitoring strategies; (d) what to do if the patient elopes (call 911, provide description, contact police Silver Alert if applicable); (e) available community resources. Document education per CL-SD-017. | At plan development; reinforced at each visit. |
| 5.2.3 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Notify the physician of the identified elopement risk and safety plan. Obtain orders for any recommended interventions as applicable. | Within 48 hours. |
| 5.2.4 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Communicate the elopement risk and safety plan to all disciplines providing care in the home. | Within 48 hours; at next case conference. |

#### 5.3 Ongoing Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | All Visiting Clinicians | Monitor for signs of wandering behavior or elopement risk at each visit. Note: (a) patient location and orientation at arrival; (b) evidence of wandering (inappropriate dress, confusion about surroundings); (c) caregiver report of wandering episodes; (d) adequacy of current safety measures. | Every visit. |
| 5.3.2 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Reassess elopement risk using Appendix A at each recertification and upon any change in cognitive status, behavioral status, living situation, or caregiver availability. | At recertification; upon change. |
| 5.3.3 | All Visiting Clinicians | If a new wandering episode or elopement is reported by the caregiver, immediately notify the primary nurse/case manager and complete an incident report per RM-ER-002. | Within 24 hours. |

#### 5.4 Elopement Event Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Any Staff / Caregiver | If a staff member discovers or is informed that a patient has eloped: (a) immediately search the immediate vicinity; (b) call 911 if the patient cannot be located within 15 minutes; (c) provide 911 with patient description, cognitive status, medical conditions, and last known location; (d) request Silver Alert activation if applicable; (e) notify the supervisor/on-call immediately. | Immediately. |
| 5.4.2 | Supervisor / Director of Nursing | Coordinate with law enforcement. Notify the patient's emergency contact and physician. | Within 1 hour. |
| 5.4.3 | Risk Manager | Complete investigation per RM-ER-002. Review and update the safety plan. Determine if additional interventions or caregiver support is needed. | Within 72 hours. |
| 5.4.4 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Reassess the patient after any elopement event. Update the Safety Plan. Determine if the current level of home supervision is adequate or if a higher level of care is needed. | Within 48 hours of patient's return. |

### 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document/Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Elopement Risk Screening | Completed Appendix A | Admitting Clinician | Patient clinical record | At SOC/ROC; recertification; upon change. |
| Elopement/Wandering Safety Plan | Completed Appendix B | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Patient clinical record; plan of care | Within 48 hours of risk identification. |
| Patient/caregiver education | Education documentation per CL-SD-017 | Clinician | Patient clinical record | At each education intervention. |
| Physician notification | Clinical record entry | Primary Nurse | Patient clinical record | Within 48 hours. |
| Incident reports (elopement events) | Per RM-ER-002 | Reporting staff | Risk Management file | Within 24 hours. |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed Appendix C | Clinical staff | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 days; retained 7 years. |

### 7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Elopement risk screening completed at SOC/ROC | Clinical record audit | 100% completion. |
| Safety Plan completed for Moderate/High risk patients | Clinical record audit | 100% within 48 hours. |
| Caregiver education documented | Education record audit | 100% for at-risk patients. |
| Elopement events reported per RM-ER-002 | Incident report review | 100% compliance. |
| Reassessment at recertification and upon change | Clinical record audit | 100% compliance. |

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on elopement/wandering risk identification during orientation.
9.2 Annual refresher training for all clinical staff.
9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

# POLICY: RM-PS-005 — High-Risk Medication Safety
### Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | RM-PS-005 |
| Title | High-Risk Medication Safety |
| Domain | RM — Risk Management & Safety |
| Subdomain | PS — Patient & Environmental Safety |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Risk Manager |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 1. Purpose
This policy establishes enhanced safety protocols for the management of high-risk medications in the home health setting by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. High-risk medications, including anticoagulants, opioids, insulin, and other agents with narrow therapeutic indices, carry an elevated potential for serious harm if not properly managed. This policy ensures patient safety through structured assessment, monitoring, education, and coordination.
### 2. Scope
This policy applies to all clinical staff who assess, administer, manage, or educate patients regarding high-risk medications, including registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, therapists contributing to medication management, and their supervisors.
### 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| High-Risk Medication | A medication or class of medications with an elevated potential for causing significant patient harm when used in error, including but not limited to the ISMP List of High-Alert Medications in Community/Ambulatory Settings. |
| High-Alert Medication Classes | Anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs, heparin); Opioids; Insulin and hypoglycemic agents; Chemotherapy/antineoplastic agents; Immunosuppressants; Digoxin; Sedatives/hypnotics; Antiarrhythmics; Methotrexate (non-oncologic use). |
| Narrow Therapeutic Index (NTI) | A medication where small changes in dose or blood concentration can lead to significant therapeutic failure or adverse effects. |
| Medication Adverse Event | Any injury resulting from the use of a medication, whether from error, adverse drug reaction, or drug interaction. |

### 4. Policy Statements
4.1 The agency shall maintain a list of designated high-risk/high-alert medications based on the ISMP List of High-Alert Medications in Community/Ambulatory Settings, updated annually.
4.2 Enhanced safety protocols shall be applied to all patients receiving high-risk medications, including increased assessment frequency, structured monitoring parameters, patient/caregiver education, and documented safety checks.
4.3 All medication adverse events involving high-risk medications shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and QA-AE-001.
4.4 The agency shall maintain competency requirements for all clinical staff involved in high-risk medication management.
4.5 High-risk medication safety data shall be monitored and reported to the QAPI Committee quarterly.
### 5. Procedures
#### 5.1 High-Risk Medication Identification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Maintain the agency's High-Risk Medication List (Appendix A) based on the current ISMP List of High-Alert Medications in Community/Ambulatory Settings. Review and update annually or upon ISMP list revision. | Annually; upon ISMP update. |
| 5.1.2 | All Clinical Staff | At SOC/ROC and at each medication reconciliation, identify whether the patient is receiving any medication on the agency's High-Risk Medication List. Flag the patient's record accordingly. | At SOC/ROC; at each medication reconciliation. |

#### 5.2 Enhanced Assessment and Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Admitting Clinician / Primary Nurse | For patients receiving high-risk medications, complete the High-Risk Medication Safety Assessment (Appendix B) at SOC/ROC, documenting: (a) specific high-risk medications; (b) indication for use; (c) current dose, frequency, and route; (d) prescribing physician; (e) relevant laboratory values (INR for anticoagulants, blood glucose for insulin/hypoglycemics, drug levels for digoxin/antiarrhythmics); (f) patient's knowledge of the medication; (g) ability to self-manage (cognition, dexterity, vision); (h) identified risk factors for adverse events; (i) drug interactions with current medication regimen; (j) monitoring plan. | At SOC/ROC; documented within 24 hours. |
| 5.2.2 | Primary Nurse / Case Manager | Establish medication-specific monitoring parameters for each high-risk medication in the plan of care, including: (a) clinical assessment parameters (vital signs, bleeding signs, hypoglycemia signs, etc.); (b) laboratory monitoring schedule; (c) assessment frequency; (d) escalation thresholds. | Within 48 hours of SOC. |
| 5.2.3 | All Visiting Clinicians | At each visit to a patient receiving high-risk medications, assess for: (a) adherence to prescribed regimen; (b) signs/symptoms of adverse effects per medication class; (c) relevant vital signs or point-of-care testing results; (d) patient's understanding and questions; (e) changes in other medications that could affect interactions; (f) safe storage of medication. | Every visit. |
| 5.2.4 | Primary Nurse | Monitor laboratory values per the medication-specific monitoring plan. Notify the physician of any out-of-range results. Document notification and physician response. | Per monitoring plan; physician notification within 4 hours of receiving results. |

#### 5.3 Medication-Specific Protocols

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Primary Nurse | Anticoagulants (Warfarin, DOACs, Heparin): (a) Assess for signs of bleeding at each visit (bruising, petechiae, dark stools, hematuria, gum bleeding); (b) Monitor INR per physician orders (warfarin); (c) Educate on dietary considerations (warfarin/Vitamin K); (d) Educate on drug interactions; (e) Educate on signs requiring emergency care; (f) Document on High-Risk Medication Monitoring Flow Sheet (Appendix C). | Every visit; INR per orders. |
| 5.3.2 | Primary Nurse | Opioids: (a) Assess pain level using standardized tool per CL-SD-014; (b) Assess for respiratory depression (respiratory rate <12 — notify physician immediately); (c) Assess for sedation level; (d) Assess for constipation and bowel function; (e) Assess for signs of misuse or diversion; (f) Educate on safe storage and disposal; (g) Assess for fall risk (sedation contributing to falls per CL-SD-015); (h) Document on Appendix C. | Every visit. |
| 5.3.3 | Primary Nurse | Insulin and Hypoglycemic Agents: (a) Monitor blood glucose per physician orders; (b) Assess for signs of hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia; (c) Verify correct insulin type, dose, and administration technique; (d) Assess injection sites for lipodystrophy; (e) Assess storage (refrigeration for unopened insulin); (f) Educate on hypoglycemia recognition and treatment; (g) Document on Appendix C. | Every visit; glucose per orders. |
| 5.3.4 | Primary Nurse | Digoxin: (a) Assess apical pulse for 60 seconds before administration (hold and notify physician if <60 bpm); (b) Assess for signs of toxicity (nausea, vomiting, visual disturbances, bradycardia, arrhythmia); (c) Monitor digoxin levels and electrolytes (potassium) per physician orders; (d) Document on Appendix C. | Every visit. |

#### 5.4 Patient/Caregiver Education

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Primary Nurse | Provide structured, individualized education to the patient and caregiver for each high-risk medication, covering: (a) purpose of the medication; (b) correct dose, frequency, and route; (c) expected therapeutic effects; (d) potential side effects and adverse effects; (e) signs and symptoms requiring immediate medical attention; (f) food and drug interactions; (g) safe storage and disposal; (h) importance of not modifying dose without physician direction; (i) laboratory monitoring requirements. | At SOC; reinforced at each visit; documented per CL-SD-017. |
| 5.4.2 | Primary Nurse | Assess patient/caregiver understanding using teach-back method. If comprehension is inadequate, modify educational approach and repeat. | At each education session. |
| 5.4.3 | Primary Nurse | For patients on opioids, provide education on safe storage (locked, out of reach of others), disposal of unused medications per FDA guidelines, and naloxone availability (if ordered). | At SOC; reinforced as indicated. |

#### 5.5 Adverse Event Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Any Clinical Staff | If a medication adverse event involving a high-risk medication is identified: (a) assess the patient's current condition; (b) provide immediate clinical intervention as indicated; (c) notify the physician; (d) file an incident report per RM-ER-002 and QA-AE-001. | Immediately upon identification. |
| 5.5.2 | Risk Manager | Investigate all medication adverse events involving high-risk medications. Determine whether the event was preventable. | Within 14 calendar days. |
| 5.5.3 | Risk Manager | Report high-risk medication adverse event data to the QAPI Committee and Risk Management Committee quarterly per RM-ER-005. | Quarterly. |

### 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document/Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| High-Risk Medication List | Appendix A | Director of Nursing | Clinical reference file; accessible to all staff | Annual review; retained 7 years. |
| High-Risk Medication Safety Assessment | Completed Appendix B | Admitting Clinician / Primary Nurse | Patient clinical record | At SOC/ROC; retained per CO-HP-007. |
| High-Risk Medication Monitoring Flow Sheet | Completed Appendix C | Visiting Clinician | Patient clinical record | Updated each visit; retained per CO-HP-007. |
| Patient/caregiver education | Education record per CL-SD-017 | Visiting Clinician | Patient clinical record | At each education session. |
| Medication adverse event reports | Per RM-ER-002 | Reporting staff | Risk Management file | Within 24 hours; retained 7 years. |
| Policy acknowledgment | Signed Appendix D | All clinical staff | Policy acknowledgment file | Within 14 days; retained 7 years. |

### 7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-risk medications identified and flagged in patient record | Clinical record audit | 100% compliance. |
| High-Risk Medication Safety Assessment completed at SOC/ROC | Clinical record audit | 100% completion. |
| Monitoring parameters established in plan of care | Plan of care audit | 100% for patients on high-risk meds. |
| Medication-specific assessments performed at each visit | Visit documentation audit | ≥95% compliance. |
| Patient/caregiver education documented with teach-back | Education record audit | ≥95% for patients on high-risk meds. |
| Adverse events involving high-risk medications reported | Incident report review | 100% compliance. |
| Quarterly QAPI reporting on high-risk medication safety | QAPI meeting minutes | 4 reports per year. |

#### Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-risk medications not identified in patient record. | Enhanced monitoring not initiated; adverse events. | Enforce §5.1.2 identification at SOC/medication reconciliation. |
| Monitoring parameters not established. | Inadequate surveillance; delayed detection of adverse effects. | Enforce §5.2.2; include in care plan audit. |
| Laboratory results not followed up timely. | Therapeutic failure or toxicity. | Enforce §5.2.4; 4-hour notification standard. |
| Education insufficient; patient does not understand medication risks. | Non-adherence; self-medication errors; adverse events. | Enforce teach-back method per §5.4.2. |

### 8. Regulatory References

| Citation | Relevance |

| 42 CFR § 484.55 | Comprehensive assessment includes drug regimen review. |
| 42 CFR § 484.60 | Care plan must address medication management. |
| 42 CFR § 484.65 | QAPI must address patient safety including medication safety. |

### 9. Training Requirements
9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on high-risk medication safety during orientation within 14 calendar days of hire.
9.2 Annual competency evaluation for all clinical staff on high-risk medication management, including medication-specific protocols for anticoagulants, opioids, insulin, and digoxin.
9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix D within 14 calendar days.

# RM-EP-001 — Emergency Preparedness Program


## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |

| Policy ID | RM-EP-001 |

---

## 2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive Emergency Preparedness (EP) Program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. as required by 42 CFR §484.102 — Condition of Participation: Emergency Preparedness. This CoP is a standalone, separately surveyed Condition that requires a unified, documented EP program with all four required elements:

**(a) Risk assessment and EP plan** — an all-hazards approach based on the geographic service area's specific risks  
**(b) Policies and procedures** — detailing how services will be maintained through emergencies  
**(c) Communication plan** — for patients, staff, and external entities  
**(d) Training and testing** — including two exercises per year, at least one of which must incorporate an actual emergency event or a community-based exercise when available

CMS State Operations Manual Appendix B surveys emergency preparedness as a unified CoP. Fragmented coverage across individual policies (CL-PR-005, OP-FM-005, OP-SL-006, HR-TD-005) does not satisfy the CMS requirement for a documentable, integrated EP program. This policy serves as the governing EP Program document; the pre-existing policies remain in force and are cross-referenced as subcomponents.

---

## 3. Scope

This program applies to:

* All employees, contractors, volunteers, and students of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
* All patients actively enrolled in care with the agency, from the date of admission through the date of discharge
* All operational sites: main office, any satellite/branch offices, and the full geographic service area in which home visits are conducted
* All emergency and disaster scenarios identified in the Risk Assessment (Section 6.1)

This program covers emergencies that require implementation of contingency operations, including but not limited to: natural disasters (earthquake, wildfire, flood, extreme heat events, mudslide), severe weather, public health emergencies (pandemic, disease outbreak, environmental contamination), terrorism or civil unrest, infrastructure failures (utility outages, building evacuations, telecommunications failure), and individual patient emergencies requiring care continuity.

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Emergency / Disaster | Any event, natural or man-made, that disrupts or threatens to disrupt the agency's ability to provide safe, effective care to patients or threatens the safety of staff. |
| All-Hazards Approach | An EP planning methodology that addresses a broad range of risks without specifying a single type of hazard — focusing on capabilities, roles, and communication that apply across risk types. Required by 42 CFR §484.102(a)(1)(i). |
| Incident Command System (ICS) | A standardized, hierarchical approach to emergency response management that establishes clear command authority, span of control, and communication protocols. The agency uses an ICS-based structure during declared emergencies. |
| Essential Patients | Patients in the agency's active caseload who require more frequent monitoring or have physical or cognitive limitations that make them particularly vulnerable during an emergency. Identified through the Vulnerability Assessment at admission per Section 6.2. |
| Alternate Care Site | A location, other than the patient's primary residence, where care could be coordinated or services temporarily provided if the patient's home is inaccessible during a disaster. |
| Business Continuity | The agency's capacity to maintain critical operations (patient care, billing, communications) during and after an emergency event. |
| After-Action Report (AAR) | A structured review of how the agency performed during an actual or simulated emergency, identifying gaps and improvements. Required after each training exercise. |
| Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) | The operational subplan detailing how the agency will sustain or rapidly restore essential services during and after an emergency. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a comprehensive, written Emergency Preparedness Program that meets all four elements of 42 CFR §484.102 at all times. The program shall be based on an all-hazards risk assessment specific to the agency's geographic service area and patient population.

5.2 The Administrator is the designated EP Program Responsible Person. The Risk Manager is the operational EP coordinator. The Director of Nursing is responsible for clinical EP coordination. All three shall have designated alternates.

5.3 The EP Program shall be reviewed and updated no less than annually, and within 30 calendar days of any of the following: (a) a significant change in the agency's service area, patient population, or operations; (b) completion of an emergency exercise or response to an actual emergency that identifies program deficiencies; (c) a change in the regulatory EP requirements.

5.4 The agency shall conduct a minimum of two emergency preparedness exercises each calendar year: (a) at least one full-scale exercise, community-based exercise, or response to an actual emergency; and (b) at least one tabletop exercise, drills, or other exercise type, as an alternative. Where the agency participates in a community-based exercise, this shall count as the full-scale exercise requirement.

5.5 All employees shall receive EP-specific training at orientation and at least annually thereafter, sufficient to enable them to execute their roles in the EP plan.

5.6 The Governing Body shall review and approve the EP Program annually per GV-GB-001, Section 6.2.6.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 All-Hazards Risk Assessment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Administrator / Risk Manager | Conduct a written all-hazards risk assessment covering the agency's full geographic service area. The assessment shall identify: (a) natural hazards likely in the service area (Los Angeles / Southern California context: earthquake, wildfire, flood, landslide, extreme heat event, Southern California Edison Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) events, Santa Ana wind events); (b) man-made hazards (power grid failure, civil unrest, terrorism, regional contamination, water supply disruption); (c) public health hazards (pandemic influenza, novel pathogen emergence, regional outbreak); (d) technology hazards (EHR system failure, cybersecurity incident, telecommunications outage). | Completed annually; initial assessment within 30 days of program adoption. |
| 6.1.2 | Risk Manager | For each identified hazard, assess: (a) likelihood of occurrence (Low/Medium/High based on CalOES Hazard Mitigation Plan data for the service area); (b) potential impact on patient care operations (Low/Medium/High); (c) existing controls mitigating the risk. | As part of annual risk assessment. |
| 6.1.3 | Administrator | Use the risk assessment findings to prioritize EP planning: highest-likelihood + highest-impact hazards shall have specific, more detailed procedures in the EP plan. Low-likelihood / low-impact hazards are covered under the general all-hazards protocols. | At adoption; annually updated. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Integrate the community hazard assessment into the patient vulnerability assessment process (Section 6.2) to identify which patients are most at risk from the identified hazards. | Annual integration with risk assessment cycle. |

### 6.2 Patient Vulnerability Assessment and Prioritization

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Admitting Clinician | At admission, complete the Patient Emergency Preparedness Vulnerability Assessment (Appendix A) for every patient. The assessment shall document: (a) patient reliance on electrically powered medical equipment (ventilator, oxygen concentrator, IV infusion pump, electric hospital bed, stair lift); (b) patient mobility limitations (non-ambulatory, wheelchair-dependent, unable to self-evacuate); (c) patient cognitive limitations affecting self-protective action; (d) patient's access to emergency contacts or caregivers; (e) geographic risk of the patient's location (flood zone, high fire hazard area, hillside property). | At admission; reviewed at each recertification or significant change in condition. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing | Maintain a current list of all Essential Patients (those with electric-dependent equipment, no self-evacuation capacity, or living alone with cognitive impairment). This list shall be updated in the care management system within 24 hours of any change in patient status, and shall be available to the on-call nurse at all times. | Maintained continuously; updated within 24 hours of change. |
| 6.2.3 | Scheduler / Director of Nursing | Register patients with electrically powered life-sustaining equipment with their utility provider's Medical Baseline or Life Support program and with the local public safety agency's Access and Functional Needs (AFN) registry where available. Document registration in the patient record. | Within 14 days of admission for qualifying patients. |
| 6.2.4 | Director of Nursing | During any declared emergency or Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) event: activate the Essential Patients contact protocol — direct care staff to attempt contact with all Essential Patients within 4 hours of emergency declaration; document contact attempts and patient status. | Within 4 hours of emergency activation. |

### 6.3 EP Policies and Procedures — Continuity of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Administrator / Director of Nursing | Maintain written Continuity of Care Procedures (Appendix B) covering at minimum: (a) how scheduled visits will be prioritized and rescheduled during emergency-related service disruption; (b) how Essential Patients will be triaged for available staff capacity; (c) how abbreviated clinical visits or telephone check-ins will be authorized as an emergency substitution; (d) criteria for suspending vs. continuing services to patients in affected areas; (e) procedures for coordinating with discharging hospitals or receiving facilities if patients must be evacuated or hospitalized. | Current procedures maintained as Appendix B; reviewed annually and after each exercise. |
| 6.3.2 | Administrator | Maintain written Office/Operations Continuity Procedures (Appendix C) covering: (a) ability to process payroll, benefits, and employee communications when the main office is inaccessible; (b) access to EHR when primary server or internet is unavailable (identify alternate access method, e.g., mobile hotspot, printed backup schedule, EHR vendor's offline mode); (c) backup contact lists for all staff and key Agencies (accreditation body, Medicare administrative contractor, CDPH, local emergency management); (d) procedure for operating from an alternate site if the main office is uninhabitable. | Current procedures maintained as Appendix C; reviewed annually. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Maintain written procedures for how clinical documentation will be captured and preserved during an EHR or telecommunications outage, including: (a) use of agency-approved paper documentation forms; (b) required elements to be transcribed into EHR within 24 hours of service restoration; (c) chain of custody for paper records generated during outage. | Current procedures maintained as Appendix B; reviewed annually. |
| 6.3.4 | Risk Manager | Ensure the agency maintains minimum operational supply levels at all times including: (a) 72-hour supply of commonly used clinical supplies (wound dressings, IV supplies, medication management supplies) distributable to Essential Patients if resupply is disrupted; (b) 72-hour supply of PPE; (c) backup communication devices (charged portable mobile devices for key staff). | Supplies maintained at minimum levels; reviewed quarterly. |

### 6.4 Emergency Communication Plan

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | Administrator | Maintain a current, printed Emergency Contact Directory (Appendix D) that is distributed to all supervisors and updated at least annually (or within 14 days of any contact change). The directory must contain: (a) All agency staff with primary and secondary phone contact methods; (b) Governing Body members; (c) Medicare Administrative Contractor (CGS or Palmetto, as applicable); (d) California Department of Public Health HCAI regional contact; (e) Cal OES State Operations Center (916-845-8911); (f) Local emergency management agency; (g) Local fire and law enforcement non-emergency lines; (h) HHA accreditation body (if applicable); (i) Key vendors (medical supply, pharmacy, EHR vendor). | Maintained continuously; distributed to all supervisors; updated within 14 days of change. |
| 6.4.2 | Administrator | Establish and document the staff notification tree for emergency activation: (a) Risk Manager notifies Department Heads; (b) Department Heads notify all assigned staff via the agency's designated mass-notification method (phone tree, text broadcast, or EHR notification); (c) confirm receipt and availability of all staff is documented on the Staff Notification Log (Appendix E). | Protocol established; tested in each annual exercise. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Establish the patient notification procedure for emergency disruption: (a) if scheduled visits cannot be made, notify the patient (or caregiver) by phone no later than 2 hours before the scheduled visit time; (b) provide safety guidance matching the emergency type (e.g., shelter-in-place, evacuation route resources); (c) document all patient contacts and outcomes in the Emergency Patient Contact Log (Appendix F). | Upon emergency activation; contact within 2 hours of missed visit. |
| 6.4.4 | Administrator | Identify and document the agency's alternate communication methods in the event of phone system and internet outage simultaneously: designated emergency FM radio station for public alerts; agency-issued satellite phone or satellite communicator for Administrator and Risk Manager; walkie-talkie/radio for on-site staff if main office is occupied during civil event. | Documented in EP plan; devices maintained and charged. |
| 6.4.5 | Administrator | When an emergency disrupts normal operations for more than 24 hours, notify the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) per MAC guidance for the affected geographic area. Document the notification and retain in the EP file. | Within 24 hours of extended operational disruption. |

### 6.5 Training and Testing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Risk Manager / Training Coordinator | Provide EP training to all new employees as part of orientation, before they begin patient care duties, covering: (a) their specific role in the EP plan; (b) the patient vulnerability assessment and Essential Patients protocol; (c) communication tree and staff notification procedure; (d) emergency supply location; (e) ICS structure during emergencies; (f) how to report an emergency and what to do if they are isolated during a disaster. | At orientation, before first clinical duties. |
| 6.5.2 | Risk Manager / Training Coordinator | Provide annual EP refresher training to all employees covering: (a) post-exercise lessons learned from the prior year; (b) any EP plan changes; (c) regulatory updates; (d) a scenario-based rapid runthrough of a specific emergency type. | Annually; completed within calendar year. |
| 6.5.3 | Risk Manager | Plan and execute at least two emergency preparedness exercises per calendar year (per 42 CFR §484.102(d)): (a) Exercise Type 1 — full-scale exercise, community-based exercise, OR an actual emergency response that is documented and reviewed as an exercise equivalent; (b) Exercise Type 2 — tabletop exercise with agency leadership and clinical managers, or structured drills. Both exercise types shall test the communication plan and EP procedures. | Two exercises per calendar year; at least one full-scale or community-based. |
| 6.5.4 | Risk Manager | Complete a written After-Action Report (AAR) within 30 calendar days of each exercise or actual emergency response. The AAR shall document: (a) scenario used; (b) participants; (c) strengths identified; (d) gaps or failures identified; (e) corrective actions with assigned responsible party and completion deadline; (f) plan or procedure updates required. | Within 30 days of each exercise or emergency response. |
| 6.5.5 | Risk Manager | Implement all corrective actions identified in AARs within the timeframe specified in the AAR. Unresolved corrective actions shall be escalated to the Administrator at the next management meeting. | Per AAR-specified deadlines. |
| 6.5.6 | Administrator | Present the annual EP program review, exercise results, and AAR summaries to the Governing Body for review and approval, per GV-GB-001 Section 6.2.6. The Governing Body shall review and approve the EP plan annually. | At the Governing Body's third quarterly meeting each calendar year. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Actual emergency event declared in the service area | Risk Manager activates ICS; Administrator assumes Incident Commander role. | Execute EP communication plan. Activate Essential Patient contact protocol. Document all actions in real-time on the Emergency Operations Log. | Immediately upon declaration. |
| Annual program review not completed by due date | Risk Manager notifies Administrator. | Emergency completion convened within 14 days. Reason documented. Notify MAC if regulatory deadline is at risk. | 14 days. |
| CMS survey finds EP deficiency | Administrator convenes action meeting within 48 hours. | Develop Plan of Correction per CMS timelines. Risk Manager leads all EP corrective actions. Weekly status reports to Governing Body until resolved. | Plan of Correction per CMS-specified deadline. |
| Community-based exercise opportunity not available in a calendar year | Administrator documents unavailability in EP file. | Conduct internal full-scale exercise as substitute; document basis for substitution per CMS guidance. | In lieu of community exercise if none available. |

---

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Written EP program covers all 4 elements of 42 CFR §484.102 | Annual review against CMS Appendix B EP survey protocol | All 4 elements documented and current |
| Annual risk assessment completed | Review of risk assessment document | Completed within 12 months; service-area specific |
| Patient Vulnerability Assessments completed at admission | Audit of 10% of admission records quarterly | 100% completed at admission |
| Two exercises conducted annually with AARs on file | Review of exercise documentation and AARs | 2 exercises per calendar year; AARs within 30 days each |
| All EP corrective actions (from AARs) completed on time | Review of AAR corrective action tracker | 100% closed by assigned deadline |
| All employees trained at orientation and annually | Training log audit | 100% at orientation; 100% annual rate within calendar year |
| Governing Body approval of EP plan documented | Review of Governing Body minutes | Annual approval documented at third quarterly meeting |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting an Emergency Preparedness survey under the State Operations Manual Appendix B will specifically verify:

1. That a single, integrated EP program document exists covering all four required elements — not four separate policies. Surveyors are trained to ask for "your Emergency Preparedness Plan" and will note fragmentation as a program deficiency.
2. That the risk assessment was based on the agency's specific geographic service area — not a generic template. For agencies in Southern California, surveyors know the region's hazards (earthquake, wildfire, Santa Ana winds, PSPS events) and will probe whether the plan addresses them.
3. That the patient vulnerability assessment is documented for all active patients and that an Essential Patients list is maintained in real-time.
4. That two exercises were conducted in the prior calendar year, with written AARs. Missing an exercise year, or conducting an exercise without an AAR, is a common citation.
5. That staff can describe their role in the EP plan consistently with what's documented.
6. That the communication plan is written, tested, and includes all required external contacts.
7. Governing Body approval of the EP plan is documented in board minutes.

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fragmented EP coverage across 4+ policies with no governing EP Program document | CMS Condition-level deficiency — failure to have an EP Program | This policy (RM-EP-001) is the governing EP Program; the 4 existing policies are incorporated as cross-references/subcomponents |
| Risk assessment is generic (not service-area specific) | Surveyor rejects non-specific plan as non-compliant | Section 6.1 specifically addresses Southern California hazard profile |
| Essential Patients list not maintained in real-time | Critical patients unidentified during actual emergency | DON responsible for 24-hr update of list; on-call access required |
| Only one exercise conducted per year, not two | CoP deficiency | Annual exercise calendar set by January 15; two exercises planned; AARs required within 30 days |
| AAR completed but corrective actions not tracked or implemented | Recurring deficiencies across exercise years | AAR corrective action tracker maintained; escalated to Administrator if overdue |
| No documentation that patients were contacted during an exercise | Surveyor cannot verify communication plan was tested | Communication plan testing explicitly required in exercise script; Appendix F log completed |

| Field clinical staff | Essential Patient protocol, patient contact procedures during emergency, abbreviated clinical visit documentation, field safety during specific hazard types (earthquake, wildfire) | Scenario-based in-service — 45 minutes | At orientation; annually | DON / Risk Manager |

| Leadership team (Administrator, DON, Risk Manager, Supervisors) | Full emergency exercise participation: ICS roles, command decisions, communication execution, AAR participation | Tabletop or full-scale exercise | Twice annually | Risk Manager with external facilitator for community exercise |

## C. IBM Policy Metadata Standards (Global Definitions)
### C1. Policy Status Definitions

| Status | Definition | IBM Equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACTIVE | Policy is published, in force, and operationally enforced | Published |
| DRAFT | Policy is under initial development, not yet approved | Draft |
| UNDER REVIEW | Active policy currently under scheduled or triggered revision | In Review |
| DEPRECATED | Policy has been retired, superseded, or made obsolete | Deprecated |

All 253 policies in v7.0 carry status: ACTIVE
### C2. Review Cycle Definitions

| Cycle | Definition | Trigger Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Triggered | Review initiated by regulatory change, incident, audit finding, or corrective action | Event-based; may occur at any time regardless of cycle |

### 8. Final Completeness Statement
This framework v7.0 represents the current, implemented enterprise policy taxonomy for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. All 253 policies across 10 domains and 42 subdomains have been validated for ID integrity, structural correctness, IBM metadata completeness (Owner/Steward, Status, Review Cycle, Access Tier, Regulatory Tags), subdomain uniqueness, regulatory coverage, and non-redundancy. Version 7.0 adds 9 new operational policies addressing previously uncodified regulatory requirements (HIPAA comprehensive privacy, BAA management, incident response, data governance, FWA, AI governance, Cal/OSHA IIPP, workforce training governance, and employee health), introduces the Regulatory Tag System as a formal enterprise metadata layer, and updates all indexes and counts. The framework is certified at 100% IBM Knowledge Catalog / Watson governance artifact compliance and is ready to serve as the canonical source for system and application development.
## P. Regulatory Tag Governance (NEW — v7.0)
### P1. Purpose and Definition
The Regulatory Tag System is a cross-domain classification layer used to identify policies that materially support major regulatory obligations regardless of their domain or subdomain placement within the enterprise taxonomy. Regulatory Tags are additive metadata; they do not alter the taxonomy structure, domain assignments, subdomain assignments, classification tiers, access tiers, or ownership/stewardship designations.
### P2. Active Tags (Current State)

| Tag | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| HIPAA | Policies governing PHI/ePHI privacy, security, access, disclosure, breach handling, and administrative/physical/technical safeguards under 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164, the HITECH Act, and 42 CFR Part 2 (substance use disorder confidentiality). |
| OSHA | Policies governing workforce safety, hazard prevention, occupational exposure, personal protective equipment, workplace violence, infection exposure, bloodborne pathogens, aerosol transmissible diseases, hazard communication, ergonomics, and safety programs under 29 CFR Part 1910 and Cal/OSHA (8 CCR). |
| CA | Policies governing California-specific legal requirements including the CMIA (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 56–56.37), Cal/OSHA (8 CCR), California data breach notification (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82), California Health & Safety Code, California Labor Code (including SB 553), California Family Code, and other state-level requirements that exceed or supplement federal law. |

### P3. Assignment Governance
#### P3.1 Authority
Regulatory Tags are assigned by the Compliance Officer in consultation with the relevant Domain Owner/Steward. Final tag assignments for new or revised policies shall be approved by the Compliance Officer or the Governing Body (for Tier 4 policies).
#### P3.2 Assignment Events
Tags shall be assigned or reviewed:
At policy creation: During the policy development and approval process per GV-PM-001, the Compliance Officer shall evaluate and assign applicable Regulatory Tags before publication.
At major policy revision: During the policy review and revision cycle per GV-PM-002, existing tags shall be validated and new tags assigned if the revision changes the policy's regulatory relevance.
Upon regulatory change: When a federal, state, or local regulatory change is identified per CO-RA-001, the Compliance Officer shall evaluate whether affected policies require tag addition, modification, or removal.
Annual validation: All Regulatory Tag assignments shall be validated during the annual framework review, concurrent with the policy review cycle. The Compliance Officer shall present the annual tag validation report to the Governing Body at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year.
#### P3.3 Assignment Criteria
A Regulatory Tag is assigned to a policy when the policy substantively and operationally addresses one or more requirements of the tagged regulatory framework. Tags are not assigned based on incidental keyword presence or tangential relevance. The test for assignment is:
Does this policy, if removed from the agency's policy library, create a material gap in the agency's compliance with the tagged regulatory framework?
If yes, the tag is assigned. If no, the tag is not assigned.
#### P3.4 Cross-Domain Consistency
The Compliance Officer shall ensure that Regulatory Tag assignments are consistent across domains. A regulatory requirement that is materially addressed by multiple policies across different domains shall have consistent tagging across all relevant policies.
### P4. Reporting and Filtering
Regulatory Tags enable the following capabilities:

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Policy Filtering | Application users may filter the policy library by Regulatory Tag to view all policies relevant to a specific regulatory framework (e.g., all HIPAA-tagged policies, regardless of domain). |
| Audit Preparation | When preparing for a HIPAA audit, Cal/OSHA inspection, or CDPH survey, the agency can generate a filtered view of all applicable policies as a pre-audit readiness check. |
| Survey Readiness | CMS survey preparation can leverage tag filtering to verify that all regulatory areas have corresponding policies in place. |
| Gap Analysis | Regulatory Tag coverage reports enable identification of regulatory areas that may lack sufficient policy coverage. |
| Training Assignment Logic | Regulatory Tags can be used to drive training assignment, ensuring that all workforce members receive training on policies tagged to the regulatory frameworks relevant to their role. |
| Compliance Dashboards | Dashboard views can aggregate policy compliance metrics (acknowledgment rates, review cycle currency) by Regulatory Tag for regulatory-specific reporting. |
| Cross-Domain Traceability | Tags enable traceability from a regulatory requirement to all policies supporting that requirement, regardless of where those policies reside in the taxonomy. |

### P5. Future Expansion
The Regulatory Tag System is extensible by design. Future framework versions may introduce additional tags as operational need and regulatory landscape dictate. Potential future tags include, but are not limited to:
CMS — Policies directly addressing CMS Conditions of Participation
CDPH — Policies addressing California Department of Public Health requirements
OIG — Policies addressing Office of Inspector General compliance expectations
EP — Policies addressing Emergency Preparedness requirements (42 CFR § 484.102)
MEDICARE BILLING — Policies addressing Medicare billing and reimbursement compliance
Additional tags shall be introduced through the framework revision process (EN-TG-001) and require Compliance Officer recommendation and Governing Body approval. Tags may not be introduced outside the formal framework revision process.
### P6. Integration with IBM Governance Model
The Regulatory Tag System is designed as a natural extension of the existing IBM-aligned enterprise governance model. It complements — and does not conflict with — the following existing metadata layers:

| Existing Layer | Relationship to Regulatory Tags |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | Tags are cross-domain; they operate independently of domain assignment. A tag may apply to policies in any domain. |
| Subdomain | Tags are cross-subdomain; they operate independently of subdomain assignment. |
| Classification Tier | Tags are independent of tier. A REQUIRED policy and a RECOMMENDED policy may both carry the same tag if both substantively address the tagged regulation. |
| Access Tier | Tags are independent of access tier. |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Tags are assigned by the Compliance Officer in consultation with the Owner/Steward; ownership is not affected by tag assignment. |
| Review Cycle | Tags do not alter the review cycle. However, a regulatory change affecting a tagged framework may trigger review of all policies carrying that tag. |

The Regulatory Tag System satisfies the IBM Metadata Extensibility standard by demonstrating that the framework can incorporate additional classification layers without structural modification to the existing taxonomy.
